Sell My House Fast in Jacksonville, FL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Jacksonville, FL: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Jacksonville, FL sale
  • Turn the Jacksonville, FL offer down and you owe us nothing

Sell Your Jacksonville House for Cash

Tell us about your Jacksonville house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Jacksonville?
We buy Jacksonville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How can a Jacksonville homeowner sell fast?

Your choices are a listing with an agent, a cash offer, or a sale to an as-is purchaser who takes on the repair bill and the house untouched. Whichever you choose, two witnesses sign the deed and the Duval County clerk records it. How quickly it all happens depends on the buyer's financing, the state of title and any lien that needs a payoff letter.

The city is huge and varied, which means the best route changes house by house. A well-kept house in a sought-after neighborhood can do well on the open market. One that needs a roof, rewiring or storm repair, or is tangled up in tenants or an estate, often fits a cash or as-is buyer, since no lender inspection stands in the way.

  • Listing: biggest buyer pool, longest timeline, lender appraisal and repair requests.
  • Cash or as-is: fewer conditions, and you price the condition in.
  • Family transfer: still a conveyance for value, and the homestead rules below still apply.

Jacksonville in brief

Jacksonville merged with Duval County in 1968, and it bills itself as the largest city by area in the continental United States, covering 747.29 land square miles. Population is estimated at 1,017,689 for July 2025. One municipal government covers beach communities, a riverfront downtown, suburban subdivisions and rural edges, so conditions differ block by block and a neighbor's experience may not match yours.

A typical owner-occupied house is worth $293,700, owners live in 57.6 percent of homes, and the middle rent is $1,465. Because permit, utility and code questions all go to one city, a single call there tells you about open permits before you list.

How Duval's homestead exemption plays into a sale

Selling ends your exemption, and the buyer files a new one. In Duval the base amount is $25,000, with up to $25,000 more on value above $50,000, and that second layer does not reduce school taxes.

After a sale the assessed figure jumps to market value on the next tax roll, and the Save Our Homes ceiling of 3 percent or less on yearly increases starts over for the new owner. A buyer who held a Florida homestead in any of the three prior roll years can file for portability, a separate application. The timely date for both is March 1, and late filing runs to early September.

Duval renews exemptions automatically each January 1 when nothing has changed, and a renewal card arrives as a receipt. The office also has a brochure on how short-term renting can affect exemptions, which landlords should read before listing a house they once lived in. For forms, call 904-255-5900 or email pacustserv@coj.net. Visit 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jacksonville house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Other exemptions a buyer or seller might mention

Beyond the basic homestead, the Duval appraiser runs many other exemption categories, and a buyer's eligibility for one can affect an offer. Before closing, ask the office whether a given benefit carries over or has to be refiled.

  • Military and service members: armed forces deployment, disabled veteran, and service-connected total and permanent disability exemptions.
  • First responders: a total and permanent disability exemption for them and their surviving spouses, and a homestead exemption for surviving spouses of military personnel or first responders.
  • Seniors: a senior citizen exemption with its own application and the Duval 501 form.
  • Other: blindness, widow or widower, disability, a granny-flat assessment reduction for parents' or grandparents' quarters, conservation land, and institutional or non-profit exemptions.
  • Historic preservation: available through the City of Jacksonville.

Several forms are handed out by phone or email, so call 904-255-5900 to make sure you hold the current version.

Where the sale proceeds from here

Two offices will carry most of your questions. The Duval County Property Appraiser covers exemptions and portability, and the Duval tax collector quotes the balance due. The city itself handles permits, utilities and code questions, so one call there can show whether any work on the house is still open.

Next, decide how you want to sell. A tidy house in a sought-after area may net more through an agent, though showings and a lender's appraisal slow the schedule. A house with a worn roof, tenants or a tangled estate often moves quicker to a buyer who pays cash and accepts it as is. Whatever the route, collect offers in writing, compare the amount you keep rather than the headline price, and confirm who pays recording and deed tax before you sign. Keep the lease, tax bill and permit receipts in one folder so a buyer can verify the house quickly.

Transfer costs and tax dates

Here the deed rate matches the rest of the state, 70 cents for each $100 paid, and every signer is liable. A mortgage on the property is part of the consideration, assumed by the buyer or not.

You pay the clerk at the recording counter. Section 28.24 fees open at $5.00 for a first page and rise with extra pages, names and technology charges.

Property tax has its own rhythm: January 1 sets value, November brings bills, early-payment discounts shrink through February, and April 1 marks delinquency. At closing the title agent prorates the year, so get your actual balance from the Duval tax collector rather than guessing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jacksonville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Dates and amounts for a Jacksonville sale

Unpaid property taxDelinquent April 1
Appraiser forms line904-255-5900

Foreclosure, an estate or a tenant

  • Foreclosure: once final judgment is entered, the clerk schedules a public sale 20 to 35 days later, unless the lender agrees to a longer gap. Homestead owners should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale about leftover funds.
  • Estate: summary administration fits a modest estate, meaning $150,000 or under outside exempt assets, or a death over two years ago.
  • Tenants: someone renting by the month must get 30 days' notice. A tenant who raises any defense other than payment has to deposit accrued rent with the court within five days of service.

What to prepare before a Jacksonville buyer visits

  • Recorded deed, survey if you have one, and the latest tax bill.
  • Payoff letters, and association paperwork for condos and HOAs.
  • Receipts and permits for the roof, major systems and storm repairs.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers if the house is occupied.
  • For an inherited home, the court order authorizing the sale.

With a signed contract, the title agent runs the title search, gathers payoff letters, drafts the deed and arranges the two witnesses. The clerk then records the deed and collects the tax. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, though you should ask for a written timeline from any buyer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Jacksonville charge a different deed tax?

No. Duval uses the usual 70 cents per $100, and only Miami-Dade stands apart.

When is the Duval homestead deadline?

March 1 every year. A late filing is accepted until early September, which is 25 days after proposed-tax notices go out in mid-August.

Does a buyer inherit my homestead benefit?

No. The sale resets value to market for the next roll, and the buyer applies for a new exemption.

Can I sell with a tenant living there?

Yes, and the buyer should get a copy of the lease. A tenancy by the month ends on 30 days' notice. Unpaid rent starts with a three-day written notice.

Who handles exemption forms?

The Duval County Property Appraiser. Call 904-255-5900 or email pacustserv@coj.net for form requests.

Selling in Miami?

Who sells and who buys in Miami

Miami has an estimated 489,812 residents across 36.00 square miles of land, up 10.8 percent from 2020, and only 30.8 percent of its 194,821 households own their home. Most sellers here own into a market of renters and investors. About 77.2 percent of residents speak another language at home, so expect bilingual showings and have any contract translated or explained before anyone signs.

City of Miami housing figures
Housing measureCity of Miami amount
Median home value reported by owners$518,100
Owner cost per month, with a mortgage$2,863
Owner cost per month, no mortgage$858
Median rent$1,758

A citywide midpoint hides a wide spread between a waterfront condo and an inland bungalow, so get an offer for your own address.

Short-term rentals in Miami

Rarely allowed. The city's short-term rental rules treat houses and duplexes in T3 and T4-R transect zones as generally not eligible for short-term rental or lodging use, and tie that position to City of Miami v. Airbnb.

Converting apartments and condos faces a longer checklist: a Certificate of Occupancy, a state lodging license, a Certificate of Use, a Business Tax Receipt and any county approvals. The Certificate of Use renews yearly and the city may audit or inspect without notice. Once more than 25 percent of units are in short-term use, the whole building is classed as transient, which triggers a change of occupancy and extra building code work.

Check zoning with the city before you count on nightly income as an alternative to selling.

Does Miami-Dade's recertification rule apply to my property?

Not to a single family house. Single-family homes, duplexes, and buildings with an occupant load of ten or less and 2,000 square feet or less are outside the process. It matters mostly to condo and apartment owners.

For covered buildings, the program began in 1975 and was amended June 1, 2022 after a state law on milestone inspections of condominium and cooperative buildings of three stories or more. Coastal condo buildings of that height within three miles of the shoreline built on or after 1998 are inspected at 25 years, other newer buildings at 30, and each repeats every ten years.

  • The owner receives a Notice of Required Recertification.
  • Within ninety days of the notice, a written report from a Florida-registered engineer or architect must be filed.
  • The report certifies the structure is structurally and electrically safe for continued occupancy.

A condo seller should have the building's recertification status in the document package.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Miami house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Miami-Dade deed taxes

Only Miami-Dade runs its own formula: 60 cents per hundred dollars plus a 45 cent surtax, with the surtax skipped on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Every other county charges 70 cents.

The base counts any mortgage that stays on the property, so a payoff does not shrink it. All parties on the instrument are liable regardless of who the contract names, so read that clause slowly.

  • Clerk recording charges under section 28.24 of the Florida Statutes.
  • Payoffs for mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes.
  • A draft settlement statement you review before signing.

Miami-Dade tax calendar and your closing

Value and billing sit in separate county offices. The property appraiser neither mails bills nor collects money, so any question about a balance owed goes to the Tax Collector.

The 2026 roll was certified October 16, 2026, and the June 1 estimate of countywide taxable value was $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent over 2025. A challenge to value is filed with the clerk inside a 25-day window that opens with the proposed tax notice, and the value adjustment board hears it.

Whoever buys a homestead house is taxed on full market value from the next January 1 forward, which can mean a noticeably higher bill than you paid. If you buy again in Florida, you can request portability with the new homestead filing, due March 1.

Liens, open permits and tenants

A cash sale can still close if each issue is cleared or priced in. A title search surfaces mortgages, judgments and unpaid tax, and a bill still open after April 1 is delinquent with certificates sold by June 1.

Older buildings often hide open or missing permits. Ask the city's building department what is open on your parcel, then ask the buyer whether the offer takes the work as is.

  • Inherited house: the estate may need a court order before anyone can convey title, and summary administration exists for smaller estates.
  • Past-due mortgage: ask the lender for the payoff and case status in writing.
  • Tenant in place: three days' written demand for unpaid rent, weekends and court holidays excluded, or 30 days' notice to end a monthly tenancy.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Miami houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens after the deed is signed?

The clerk of court records it and takes the stamp tax while the title company clears liens. Quitclaim, warranty, special warranty and trustee's deeds are all taxable, so changing the form does not change the result.

The appraiser's site promotes a free clerk alert that emails you soon after any deed or other paper lands on your parcel. Sign up before and after a sale to see what gets filed, and keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

Help from the Miami-Dade appraiser's office

The office runs two public branches, downtown and in Cutler Bay, with appointments online, plus neighborhood outreach events where staff review values, exemptions and portability one on one. Widow, widower and disability exemptions can be filed online with uploaded documents, and agricultural classification applications are online too. Staff also take reports of suspected homestead exemption fraud.

Before pricing, look up your parcel's exemptions and assessed value and bring the printout to any offer discussion.

How to judge a cash offer

Weigh the offer against a listing's take-home once commissions, repairs and the months of upkeep are subtracted. In the contract, find who pays the stamp tax, title policy and recording, and what happens to the deposit.

Get the closing date and closing agent in writing, and do not sign the deed until the contract is final. Pay no fee just to receive an offer. If you are unsure, request a second offer and compare terms line by line.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for a Miami cash sale

The usual order is a written offer, a signed contract, a title search, a review of the settlement statement and a signing. Bring photo ID, your payoff letter and your latest tax bill. If you own a condo, ask the association for its estoppel letter and the building's recertification status early, since both can take time.

If you rent the property out, tell the buyer whether the lease stays in place, and hand over the deposit and the rent roll at closing. After the deed is recorded, the closing agent pays off liens and sends you the balance.

Frequently asked questions

Is Miami's deed tax higher than elsewhere in Florida?

Its formula differs: 60 cents per hundred dollars plus a 45 cent surtax, but the surtax does not apply when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Other counties charge 70 cents.

Can a Miami single-family house be a short-term rental?

Generally no for houses and duplexes in T3 and T4-R zones. Verify your zoning with the city before building a plan on nightly rent.

Does recertification apply to a Miami single-family home?

No. The county exempts single-family homes, duplexes and small buildings of 2,000 square feet or less with ten or fewer occupants.

Who sends my Miami property tax bill?

The Miami-Dade Tax Collector. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but does not mail bills.

Does my reduced assessment pass to the buyer?

No. Cap savings belong to the seller, not the house. The buyer begins at market value, and you keep savings only by porting them when you claim a new Florida homestead.

Sell My House Fast in Tampa, FL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Sell Your Tampa House for Cash

Selling in Tampa?
We buy Tampa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Fastest route to sell a Tampa house

A cash sale is usually quickest, with no appraisal and no buyer loan to fall through. A listing reaches more buyers but moves slower.

Tampa has about 413,554 residents, and owned homes have a median value of $420,400. About half of the homes, 50.3%, are owner-lived, which leaves plenty of room for investors to compete with owner-occupants. That depth of demand helps a seller who needs speed.

Older houses and historic districts

Many Tampa subdivisions date to a building boom between 1923 and 1926, Davis Island among them. Historic Hyde Park, just west of downtown across the Hillsborough River, has homes from the 1920s and 1930s, and Ybor City, about 2 square miles, is a National Historic Landmark District.

Houses of that age tend to carry old wiring, plumbing and roofs, which cash buyers price into an offer. Historic districts can also bring design review for exterior changes, so ask the city's historic preservation office before planning work.

MacDill Air Force Base and short-notice moves

U.S. Central Command and U.S. Special Operations Command are headquartered at MacDill Air Force Base, so military orders create steady turnover. Service members who must relocate fast often need a quick sale and a firm closing date.

If you are on orders, tell the buyer your latest move date at the start, and ask your closing agent how soon a signed deed can be recorded. A power of attorney arranged ahead of time lets a trusted person sign if you have already left.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tampa house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps from offer to closing

The path is short once you pick a buyer.

  1. Sign the purchase agreement and open title work with a closing agent.
  2. The agent searches records for liens, back taxes and ownership gaps.
  3. You sign the deed in front of two witnesses, as Florida law requires (s. 689.01).
  4. The buyer funds, the clerk records the deed, and you receive proceeds after payoffs.

If anyone signing would be more comfortable with translated explanations or an interpreter, ask the closing agent to arrange it.

Storm damage and appraisals

If your house took storm damage, ask the Hillsborough appraiser whether the Hurricane Damage Adjustment Form applies. Damage also affects sale options: lenders hesitate over open roof or structural problems, while cash buyers purchase as-is. Keep claim papers, estimates and photos together.

Hillsborough County property taxes

The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser is on the 15th floor of 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard downtown, phone (813) 272-6100. The office has posted a statement on how Amendment 3 affects owners. Read it before you list.

Non-homestead assessments rise no more than 10 percent a year, and that cap resets on a sale (Department of Revenue). Many Tampa rentals fall in that group.

  • The homestead exemption can lower assessed value by as much as $50,000.
  • Renting the house can end homestead.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tampa houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Seller closing costs

Charges on a Tampa deed

Recording, first page$5.00
Recording, later pages$4.00 each, plus extra charges

On top of that, budget for your share of the year's property tax and for any payoffs. The deed rate is described by the Department of Revenue, and the clerk's fees are in s. 28.24. Deed tax is billed separately from recording.

Selling a Tampa rental

You can sell with the tenant in place. To clear the house, a nonpayment notice allows three days (s. 83.56). Never change locks or cut utilities yourself; the sheriff executes a court writ.

Collect the lease, rent ledger and deposit record to hand to the buyer, who takes the lease along with the house.

Inherited houses

Heirs can sell after a personal representative has authority. Estates up to $150,000 outside exempt assets can use summary administration (s. 735.201). Bring the death certificate, any will and the newest tax bill.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a cash sale skips

Without a buyer's loan there is no lender appraisal and no underwriting, so a sale does not collapse over financing. You still go through title work, payoffs, a signed deed and recording by the Hillsborough County clerk. The savings are in repairs, staging and showings, since a cash buyer expects to take the house as it is.

The trade is price. Compare the cash figure with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and the months you would carry the house. A cash offer wins when the house needs work or your date is firm.

Homestead status before you sell

Check whether the house still carries a homestead exemption, and whether it still should. Renting the house can end homestead, and the sale itself removes it from the property. Your buyer applies for their own exemption, and the assessment returns to market level, so tell them not to count on your tax bill.

If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the Hillsborough appraiser how to move part of your capped value to the next house. The appraiser's office at 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard can walk you through the forms.

Title problems and how to clear them

The closing agent's title search is where hidden problems appear: an old lien, back taxes, a missing owner signature or a gap in the chain of ownership. Anything found gets cleared before the deed can be recorded, and payoffs come out of your proceeds.

  • Ask the closing agent for the search results as soon as they are ready.
  • Contact every co-owner early, since all of them must sign.
  • If the house sat vacant after a death, find out who has authority to sell before you list.

Disclose problems you already know about. Buyers who find them on their own tend to cut the price or walk away. Bring a photo ID to closing, and check that the names on the deed match your ID exactly, since a mismatch can hold up recording.

Preparing a Tampa house for a quick sale

Preparation costs little and speeds everything up. Start a week before you call buyers.

  • Pull the deed, survey and latest tax bill.
  • Get payoff letters for every loan and lien.
  • Save storm and roof repair records and insurance claim numbers.
  • For a rental, find the leases and deposit records.
  • Clear out personal items; a cash buyer can see past clutter but needs access to every room.

Every buyer should put the offer on paper: closing date, who covers closing costs, and the outcome if an inspection turns up trouble.

Frequently asked questions

How soon can I close on a Tampa house?

Cash sales often close in days to weeks, depending on title. A clean title and a ready payoff letter shorten the timeline most, while a lien, a probate case or a tenant dispute stretches it.

Can I sell a Tampa house that needs a new roof?

Yes. Cash buyers will take it as it stands, at a price that accounts for the work. Tell the buyer about leaks, past storm claims and unpermitted work so the offer stays firm through closing.

Does the buyer get my homestead tax cap?

No. After the sale the assessment is reset to market level, and the new owner's first bill may not resemble yours. Buyers can ask the Hillsborough appraiser about their own exemptions.

What does recording a Tampa deed cost?

State law sets $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after it, with extra charges added. Deed tax is billed separately.

Can I sell a Tampa house with a tenant in it?

Yes. The buyer takes the lease, or you end the tenancy by the statute's notice rules first. Have the lease, rent ledger and deposit record ready for the buyer, along with the tenant's contact details and the date the current term ends.

Selling in Orlando?
We buy Orlando houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Choosing how to sell an Orlando house

Orlando sellers can take a cash offer, hire an agent or sell directly. The best fit depends on how much work the house needs and whether a historic district rule covers the address. The city had an estimated 333,888 residents in July 2025, and its homes range from downtown condos to bungalows built in the 1920s.

  • Cash offers suit houses with deferred repairs, tenant trouble or a tight deadline, since no lender stands between you and closing.
  • A traditional listing suits a house that shows well and can handle rounds of open houses.
  • A direct sale suits an owner with a buyer already in mind, perhaps a neighbor or the current tenant.

Before you choose, find out whether your street sits inside one of the city's six historic preservation districts. A district limits what the next owner can do to the exterior, and buyers will ask.

Orlando housing numbers

Renters outnumber owners here: only 39.5% of homes are owner-occupied. Investors with rental plans are regular bidders, and plenty of sellers own rentals themselves.

  • Residents, mid-2025: 333,888, up 8.4% since April 2020
  • Households: 131,179
  • Midpoint value of an owned home: $394,100
  • Owner cost per month with a mortgage: $2,231
  • Typical rent per month: $1,747

The city covers more than 110 square miles, so values differ a great deal from one neighborhood to the next. Treat the midpoint as a rough reference and get a price opinion for your own street.

Older neighborhoods and Lake Eola

Downtown Orlando grew around Lake Eola. Jacob Summerlin bought 200 acres there in 1873, and the Summerlin family donated land around the shore in 1883. The lake became a public park in 1888.

The land north of the lake was planted in citrus until the freezes of 1894 and 1895 destroyed the groves, and it was then subdivided for homes. Lake Eola Heights grew most between 1905 and 1925. Colonialtown South was platted in part in 1883, and most of its houses went up during the 1920s land boom. Houses from those eras turn up often among sale listings, and their age is why the district rules below matter.

Does a historic district change how I sell?

It can. A house in one of Orlando's six local historic preservation overlay districts needs city approval before exterior changes. The city's Orlando Locator, which takes an address, shows whether you live in a district. Most districts require a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Board. The Downtown Historic District uses a Certificate of Appearance Approval from the Appearance Review Board.

Rules inside the districts

  • Major work such as additions, new construction, relocation and demolition goes to a board hearing. Plan on about seven weeks.
  • Lake Eola Heights does not require approval for landscaping, paint color, or patios and walkways out of public view.
  • In Lake Copeland, approval is not needed for work that needs no city building permit or for structures built after January 1, 1940.
  • Chain-link fencing is restricted in Lake Eola Heights and Lake Lawsona.

On August 10, 2026 the City Council approved a 36-month temporary change that moves reviews of new or renovated downtown projects from the Historic Preservation Board to the Appearance Review Board. Questions go to the Historic Preservation Officer at 407.246.3416 or to Permitting at 407.246.2271. If a buyer plans exterior work, a call to one of those lines before you accept an offer can save a surprise later.

Tax break for rehabilitated historic homes

Orlando adopted a property tax exemption in 1994 for the substantial rehabilitation of locally designated historic property. It runs 10 years and covers 100 percent of the city's share of the tax tied to the value added by the rehabilitation. The exemption stays in place when the property sells. If your house has had that work done, mention it in the listing and keep the paperwork for the buyer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Orlando houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and your tax bill at sale

Homestead lowers a home's taxable value by as much as $50,000. On the Orange County Property Appraiser's website there is a tax estimator built for people thinking of buying or selling. Tax bills go out every November, and the biggest early-payment discount goes to whoever pays that month.

When you sell, your homestead ends. The new owner files a fresh application by March 1, and the assessor resets the value to just value, as it does after any sale, foreclosure or title transfer (spouses and some transfers at death are exceptions). Moving to another Florida home? Portability lets you carry part of your capped assessment over, provided you set it up within three years.

Some owners hold added breaks that the buyer will not inherit. A local ordinance can give people 65 and older an extra exemption of up to $50,000 within an income limit, and a person with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount matching the VA rating. Ask the property appraiser what applies to you.

Deed stamp tax at closing

The state's deed tax is $0.70 per $100 of consideration, and Orange County charges the standard amount. Whoever signs the deed answers for the tax, whatever the sales contract says, and the clerk takes payment when the deed goes on record. Page count, the number of names and technology add-ons drive recording fees, which are billed on top. Your closing statement will show the final figure.

Selling with a tenant in the house

If someone rents your house, that sets the pace. Ending a year-to-year tenancy takes 60 days' notice in Florida, and once a court sides with the landlord the sheriff gives 24 hours of posted notice before possession returns. Investors often buy houses with tenants inside, so a lease need not block a sale. Pull together the lease, the rent ledger and deposit records first, since every buyer asks.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a cash sale skips

A cash sale skips the loan approval and the lender's appraisal, so the usual delays tied to a buyer's financing drop out. You still need clear title, a signed deed and a closing agent to record it. Ask for the closing date in writing, and confirm who pays for the deed stamps and recording before you sign.

For an old house, ask whether the buyer will take it as is. That means no repair requests after inspection, and you should confirm it in the contract, not on a phone call.

Frequently asked questions

How can I tell whether my address is in a historic district?

Enter your address in the Orlando Locator on the city's website, or call the Historic Preservation Officer at 407.246.3416. Six local districts exist: Downtown, Lake Cherokee, Lake Copeland, Lake Eola Heights, Lake Lawsona and Colonialtown South.

How long do historic approvals take?

Minor work can clear a quick review in 2 to 10 days in most districts and 10 to 15 days downtown. Major work needs a board hearing, and the city says to plan on about seven weeks.

Does my Save Our Homes cap pass to the buyer?

No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the county returns the property to just value. The buyer applies for a fresh homestead by March 1 if they live there on January 1.

What is the stamp tax on a deed in Orange County?

It is $0.70 per $100 of consideration, paid through the clerk at recording. Your closing agent can quote the exact amount.

Can I sell an inherited Orlando house quickly?

Often, once the estate has authority to sell. Florida offers a simplified summary administration for some smaller or older estates, and creditor claims have their own cutoff dates. A probate attorney can confirm which path your estate takes.

Selling in Port St. Lucie?

Why selling in Port St. Lucie is different

St. Lucie County's biggest city is also one of its youngest. Estimates put Port St. Lucie at 268,062 people in July 2025, a rise of 30.9 percent over April 2020, and the city expects another 125,000 residents within 10 to 15 years.

All that growth puts new construction near almost every street, and your house competes with it. Buyers can line yours up against a fresh build, so condition and price both count. Most sellers choose one of three routes.

Before choosing, list what you know about the house: roof and air conditioner age, any septic system, open permits, HOA dues and who lives there. A cash buyer discounts for problems, and a retail buyer finds them in an inspection, so being upfront saves time either way.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure to buyers, along with repair requests.
  • Owner-handled sale: lower cost, with the paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: a fit for deferred work, a vacancy or a short timeline.

Old lots, septic and sewer

A development group incorporated the city in 1961 to sell quarter-acre lots to retirees, with no sidewalks, streetlights, water or sewer. General Development Corporation turned 66 square miles into mostly single-family lots in the 1960s, and later growth reached St. Lucie West and land west of I-95.

That layout explains why many early lots were sold without sewer service. The city is converting septic systems to sewer in one of the larger projects of its kind, and the city utility can tell you where your street stands. A buyer will ask, and a cash buyer will price in any septic work.

Housing in Port St. Lucie

Property taxes and Save Our Homes

The city's cut of a typical bill is just 22 percent; the county, school district, fire district and others share the remainder. Assessments are redone each January 1 by the St. Lucie County Property Appraiser. Your buyer starts without your exemptions and caps, which can raise the bill.

Save Our Homes keeps a homestead's annual rise to the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and savings begin to build in the second year. File or renew between January 1 and March 1. The homestead stays with you as an owner, not with a new address.

Amendment 3 won approval on November 3, 2026, and a bigger non-school homestead exemption follows in 2027. Ask the St. Lucie office how it affects your parcel.

  • Bills arrive in early November, and the early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 3, 2 and 1 percent in December, January and February.
  • Anything unpaid is delinquent on April 1.
  • Have the title agent prorate this year's bill at closing.

Foreclosure timing

A court foreclosure ends with a clerk's auction, set under section 45.031 for 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff allows more time. The winning bidder puts down 5 percent. If nobody objects in the 10 days after the certificate of sale, the clerk issues the certificate of title.

Owners of a homestead need to ask the clerk about leftover funds within 10 days of the auction. A private sale that closes first may leave you more equity, so phone a lender or attorney as soon as judgment is entered. Stamp tax on the certificate of title is figured on the highest bid.

Deed and closing details

Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents for each $100 of consideration here, with an assumed mortgage included. Because every party is liable, your contract should say who pays, and the clerk takes the tax at recording.

A land conveyance needs two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01, and the witnessing can happen by audio-video link.

  • Ask every lender for a payoff letter.
  • Check city records for open permits on sheds, pools, enclosures or additions.
  • Gather HOA or special-district statements if the neighborhood has them.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Port St. Lucie houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Heat, humidity and the river

In heat and humidity, an inspector looks first at the age of the air conditioning and the roof. A home beside the North Fork of the St. Lucie River or a canal invites flood-zone and insurance questions, so keep your policy and permit records for roof, window and enclosure work handy.

For a house within a short drive of the river, mention trails and parks in your pitch. Buyers compare those amenities with newer neighborhoods farther west.

Selling a vacant or rented house

A vacant house in this climate needs attention. Keep the air conditioning running at a safe setting, have someone check for leaks after storms and keep the yard presentable, since a neglected property invites lowball offers and sometimes code letters from the city.

If tenants live there, the sale does not cancel the lease. The buyer takes the house subject to it, so give the title agent a copy of the lease, the deposit records and the tenant's contact details. A cash buyer who wants the house empty may offer to wait until the lease ends, so ask what the buyer plans before you agree. Put any agreed move-out date in the contract, along with who handles the deposit and the final utility bills.

Steps from offer to funds

  1. Give the buyer the address, payoff amount and any tenant or vacancy details.
  2. Read each written offer for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent searches the record and asks lenders for payoffs.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses present.
  5. The clerk records it, and you get your money.

For the first conversation, have a current mortgage statement, your newest tax bill, an HOA contact and the repairs you already know of. That lets a buyer write a firm offer and lets the title agent open the file at once. Put three questions to every buyer: who pays for the title policy, how long the offer is good, and whether an inspection can change the price.

At the table you will sign the deed and the settlement statement, so ask for copies of both. Once the clerk records the deed, your money is released and ownership passes. Give the buyer the keys, garage openers and any gate or community access cards, and end your utilities as of that day. Take photos of the empty house during your last walk-through so you have a record of its condition.

With no buyer's lender involved, title drives the timeline. Plan on a few days for payoffs, HOA statements and the signing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Is a cash offer realistic for a Port St. Lucie house?

Yes, and more so when the house needs work or the date is fixed. There is no lender appraisal, though the title must be clear and the deed witnessed and recorded.

Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption in Port St. Lucie?

No. Your exemptions and caps end with the sale, and the buyer starts at the new assessment.

How long until a foreclosure sale after judgment?

Typically 20 to 35 days under section 45.031. Closing a private sale before then can protect equity.

Who pays documentary stamps on the deed?

The contract assigns it, but each party stays liable under state rules. The rate is 70 cents per $100 in this county.

What share of my tax bill is the city's?

About 22 percent. The county, school district, fire district and other taxing bodies split the rest.

Selling in St. Petersburg?

What sets a St. Petersburg sale apart

Waterfront location, storm repairs and permit history decide how fast a St. Petersburg house closes. The city sits on a peninsula in Pinellas County, with 244 miles of shoreline along Tampa Bay, Boca Ciega Bay, the Gulf of Mexico and intracoastal waterways. More than 265,000 people live here, spread over 100-plus neighborhoods.

The coast supports prices and complicates disclosure. Buyers, lenders and insurers ask whether the property is in a flood hazard area, whether past storm damage was repaired under permit, and what the city has on file. Proximity to the waterfront, the Pier and downtown can move prices block by block, so compare your house with sales in your own neighborhood. Collect your answers early and you can accept a strong offer quickly, whether it comes from a listing or a cash buyer.

Permit history and the building department

Permit and flood records sit with the city's Construction Services and Permitting Division at the Municipal Services Center, One 4th St. N. Homeowners are expected to get permits before repair, improvement or construction begins.

Florida House Bill 803 lets the city issue a Permit Exemption form for work on a single-family dwelling totaling less than $7,500. It applies only outside flood hazard areas and does not cover structural components (window, door, roofing, soffit and siding work), mechanical, electrical, plumbing or gas work.

Certificates issued by the St. Petersburg permitting office
CertificateWhen it is needed
Certificate of OccupancyNew construction, change of use, combining units, rebuilding after condemnation or fire
Temporary Certificate of OccupancyNew construction delayed on a non life-safety item, once major trades have a partial final
Certificate of CompletionFinished work that does not need a CO; required for a building shell, otherwise optional
Elevation CertificateFEMA document showing height above sea level and base flood elevation; city records go back to 1990

You can research Certificate of Occupancy history for free in the city's property cards database. Pull yours before you list. If you visit in person, bring a photo ID and a floor layout. An optional preliminary plan review is also available, handy if a buyer wants to add to the house after closing.

Flood and storm history

If your house is in a flood hazard area and was damaged, the repair path matters to the sale. The permitting office points owners to FEMA's 49% Rule, which can affect a property after storm damage, and asks visitors to bring photos, a damage summary and a floor layout.

There is a tax side too. When a structure is damaged or destroyed, taxes can still rise for long-time homesteaded owners because of the Save Our Homes cap recapture rule, and if the building value fell below land value, the assessed value may not drop. Read any value reconsideration letters you receive, since a building value can differ from the year before.

  • Keep storm photos, adjuster reports and repair invoices together.
  • Find out whether the city holds an elevation certificate for your address.
  • Confirm every repair that needed a permit has a final inspection.
  • Ask the buyer's insurer early about flood coverage, since it can change the closing timeline.

Cash buyers often purchase storm-damaged houses as they are, but expect a discount tied to the unknowns.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your St. Petersburg house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Pinellas County property taxes at a sale

Your home's value is set as of January 1 by the Pinellas County Property Appraiser, and the bill arrives from the Pinellas County Tax Collector in November. After you sell, the county removes the exemptions and caps you had on the next January 1, and the new owner's value moves toward market.

The homestead exemption, worth up to $50,000 of taxable value, needs an application by March 1. Paying early earns 4 percent off in November, shrinking to 1 percent by February. At closing, the agent prorates the year's taxes between you and the buyer.

A buyer coming from another Florida homestead may carry over a savings cap through portability. The buyer files that application, within three years of January 1 of the year the earlier homestead was given up.

Deed and recording charges

Documentary stamp tax on a Pinellas deed runs 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and the clerk takes it when the deed is recorded. Every party on the document stays liable under Department of Revenue rules, even if the contract puts the cost on one side.

Statute 28.24 sets recording at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, with further per-page charges on top. The settlement statement lists each item.

Cash offers often skip lender steps such as appraisals, which can shorten the schedule. Even so, ask who covers title insurance, stamp tax and tax proration, and get the split in writing before you accept.

Checking contractors and open permits

Before hiring anyone, confirm the contractor's license through the Pinellas County Licensing Board. Trouble scheduling an inspection can trace back to an unknown license status, so permits and licenses are tied closely here.

For work in progress, the city's online portal lets you enter a permit number to schedule or cancel an inspection and to check plan review status trade by trade. E-plan applicants have ten business days to finish uploads or answer comments before the application is denied and the workflow ends.

  • Look up each contractor on the county licensing board's site.
  • Enter permit numbers in the city portal to see open reviews.
  • Call the permitting division at 727-893-7231 with license status questions.

A buyer's inspector will usually find stalled work, so finish it first or disclose it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy St. Petersburg houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Choosing a sale route

A listing means preparing the house, opening it for showings and answering repair requests after the buyer's inspection. The price can be higher, and the timeline is longer. With a cash buyer, you usually sell as-is, and the date depends on title work instead of a lender.

Before you commit to either, ask each buyer or agent how they would treat open permits and storm damage, because that answer shapes the price. Whichever route you choose, the steps are the same at the end: the title agent searches the records, any liens and mortgages are paid from proceeds, you sign the deed, and the clerk records it. Gather the deed, permit list, storm records and a recent tax bill beforehand, and you can answer an offer in days instead of weeks. If the house is vacant, arrange for someone to check it after storms, keep utilities on until closing, and hand over every key at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I get permit records for a St. Petersburg house?

Ask the city's Construction Services and Permitting Division at One 4th St. N. A free property cards database covers Certificate of Occupancy history, and the online portal tracks permit status.

Do small repairs in St. Petersburg need a permit?

Not always. A form lets the city exempt single-family work under $7,500 outside flood hazard areas, but not structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing or gas work. Check with the building department first.

Does the buyer get my Save Our Homes cap?

No. The assessment returns to just value on the next January 1 after a sale, so the buyer's bill may be much higher than yours. A new homestead exemption can be filed by the buyer through March 1.

Is selling a storm-damaged St. Petersburg house as is possible?

Yes. Plenty of buyers take houses as-is, though you should disclose known damage and any unpermitted repairs. In a flood hazard area, ask the city about FEMA's 49% Rule before you decide to repair or sell.

How do I check a contractor's license?

Use the Pinellas County Licensing Board's site. For permit questions tied to a license, call the permitting division at 727-893-7231.

Sell Your Cape Coral House for Cash

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Cape Coral?
We buy Cape Coral houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Utility assessments come first in Cape Coral

The question buyers raise most here is whether your special assessment is paid. Cape Coral began as a 1957 land-sales platting laced with canals, and the city has been pushing water, sewer and irrigation lines out to parcels that never had them. Those extensions are repaid through special assessments.

The city's budget book describes more than 400 miles of waterways reaching the Intracoastal Waterway and the Gulf of Mexico, so many sellers also have seawalls, docks and canal-front insurance questions. Those answers come from other offices, but the assessment question starts with the city's billing office.

  • Look up whether your street sits in a Utilities Extension Project area.
  • Check your tax bill for a non-ad valorem line from the city.
  • Ask whether city water and irrigation are already connected.

Do special assessments pass to the buyer?

Generally yes, because they attach to the lot. An unpaid assessment passes to the new owner, who takes over the remaining balance, unless it is paid in full first.

The charge is treated as a tax levy and is recorded with the Lee County Clerk as a notice, not as a mortgage-style lien. Hardship and deferral programs are the exception. They require a lien on the property, and those liens must be paid in full at closing.

Assessments appear once a year on the Lee County Tax Collector's tax bill, so skipping one carries the same risk as skipping any part of the bill: a tax certificate. Payoffs can be made by mail, in person at the cashier window at City Hall, or online through the city's page for tax-billed assessments.

How an assessment is calculated

The city charges by lot area, not by the value of the house, and it bills vacant lots as well as built ones.

The two Cape Coral line-extension charges
ChargeWho paysUnit used
UEP special assessmentEvery parcel in an approved project area, built or vacantPer equivalent lot of 5,000 square feet, or per parcel of 10,000
Contribution in aid of constructionParcels outside a project area where a developer already paid for linesEquivalent parcels of 10,000 square feet, times the rate set by council

Each project area has its own billing term and interest rate, listed on the city's special assessments page. The charge repays project costs, including financing fees, once the council approves the project. If you are selling to an investor, get the remaining balance and its end date from the city in writing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cape Coral house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The northeast irrigation rule

It can matter. In May 2025 the city mailed letters to about 1,000 owners in a northeast water-shortage area served by the Mid-Hawthorn Aquifer, telling them to connect to city irrigation within 180 days under Ordinance 7-25. The rule applies only where city irrigation service is already available.

The city ties the rule to its joint plan with the South Florida Water Management District, which followed that agency's water shortage declaration in November 2023. Owners are charged for irrigation water when they connect or when 180 days pass, whichever comes first.

  • With in-ground sprinklers, you need a free permit and inspection to connect.
  • Without sprinklers, a Kit-A outdoor spigot is installed and no permit is needed.
  • A plumber does the work, and any damaged swale or road must be repaired before the permit closes.
  • Keep trees seven feet and palms five feet from utilities.
  • In a mapped eagle nest zone, no machine digging from October 15 to May 15. Hand digging is allowed.

If you got a letter and have not complied, tell your buyer and your closing agent. Without a letter, the rule does not touch you.

What does the Lee County calendar mean for a seller?

It sets the year's clock. Value is fixed as of January 1, exemption requests are due March 1, and the appraiser mails TRIM notices in August. Late exemption applications may be granted for the following year, and you can ask for an informal conference at any time to talk through a value.

The Lee County Tax Collector mails bills in November. Paying early earns a 4 percent discount that month, dropping monthly to 1 percent in February, and anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

A TRIM notice lists proposed levies and any proposed or adopted non-ad valorem assessments, which is where a city utility charge would show up. Read that line before you set a price, then ask the city's customer billing office to confirm the balance in writing. That office also handles new construction and project questions.

Vacant lots in the same project area are assessed too, so a lot next door is not exempt. Talk to the title agent early so the payoff or the transfer of the balance is written into the contract.

Lenders and unwanted occupants

Time gets short once a foreclosure judgment is entered. The public sale is set 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to more, with two weeks of notice first. A lender may instead ask for an order to show cause, and a homestead exemption on the latest roll is presumed to mean the home is owner-occupied. Call a Florida attorney if either has begun.

If someone is living in a vacant house without permission, an owner or agent can file a verified complaint with the sheriff to remove persons unlawfully occupying residential property. It requires no tenancy, no family tie, a property closed to the public, a demand to leave and no pending suit. A false statement can cost up to triple the fair market rent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cape Coral houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief programs

Several programs exist, depending on age and service. A city or county ordinance may add a homestead break for owners 65 and older within an income limit. Owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount equal to their VA rating. A disabled ex-servicemember may get a flat $5,000 cut in assessed value.

You can also ask the Tax Collector about deferral on Form DR-570, filed by March 31 after the assessment year. Find out which programs your household meets before you sell under pressure.

What belongs in the folder for a Cape Coral buyer?

  • Your latest Lee County tax bill, with its non-ad valorem lines.
  • City utility status: connected, assessed, or not yet extended.
  • A recorded deed copy from the Clerk.
  • Payoff letters for loans, liens and association balances.
  • Permit records for roofs, windows, docks or additions.

Deed stamp tax in Lee County runs at the standard seventy cent rate, and every signer is liable. Recording is charged per page under section 28.24.

Hand the folder to the title agent early. A buyer who sees the assessment balance and permit records up front has fewer reasons to renegotiate after the inspection, and a seller who can answer those questions the same day keeps a quick sale on schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Cape Coral utility assessment stay with the house?

Who gets the irrigation connection letters?

Only owners in the northeast water-shortage area where city irrigation is already available. The city mailed about 1,000 in May 2025.

When must I file for homestead in Lee County?

By March 1 of the tax year, with the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

Can I remove someone living in my vacant Cape Coral house?

Possibly, through the sheriff complaint process if the statutory conditions are met, such as no tenancy and a prior demand to leave. Talk to an attorney first.

Hialeah in brief

Hialeah incorporated in 1925 and celebrated its centennial in 2025. The city sits in Miami-Dade County, which means your bill comes from the county's Tax Collector, while your value and exemptions come from its Property Appraiser. Hialeah Park, a National Register site opened the same year as the city, remains the best-known landmark inside city limits.

County offices control most of what a seller touches, so the sections below cover those offices, the dates to watch and the paperwork buyers request.

Miami-Dade tax bills and due dates

Annual notices go out from the Miami-Dade County Tax Collector at the end of October, and online payment opens that same day. Visit 200 NW 2nd Avenue, Miami, or call 305-375-5448. BillExpress subscribers get the notice by email on the mailing date.

The collector only bills. Value comes from the Property Appraiser, reduced by exemptions, and every taxing authority picks its own rate. If the 2026 real estate taxes are not paid before June 1, 2027, a tax certificate may be issued, and the annual certificate sale starts June 1, 2027.

  • Water, road and sewer assessments, such as OJUS, are collected in annual installments. A bill containing one must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold for the remaining lien balance.
  • Discounts for paying early step down each month, with the largest in November.

What Amendment 3 changes for a Hialeah homestead

Amendment 3 won voter approval on November 3, 2026 and starts January 1, 2027. It affects non-school property taxes only. The school board exemption remains $25,000.

Homestead exemption amounts, Miami-Dade
Tax yearUp to, non-school taxes
Through 2026$50,000 (state homestead exemption)
2027$150,000 for residents established by December 31, 2026
2028$250,000 for the same group
2029 onwardAdjusted yearly for positive CPI change

Newcomers who establish residency after December 31, 2026 begin at up to $50,000, and they generally reach the larger amount in their fifth year of receiving a homestead exemption. Federal constitutional limits and implementing legislation shape that rule, so a buyer relocating from another state should ask the appraiser how it applies.

How to file for, keep or lose homestead

  • Deadline: applications and documents are due March 1. A late application may still be taken up to the date printed on the TRIM notice, possibly with a $15 fee and a Value Adjustment Board petition.
  • Residency proof: one item is enough, such as a Florida driver license, vehicle registration, voter registration, a W-2 or tax return, bank statements, utility payments or a recorded Declaration of Domicile.
  • Where to file: use the online Application Portal, or go in person to the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1 Street, Suite 710, or to the South Dade Government Center. The phone line is 305-375-4712.
  • Renewal: homestead owners get a renewal receipt in late December, and a property with a deed change gets none.

Leasing the house endangers the exemption. An unreported change can mean back taxes for up to ten years of exempted taxes, 15 percent interest per year and a penalty of 50 percent of the taxes exempted. Tell the appraiser about any change before you advertise the house for rent or sale.

Deed tax for a Hialeah seller

Only Miami-Dade has a rate of its own: 60 cents per $100 on a deed, with a separate 45 cent surtax per $100 that skips any document transferring only a single-family dwelling. The rest of Florida pays 70 cents.

The clerk takes payment when the deed is recorded, and each person on the deed is liable whatever the contract assigns. Quit claim deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are taxed. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not. For recording charges on your closing statement, look at the Miami-Dade Clerk's current schedule.

Permits and inspections

Request the permit history for your address from the City of Hialeah building department, and look for any permit that is open or expired before you list. Buyers most often ask about roofs, replacement windows, electrical panels, additions and fences.

Work done without a permit leaves a buyer three options: require a permit, require repairs, or lower the price. Some cash buyers will take the house with open items, while a buyer with a loan rarely will. Learn the facts first, then pick your route.

Disputing an assessment or exemption denial

To challenge value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. To contest a denied exemption, take it to the value adjustment board, which accepts the petition 30 days after the denial letter is mailed. The appraiser sends the proposed notice by the end of August, and the late-filing date on it usually falls 25 days after mailing.

Selling is a good time to review the parcel record, since the value and exemptions on it drive both your proration and your buyer's first bill. Check the owner name, the exemptions shown and the mailing address on the tax roll, so notices actually reach you.

Ways to sell a Hialeah house

  • Agent listing: more exposure and more showings, plus inspection requests and a closing tied to the buyer's loan.
  • Cash buyer: the house is taken as it sits, timing is negotiable, and the price deserves a side-by-side look with a listing estimate.
  • Relative: still a taxable deed event, and the assessment can change if the cap resets.

Whoever the buyer is, get terms on paper, including the date money reaches you and who pays recording and deed tax. File the Miami-Dade tax bill, any assessment notice and permit records alongside the contract.

Before you list: a short checklist

Gather the recorded deed, the latest Miami-Dade tax bill and any assessment notice. Pull the permit history from the city. Tell the Property Appraiser about any change in how the house is used, especially if it was rented while homesteaded, because back taxes and penalties are far easier to sort out before a buyer is waiting. If the house carries a water, road or sewer assessment such as OJUS, ask the tax collector how much remains so the closing agent can deal with it.

Once a buyer is under contract, the closing agent orders title work, asks each lender for a payoff letter, and splits the year's property tax between you and the buyer. A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal, though recording and payoffs still take days, so ask for the expected closing date in writing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Other appraiser rules to know

If you apply for homestead in another Florida county, cancel the Miami-Dade exemption. Applications can be tracked on a status page, and suspected homestead fraud is reported to an investigation unit at 305-375-3402. The buyer of your house should file a new application, since a property with a deed change gets no renewal receipt.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Hialeah in?

Miami-Dade County, so the Miami-Dade Tax Collector and Property Appraiser handle your tax bill and exemptions.

What is the Miami-Dade deed tax rate?

60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax per $100. The surtax does not apply to a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling.

When is the homestead deadline in Miami-Dade?

March 1. A late application may still be taken until the date shown on the TRIM notice, and a $15 fee may apply.

What happens if I rent out a homestead house?

The exemption can be lost, and unreported changes can be back taxed for ten years with 15 percent interest and a 50 percent penalty.

When does a tax certificate sale happen?

The annual sale starts June 1, 2027 for unpaid 2026 real estate taxes.

Can you sell a Tallahassee house fast?

Yes, provided the price is realistic and your documents are in order. A cash buyer removes showings and lender steps, so a Tallahassee house can close on a timetable you set rather than a bank's.

Tallahassee is Florida's capital and the Leon County seat, with about 204,902 residents. Tenants outnumber owners here. Only 40.6% of homes are lived in by their owners, median rent is $1,293, and a typical owned home is valued at $294,400. Landlords and investors are therefore a large share of buyers, and many want a house they can rent soon after closing. A house near the lakes and one near the campuses draw different buyers, so ask each bidder how they reached their number.

Paperwork to gather

Whichever route you take, a slim folder of records saves days at the title company.

  • The recorded deed, plus any survey or plat.
  • The most recent Leon County tax bill and proof of any exemption.
  • A payoff letter for each loan or lien.
  • For a rental: leases, deposit records and ways to reach each tenant.
  • Roof, air conditioning and plumbing records, with receipts for any storm repairs.

With these in hand, a buyer can make a firm offer in one visit and the closing agent can start the title search immediately.

Weather, trees and inspections

Tallahassee gets about 63.5 inches of rain a year over 116 rainy days, with 91 days above 90 degrees. Roofs, gutters and air conditioning units work hard here, and buyers look at all three during inspections.

  • Seven roads in Leon County, including Old Bainbridge, Meridian and Miccosukee, are designated canopied roads, which limits roadside development.
  • Large live oaks and other mature trees can overhang roofs and driveways, so expect questions about limbs and roots.
  • Summer humidity makes moisture, mold and HVAC condition standard inspection topics.

A seller who documents roof age, HVAC service and any storm repairs gives a buyer less to argue about.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tallahassee house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Listing, investor sale or cash offer

Three paths exist, and each trades time for price in its own way.

  • An agent listing: the largest audience, with showings, buyer loans, inspections and a closing date that can move.
  • An as-is investor sale: fewer repairs and a quicker close, often at a lower price than a polished house.
  • A cash offer: no appraisal gap, a closing date you can negotiate, and repairs left undone.

Ask each buyer for the amount that will reach you after every cost, then compare it with a listing's net after commission and repairs. Put the closing date, the payer of title charges and any inspection condition in writing before you sign anything, and keep copies of every offer you receive, including the ones you decline.

Selling a house with tenants

You may sell a rented house with the tenant still living there, and the buyer takes over the lease. To clear the house first, state law allows three days' notice for a tenant who has not paid (s. 83.56), while a month-to-month tenant needs 30 days' notice ahead of the end of a monthly period.

Collect the lease, the deposit figure and the rent ledger before asking for offers. Investors in a renter-heavy city like this one tend to value a paying tenant.

Leon County property taxes

Property tax calendar for a Tallahassee seller
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is fixed
NovemberBills go out with a 4 percent discount, which shrinks each month to 1 percent in February
March 1Exemption claims close
April 1Unpaid bills become delinquent

Values and exemptions come from the Leon County Property Appraiser, and the tax collector sends the bills (Department of Revenue). Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027, and does not touch 2026 bills. Call the appraiser about how it affects your situation while you plan a timeline. The title agent splits that year's bill between you and the buyer by days owned.

  • Homestead may take as much as $50,000 off the assessed value.
  • Renting the house out can end the homestead.
  • The new owner's assessment resets after a sale.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tallahassee houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing taxes and fees on a deed

Leon County deeds are taxed at $0.70 for each $100 of price, the same as everywhere in Florida but Miami-Dade, and the state holds everyone on the deed responsible (Department of Revenue). The sale contract only allocates the cost.

The clerk gets paid when the deed is filed. Page one costs $5.00 to record and later pages $4.00, with other per-page charges (s. 28.24). Request an itemized statement from the title company.

Can heirs sell an inherited Tallahassee house?

Yes, once someone holds authority. That usually means a personal representative appointed by the Leon County probate court. Estates at or under $150,000 beyond exempt assets, or deaths more than two years back, may qualify for summary administration (s. 735.201).

No Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004. Before talking to buyers, heirs should collect the death certificate, the will and the latest tax bill.

Selling with taxes owed

When Leon County tax goes unpaid, the county first sells a certificate to an investor. A tax deed application has to wait until two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. If you are behind, redeem the certificate or sell, since a title company will not close over it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a cash sale skips

With cash there is no buyer's loan, so the lender's appraisal and underwriting never happen, and the sale cannot fall apart because financing did. The title search, payoffs, deed signing and recording still happen, and the closing agent handles them as in any sale.

Repairs are the other big difference. A cash buyer usually takes the house as it is, so the cleanup, patching and roof work you would do before a listing can wait. The price reflects that, which is why you should compare net figures instead of headline offers.

Steps from offer to closing

  1. Accept an offer and sign the contract, naming who pays deed tax and recording.
  2. The title company searches for liens, mortgages and heirs, and you clear any problem found.
  3. Order payoff letters and ask the tax collector for the current balance.
  4. Sign the deed in front of two witnesses.
  5. The clerk records the deed, and the buyer files for their own homestead the next year.

If the house is vacant, keep it secured and the utilities on until the day you hand over the keys. An empty house that has a roof leak or a storm-damaged tree limb can change a buyer's mind quickly.

Quitclaim deeds and family transfers

A family transfer is possible, but the deed form matters. Land deeds need two witnesses, and quitclaim deeds are taxable instruments. Changing names on a title shortly before a sale can reset the assessed value, so check with the title agent first.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a Tallahassee sale close?

Once title is clear, cash can close within days or a few weeks. A financed purchase takes longer while the appraisal and loan approval happen.

Must I fix things before selling in Tallahassee?

No. In an as-is sale the buyer handles repairs and the price reflects the condition. A listing buyer, by contrast, will often request repairs after inspection.

Who covers deed tax on a Tallahassee sale?

The contract decides. All parties stay liable to the state either way.

Does my homestead exemption move with me?

Part of it can. Under portability, some of your assessment savings carry to a new Florida homestead when you claim it within three years.

What happens when a title problem turns up?

The title company must clear it before closing. Disclose known liens or heirs early.

The fastest way to sell in Fort Lauderdale

Selling directly for cash tends to be fastest. The buyer accepts the home as it stands and closes as soon as title is clean. In Fort Lauderdale, settle three questions first. Who owns the property, what is owed against it, and does anyone live in it? Each property carries its own complications: a mortgage payoff, a lease in place, or an estate nobody has opened.

Broward County has 31 municipalities, and Fort Lauderdale is the biggest, ranking among the ten largest cities in Florida. An estimated 188,677 people live here. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $486,700, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes. At those values, the deed taxes and exemption rules below deserve a careful read.

Homestead after a Fort Lauderdale sale

Legal Florida residents may claim homestead through the Broward County Property Appraiser on a home they make their permanent residence as of January 1. The basic exemption trimmed a Broward owner's bill by between $673 and $1,020 in 2026, with the exact amount tied to the city's millage rate, for homes valued at $75,000 or higher.

Your exemption ends with the sale. The Save Our Homes assessment goes back to just value on the January 1 after ownership changes, so the buyer needs an application of their own.

March and September homestead dates

Whether a buyer gets the exemption in year one comes down to timing. No reason, however good, lets someone file after the September cutoff, so hand your buyer these dates at closing.

What a Fort Lauderdale closing costs

Deeds in Broward are taxed at the usual statewide figure, 70 cents per $100 of consideration, since Miami-Dade is the lone exception. Anyone named on the deed can be held liable, and the Broward clerk takes payment at recording. Section 28.24 governs the per-page recording fees.

Here is who handles each piece:

  • Deed tax and recording: the Broward County Clerk, at recording.
  • Homestead filing: the Broward County Property Appraiser, by March 1 each year.
  • Tax bill: the Broward County Tax Collector, sent in November and delinquent after April 1.

Ask your title company for a closing statement showing every charge before you sign.

When a tenant lives in the house

Having a tenant will not stop a sale, yet the rules for ending a tenancy stay in force. Chapter 83 requires brief written notices for unpaid rent and lease violations, and longer ones that depend on how often rent is paid, with a separate monthly-tenancy rule.

Find out if the buyer will honor the current lease; that sidesteps notices and court. Should you need the tenant to leave, consult a Florida landlord-tenant attorney before serving any paper.

Selling an inherited Fort Lauderdale house

Buyers of an inherited house want to see who is allowed to sign for the estate. Smaller estates may qualify for summary administration, a streamlined court process, while creditors get a fixed window to file claims.

No estate tax applies in Florida for deaths after 2004, and the deed a personal representative signs under a probated will owes no stamp tax. The Broward County Clerk of Courts or a probate attorney can say which procedure suits you.

Homestead paperwork for sellers and new owners

The appraiser asks applicants to bring proof of ownership, usually the recorded deed in the applicant's name. A deed already recorded in Broward's Official Records need not be copied. Where co-owners hold as tenants in common, each owner who lives there must file to claim full coverage.

For married couples and joint tenants with right of survivorship, one owner can secure full coverage, although the office recommends that every eligible owner-occupant file. Trust-held houses follow separate requirements, so phone the office ahead of the sale.

  • Bring identification and proof that the house was your permanent home on January 1.
  • Apply through the office's online portal or in person.
  • Ask about a mobile exemption event if travel is hard.

From accepted offer to closing

Acceptance starts the title work: a search for liens and unpaid taxes, and payoff letters from every lender. Then comes the contract, and at closing a deed signed before two witnesses. Lender, stamp tax and recording charges are paid out of your proceeds, with the rest released to you. No buyer's loan means no appraisal and no underwriting step. Judge offers by your net, and decline anyone who wants you to pay before closing.

Listing or selling for cash

Putting the house on the market exposes it to the most buyers and may fetch the highest price. It also means showings, repair requests, an appraisal and a financing deal that can collapse. Cash gives up part of that price in return for speed and certainty. Neither answer is right for everyone. A house with a fresh roof and a calm timeline may do well on the market, while one needing work, with a tenant or a lender deadline, often suits a direct buyer better.

Whatever you decide, get offers on paper and add up what each leaves after payoffs, stamps, recording and unpaid taxes.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you accept an offer

Early paperwork speeds the title search and takes away a buyer's excuses to reopen the price.

  • The recorded deed, plus trust documents or a probate order if someone other than you is signing.
  • A written payoff from each mortgage lender or lienholder.
  • Permit records for roof, electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work.
  • Any lease and deposit records, if the house is rented.
  • Your latest tax bill and the contact details for any association.

If a document is missing, tell the buyer at the outset. Gaps that are disclosed can often be worked around, while surprises found late tend to end deals.

Closing day

The title agent goes over the settlement statement with you at the table. Read every figure and ask about anything unfamiliar. After the deed is signed and recorded, keys change hands and your proceeds arrive by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the Broward appraiser and tax collector so later notices find you, and keep copies of everything you signed.

Checking your record before you list

Open the Broward property appraiser's record for your parcel and compare it with your deed. Owner names should match, homestead should appear if you live there, and the mailing address should be current. Fix mismatches before an offer arrives, since a title company will find them anyway. If you did work on the house, confirm the permits are closed. These small checks cost an afternoon and can save a week.

Frequently asked questions

What are Fort Lauderdale homes worth?

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $486,700, and owners live in 54.1 percent of homes.

When is the Broward homestead deadline?

Every March 1. The timely window for 2027 closes March 1, 2027, and the last day to late file is September 20, 2027.

Is the deed tax different in Broward?

No, Miami-Dade is the only county with its own rate. Broward applies the statewide 70 cents per $100, which the clerk collects at recording.

How much notice does a month-to-month Broward tenant get?

The minimum depends on the kind of periodic tenancy under chapter 83. Read the statute or ask an attorney before you serve notice.

Can a probate house be sold in Broward?

Usually, after the personal representative has court authority or the estate has completed a short process. Confirm the right path with a probate attorney.
