Selling in Pembroke Pines

Pembroke Pines lies in southwest Broward and counts more than 170,000 residents. Major highways, jobs, parks and golf courses are all close. On January 16, 1960 it incorporated as the Village of Pembroke Pines, home to about 1,500 people. Hurricane Andrew in 1992 set off a building rush that made it one of the fastest growing cities in the country, so a large share of its housing dates from the 1990s or later.

Families drawn to schools and parks make up much of the buyer pool, along with residents of the Century Village area. Your home's age is a good first clue to whether a cash offer or a listing suits you better.

House age by side of town

The city annexed land west of US 27 by 1981, so the age of a house depends on which side of town it stands. Fire Station 79 opened in 1981 on that annexed land, and Station 89 followed in 1986 at Century Village.

  • Find out how old your roof, wiring and plumbing are.
  • Ask a title agent to list recorded items on your lot.
  • Keep permit and inspection records where a buyer's inspector can see them.

What Florida charges to transfer a house

Stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, and everyone on the document answers for it.

Which documents carry stamp tax on a real estate transfer
DocumentStamp tax applies?
Warranty deedYes
Quit claim deedYes
Deed in lieu of foreclosure saleYes
Personal representative deed under probated willNot taxable

The clerk of court collects when the deed is recorded. Have your closing agent work out the amount on your price and give it to you in writing.

The Broward tax cycle

Broward's property appraiser sets value as of January 1 and accepts exemption filings until March 1. The office phone is 954-357-6830.

  • A proposed tax notice comes in August.
  • Bills paid in November get the biggest discount, 4 percent.
  • Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

At closing, the year's tax is divided between you and the buyer. Make sure the division respects your exemption status.

Homestead and portability if you move

Long-time owners benefit most. Save Our Homes limits yearly assessment increases to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and the savings built up, up to $500,000, can be ported to a Florida home you buy next.

Begin the new homestead inside three years of the January 1 that follows giving up the old one, and send Form DR-501T along with the DR-501 by March 1. Amendments passed later reach the 2027 roll first, so ask the appraiser which rules apply today.

Inherited, rented or facing foreclosure

Three situations here come with deadlines. For an estate, summary administration is possible when non-exempt assets total $150,000 or less. Creditors must file by three months after publication or 30 days after service, whichever ends later. Once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the sale arrives 20 to 35 days afterward.

Collect your documents first, because every one of these facts changes the offers you will get.

Fire rescue and insurance ratings

Fire rescue here began as a volunteer group in 1953, hired three full-time employees in 1973 and now works from six stations. In 2014 the city became the South Region answering point for the Broward County Regional 911 system. Buyers ask about response times and insurance ratings, so find out from your insurer what rating your address gets and keep the answer with your sale papers.

Tax certificates and tax deeds

Tax not paid by April 1 goes delinquent, and certificates are offered by June 1. When two years have gone by, the holder may pay $75 to apply for a tax deed, which leads to a clerk's auction.

On a homestead, the opening bid is one half of the latest assessed value plus what is owed. A seller who is behind can ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff figure and may do better selling before a deed application.

  • To pay in installments, file the application by May 1.
  • Seniors can defer on Form DR-570, due March 31.

What buyers ask about the city

The city lists 41 arts and cultural facilities along with parks, golf courses and tree-lined neighborhoods, and it has been recognized as an All-America City. Its stated mission is a place to live, work and raise a family, so lead with those points when you describe the neighborhood. Fire Station 69 opened in 1978 and Station 101 came in 2001 with a communications center, which gives a buyer a sense of how long the area has had full-time coverage.

Mention anything that is true of your street, such as a nearby park, a golf course view or a quiet cul-de-sac, and keep it factual. Buyers check a map, so a plain description beats an inflated one.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Senior and military exemptions

Owners past 65 can claim up to $50,000 more if the local ordinance permits and income is low enough. A disabled veteran gets $5,000 off assessed value, and an older owner with a service-connected disability may get a discount matching the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may get an exemption in proportion to time away and can rent out the house without losing homestead. Ask the appraiser's office about proof. The buyer does not inherit any of these breaks.

Family transfers

Giving someone legal or beneficial title counts as a change of ownership for assessment, apart from spouse transfers and some transfers at death. A quit claim deed also draws stamp tax. Florida wants the conveyance in writing and signed before two witnesses, so a title agent should draw it up.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer needs no loan, so the lender's appraisal and weeks of underwriting drop away. Clear title, a signed deed and a closing agent to record it are still required. Before agreeing, have the closing date and as-is terms written down, decide who pays stamps and recording, and ask if the buyer will assume an association balance or an open permit.

Any mortgage balance is paid from your proceeds, with the closing agent getting the final figure from your lender. If association dues are overdue, request a statement so the balance is cleared at closing and not discovered afterward.

Selling with a tenant

Having a tenant need not stop a sale, though the lease controls your timing. Unpaid rent draws a 3 day notice, and many fixable breaches get 7 days. A sale does not end a lease, so read it before listing and show buyers the rent record early. Investors often buy with a tenant in place, which can spare you the wait.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept, the title agent searches the record, collects payoffs and drafts the deed for two witnesses to sign. The clerk records it and takes the tax.

  • Name the stamp payer in the contract.
  • Order mortgage payoff and association statements.
  • Check your exemption status before the tax split.
  • Have permit and inspection records ready for the buyer's inspector.

Preparing to sell

Begin with paperwork: the deed, the newest tax bill, any association papers, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions. Then compare a listing, a private sale and a cash offer by what you net, and insist on a written offer you have read line by line. With a cash buyer, get the closing date in writing and confirm the house is taken as is, so no repair requests show up after inspection. Nearby sales are easy to compare in a city this size, so get a short list from an agent before you set a price.

Frequently asked questions

When did Pembroke Pines incorporate?

January 16, 1960, when it was a village of about 1,500 people.

What doc stamp rate applies to a Pembroke Pines deed?

70 cents per $100 of consideration, the same rate countywide.

Can I carry my Save Our Homes savings to a new house?

Possibly, if you start a new Florida homestead within three years. Portability can carry up to $500,000 of the difference.

Who pays the deed tax?

State rules make each party liable, so the contract should name who pays.

Is an inherited house taxed when it transfers?

Not when a personal representative signs under a probated will. Other transfers may be taxed, so ask a title agent.

Choosing a way to sell in Hollywood

Three routes dominate in Hollywood: list with an agent, take a cash offer, or sell as is. How much work the house needs, how soon you must close, and whether a bank or a judge controls your calendar will steer the choice.

A listing gets the most eyes on the house but adds showings, loan approvals and an appraisal that can fall short. A cash offer drops most of those hurdles. Both paths finish at the Broward County records office with a witnessed deed, the transfer tax and recording.

  • Agent listing: biggest pool of shoppers, longer wait, outcome tied to a loan.
  • Cash or as-is buyer: few conditions, no repair demands, quick signing.
  • Sale to a relative: money still changes hands, so deed tax and homestead rules still apply.

Hollywood in brief

Hollywood lies in southeastern Broward County, between Miami and Fort Lauderdale. The city covers about 30 square miles and is the third-largest municipality in Broward, home to 153,067 people in 2020 and an estimated 157,019 by mid-2025. Shoppers think of three zones: the barrier island on the Atlantic, the historic downtown around Harrison Street and Young Circle, and the western Hollywood Hills section.

Homeowners occupy 58.9 percent of housing, with a median value of $410,600 and a median rent of $1,653. About four in ten households rent, so landlords make up many of the sellers, and they face a different tax picture and closing checklist.

Beach, downtown or the west side

Where your house sits shapes who shops for it. The Broadwalk on the beach side runs nearly 2.5 miles past resort towers, condos and small inns, so buyers there are often thinking about condos, short stays or a second home. Downtown, around Harrison Street and Young Circle, mixes arts venues, bars and restaurants. The western Hollywood Hills area grew after Hollywood Boulevard was extended toward U.S. 27 in 1954.

The West Lake area borders the Anne Kolb Nature Center, which preserves more than 1,500 acres of mangroves. The Seminole Indian Reservation lies inside city limits as an independent entity. Describe the setting honestly in your listing or offer request and let the buyer judge the fit.

Public projects near your house

Public money can change what buyers will pay on a given street. Voters approved a $54 million bond in 2004 for public safety and parks, and a $165 million bond in 2019 for safety, technology, parks, neighborhood work and resilience. More than 30 projects were under construction under the later bond, and the city bought more than 45 acres of open space. Main roads are being rebuilt with bike lanes, wider sidewalks and bus bays.

If you are near the beach, downtown or a rebuilt corridor, mention these projects in the listing. Elsewhere, ask a local agent how your streets compare.

What happens to homestead when you sell

Living in the house means the exemption ends when you sell, and the buyer has to apply separately. Broward's property appraiser carries a seller's exemptions through the year of sale and no further.

A change of ownership also resets assessed value, so the buyer's first tax bill may be higher than yours, a point careful buyers raise while negotiating. If you will buy another Florida home, portability can carry part of your capped-value savings over once you file a homestead application, so ask the appraiser about it. The timely filing date is March 1, and the last possible late-filing day for tax year 2027 is September 20, 2027.

Landlords face a separate risk. Leasing a homestead house can forfeit the exemption, and a change nobody reported can trigger back taxes for up to ten years, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

Deed tax, recording fees and the tax calendar

Expect the state deed tax to be the biggest closing charge. It comes from section 201.02 at 70 cents per $100 of the price, and the state can pursue any party named on the document whatever the contract says. If a mortgage sits on the property, it counts as consideration whether or not the buyer takes it over.

The Broward clerk takes the tax at recording. Section 28.24 fees open at $5.00 for page one and climb with extra pages, extra names and technology charges. Your closing agent can total them for your deed.

The property tax bill works separately. Hollywood parcels are valued each January 1 and billed in November. A discount shrinks the longer you wait, and April 1 is when an open balance becomes delinquent. Your closing agent prorates the year between you and the buyer.

Foreclosure, probate and tenants

  • Foreclosure: following a final judgment, the clerk schedules a public auction 20 to 35 days later unless the plaintiff allows more time. Closing your own sale first can head it off.
  • Probate: summary administration suits a smaller estate (up to $150,000 non-exempt) or a death more than two years back. Start with a lawyer who can list the creditor-claim deadlines.
  • Tenants: expect to give month-to-month occupants at least 30 days' notice, while a missed rent payment starts with a three-day written demand.

Deaths after 2004 carry no Florida estate tax.

What a landlord should do before selling

A tenant is the biggest unknown in a rented house. Gather each lease and every tenant's contact information, then decide whether the buyer will keep the tenancy or the house must be empty at closing. Because month-to-month occupants are owed at least 30 days' notice, begin that clock as soon as your plan is set.

Tell the Broward Property Appraiser about any change in use, since renting a homestead house can cost the exemption. A buyer who plans to keep tenants will want rent records, so have them ready alongside the tax bill.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Documents to gather for a cash offer

  • The recorded deed and your latest tax bill.
  • A payoff letter for each mortgage or lien, plus estoppel details from a condo or HOA.
  • Copies of leases and tenant contacts.
  • A list of known repairs, open permits and storm claims.
  • For an estate, the court's letters of administration.

Florida requires two subscribing witnesses on a land conveyance. Book the signing around that, or use the remote witnessing the statute allows.

From contract to recording

Once you accept an offer, the closing agent orders title work and requests a payoff from each lender. A condo or HOA supplies its own estoppel details. You sign the deed in front of two witnesses, and it is filed with the Broward clerk, who collects the transfer tax along with the recording fee.

A cash buyer takes loan underwriting out of the schedule, yet payoffs and recording still need days, so get a timeline in writing. Share leases, permit records and storm claim papers early. Late surprises are the usual cause of a delayed closing, and a tidy folder of documents prevents most of them.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to repair my Hollywood house first?

No. Cash and as-is buyers take the house in its present state and adjust their price. A buyer using a loan may still ask for fixes.

Who covers the deed tax in Hollywood?

The contract decides who pays in practice, though the state holds every party to the deed responsible. Confirm the line item with your closing agent.

Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. The buyer files a new application, because your exemption ends with the year of sale.

What if back taxes are owed on my Hollywood home?

Usually the closing agent pays them from your proceeds after the Broward tax collector gives a payoff amount. Balances left unpaid are delinquent as of April 1.

How soon can a Hollywood sale close?

It depends on title work, liens and who is buying. Without a lender the process is shorter, yet payoffs and recording still take days, so request a written schedule.

Ways to sell in Gainesville

Gainesville is Alachua County's seat and largest city, a university-driven hub for north central Florida on the I-75 corridor, roughly halfway between Atlanta and Miami. Owners typically pick one of three routes: list with an agent, line up a buyer themselves, or take a cash purchase.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, but showings and buyer loans to manage.
  • Direct: you set the price and sign every form.
  • Cash: few conditions, flexible timing and a price that discounts for repairs.

Judge each bid by what you net after payoffs, tax and recording, and get every offer on paper. If a buyer wants a deposit from you, early transfer of title or an up-front fee, show the paper to an attorney first.

The Gainesville market

The University of Florida was chosen for Gainesville in 1905, and the city's character has followed the campus ever since. Population is 151,275, median age is 26.4 and median household income is $43,783. Demand for houses tends to follow the academic calendar, and investors weigh rent against price, with plenty of campus-area rental stock in the mix.

The housing itself is varied: older frame houses near downtown, postwar neighborhoods and newer subdivisions toward the I-75 malls. Neighborhoods such as the Duckpond, the southeast and Pleasant Street became historic districts in the 1980s to protect their Victorian homes, and houses close to restored blocks are often the ones carrying historic-district rules.

Historic districts

The city has five local historic districts protecting more than 1,500 historic structures, plus 10 buildings listed individually on the Local Register. Alterations and additions on those properties follow the city's Rehabilitation and Design Guidelines, and an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness begins with a pre-application conference with the Historic Preservation Planner.

Ask that planner whether your house is covered. If it is, say so in your first buyer conversation, since it limits renovation plans, and hand over any Certificate of Appropriateness paperwork you have.

Papers to gather

A complete folder shortens the path to the closing table and gives a buyer fewer reasons to renegotiate.

  • Documents showing who can sign: the deed, trust papers or a probate order.
  • Written payoffs for every mortgage, lien or judgment on file in Alachua County.
  • Lease copies, deposit records and rent history for any tenant.
  • Repair and permit records for roof, plumbing, electrical and air conditioning.
  • Your latest tax bill and TRIM notice.
  • Certificate of Appropriateness paperwork when the property is in a historic district.

Florida requires two witnesses to a deed under s. 689.01, so plan a signing with your title agent, a notary and the witnesses present. Get your estimated costs and net in writing before committing.

A house with a renter inside

An occupied house attracts a different crowd than an empty one. Investors ask for lease end dates, rent amounts and maintenance history. Section 83.57 governs month-to-month tenancy: the landlord's notice must come 30 or more days ahead of the end of the period. A written lease usually stays in force for the next owner. Decide whether you will hand over keys at closing or transfer the tenancy, and tell every prospective buyer which it is.

Gainesville rental rules

The city adopted a Rental Housing Ordinance on September 17, 2020, setting annual permits, inspections and property standards for residential rentals. The city now reports that the ordinance is being repealed and that no specific rental regulations apply at present, although rentals must still meet other city codes.

  • Rentals under 30 days: the city has not regulated them since October 1, 2021.
  • Longer rentals: property maintenance and code enforcement rules still apply.

Ask city Sustainable Development staff for the current status before you describe the rule to a buyer, and ask whether an old landlord permit needs to be closed.

Recording costs at closing

Doc stamps on a Gainesville deed come to 70 cents per hundred dollars of price. The Alachua County clerk takes payment at the counter, and everyone who signs shares liability regardless of what the contract says. Recording fees under s. 28.24 are charged page by page, with trust fund and technology add-ons. Have the title agent print the full total on your closing statement before you sign.

Alachua County tax dates

Taxes follow a fixed yearly rhythm, and a closing agent prorates the year's bill at settlement. The tax collector can state the balance.

A sale resets the buyer's assessed value to market the next January. The homestead exemption is up to $50,000.

Inherited house or foreclosure

Florida statutes lay out the sequence in each case. Smaller or older estates may qualify for summary administration under s. 735.201, and s. 733.702 sets a creditor filing cutoff. After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk sells the property at auction on the schedule in s. 45.031. Selling beforehand can preserve equity that an auction may not. An attorney who handles probate or foreclosure can explain your options.

How a cash sale runs

After you accept a written offer, a title company opens a file and searches the Alachua County record for liens, judgments and unpaid taxes. Anything it finds has to be cleared or paid from your proceeds. You then sign the contract, and at closing sign the deed with two witnesses. The agent pays off your lender, collects the stamp tax and recording fees, and sends you the balance. Because no buyer's lender is involved, nobody orders an appraisal, and the buyer is not waiting on underwriting. That is where the speed comes from.

Ask the buyer to say in writing when closing will happen, who pays which cost, and what happens to items left in the house.

Listing or selling for cash?

A listing may bring a higher price, but it asks for patience: showings, inspection requests, a buyer's loan and weeks of carrying costs. A cash buyer offers speed and certainty, and takes the repairs off your hands, so the price reflects that work. A house with a new roof and a flexible date can do well on the market. One with deferred maintenance, a tenant or a lender's deadline often fits a direct sale better.

Whichever route you favor, get at least two written offers and compare them by net proceeds, not by the number on top.

Closing day

At closing the title agent reviews the settlement statement with you. Read each line, ask about any charge you do not recognize and confirm that payoffs match your letters. Once the deed is signed and recorded, hand over keys and remotes, and your proceeds arrive by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the property appraiser and keep copies of everything you signed, including the final settlement statement.

Frequently asked questions

How big is Gainesville?

The city covers about 65.27 square miles and has a population of 151,275 from the 2025 BEBR update. Its median age is 26.4.

Does Gainesville regulate short-term rentals?

The city has not regulated rentals of fewer than 30 days since October 1, 2021. County and state rules are separate.

Who can tell me if my Gainesville house is historic?

The city's Historic Preservation Planner can. Gainesville has five local historic districts covering more than 1,500 structures, with extra rules for work on them.

Who pays documentary stamps on a Gainesville sale?

The contract usually assigns it, yet all parties to the deed are liable under the statute. The clerk takes payment at recording.

When do Alachua County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. November bills carry the largest early-payment discount, and it fades by February.

City water, sewer and septic in Palm Bay

Not every Palm Bay house runs on city water and sewer. The Utilities Department's service area covers a large share of the city but not all of it, and thousands of homes still rely on septic tanks or private wells. The city counts more than 32,000 septic systems and 12,000 drinking water wells.

A buyer's lender, inspector and insurer will all ask what the house drains into and where its water comes from, so settle the answer before listing. The city offers an interactive map: type the full address and it shows whether lines are in place.

The utility is an enterprise fund, which means it takes no property tax money and lives on customer revenue. Rates are adjusted every October 1.

The mandatory connection ordinance

An ordinance approved November 2, 2023 requires developed properties with city lines readily available to hook up. Section 381.00655(1)(a) of the Florida Statutes governs mandatory sewer connection.

As of October 1, 2023, about 1,066 developed parcels had sewer available but not connected, called SANC, and 2,344 had water available but not connected, called WANC. Of those, 289 have neither service.

  • The city notifies owners in writing, in phases that began in summer 2024.
  • Each owner then has one year from the date of the notice to connect.
  • Households in the active phase receive information on septic-to-sewer funding eligibility.
  • Eligible owners work with a pre-approved contractor, and the funding source reimburses the contractor after the agreement is met.
  • A sewer account must be opened, and a $100 deposit may apply.

If a notice has arrived for your address, the one-year clock is part of the sale.

How a septic-to-sewer switch works

The job runs through the utility, the Health Department and the Building Division, in that order. Knowing the order helps you judge how long a switch would take before closing.

  1. Check availability on the city map and confirm costs with Customer Care.
  2. Complete a residential application and pay the connection charges.
  3. The utility issues a work order to locate the clean-out or tap-in point for the sewer lateral.
  4. A septic contractor or the owner obtains a permit from the county Department of Health, and a city building permit is also needed.
  5. The contractor abandons the tank while an environmental health inspector watches.
  6. A plumber connects the lateral to the house, ideally before the tank is abandoned so service is never interrupted.

The city recommends hiring a septic contractor and an insured plumber who both hold current Florida credentials. Ask each for proof before you sign. The Building Division is in the City Hall Annex at 120 Malabar Road SE, phone (321) 953-8924.

Selling a septic or well house

Decide whether to connect first or to sell as is, and tell buyers which one you chose. Both work. Cash offers tend to discount for the switching cost, while a financed buyer's lender may want repairs finished.

  • Pull the city map result for your address and save a copy.
  • Keep any mandatory connection notice, since its one-year window passes to the next owner.
  • Gather septic pumping and well records if you have them.
  • Ask Customer Care about payment agreements, which apply to owner-occupied accounts.

Selling as is to a renovator skips the hookup work altogether. Whichever way you go, put the water and sewer facts in writing so they are never a surprise at inspection.

When you meet a buyer, bring the map printout, any connection notice, and the well or septic records. A buyer who sees the facts up front is less likely to ask for a price cut after the inspection, and the title agent can plan the closing date around any open utility account.

The November flood and your sale

The city's flood event page describes waived permit fees for residential flood repairs, a damage reporting form run through Brevard County Emergency Management, and a Disaster Relief Program for owners who meet homestead, payment and income tests.

Owners with a National Flood Insurance Program policy need a substantial damage inspection as part of the claim and before permits. The Building Department asks owners to call (321) 953-8924 before starting work.

A house that took on water can still be sold. Keep photos, estimates and permits together, since a buyer's insurer will ask. If you would rather skip repairs, an as-is cash sale shifts that work to the buyer.

Flood zone papers for a listing

Lenders check the flood zone on every purchase, so having paper ready speeds things along.

  • Elevation certificates: the Building Department keeps floodplain review copies with FEMA Elevation Certificates for homes built since 1993.
  • Map history: a FEMA map that took effect March 17, 2014 moved about 2,000 structures out of the Special Flood Hazard Area, and those owners may qualify for a Preferred Risk policy.
  • Insurance discount: the city holds a Community Rating System rating of 7, described as a 15 percent reduction in federal flood insurance premiums.

Mortgages backed by federal agencies require flood coverage inside the hazard area, so a buyer will price that policy into the offer.

Which permit rules catch sellers off guard?

The permit list is longer than people assume. It includes fences, sheds, re-roofing, window and door replacement, air conditioner change-outs, electrical, plumbing, gas work and generators.

Work begun without a permit risks a penalty reaching four times the fee. Residential permits average 14 working days for approval, and applications go through an online portal. An owner-builder permit is allowed only when the property will not be sold or leased for a year, which matters for anyone planning a quick flip. Open permits and unpermitted work come up at inspection, so close them out before listing.

Brevard County taxes and deed costs

The Brevard County Property Appraiser values property each January 1, and bills arrive in November with a 4% discount that shrinks to 1% by February. Unpaid bills are delinquent after April 1, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

Homestead reduces taxable value by up to $50,000, and the new owner is reassessed after a sale. Deed stamps are 70 cents per $100 in Brevard, collected by the clerk at recording. Ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement early so stamps, recording fees and prorated taxes are clear.

Frequently asked questions

How do I know if my Palm Bay home can connect to city sewer?

Enter your full address in the interactive map on the Palm Bay Utilities service availability page, or call Customer Care at (321) 952-3420 to confirm.

What is the deadline to connect once Palm Bay sends a notice?

Twelve months after the written notification, under the mandatory connection ordinance approved November 2, 2023.

Can I finance a Palm Bay water or sewer hookup?

Yes for owner-occupied residential accounts. Connection payment agreements run up to five years, with a $10 monthly service charge, and the meter and deposit are excluded.

Are Palm Bay permit fees waived for flood repairs?

The Building Department waives permit fees for residential flood-related repairs. Call (321) 953-8924 before starting work.

Does my homestead savings pass to the buyer?

No. A sale triggers reassessment at just value, so the buyer does not receive the seller's capped assessment.

Selling a house in Miramar

Miramar sits at the southwest edge of Broward County. The Broward County Property Appraiser assesses your house, and the city tacks its own fees onto the same bill. Population is 137,107 across 31 square miles, bounded roughly by Pembroke Road to the north, County Line Road or Honey Hill Road to the south, U.S. Highway 441 (State Road 7) to the east and the Everglades Conservation Area to the west.

The city was incorporated on May 26, 1955, and grew from under 200 residents on about 2.9 square miles. That is why a house from the 1960s and a much newer one can stand a few miles apart and come with very different permit files, association rules and flood exposure. Start with your own permit and lien history instead of a citywide average.

What Miramar puts on a property tax bill

Broward's appraiser sets the assessed value, several taxing authorities set rates, and bills go out each year starting November 1. Of every ad valorem tax dollar, 35 cents goes to the city and 65 cents to other Broward taxing agencies.

Miramar charges on the tax bill

Call the Broward tax office or the city for the millage rate that applies to your closing year. The fire and stormwater charges are non-ad valorem assessments. They show up on the same bill but do not rise or fall with your home's value. The city also runs a fire fee hardship exemption for qualified homeowners, with an application window each year.

Permits, records and liens

Building permit applications go through an online portal that stays open around the clock, with counter help on limited weekdays. A residential permit usually takes about 15 business days to issue, and building fees carry an 8 percent surcharge. For questions before a home improvement project, call the Building Division at 954-602-3200.

Records matter at closing. The city is not likely to hold blueprints for homes more than 10 years past their certificate of occupancy, because state rules let it discard residential plans after that. If you did work years ago, look up the permit now so a buyer's inspector does not find an open or expired one.

  • An electric vehicle charger at home needs a city permit and inspection, even under a utility install program.
  • Homes in an association also need association approval for a charger.
  • Only people listed as contacts on a code case can check its status online.

The city offers a lien search, and a check for it must match the exact fee. Order one early so no lien appears for the first time on the settlement statement.

Deed tax, homestead and delinquent taxes

A Broward deed carries the base statewide stamp rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, paid to the county clerk at recording. Everyone on the deed is liable, so the contract should name who pays.

  • Homestead applications reach the property appraiser by March 1. The Broward office takes exemption questions at 954-357-6830.
  • The TRIM notice arrives in August, and a value petition is due with the clerk within 25 days.
  • The early payment discount slides from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.
  • Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold by June 1.

A sale resets a homesteaded property's assessment to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours. A certificate holder cannot demand payment until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, but a tax deed application can follow. Clear any delinquent taxes before you list.

How can I sell a Miramar house fast?

Sellers here usually compare a listing, a direct sale and a cash bid. Condition, loan payoff and your deadline drive the choice. A cash offer typically saves weeks but comes in below a retail price, so collect more than one written number.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, with repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale to an investor: as-is purchase and a closing date you can bend.
  • Short sale or pre-foreclosure sale: needs lender approval and starts before a judgment.

If a lender has already sued, Florida rules put the auction 20 to 35 days after final judgment, require a 5 percent bidder deposit and allow a 10 day objection window. Selling ahead of that date keeps the price in your hands.

What a cash sale skips is the lender's appraisal, the loan approval window and most repair negotiation after an inspection. What it does not skip is the title search, the deed and the stamp tax. Ask each buyer in writing who pays for title work and the deed stamps, and whether they will take the house with any open permit or lien still attached.

What to gather before accepting an offer

Pull together the items that set your net proceeds before you sign. Miramar has several charges outside the base tax rate.

  • The fire assessment and stormwater lines from your tax bill. The residential fire assessment is $479.21 a year, and stormwater is $120 per equivalent residential unit of 3,619 square feet.
  • Proof of your homestead or other exemption from the Broward County Property Appraiser.
  • A city lien search and a list of permits pulled on the property.
  • Association documents and any balance owed, if the home is in a community with dues.

The fire assessment helps maintain fire ratings that can lower insurance costs, and a buyer's agent may bring that up. Have your insurance declaration page on hand before you negotiate.

Steps from signed contract to closing

After a contract is signed, the title company searches the record for liens, open permits and tax balances. You order payoff letters from each lender, and the association issues its paperwork if the home has one. Resolve anything the search turns up, because a lien from the city or a permit left open will surface for the buyer's lender. At the signing, the deed is executed and sent to the county clerk, who collects the stamp tax and records it.

A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and loan underwriting, so most of the remaining time goes to the title search and payoffs. Bring photo identification to the signing, keep your keys, garage remotes and any association gate devices together, and confirm the date your utilities and insurance should stop. If the property is homesteaded, remember the exemption is yours, not the house's, and the new owner files separately by March 1.

Frequently asked questions

Who sets the property tax rate for a Miramar house?

Several taxing authorities do, while the Broward County Property Appraiser sets the assessed value. The city has proposed a millage of 7.1172, so confirm the final figure with the city or the Broward tax collector.

How long does a Miramar building permit take?

About 15 business days for a residential project. Plan for that if a buyer wants an old issue closed out before the sale.

Will a buyer ask for permit records on my Miramar home?

Often a buyer's inspector will ask about permits on past work. The city is not likely to keep plans for homes more than 10 years past the certificate of occupancy, so search for yours early.

What is the Miramar fire assessment?

It is a yearly non-ad valorem fee on the property tax bill that pays for fire and emergency resources. A residential unit pays $479.21 per year, and qualified homeowners can apply for a hardship exemption.

Where can I check for liens before selling in Miramar?

Use the city's lien search through its Financial Services pages and ask your title company for a full title search. Pay for the lien search in the exact amount required.

Listing versus a quicker sale

Around Coral Springs, sellers usually ask one thing first: spend months on the market, or take a faster deal and leave the house untouched? What the repairs would cost and how much principal remains on your loan tend to answer it. The city spreads over 24 square miles in the northwest corner of Broward County, and family buyers dominate the market. Whichever route you choose, write down your lowest acceptable price and your deadline before the first offer arrives.

Prices, rents and owner costs

The city counts 138,783 residents, a 3.3 percent rise since 2020. Roughly six in ten occupied homes (60.3 percent) are owner-lived, and the rest are rentals, so investor buyers are part of the competition on your street.

At $2,845 a month for a mortgaged owner, a single missed payment stings quickly, and that pressure is behind many sales.

How the Broward appraiser and tax collector fit in

Your parcel's value comes from the county appraiser, yet that office never sends the bill. A warning on its home page says a new owner is assessed at full market value, which means your own bill understates what the next owner will face.

  • Homestead filings must reach the appraiser by March 1.
  • For the 2027 roll, a late filing is accepted through September 20, 2027, with no exceptions for good cause beyond that date.
  • Sign up for the appraiser's free Owner Alert to learn when anyone records a change of ownership on your parcel.

Tax bills are issued by the tax collector, who gives 4 percent off in November and steps down to 1 percent by February.

Deed tax and recording

Broward falls under the standard statewide deed rate of 70 cents per $100. Under s. 201.02 a loan secured on the property is treated as part of the price, so retiring it does not reduce the taxable amount.

  • Payment goes to the clerk at filing.
  • Each person named as a grantor stays liable for the tax.
  • The first recorded page is $5.00.

An itemized closing statement keeps any charge from surprising you.

Selling when you owe more than you can pay

Once a court enters judgment, the foreclosure auction follows in 20 to 35 days. The high bidder puts down 5 percent, and the result holds unless someone objects inside 10 days.

  • If money is left after the auction, claim it with the clerk before it is reported unclaimed.
  • A homestead owner should reach out to the clerk during that 10-day period.
  • Handing the lender a deed in lieu still triggers the deed tax.

A sale that closes before the judgment date can leave the proceeds with you.

Inherited and tenant-occupied houses

Probate may have to come first for an inherited house. A shortened process exists under section 735.201 for modest estates, and for owners who died more than two years back.

An occupied rental adds steps. Ending a monthly tenancy takes 30 days' notice, and a demand for unpaid rent allows 3 days, leaving out weekends and court holidays. When a judge sides with the landlord, the sheriff posts a notice giving 24 hours. Should the tenant stay through the sale, spell out in writing whether the buyer inherits the lease.

Before you accept an offer

  1. Ask your lender for a payoff letter, and look for liens on the parcel.

  3. Decide in writing who pays the November tax bill.
  4. Find two witnesses for the deed signing.
  5. Compare any offer with what an agent listing would net after repairs and fees.

Recording and ownership questions are answered on the appraiser's FAQ page or by phone at 954-357-6830. Homestead forms can go in online, by email, by fax or by mail.

Save Our Homes and portability

Owners who have homesteaded in Coral Springs for years often sit far below market value because of the Save Our Homes cap. The state's chart prints the cap as 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024.

None of that cap stays with the old house once it sells. A share can travel to your next Florida home through Form DR-501T, provided the new homestead starts inside a three-year window that is counted from January 1 of the year you moved out. The transfer tops out at $500,000. Amendments in chapter 2026-239 first reach the 2027 roll, so confirm the details for your case with the appraiser.

Senior, disability and deferral options

Florida offers several breaks for people still living in their homes. Every one of them ends or changes when you sell.

  • A senior whose income is under the limit may receive an extra $50,000 exemption where a local ordinance provides it. The Broward appraiser can say whether it applies.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember may get $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Form DR-570, filed by March 31, defers the part of the tax that exceeds 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 or older.

If you have a deferral, ask the collector what it means for a sale and get a payoff figure before closing. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and a certificate can be sold against the account by June 1.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Language and listing materials

A large minority of residents, 32.1 percent, were born abroad, and 37.5 percent of people aged five and up use another language at home. Offering photos and a summary of your terms in a second language widens your audience and avoids mix-ups. Keep the translated text short and have a bilingual friend or your title agent look it over before you share it.

The city is also stable: 87.7 percent of households stayed put during the past year, so word of a sale can travel through neighbors.

Where to call

County offices handle anything that touches your parcel. Completed applications can be mailed to the appraiser at 1801 NW 49 Street, Suite PA1, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309. Staff are in on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm. The tax collector answers at (954) 357-4829.

Storm or fire damage behind your sale? The appraiser has a catastrophic structural damage report form for a home that stayed uninhabitable for at least 30 days. When you go in person, take your deed, photo ID and newest tax bill, and jot down who helped you so a follow-up call goes smoothly. Before any buyer visit, take dated photos of the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanicals, so the condition you describe matches what you can show. If a buyer's inspector later finds something you knew about, you will be glad you disclosed it early in writing.

Frequently asked questions

What does a Coral Springs home typically cost?

The typical owned home is valued at $545,400 for 2020-2024. Your house may sell above or below that depending on condition and street.

Which county collects Coral Springs property taxes?

Broward County. Its appraiser sets values and its tax collector sends the bills each November.

What documentary stamp rate applies to a Coral Springs deed?

70 cents per $100 of price, the rate that applies in every Florida county except Miami-Dade.

When must I file for homestead?

By March 1 with the appraiser, after making the house your permanent home as of January 1.

Can I sell if the house is in probate?

Only once a personal representative has authority to convey it. A deed under a probated will is listed as non-taxable.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in West Palm Beach?
We buy West Palm Beach houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How a West Palm Beach owner can close quickly

The quickest paths are a sale to a cash buyer or investor and a listing priced to move. If timing is what you need most, balance three things: the price, the number of days to close, and how many repairs the buyer will insist on.

  • Cash or investor sale: no repairs asked of you, and the closing date is frequently yours to set.
  • Agent listing: more potential buyers and often more money, but showings and loan approval take time.
  • Hybrid: put it on the market, and switch to a cash offer if interest stays thin.

Put three questions to every buyer: how title problems get handled, who orders the title search, and what happens to the deposit if they back out. With so many houses dating from earlier decades, those answers count as much as the price. Then add up what each offer leaves you after deed tax, title charges, unpaid taxes and any rental license filing. A big headline number sometimes nets less than a modest cash bid.

West Palm Beach housing mix

West Palm Beach is the seat of Palm Beach County and was incorporated on November 5, 1894. Buyers know The Square, Clematis Street, Antique Row and Northwood Village, and the Grassy Waters Everglades Preserve sits on the western edge.

Housing here spans many eras, with historic neighborhoods next to newer waterfront and downtown buildings. Older houses often come with deferred maintenance, and an as-is sale means you never pay for those repairs before listing.

Rental license rules

Every rental unit in the city needs a rental tax application, whether it is a short-term listing on a platform like Airbnb or a lease to a tenant. Processing generally takes seven to 10 business days.

Owners also complete a zoning review that verifies the number of units. Inspectors check interior and exterior conditions such as working appliances, window screens, paved parking and visible address numbers. After applying, the owner contacts Code Enforcement at (561) 822-1465.

West Palm Beach rental property types
TypeDescriptionExtra requirement
Type 1Owner-occupied single-family, multifamily or duplexProof the property is owner-occupied; owner name must match the recorded deed
Type 2Not owner-occupied single-family or duplexEntire dwelling unit rented
Type 3Not owner-occupied multifamily, such as apartments or condosBuilding and unit counts; compliance with any geographic caps

When you sell a rental, tell the buyer which type it is. Ownership on the application must match the deed recorded with the Palm Beach County Clerk's Office, which means the new owner files separately.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your West Palm Beach house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Code enforcement and permits

Open violations and unpermitted additions can slow a closing. An extra unit added without paperwork is a likely sticking point, since rental owners must hold a license and pass an inspection.

The code compliance division sets minimum standards for substandard housing conditions, trash and debris, yard upkeep and parking areas.

Walk your lot before listing and look for visible problems, and confirm that any garage conversion or added unit has permits on file. Call Code Enforcement to ask whether your address has open cases. Cash buyers will take a property with problems, but they subtract the cleanup from their price.

Property tax due dates and discounts

The county sends out over 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, and they can be paid from that day through March 31. In August the Property Appraiser mails a proposed-tax notice.

  • November: 4 percent discount
  • December: 3 percent discount
  • January: 2 percent discount
  • February: 1 percent discount
  • March: no discount; April 1: taxes become delinquent

Once a tax is delinquent, you cannot pay it online, and a postmark no longer proves timely payment. If a bill reaches you after you sold, pass it to the new owner or notify the office with a Property Sold Form. Call the Property Appraiser at (561) 355-2866 about mailing addresses or exemptions, and the Tax Collector at (561) 355-2264 about delinquent amounts.

Your bill includes non-ad valorem charges as well as ad valorem tax. The Solid Waste Authority fee is one example, set by the type of property.

Deferring or limiting property taxes

Certain owners can put off payment. A homestead deferral request goes to the tax collector on Form DR-570 by March 31, and installment plan applications follow by May 1.

Non-homestead property has its own protection: assessed value growth is limited to 10 percent each year. Homestead property gets the Save Our Homes cap: yearly increases cannot exceed the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. That cap resets when title changes, so your buyer may be assessed higher than you were come the next January 1.

Papers to gather before you list

A tidy folder speeds up every offer. Start with your recorded deed, which shows the exact owner name the city and county will see. Add your latest tax bill, a mortgage payoff letter if you owe a lender, and any permit records for additions or major repairs.

For a rental, include the current rental tax application and the lease. For an older house, include dated receipts for the roof, air conditioning and plumbing. A buyer who can see this record spends less time guessing, and fewer guesses mean fewer price cuts late in the deal.

What a cash sale skips

Without a mortgage, a cash deal has no lender appraisal and no underwriting wait. On an older house that matters, because an appraiser's repair list can derail a financed purchase. You also avoid staging and weeks of showings.

Once you accept an offer, a title search comes first, then a look at the settlement statement, then you sign the deed and the clerk records it. Can I sell a rental property in West Palm Beach without ending the rental license?

How long does the West Palm Beach rental license take?

The city says it is generally processed in seven to 10 business days. A zoning review of the unit count is part of the process.

When do West Palm Beach property taxes become delinquent?

On April 1. From then on, you cannot pay online, and a postmark stops counting as proof of payment.

Which discount applies if I pay in December?

December payments earn 3 percent off. The other months run 4 percent in November, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.

Must I pull a permit for repairs I make before selling?

Usually, yes. Florida's 2026 exemption for projects under $7,500 has limits, and electrical, plumbing and structural jobs still require permits. Check with the city's Development Services staff first.

Ways to sell a Lakeland house fast

A Lakeland owner has three routes: sell to a cash buyer, hire an agent, or sell on your own. The cash route is fastest because nobody waits on a lender and the buyer accepts the house with its flaws.

A listing may draw a higher bid, but you have to prepare the house, host showings and answer inspection requests. If the house is full of an estate's belongings, has a dated interior or needs a new roof, that preparation can drag on for months. A turnkey house with a flexible timeline suits the open market better.

  • Cash: skip repairs, choose the closing day.
  • Agent listing: broader audience, longer timeline.
  • Sale by owner: you carry the paperwork and negotiation.

Whichever route you pick, ask each buyer to put the price, closing date, deposit and repair terms on paper so you can compare offers line by line.

About Lakeland and its lakes

Water defines the city. Lakeland, incorporated in 1885, has 38 named lakes plus many smaller ones, ranging from 2.5 acres at Lake Blanton to 2,272 acres at Lake Parker, inside city limits of 75.16 square miles.

All storm drains empty into a lake, pond, wetland or other waterway, and the lakes help reduce local flooding. Yard debris left in the street counts as an illegal discharge because clippings feed algae blooms, so keep grass and leaves out of the gutter before photos are taken. Note any lake frontage in your own records, and use the city's pollution hotline, listed on its lakes and stormwater page, to report a discharge.

Is my house in a historic district?

Possibly. Lakeland has seven local historic districts covering 1.42 square miles, protecting more than 1,600 buildings and 13 landmarks. The program dates to 1980, and the districts hold 7.15 percent of the city's parcels and about 6 percent of its residents.

Recent resurveys documented 770 resources in the Dixieland and Munn Park districts and 1,042 in the East and South Lake Morton districts. Munn Park has 66 contributing properties and Dixieland has 466. Contributing status affects which exterior changes a buyer can make.

Email the city's historic preservation office to learn whether your home is a contributing structure. The Lake Morton survey page also offers an address lookup. Get that answer before you list and pass it on to buyers with your disclosures.

Period dates may shift. The Dixieland report recommends widening the district's period of significance to 1975, while Munn Park keeps its 1884 to 1946 window. If Dixieland changes, more mid-century houses could count as contributing, so ask the office about any house built before 1975.

  • Look up the address.
  • Ask about design review for windows, roofs and additions.
  • Save any approvals for past work.

Polk County delinquent taxes

A Polk real estate bill still open on April 1 of the year after assessment is delinquent. The Polk County Tax Collector adds 3 percent interest and an advertising charge on that date.

If June 1 arrives with the balance unpaid, the lien goes to an online auction where bidding opens at 18 percent and moves down. A certificate lapses at seven years, though its holder can seek a tax deed once two years have gone by. Redeeming costs either the rate bid or a minimum 5 percent charge, whichever is higher.

Polk County uses the standard Florida deed tax of 70 cents for every $100 of consideration. The state holds every signer of the deed responsible, so the contract's split is only a private understanding between you and the buyer. Any mortgage on the property counts as part of consideration.

Recording starts at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each further page, with extra statutory charges. Two witnesses must see the deed signed.

The sale closes out your homestead on this house, and the buyer is assessed fresh the next January 1. If you are moving within Florida, ask the property appraiser about portability, which has a March 1 filing date.

Inherited or rented houses

Settle who can sign first, then deal with the occupants. A streamlined court procedure exists for small estates, and for any estate once two years have gone by since the death. A probate attorney can tell you whether it fits.

Renters on a monthly basis need 30 days' notice to end the tenancy.

  • Collect letters of administration or the death certificate.
  • Confirm tax status with the Polk tax collector.
  • Gather leases and notices for any tenant.

What a cash sale skips

With a cash buyer there is no loan approval, no appraisal and no lender timetable. You still need a clear title, so expect a title search for mortgages, liens and unpaid tax before the deed is signed.

The usual path is an offer, a signed contract, a title search, a settlement statement you review, and a signing with two witnesses. Bring photo ID, your payoff letter if a mortgage exists, the latest tax bill, and the names of everyone on the deed, since each owner must sign. Ask the title company how soon funds are released after the deed is recorded. Read the settlement statement before you sign and confirm who covers recording, the deed tax and the title policy.

Getting a Lakeland house ready to show

Buyers of older Lakeland houses ask about the roof, the air handler, the electrical panel and the plumbing. Write down what was replaced and when, and keep receipts and permit papers in one folder. A one-page summary answers most questions before they turn into price cuts.

Walk the yard and the street edge. Clippings in the road, a damaged seawall or dock, and peeling paint at the curb all show up in photos. If the house sits on a lake, say so in the listing and keep any survey handy.

Florida humidity is hard on a closed-up house. Run the air conditioning, open the blinds and check for damp smells before each showing. If you plan to take a cash offer instead, you can skip most of this, but a short list of known defects still helps the buyer price the house fairly and keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Test smoke alarms and replace batteries.
  • Fix dripping faucets and loose handrails.
  • Book final utility readings for the closing day.

Frequently asked questions

How large is Lakeland?

The city limits cover 75.16 square miles, with 38 named lakes inside. Lake Parker is the biggest at 2,272 acres, and Lake Blanton the smallest named one at 2.5 acres.

Can a historic district block my sale?

No. It governs exterior changes, not who may buy. Ask the city's historic preservation office whether your house is a contributing structure and keep that answer with your sale papers.

What is a Polk tax certificate?

It is a lien that the tax collector auctions to an investor after the delinquency date, and it does not transfer the house. A holder can ask for a tax deed after two years, so pay the balance before you list.

Does a sale end my Florida homestead?

Yes, on that house. Portability may let you move part of your capped value to another Florida homestead.

Who pays the Florida deed tax?

The contract assigns it, though the state treats every party to the deed as liable. The Polk County rate is 70 cents for each $100.

Selling in Pompano Beach: your options

Pompano Beach is a beach city in the north of Broward County, halfway between Miami and Palm Beach. Year-round residents number over 101,400, and the count passes 150,000 when part-time owners come back for winter.

That seasonal pulse shapes a sale. Showings pick up while snowbirds are in town, and an empty house can sit quietly through summer. A seller with postponed repairs, a tenant or a lien on the house generally has three ways to go.

Consider who will most likely buy. Investors may plan to rent the place out, and owner-occupants often want a house they can move into. Cash buyers deduct repairs from their price, while retail buyers may ask you to fix things. Your likely buyer points to the right route.

Homes near the Pompano Beach Air Park may hear aircraft, and the city publishes quiet-flying guidelines because of the effect on residential areas. If your street is affected, mention it early.

Flood zones and insurance near the water

A house near the water brings questions about flood zones and insurance. Before a buyer asks, collect your policy, any elevation certificate, and permits for roof, window or seawall work. One folder with all of it speeds the buyer's review and firms up a cash offer.

What the Broward homestead exemption means when you sell

Back taxes get paid from your proceeds at the closing table, which hands the buyer a clean record. Request the exact balance from the Broward tax collector ahead of time, and check for special assessments on the parcel.

Your exemption stops when you sell. It does not run past the year of the sale, and the next occupant must apply on their own.

Each year's deadline is March 1, and September 20, 2027 is the final late-filing date for 2027. If you rent the house out, the exemption is probably lost. An unreported change can bring back taxes plus a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

After ownership changes, Florida re-values the property, so the first bill a buyer receives is often higher than yours. Sales, foreclosures and title transfers all trigger the reset, though transfers between spouses are an exception.

  • Hold on to the annual receipt Broward mails in January.
  • End the exemption on any house you no longer live in.

The November 2026 amendment

It may affect what buyers are willing to pay. Amendment 3 won voter approval on November 3, 2026. The non-school homestead exemption can reach $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, and the non-homestead cap drops to 5 percent.

Implementing legislation will settle some details, so ask Broward's property appraiser how the changes will reach your parcel.

Costs and paperwork for a Pompano Beach deed

On a deed, Florida charges 70 cents per $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade. All parties to the document are liable, so the purchase contract should settle who pays.

The Broward clerk records the deed and takes the tax at that time. Under section 28.24, recording starts at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, before technology surcharges. Ask for a quote.

What if the house has tenants, a foreclosure case or an heir?

Each situation can lead to a sale, but each has its own clock. For a tenant, ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days' notice (section 83.57), and unpaid rent begins with a three-day written notice (section 83.56).

In a foreclosure, the clerk's sale is set 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless it is extended (section 45.031). Closing before then protects your equity.

Heirs can use summary administration when the estate is $150,000 or less, or when the death was more than two years ago (section 735.201).

How a cash sale works

Season matters here. Houses draw more eyes while winter residents are in town, so a seller with time may do better listing then. A seller who must move sooner can accept cash and pick the date, whatever the month.

  1. Tell the buyer the address, mortgage balance and any tenant details.
  2. Review the written offer for price, repairs and closing day.
  3. The closing agent searches title and requests payoff letters.
  4. Two witnesses watch you sign the deed.
  5. The Broward clerk records it, and you receive your proceeds.

Before you talk to anyone, assemble a short packet: your payoff statement, the latest Broward tax bill, any lease, your insurance declarations page and the permits you have on file for major work. Ask each buyer how long the offer stays open and who pays for the title policy. Written answers protect you if the closing day moves.

On signing day, expect to review the settlement statement line by line. It should show the stamp tax, recording fees, payoffs and the prorated tax bill. If a line differs from your contract, ask the closing agent to correct it before you sign. Once the clerk records the deed, funds are released and the sale is final. Walk through the house one last time before the signing, take your keys and garage openers to the closing, and leave behind only what the contract lists. Appliances and fixtures not named in the contract can cause arguments at the last minute.

Cash removes the buyer's appraisal and loan approval, the two steps that most often stretch a listing. Title work and signing stay. Afterward, file your recorded deed, settlement statement and tax records together.

Usually, because no lender appraisal is needed. The title still has to be clear, and the deed must be witnessed and recorded in Broward.

Your contract decides, though the state can hold every party liable. Outside Miami-Dade the rate is 70 cents per $100.

Will my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. It ends with the sale year, and the buyer must apply again before March 1.

Can I sell while I am behind on the mortgage?

Yes, as long as you close before the clerk's foreclosure sale. Act early, because that sale can fall 20 to 35 days after judgment.

Which office records my deed?

The Broward County clerk, who also collects the stamp tax when the deed is recorded.

What a Clearwater seller should know first

You have three basic options in Clearwater: hire an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash purchase. The right one depends on the condition of the house, your timetable and any mortgage or renter attached to it. Population was 114,364 in July 2025, down 2.5% from the April 2020 estimate base, so local demand is not growing.

Roughly 24.1% of residents are 65 or older, so downsizing and estate sales account for a fair amount of the activity. Those sellers often prefer an as-is deal to a round of repairs.

Clearwater housing at a glance

A typical owner-occupied Clearwater home was valued at $361,300 for 2020 through 2024, and just 58.6% of housing is lived in by its owner. The rest is rental housing, which is why plenty of sellers in town are landlords with tenants still living in the house.

The gap between $1,908 and $811 suggests many owners have paid off their loans and sell with a large share of equity.

Selling a Clearwater rental house

Yes, a landlord can sell. The city's Planning and Development Department publishes a Business Tax Receipt application for residential rentals, and it spells out what Clearwater expects of a rental. The form treats stays of under 31 days, or one calendar month if that is less, as outside a residential use in a residential zoning district.

If you rent by the night, read that wording before you list, because a buyer planning short stays will ask. The form also names the housing code items an inspector can review:

  • Kitchen sink, stove and refrigerator, plus bath fixtures and hot and cold water.
  • Heating, smoke detectors and fire protection.
  • Windows, ventilation and lighting in halls and stairways.
  • Electrical outlets and lights.
  • Walls, roofs, ceilings and floors, checked for leaks.
  • Stairs, porches, doors, and pest control.

It also requires a local property manager with a street address in Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee or Sarasota County. Before a rental changes hands, ask Planning and Development about the current fee and the registration steps for the new owner.

Exterior code standards

The same application lists exterior standards that code officers apply to any residential lot: abandoned vehicles, address numbers, debris, sound fences, graffiti, overgrown grass, outdoor storage, parking, lighting and trash facilities.

Walk the lot with that list before the first showing. A boat on the grass or a tall lawn can draw a complaint mid-sale, and a buyer's inspector will note the same things. Fixing them costs little next to a price cut, and a clean exterior also makes a stronger first impression in photos and drive-bys.

Value and exemptions at the Pinellas County Property Appraiser

The county property appraiser sets values. Visit the main office at 315 Court Street, 2nd floor, Clearwater, weekdays from 8 AM to 5 PM. Condos and manufactured homes come with their own paperwork, so ask the office which forms fit your property type.

Values are set as of January 1. Exemption applications close March 1, and a TRIM notice with proposed values comes in August. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so the next January 1 the home is revalued at full just value.

Deed tax and tax bills at closing

State tax on a Pinellas deed is 70 cents per $100 of price. The statute makes every signer answerable regardless of who the contract says pays. The clerk collects at recording. Look for that line on your settlement sheet before you sign.

Tax bills are mailed in November. The discount is 4 percent for November payment and falls a point each month to 1 percent in February. Unpaid bills are delinquent from April 1. A closing in mid-year means the title company shares the bill with the buyer. Ask how it plans to divide it.

What if a Clearwater owner is behind on the mortgage?

Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. After final judgment the clerk sets an auction between 20 and 35 days out, or later if the lender agrees, and the winner leaves a 5 percent deposit. A sale before the auction pays the lender from proceeds and may end the case.

The certificate of title that follows an auction triggers deed tax measured on the top bid. Call your loan servicer or a Florida attorney soon, and set a cash offer beside a short sale before an auction date arrives.

Selling an inherited Clearwater home

Settle who has authority first, because heirs cannot convey clean title on their own. Summary administration, a streamlined court process, is open to estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets and to estates opened over two years after the death. If a will goes through probate, the representative's deed is listed by the state as free of deed tax.

Creditor claims are barred unless filed within three months of first publication of the notice, or 30 days after a creditor is served, whichever is later. For deaths after 2004 there is no Florida estate tax. The probate court clerk can say which path applies to this estate.

Showing the house well

Even a quick sale goes better when the house presents cleanly. Clear counters and closets, trim overgrown plants, and fix small leaks and loose fixtures. If an inspector will be walking through, make sure attic and utility areas are reachable. Tell buyers about known defects rather than hoping they miss them, because a late surprise is the most common reason an agreed price gets reopened. Keep your receipts and any warranty papers together so you can hand them over at closing. If the house is rented, give the tenant plenty of warning before any showing, and be courteous, since a cooperative tenant makes the whole sale smoother.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A simple plan for a fast Clearwater sale

Pick the route first, then work backward from the closing date. Collect your deed, newest tax bill and lender payoff letters. Inspect the yard for exterior problems, and have the city check your address for open permits or violations. With tenants in place, add the lease, deposit record and rent ledger. Request written offers with proof of funds, and compare the net after fees and repairs. Choose a closing date you can truly meet. A few days ahead of signing, get a draft settlement statement from the title company.

Frequently asked questions

Is a cash sale in Clearwater faster than listing?

Closing can come within days or weeks, since no lender or appraisal stands in the way. A listing adds showings, repair negotiations and loan timelines. Estimate your net on each path first.

Does Clearwater require a permit or inspection to sell?

No city permit is required merely to sell. Open permits and code violations can still hold up a closing, so ask Planning and Development to check your address.

Can I sell a Clearwater house with tenants?

Yes. A sale does not cancel the lease by itself. Unpaid rent calls for 3 days' written notice, and ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days, so the buyer either keeps the tenant or waits out proper notice.

Who pays deed tax on a Clearwater sale?

The state can pursue any signer, and contracts usually put the cost on the seller. The state rate is 70 cents per $100.

Where do I check my Clearwater homestead status?

City certificate required before a sale

Miami Gardens requires a Certificate of Re-Occupancy before a property is purchased, sold, conveyed or transferred. That city step comes before closing, so build it into your timeline from day one. It takes five to seven business days when all information is provided, and it applies to every kind of sale, retail or investor. Its purpose is to help the city track changes to structures.

  • Ask for the certificate early, before a contract deadline forces a scramble.
  • Gather the permits for past repairs and upgrades.
  • Ask the city whether open violations or liens are recorded against the parcel.

How the re-occupancy certificate works

The owner applies through the city's code enforcement and business licensing office, reachable at reoccupancy@miamigardens-fl.gov. The city inspects for changes made without a permit, and altered space such as added square footage is reported to the county so the property record and taxes can be corrected.

Violations do not stop a sale. It can go ahead as long as the buyer signs a stipulation agreement with the city promising to fix the problems. That helps with tired houses, since a buyer willing to cure the violations can still close.

Unpermitted work is handled by legalizing it, which means securing a permit after the fact. That can bring penalties and, in the worst case, demolition of the structure, so find out before you list.

Work that needs a permit

The city lists fences, hurricane shutters, door and window installations, sheds, screen enclosures, pool barriers, patio slabs, gazebos, plumbing and electrical work, air conditioner change-outs, room additions and sea walls. The list is not complete, so call the building department before assuming anything is exempt.

If you replaced an air conditioner, enclosed a patio or put up a shed, dig out the permit papers now. Gaps in that record are a likely reason an inspection drags on.

Yard and street rules can also draw citations before a sale. Open-air storage is prohibited, portable storage containers should be removed within thirty calendar days, and vehicles on the swale or public right of way may be towed. Clear those items before an inspector or buyer visits.

Landlord rules and tenants

A rented house needs a Landlord Permit, renewable every year by March 31. The application needs the permit fee, the names and birthdates of all occupants, and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

A sitting tenant changes the sale. Florida's demand for unpaid rent runs 3 days, leaving out weekends and court holidays, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. After a court win, the sheriff restores possession once a 24-hour notice has been posted.

An investor may want the house empty, may keep the tenant, or may ask you to deliver it vacant. Write that choice into the contract so nobody guesses at closing.

Miami-Dade deed stamps

Miami Gardens lies inside Miami-Dade, so the county's own deed stamp applies: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cent surtax that a single-family-only transfer does not owe.

The clerk takes the tax at recording, and each signer shares liability. Warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds are all taxable, as is a deed given to a lender instead of foreclosure. Recording is priced per page under section 28.24, with added trust fund and technology charges.

How property taxes are billed

Miami-Dade's appraiser values the parcel and the county's tax collector issues the bill. The appraiser mails no bills and sets no taxes. Its 2026 roll was certified on October 16, 2026.

The calendar starts with a January 1 valuation date and a March 1 exemption deadline, then proposed notices in August and bills in November. Late bills turn delinquent in April, and tax certificates follow by June.

After a sale the buyer is assessed at full value from the next New Year's Day, and your homestead exemption stops. If you buy elsewhere in Florida, ask about portability, requested with the new homestead filing.

  • Have the closing agent prorate this year's bill between you and the buyer.
  • Check that no tax certificate has been sold against the parcel.
  • Ask the appraiser whether a city inspection changed the property record.

What if the house is in foreclosure or probate?

Foreclosure follows the court's calendar. The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the lender agrees to wait, and after a sale homeowners should ask the clerk about surplus funds.

An inherited house may qualify for Florida's summary administration, which fits estates of up to $150,000 in non-exempt property or deaths over two years old. Creditors lose their claims after a statutory window that runs from the notice to creditors or from service on a known creditor.

Ask a Florida attorney or the clerk's self-help staff which papers a title insurer will require before it covers the sale.

City liens on a Miami Gardens house

The city's code compliance team offers a lien resolution service with four parts: lien searches, administrative release of a lien, lien amnesty and lien reduction, and registration of vacant and abandoned property through a third party.

Order a lien search early. A fine that has piled up from an old violation is the kind of surprise that shows up on a title report days before closing. If a lien exists, ask the city whether amnesty or reduction applies, and get the release in writing so the title company can record it.

Owners of a vacant house should also ask about vacant property registration, since an empty, neglected house draws code attention. Mow, secure and clear the yard before a buyer or inspector visits.

Evaluating a cash offer

Total up the cash you would keep after every cost, then read who handles the re-occupancy certificate, any city lien payoff and the deed stamp. An as-is investor should still state in writing who pays city fees and who signs the stipulation agreement.

Before signing, get the settlement date, the closing agent's name and the deposit terms in writing.

Plan the order of steps: request the certificate and a lien search first, fix or disclose violations, then sign the contract and deed. Doing the city steps first keeps the closing date from slipping, and it gives the buyer a clear picture of what is left to fix.
