Yes. A Certificate of Re-Occupancy is required before the purchase, sale, conveyance or transfer of title of any real property, with a turnaround of five to seven business days when information is complete.

May a Miami Gardens house with open violations be sold?

Yes, when the buyer signs a stipulation agreement promising the city to fix them. Unpermitted work must be legalized through a permit.

When is the Miami Gardens landlord permit due?

It renews each year on or before March 31. The application needs the fee, all occupants' names and birthdates and a national background check for occupants aged 15 and over.

What deed stamp tax applies in Miami Gardens?

Miami-Dade uses 60 cents per $100 and a 45 cent surtax, and a deed moving only a single-family home owes no surtax.

Which office mails Miami Gardens property tax bills?

The Miami-Dade tax collector. The property appraiser assesses value and neither mails bills nor collects taxes.

Ways to sell and move on in Davie

Selling in Davie breaks down into an agent, a do-it-yourself sale, or a buyer who pays cash and takes on the repairs. Match the choice to the condition of the house and how urgently you need the proceeds.

The town looks and behaves differently from the beach cities to the east. Many lots have barns, fencing, pools or other outbuildings, and an inspector will flag those extras, so plan for them from the first day.

  • Agent: widest reach, with open houses, a lender's appraisal and a financing contingency to get through.
  • Owner sale: contract, disclosures and closing coordination all land on you.
  • Cash buyer: no lender involved, often picked for estate homes, rentals and houses in poor shape.

Western Theme rules and lot types

Davie describes itself as a ranching and western-lifestyle community with horse trails, an annual rodeo and a western-themed downtown, and it has more than 107,000 residents. The Town publishes a Western Theme Design Manual meant to preserve citrus, cattle, equestrian and rodeo heritage. Check with the Town on whether it reaches exterior work on your parcel, especially inside the western-themed district.

Two sellers on opposite sides of town can face very different sales. A half-acre lot with an equestrian setup is priced and marketed differently from a townhome in a planned community. Sort out roof age, pool condition and outbuildings before showings begin.

Association approvals

If an association covers your property, request its governing documents early. In many communities a sale needs association approval, estoppel letters and a check for pending special assessments. A late answer from the association can stall a closing longer than a repair would.

Vacation rental registration

Davie regulates short stays through a registration program. The Town Code (Chapter 16, Article IX) and Florida Statutes section 509.242 define a vacation rental as a unit let to transient guests on more than three occasions in a year, each for under thirty days, or one advertised as regularly let that way.

A state DBPR license must be in hand before the Town will take your application. The packet also wants proof of ownership pulled from the county appraiser, corporate papers if an entity owns the home, interior and exterior sketches, a Department of Revenue registration and a Broward tourist tax number.

A violation can bring a civil penalty of up to $500. Call the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before you advertise.

Offices and records you will need

A Davie seller can get most of the records needed from three places. Vacation rental registration and code questions go to the Police Code Compliance Division, 1230 South Nob Hill Road, phone 954-693-8237. Proof of ownership comes from BCPA.net, the Broward appraiser's website. Where an LLC or corporation holds title, the Town wants corporate documents from Sunbiz.org.

Gather them before a buyer's attorney asks. A clean ownership record, a recent tax bill and written word that no code case is open all make the contract easier to sign.

One more item matters to a disabled veteran. The Town's rental program asks for a DD214 and disability papers before applying a veteran exemption, and those same papers support any question a buyer raises about the state's assessment reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers.

Broward property taxes and the sale

Your Davie property is valued and billed by Broward County on the state's schedule. Value is fixed on January 1, a notice of proposed taxes arrives in August, and the bill follows in November.

  • Exemptions and classifications must be filed by March 1, which is important for a lot with an agricultural classification.
  • Petitions on value go to the clerk in the 25 days following the August notice.
  • Paying early earns 4 percent in November, shrinking to 1 percent in February.
  • April 1 is when delinquency starts.

Without homestead, assessed value can climb no more than 10 percent a year. A homestead gets the Save Our Homes cap, the smaller of 3 percent or the change in inflation. Selling ends the cap and the buyer starts from just value.

Land with an agricultural classification deserves a call to the appraiser about how a sale or a change in use affects it, ideally before you sign anything.

Deed transfer and recording

Deeds are recorded by the Broward clerk, and the state stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Under the statute, a mortgage or other encumbrance on the land counts toward consideration whether or not the buyer assumes it. Paying off your loan therefore does not shrink the tax base, as some sellers hope.

Liability for the tax is shared by every party. The contract decides who pays, and the title company normally collects it.

Recording fees are separate. Section 28.24 charges $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with records-fund and technology charges per page. Exemptions are listed for spousal homestead deeds and for divorce deeds on the marital home, so check with your title agent before assuming tax is due.

Inherited, foreclosure and rented houses

Florida law gives each of these a defined path, and a sale stays possible.

If an heir is selling, a personal representative's deed made under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable. A transfer for estate planning is taxable, since no specific exemption covers it. Florida has charged no estate tax on deaths after December 31, 2004.

The clerk's sale after a foreclosure judgment is set for 20 to 35 days out, unless the plaintiff agrees to extend it. A buyer who closes ahead of that date pays off the lender and leaves you any equity.

For unpaid rent the landlord serves a three-day written demand, leaving out weekends and court holidays. Should a tenant raise a defense other than payment, the rent must be deposited with the court within five days, or the defenses are lost.

Before closing day

Request a lender payoff letter, decide who will hold the keys, and get a draft settlement statement from the title agent shortly before closing. Check it against your contract line by line so a mismatch surfaces early. Bring photo ID, and save a copy of everything you sign. After closing, forward your new address to the tax collector and your insurer, and cancel your homeowner's policy only once the deed has been recorded.

Yes. The Town runs a vacation rental registration program tied to Chapter 16, Article IX of its code, and it asks for a state DBPR license first. Contact the Police Code Compliance Division at 954-693-8237 before advertising.

What is the Davie vacation rental fee?

A full registration year runs $500 and the half year from April 1 runs $300. Renewals cost $450 when the owner does not live there and $400 when the owner does.

Who records a deed for a Davie property?

The Broward clerk records it and takes the deed stamp tax of 70 cents per $100, and the title company usually arranges both.

What happens to my property tax benefit when I sell in Davie?

The cap ends with the sale, and the buyer is assessed at just value the next January 1. Buying another Florida homestead? Ask the Broward appraiser about portability.

Can I sell a Davie house with tenants still living there?

Yes. A buyer may accept the lease as written. For a vacant house, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and only a sheriff can physically remove an occupant.

Palm Coast is a young city on Florida's northeast coast, incorporated in 1999. It has 70 miles of saltwater and freshwater canals, the Intracoastal Waterway and more than 130 miles of connecting trails. Water access is what many buyers look for first, so describe it clearly in your listing.

Added a deck or a screened room? Make sure the permit was closed. An inspector or title company can catch an open one, and fixing it before listing is cheaper than doing it mid-contract.

Property tax calendar

Flagler County sets your value as of January 1 and mails the bill in November. Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax, and the bill is normally prorated with the buyer at the closing table. Value comes from the Property Appraiser and the bill from the Tax Collector.

  • File for homestead by March 1. The exemption has two layers: the first $25,000 applies to every tax, and a second layer of up to $25,000 comes off the non-school taxes only, on value above $50,000.
  • Pay the whole bill in November for a 4 percent discount, which shrinks to 1 percent by February.
  • Assessments on non-homestead property are capped at a 10 percent yearly increase.

If someone is living in the house without permission, the sheriff can act on a verified complaint, but only where there is no tenancy, no family tie and no pending lawsuit. A claim of adverse possession needs seven years of possession plus tax payments and a return filed with the property appraiser, and living in a home on that claim before filing is trespass. A month-to-month tenant is different and gets 30 days' notice before a monthly period ends.

Only one other city in Palm Beach County is larger than Boca Raton. More than 75 percent of its housing was built after 1970, and the median single-family price climbed from $268,000 in 2000 to $502,272 in 2019. The city counted 91,797 permanent residents in 2017 and projects 101,652 full-time and seasonal residents by 2040, so ask your agent or buyer how the winter season affects timing.

City rules and open permits

Code enforcement handles housing standards, and the city plans systematic inspections in areas with older structures. Older houses with historic standing are covered by the Historic Preservation Ordinance. Call the city before planning rehab work or a teardown.

  • The Community Appearance Board enforces upkeep standards, mostly on commercial and industrial property.
  • Periodic bulk trash pickups make it easier to clear a house before listing.
  • The city helps owners of historically significant housing apply for state and federal assistance programs.

For open permits, ask the city's Planning, Zoning and Building staff. The county appraiser does not keep permit or situs address records, so a buyer's agent will be sent to the city for those.

How the county values your home

The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets three numbers for each parcel. Just value is market value. Assessed value is just value less caps such as Save Our Homes. Taxable value is assessed value less exemptions, and it is the figure the tax collector bills.

Each value is struck as of January 1. Staff look at every property at least once in five years, in person or from aerial photos. Each parcel page has a tax calculator where a buyer can enter a purchase price and say whether they will homestead, which lets them estimate their own bill before making an offer.

Your homestead exemption when you sell

The exemption is yours, so it travels to your next home. The buyer has to file for their own. If you sell during the year, it can stay on the property until the next January 1, but it is no longer working for the new owner.

With portability, your Save Our Homes savings can follow you to a new Florida homestead. You have three tax years to port after losing a homestead. The portability form goes in with the new homestead application, due March 1. The new homestead must be established within three years of the January 1 of the year you gave up the old one.

Watch renting if the house sits empty before the sale. Renting on January 1 loses the exemption, and renting for more than six months counts as abandonment. Changing the name on the deed can also remove a homestead, so review any transfer to an heir before you sign.

Condominiums and commercial property

Condo sellers should ask the association about assessments before listing. If Florida's SB-4-D building safety law affects the condo market, the appraiser says it will value those properties accordingly and review the effect of assessment fees case by case.

Boca Raton, Boynton Beach and West Palm Beach charge a Fire Rescue Assessment on commercial property, based on use and square footage. For some properties it can exceed $10,000. If you own rental or small commercial property, get the county's figure before you agree on a price.

Deed tax and recording costs

On a Palm Beach County deed the state's documentary stamp tax is 70 cents for every $100 of consideration. Everyone named on the deed is answerable for it. Ask the clerk whether any local housing surtax applies to your deed.

The clerk also adds page-based recording charges, and the deed needs two subscribing witnesses. Think your assessment is wrong? Phone the appraiser at 561.355.3230 and ask for an informal review. The next step is a petition to the Value Adjustment Board, filed through the county clerk.

Storm damage and missed mortgage payments

Storm damage reaches the tax bill the year after it happens, since values follow the condition of the home on January 1. A home that is uninhabitable for more than 30 days may qualify for a partial refund, and a rebuilt home that stays within 110 percent of the original square footage can keep its homestead after a calamity.

With a mortgage in default, a Florida court can order a public sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, and the bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit. Any surplus runs through the clerk. Talk to a Florida attorney or housing counselor early, so you know your choices before a sale date is set.

Timeline for a quick Boca Raton sale

A cash purchase can move fast, but only if the paperwork is ready. Start by pulling your parcel page and checking which exemptions sit on it. Next, order a payoff from each lender and ask the city about open permits. Then collect offers in writing and compare what each would leave you after recording charges, tax proration and any repairs you agree to make. Once you pick one, the title agent orders the search and prepares the deed. Signing happens before two witnesses, and the clerk records the deed afterward.

Condo and association properties add a step. Associations may have to approve the buyer or issue a statement of dues you owe. Make that request the day you decide to sell.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to line up before closing

Paperwork gaps cost sellers more time than price disputes do. Before you accept anything, make sure each owner on title can sign, then ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement. Read it line by line, since the deed tax, recording charges and any prorated tax bill all land there. When a buyer wants repairs, ask for the request in writing and decide what you will fix before the contract deadline.

Frequently asked questions

Is Boca Raton in Palm Beach County?

Yes. Property records come from the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, and the county tax collector sends the bills.

Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. Exemptions move with the owner, so the buyer files their own, and the sale resets assessed value to market on the next January 1.

What is the doc stamp rate on a Boca Raton deed?

It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Every party to the deed is liable to the state.

Can I rent out my Boca Raton house and keep homestead?

Only within limits. Short stays of 30 days or less in a year are allowed, but longer rentals risk the exemption, renting on January 1 loses it, and more than six months is abandonment.

How do I dispute a Boca Raton assessment?

Start with an informal review by calling the appraiser at 561.355.3230. If the issue remains, petition the Value Adjustment Board through the county clerk.

Ways to sell a Fort Myers house

Fort Myers owners generally choose between an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash buyer willing to take the house untouched. Each costs you something different: price, time, or a higher chance that the deal collapses.

A listing draws the most eyes and also brings open houses, inspection reports and a lender's appraisal. Cash skips those hurdles, though the offer usually comes in lower, so decide what a quick, quiet exit is worth to you.

  • Listing: wide exposure, many moving parts, timing tied to a lender.
  • Selling alone: you take on the agent's work and the agent's risks.
  • Cash: few contingencies, no repairs, often a closing date you choose.

Fort Myers housing in brief

The city counts about 101,581 residents, a rise of 17.5 percent from 86,424 in April 2020. Typical value for an owner-occupied home is $384,500, typical gross rent is $1,580, and 49.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Since about half the housing is rented, your buyers may well be landlords and investors, who usually open with questions about leases and rent history.

Older neighborhoods and redevelopment areas

Fort Myers started as an army post beside the Caloosahatchee River and incorporated on August 12, 1885. Homes in the older river corridors may be decades old, so an inspector will look hard at roofs, wiring, plumbing and windows.

The Fort Myers Community Redevelopment Agency has managed redevelopment trusts since 1984. Its programs include residential grants, commercial grants, historic preservation and affordable housing development. Living in a redevelopment area? Ask the agency about grants before you sell or renovate.

Which office handles what

Building permits go through the city's online portal, and everything about assessment, taxes and recorded documents sits with Lee County. Match each question to the right office.

  • Open or expired building permits: check the city portal first, because buyers and title companies often ask.
  • Value, homestead and exemptions: the Lee County Property Appraiser, whose site has a parcel search and explains homestead and portability.
  • Deeds and recorded liens: the Lee County Clerk's Official Records search.
  • Tax bills: the Lee County tax collector, who can state what you owe.

Work done without a permit often comes out during inspection of an older house, most often roofs and electrical panels, and lenders and insurers may ask for proof. Settle it, or disclose it plainly, before anyone signs a contract.

Deed tax and the property tax calendar

The state's deed tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration (s. 201.02(1)(a)). All signers share liability, which is why the contract should say who will pay. The clerk's recording fee is added on a per-page basis under s. 28.24(13), with trust fund and technology add-ons, and your closing agent adds it all up.

Property tax keeps a separate schedule: value is set on January 1, an August notice shows proposed taxes, and the bill comes in November. The Lee County tax collector can give you the exact amount due at closing.

What happens to your homestead when you sell

The exemption stops on that parcel when you sell, and on the following January 1 the buyer's assessment is reset to full market-based value.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is lower, and the state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. That cushion stays with the old house. Part of it can follow you to a new Florida homestead set up within three years of the January 1 in the year you left, using DR-501T filed with DR-501 by March 1.

  • The homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000 and is filed on DR-501 by March 1.
  • Renting the home ends the exemption.
  • Portability is something to plan before you close, not after.

Inherited house or foreclosure

Florida law puts both situations on set timelines, and either can still end in a sale.

Small estates may use summary administration, a shorter court path under s. 735.201 that turns on the estate's size or the years since the death. Ask a probate attorney which route fits. Creditor deadlines under s. 733.702 run in the background.

Once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the clerk sets a public auction inside a fixed window (s. 45.031), and bidders have to put money down. A sale that closes first can end the case and preserve your equity. Afterward, ask the Lee County Clerk about surplus funds, since a homeowner may have a claim to money left after the lender is paid.

If a tenant lives there

A renter can stay through a sale unless the lease or the notice rules end the tenancy first. Section 83.57 sets the minimums: 30 days before the end of a monthly period, 60 days for year-to-year and 7 for week-to-week. A fixed lease generally goes along with the property.

Tell any cash buyer about the lease at the start. Some buyers insist on a vacant house, others will take it occupied. Keep the signed lease and rent records ready, and put any agreement with the tenant in plain written terms.

A cash sale from offer to keys

After acceptance, a title company hunts for liens, back taxes and open permits and requests a payoff from each lender. Next you sign the contract, and at closing the deed, with witnesses present. Payoffs, stamps and recording are subtracted from your proceeds, and you collect the rest. Get the closing date and cost split in writing, and rank offers by your net, not the headline price.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to have in hand before a buyer visits

Gather the recorded deed, any payoff letters, permit records and the newest tax bill. If tenants live there, add the lease and rent records. Collecting these early speeds the title search and keeps a buyer from reopening the price after learning about a gap. Mention anything you know is wrong with the house, since a cash buyer prices repairs in either way and a disclosed problem rarely ends a deal.

Before the first showing, walk the lot with a notebook. Write down roof age, air conditioner age, any past leaks and every repair you paid for. Buyers trust a seller who can answer those questions without hunting, and a short written list also helps you compare cash offers against what a listing might require you to fix.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Fort Myers buyer take my house with the repairs undone?

Yes, cash buyers regularly do. The price will reflect their repair bill, so get the number on paper and set it beside a listing estimate.

Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fort Myers deed?

All parties to the deed are liable regardless of who agrees to pay. The contract normally assigns the cost, and the closing agent collects at recording.

Does the Fort Myers owner-occupied rate affect my sale?

Only indirectly. With about 49.1 percent of units owner-occupied, many buyers are investors or landlords, and they tend to ask about rent rolls and lease terms.

What homestead deadline should I know after a sale?

Send DR-501, plus DR-501T if you are porting, to the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1. The new homestead has to be established within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old home.

Where do I confirm my current tax balance?

Ask the Lee County tax collector for the amount due through your closing date. Bills are mailed in November.

Selling a house in Deltona

Deltona is the largest municipality in Volusia County, sitting between Daytona Beach and Orlando, with an estimated population of 100,496. Buyers line them up side by side, and that makes condition the biggest price driver. When repairs are what stands between you and a sale, an as-is cash purchase is often the simplest route.

The sections below cover utility accounts, the county tax calendar, what the state charges on a deed, and how homestead savings can move with you.

Closing out water and city accounts

Deltona owns its water and wastewater system. The city bought it from Florida Water Services on November 7, 2003, so you close the account with the city and not with a private company.

A short list keeps loose ends from lingering after the deed records:

  • Ask the city utility for a final meter reading on your closing date.
  • Hand the buyer the account details so service moves over without a gap.
  • Confirm that no code or permit matter is open on the property.
  • Update your mailing address with the Volusia County Property Appraiser so later mail finds you.

Ask Building and Zoning Services about permits that were never finished. Those can hold up a buyer's title work, and they are simpler to close out now than mid-contract.

Volusia County tax dates and discounts

Volusia's tax collector opens collection on November 1 and expects payment in full by March 31. Whatever is left on April 1 goes delinquent. A tax certificate sale on those delinquent accounts starts on or before June 1, and a local newspaper carries the list of accounts in the weeks beforehand.

If one lump sum is hard, ask about the installment plan: four payments, due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with the application in before May 1. Homestead tax deferral requests are due by March 31. The Volusia County Tax Collector calendar has the current dates.

A sale during the year means the settlement statement splits that year's bill between you and the buyer. Have the title agent explain the division before closing day, not at the table.

Deed tax and recording charges

  • Recording is billed separately under section 28.24: a set amount for page one, a smaller one for every page after, and a few add-ons.
  • Some transfers owe nothing, for instance an estate representative's deed issued under a probated will, or a homestead deed between spouses when a mortgage is the only consideration.

Find the clause that assigns these charges before you sign anything. Buyers who promise a fast closing can normally say in advance who covers the stamps and the title policy.

List, sell as-is or find a rehab buyer?

Sellers in town usually choose among three routes.

  1. Listing the house gets the most eyes, along with showings, an appraisal and whatever conditions a lender attaches.
  2. Selling as-is for cash removes the loan and most repair haggling.
  3. A renovation buyer fits a house with roof, plumbing or electrical problems that would make a lender balk.

If a mortgage is attached, get the payoff figure in writing. Then ask every buyer what you would actually net once all costs come out. Foreclosure papers already on file change the clock. After final judgment the clerk schedules the auction 20 to 35 days out, unless the plaintiff consents to more time.

City departments worth a call before you list

The city runs from a City Manager's Office through Enforcement Services, Public Works and Utilities, and Fire and Rescue. Three of its offices matter to a seller.

  • Building and Zoning Services can look up open permits at your address.
  • Enforcement Services handles code matters, so ask whether anything is pending against the lot.
  • Public Works and Utilities is where the water account lives.

Because so many Deltona homes were built in the same wave, buyers tend to compare roof age, air conditioner age and windows when they bid. Having dates and invoices for those items on hand helps you hold your price.

Taking homestead savings to your next home

Moving to another Florida home? Portability lets part of your Save Our Homes benefit follow you. Set up the new homestead inside three years of that January 1, then send Form DR-501T with Form DR-501 by March 1. The new home's assessed value is reduced by whichever is smaller: $500,000, or the difference between just value and assessed value on the old home.

An amendment from 2026 first reaches the 2027 tax roll. Call the Volusia County Property Appraiser to learn which rules govern your year.

A house's first homestead year is assessed at just value. Growth after that is limited each year to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower. The cap history stays behind when you sell, so anyone who has owned in Deltona a long time should speak with the appraiser before closing.

How a cash sale runs, start to finish

The sequence is plain, even when the house is not. First you describe the property candidly: condition, any tenant, any lender. A written offer comes back. On acceptance, a title company opens a file and hunts for liens, back taxes and open permits. Next come the contract and, at closing, a deed signed before two witnesses. The agent pays off loans, collects the stamp tax and recording charges, and hands you the balance. No inspection-driven repair list and no lender appraisal sit in that chain, which is why dates are easier to promise.

Before you accept, check the offer for the closing date, who pays costs and what happens to belongings left behind. Walk away from anyone asking for money from you before closing.

What to have ready for the title agent

Most delays at closing come from missing paper. Gather your recorded deed, a lender payoff letter if you owe one, the newest tax bill and permit records for major repairs. Add the lease and deposit records when the house is rented. If an owner has died, expect the title company to ask who has authority to sign. Delivering all of this at the start lets the agent open the title search immediately, and the title search is what sets the speed of a cash sale.

Yes. Deltona is the largest municipality in Volusia County, with an estimated population of 100,496, and it sits between Daytona Beach and Orlando.

When did Deltona become a city?

December 31, 1995, after residents voted for incorporation that September. Earlier attempts in 1987 and 1990 failed.

The city itself, which took over the water and wastewater system on November 7, 2003. Request a final reading dated to your closing.

By what date must a Volusia tax bill be paid in full?

March 31. After that the bill is delinquent on April 1, and the certificate sale opens by June 1.

Yes, provided closing happens ahead of the clerk's auction, which follows final judgment by 20 to 35 days barring the plaintiff's consent to longer. Contact a buyer and a title company as soon as you are served.

Can a Plantation homeowner sell for cash on a short timeline?

Yes. With no mortgage involved, a cash purchase in Plantation moves at the speed of the title search, the payoffs and the deed signing. A traditional listing adds an appraisal, an inspection round and loan approval for the buyer.

Plantation sits in Broward County, directly west of Fort Lauderdale. The Broward County Property Appraiser has current values, since these numbers are old. Commuters bound for Fort Lauderdale, Miami or the port ask first about access to I-95, I-595 and I-75, so open with your commute when you talk to any buyer.

Think about what you need most: speed, price or certainty. A seller facing an estate, a move or a code problem often values a fixed closing date. A seller with a well-kept house and no deadline can test the market with an agent first and still keep a cash offer as a fallback.

  • Cash fits deferred repairs, code issues or a tenant in place.
  • A listing fits a house that shows well while demand is strong.
  • Estates and liens need paperwork under either path.

Why lot sizes vary across Plantation

Frederick Peters bought 10,000 acres along State Road 7 in the 1930s and hired architect Russell Pancoast to plan a city. The plan barred neighboring homes from looking alike, set minimum lot sizes and divided land into residential, commercial and industrial zones. His idea of long acres offered one-acre lots, with two thirds kept for gardens and fruit trees.

Plantation incorporated on April 30, 1953. Later annexations pushed the western edge out to Flamingo Road, roughly seven miles from State Road 7, so the west is newer than the east. A Plantation Acres lot looks nothing like a house out west. Tell buyers which side you are on, because lot size and building age differ across town and both move the price.

With heavy rain and heat, inspectors look hard at roofs, drainage and air conditioning. Pull together permits and service records before anyone visits.

Recreation and amenities that help a sale

Parks and golf help sell houses in Plantation. The city operates the Plantation Preserve Golf Course and Club, and newer parks include Plantation Woods in the historic district and Camp Everglades at Volunteer Park. The Helen B. Hoffman Plantation Library serves residents alongside the county's West Regional Library, and the city lists Nova Southeastern University, Florida Atlantic University, Broward College and McFatter Technical Center within a 10 minute drive.

Plantation Gateway, Plantation Midtown and Plantation Technology Park offer jobs close to home. The airport is 15 minutes away by the city's count, with Tri-Rail, Amtrak and county buses also in reach.

  • List the park or golf course closest to your address.
  • Name your school zone only after confirming it with the district.
  • Stay factual in your descriptions.

Closing charges on a Plantation deed

The deed stamp tax in Broward is the statewide 70 cents on every $100. Recording costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per added page. Because each party named on the deed can be held liable for the tax, the contract should say who pays it.

Have the title agent list every charge, payoffs included, before you commit to a closing date.

Expect the stamp tax, recording charges, payoffs, prorated taxes and any association fees to appear on one settlement statement. Broward's offices can quote the current millage for your address.

What if my house has a foreclosure, an estate or a tenant?

Any of the three can still end in a sale. The clerk sells a foreclosed house 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the date is pushed back, and the winning bidder puts down a 5 percent deposit. Estates worth $150,000 or less may use summary administration, and Florida's estate tax stopped applying to deaths after 2004. In a rental, unpaid rent starts with a three-day notice, and a monthly tenancy ends with 30 days' notice.

If the house is rented, tell the tenant in writing that a sale is under way, and keep showings to reasonable hours. The lease stays in force after the sale unless it ends on its own terms, so the buyer takes the house with the tenant in it. For an estate, the person with court authority signs, and the title agent will ask for that paperwork before setting a closing date. For a foreclosure, speed matters most: a buyer who can close before the auction date can pay the lender and leave you with whatever equity remains.

Talk to a Florida attorney before anyone signs a deed for an estate or for an owner in default.

Steps in a Plantation sale

  1. Gather payoff letters, tax bill and tenant information.
  2. Review written offers for the price, closing day and repair terms.
  3. The title agent clears the record.
  4. You sign the deed in front of two witnesses.
  5. Broward's clerk records it and funds are released.

Keep your recorded deed with your tax records. Ask each buyer when funds will be available, who orders the title policy and whether an inspection can change the offer. Houses in Plantation run from modest single-family homes to properties worth well over $1 million, so the pool of buyers and the paperwork shift with price. Owners of higher-value houses should raise payoffs, survey needs and association approvals with the title agent at the start.

Start with a short packet: your payoff letter, the latest tax bill, any survey you have, and a list of repairs or permits you know about. The title agent can open the file and order the record search the same day, which is what keeps a cash timeline short. Keep a copy of every page you sign.

Choosing cash means no repairs, no staging and no waiting on a buyer's bank. Lien payoffs, the tax proration and the signing remain, and they take a few days. With tenants in the house, pass the lease and deposit records to the buyer before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Which county records a Plantation deed?

Broward County, through its clerk.

Why do Plantation lot sizes vary so much?

A 1930s master plan set minimum lot sizes, and later annexation added western land out to Flamingo Road, so older and newer areas differ.

What does it cost to record a deed in Broward?

Recording is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, and the 70 cents per $100 stamp tax applies on top.

Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer?

No. The buyer is assessed at market value starting the next January 1.

Where can I find current home values?

The Broward County Property Appraiser. City figures from 2018 are background only.

Selling a Sunrise house quickly

Your options in Sunrise are an agent listing, a sale you run yourself, or a cash offer, and each one runs into the city's permit rules and Broward County's records. Sunrise is a planned city on the western edge of Broward County, with more than 98,000 residents and a lot of highway access, which buyers like to see in a listing.

Fast sales hinge on documents. Pull together the deed, any homeowners association papers, permit records and a recent tax bill, and you can answer a buyer's questions in a day instead of a week.

How Sunrise permitting works

Sunrise uses two tracks. Work that changes a building's footprint or exterior goes through Broward County and the city's Community Development Department. Smaller jobs go straight to the Building Division. Re-roofing, interior renovation, fencing, interior plumbing or electrical repairs and AC changeouts skip Planning and Development review.

Steps in a Sunrise permit application

2. File the applicationThe city issues a Control Number used for the whole approval
3. Correct plansApplicant is notified of corrections; Wednesday mornings are Professional Day
4. Receive the permitIssued after structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and fire approvals; fees due at submittal

The Building Division's number is (954) 572-2354, and applications can be filed electronically. If a previous owner added a room or screen enclosure, ask the division whether it was permitted and finaled.

Permit problems that slow a sale

Unfinished permits and unpermitted additions cause the most trouble, because they turn up in a buyer's title or inspection review.

  • Additions or garage conversions that changed the exterior, which need both county and city sign-off.
  • Roof, AC and plumbing work done by a contractor without a final inspection.
  • Fences and other work done without any permit.

If you find a gap, you can close it before listing or disclose it and let the price reflect it. A cash buyer will usually accept either, but get the terms in writing. Do not assume your own report is enough, since lenders and title companies pull their own records.

Broward County property taxes

The Broward property appraiser sets your home's value as of January 1, and bills come from the tax collector in November. A closing in the second half of the year means prorating the full-year bill. Selling ends your Save Our Homes cap, and on the following January 1 the buyer is assessed at just value.

The homestead exemption can remove up to $50,000 if the owner files by March 1 and had made the home a permanent residence by January 1. Owners 65 or older may qualify for an extra local exemption if the city or county has enacted one and income limits are met, so ask the Broward County property appraiser which apply to your address.

Paying in November earns the printed 4 percent discount, which drops one point each month through February.

Stamp tax and recording on a Sunrise deed

Deeds in Broward are taxed at the usual state rate, 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and Miami-Dade stands alone with a different structure. The clerk takes the tax when the deed is recorded, and everyone on the document is liable.

Under section 28.24 the clerk charges $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 afterward, plus extra per-page fees. Title insurance and lien payoffs come on top.

Before signing, ask any buyer for a written cost split covering stamp tax, title and recording, and whether the offer depends on an inspection.

Listing or cash offer?

Compare them on timeline, certainty and net proceeds. Listing puts the house in front of the most buyers, at the cost of showings, inspection haggling and the chance a loan falls through. Cash gives up some price in return for a faster close with fewer surprises.

  • Get every buyer's closing date in writing.
  • Ask what happens if their inspection finds permit gaps.
  • Settle who orders and pays for the title search.
  • Ask whether proof of funds is available on request.

A Sunrise home with a finished permit file, a clear tax picture and a deed ready to record is easy to price either way. With a mortgage on the house, get a payoff letter first. It shows the lowest offer you can afford to accept.

Documents to gather before you call buyers

Sellers who show up with paper get better, faster offers. A short folder is enough, and most of it is already in your files.

  • The recorded deed and any survey.
  • Your latest Broward County tax bill and proof of any exemption.
  • Permit records for the roof, AC, plumbing, additions and fences, with final inspection dates.
  • Homeowners association rules, fees and contact details, if there is an association.
  • A payoff letter for each mortgage or lien.

If a permit is missing, call the Building Division before you list. Staff can tell you whether it was never filed, filed but not finaled, or sent to the county first because the work changed the exterior. Knowing which one it is lets you pick between closing the gap and pricing it in.

Pricing a house with permit gaps

A gap does not stop a sale, but it changes who will pay what you ask. Conventional buyers rely on lenders and title companies, and those pull their own permit records, so a gap that you skip mentioning will surface anyway. Cash buyers usually accept an open permit and take the cost off the offer.

When you compare offers, ask each buyer to say in writing how an open permit, an unpermitted fence or a garage conversion would affect the price and the closing date. That answer tells you whether it is cheaper to finish the paperwork yourself or sell as-is.

From signed contract to recorded deed

Once an offer is accepted, a title agent searches the records for mortgages, liens and unpaid taxes. Anything found is paid from your proceeds at closing. You sign the deed, the closing agent submits it to the Broward County clerk, and stamp tax and recording fees are collected at that moment.

  1. Order payoff letters for every loan or lien.
  2. Ask the tax collector about the balance and proration for the year.
  3. Finish or disclose any open permit.
  4. Request homeowners association documents if the home sits in a community with an association.

If the house is vacant, plan the key handoff and utility transfers for closing day. Ask the closing agent for a written settlement statement ahead of time, and read each line, including stamp tax, recording, title insurance and any tax proration, so that nothing at the table is a surprise. Keep a copy of the recorded deed once the clerk returns it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Sunrise have its own building division?

Yes. The City of Sunrise Building Division handles permits at (954) 572-2354. Work that changes a building's exterior or footprint also goes through Community Development, and larger jobs need Broward County approval first.

Is a permit required to replace a roof in Sunrise?

Yes, in most cases. Re-roofing goes straight to the Building Division. Confirm with the division before work begins and keep the final inspection record.

What if I find an open permit on my Sunrise house?

Either finish it with the Building Division before listing or disclose it and let the price reflect it. Cash buyers often accept open permits at a lower figure.

Is the documentary stamp rate different in Broward County?

No. Broward charges the usual 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and Miami-Dade is the sole exception.

Will my homestead exemption stay with the house?

No. Your buyer files a new application by March 1, and the sale resets the assessment to just value.

How quickly can a North Port house sell?

A cash sale can close in a few weeks, while a financed sale takes longer because of the appraisal and loan timeline. North Port covers 99.38 square miles of land, so lots, wells, septic tanks and utilities vary from street to street more than they would in a compact city.

Growth has been quick. About 96,551 residents live here as of July 2025, up 28.7 percent from April 2020, and people 65 and over make up 27.7 percent of the population. Retirees and move-up households are a big part of the buyer pool, which should shape how you present the home.

  • Cash buyer: fast, flexible dates, house taken as is.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus showings and a lender timeline.
  • Owner sale: no commission, more paperwork on you.

Platted lots and what they mean for a sale

North Port was platted by a land developer instead of growing around a downtown. General Development Corporation began in the mid-1950s, sold lots on terms of $10 down and $10 a month, and ultimately platted about 70,000 lots, nearly all meant for single-family homes. The first 5.5 square miles were incorporated as the City of North Port Charlotte in June 1959, and annexations pushed the area past 100 square miles within about eighteen months.

The result is tens of thousands of individually owned lots joined by roads, swales and canals. Lot size and position vary widely, and many homes in the older platted areas were built on wells and septic systems, because the company's water and sewer service covered only a core area. The city acquired that utility after the company's bankruptcy.

Does my North Port house have city sewer or a septic tank?

It depends on where the lot is, and buyers and their lenders will ask. The original developer built water and wastewater service for a core area only, so much of the platted land relies on individual wells and septic tanks. The city has produced utility master plans since 1992 and is working through a long program to move platted areas to central service.

The first planned area is Blue Ridge-Salford North, with 1,583 properties and an estimated 12 to 15 years to finish. Commissioners approved early incentive maximums of $4,045 for wastewater and $6,655 for combined water and wastewater, a 30-year payment plan and a hardship program. Without incentives the cost could reach $35,000. Those are planning figures, so call North Port Utilities to learn whether your street is in a planned area and what a connection would cost.

  • Ask the utility whether the address has central water, sewer, or both.
  • For a well or septic system, contact the Sarasota County Health Department about permits and service history.
  • Keep pump-out and repair receipts for the buyer.

A buyer who sees a septic system may ask for an inspection. You can order one first or accept a lower offer that prices in the unknowns.

Sarasota County tax and closing costs

North Port sits in Sarasota County, which follows the standard Florida deed stamp rate. Every county but Miami-Dade charges 70 cents per $100 of consideration or portion thereof, and all parties to the deed are liable whichever side the contract says will pay. The clerk collects it at recording, along with a separate per-page recording charge set by statute.

The Sarasota County Property Appraiser lists the ways a homestead can be lost, and several matter at a sale. Renting the property on January 1, or renting it for more than 30 days a year in two consecutive years, can end the exemption. A divorcing couple that still owns the home jointly can lose 50 percent of it. The buyer must file a new homestead application by March 1, as the state calendar on the Department of Revenue taxpayer page shows.

The Save Our Homes cap holds back a homestead's yearly rise in assessed value, but a transfer of title resets it to just value, so the buyer's bill will likely run higher than yours.

Permits and approvals

A sale needs no permit of its own, but open or expired permits can hold up a closing, so check first. Think through work done on the house: a pool cage, a garage conversion, a new roof, a fence or a shed. If a contractor left a permit open, the building division can say which inspection is missing.

  • Search the address for open permits and unfinished inspections.
  • Confirm any well or septic permit with the Sarasota County Department of Health.
  • Check zoning if the property is a vacant lot.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Port houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited houses and empty lots

An heir can sell once the personal representative or successor holds authority to sign, and the title company will want to see it. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's no-tax list, while other deeds, quitclaims included, are taxable.

Many North Port owners hold an unbuilt lot. A lot sale uses the same deed, title search and recording as a house, and a buyer will ask about utility access, flood zone and whether the plat allows the planned use. Taxes are billed on a lot with no house, so get the balance from the Sarasota County tax office before you name a price.

Signing with two witnesses is required, and audio-video witnessing is allowed, which helps when heirs live far away.

What happens between offer and closing?

After you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens and unpaid taxes and the buyer's side arranges any inspection. Have your payoff letter, latest tax bill and utility information ready, including whether the house runs on a well or septic tank. If the house is financed by the buyer, expect an appraisal. A cash purchase skips it. Closing means signing the deed before two witnesses and having the clerk record it and collect the stamp tax. Agree in the contract on who pays for any repairs the inspection finds, and confirm the day you hand over keys. If you are selling a lot, bring any survey you have and the latest tax bill so the buyer can check boundaries and what is owed.

Frequently asked questions

Does North Port have sewer for every home?

No. The developer built central service only for a core area, and much of the platted land uses wells and septic tanks. Call North Port Utilities to learn about your address.

How much is deed stamp tax in Sarasota County?

It is 70 cents per $100, the rate for every county except Miami-Dade. All parties to the deed are liable, and the clerk collects it at recording.

Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?

The exemption stays with you as a person, not with the house. You may be able to move your Save Our Homes savings through portability if you buy another Florida homestead within three years, and you must file a new application for the new home.

Will a buyer care that my house is on septic?

Yes, many buyers and lenders ask about it. Keep service records and consider an inspection before listing so a surprise does not cut your price.

Can I sell an empty lot in North Port quickly?

A lot can sell, but buyers check access, utilities and zoning, and many want a survey. Ask the county for any tax balance before you accept an offer.

Selling in Deerfield Beach?

Picking a route out of a Deerfield Beach house

Choose a route first, then collect what any buyer will ask for: the deed, permit records, the latest tax bill and association paperwork. Cash purchases tend to close soonest, since no lender underwriting sits between signature and closing.

Deerfield Beach is a coastal city in Broward County, and its strategic plan describes housing that ranges from beachfront properties and upscale communities to affordable, family-friendly neighborhoods. Your sale may involve a condo board, an HOA or neither, and that shapes the timeline more than most things.

  • Agent listing: the broadest reach, with showings and financed buyers.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you run the contract, disclosures and closing.
  • Cash offer: the house goes as-is, which fits inherited, empty, rented or run-down properties.

The city and its plans

Deerfield Beach became a city on June 11, 1925. Its 2023 strategic plan lists a land area of 16.22 square miles and a population of 87,414, plus a 5,700-foot public beach and 1,377.68 acres of parks and open space.

The plan sets out priorities that may matter near your property: redevelopment of the City Hall and downtown campus and of central areas, an update of the Comprehensive Plan and the Land Development Code, and a development agreement for 1045 SW 11 Way. In the plan's resident survey of 206 respondents, 63% said the city is improving as a place to live. If your street is close to a redevelopment area, ask city planning staff for the current status before a buyer asks you.

Permits and condo work

Florida Building Code permits run through an online system, and new applications and plans have gone in electronically since December 15, 2025. The Building Division is at 150 NE 2nd Avenue, open 7:30 am to 4:30 pm, phone 954-250-4060.

  • Inspections are requested online, and a request in by 3:00 PM gets next-business-day service.
  • Every residential permit needs an HOA affidavit.
  • Permit payments over $10,000 are made in person at the city cashier.
  • Online card or bank payments carry a separate transaction fee.

Condo owners get a specific warning on the city's page: the building code does not let a condo owner do the work personally. A permit and a contractor with the proper state credentials are required for items such as water heaters, air conditioner replacements, kitchen and bathroom renovations, windows and doors, hurricane shutters and balcony enclosures. The page adds that hiring an unlicensed contractor is a felony under section 489.127(1)(f).

Unpermitted work on a condo can resurface in an inspection or an insurance review. Collect permits and final inspection records before you list.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Deerfield Beach house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Vacation rental registration

A vacation rental is allowed only with registration. Section 98-106 of the Land Development Code makes it unlawful to operate one without it, and registration must be renewed every year by October 1.

Deerfield Beach vacation rental registration terms
RequirementTerm
Renewal dateAnnually, by October 1
Changes to registration detailsReport within 30 days
InspectionsAllowed on reasonable notice
First-offense fineUp to $250 per day

Registrants confirm that every city, county and state registration is current, attach the business tax receipt and confirm that the Deerfield Beach address is the one used for casualty insurance. If the house you are selling was used this way, make sure the registration is current, because a lapse can affect what the buyer is allowed to do with the property.

How the Broward tax bill reaches an owner

Broward County sets values and mails the bill. Value is fixed on January 1, a notice of proposed taxes lands in August, and the bill itself arrives in November.

Exemption applications are due March 1. Homestead reaches $50,000, and the first $25,000 also counts against school taxes. Discounts for early payment slide from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February, and April 1 starts delinquency.

A sale ends the Save Our Homes limit on yearly increases, so the buyer is assessed at just value from the next January 1. If you are moving within Florida, you may be able to carry some of your savings to a new homestead set up within the portability window.

The deed step

The clerk records the deed and collects documentary stamp tax under section 201.02. Under the revenue department's rules every party is liable, so your contract decides who pays.

Recording charges follow section 28.24 and are billed per page. Spousal homestead deeds and divorce deeds for the marital home have listed exemptions, so ask your title agent whether either fits.

A taxable deed is also a change of ownership. Even a quitclaim to a relative resets the property to just value, unless an exception such as a spousal transfer applies.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Deerfield Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited, in default or tenant-occupied

No one can sign a deed for an inherited house until the court grants authority. A shortened process called summary administration fits estates under a $150,000 non-exempt ceiling or a death more than two years back, and creditor claims close on a schedule tied to publication or service.

Once a lender has sued, the judgment sets a sale a few weeks out and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A seller who closes first can repay the loan and keep any surplus.

With a tenant in place, unpaid rent calls for a three-day written notice, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. After judgment, only the sheriff carries out removal.

Getting ready to list

Start a folder for the deed, the latest tax bill, permit and final inspection records, your insurance declarations and any HOA or condo documents with a current balance statement. Photograph the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanical systems, and write down the dates of repairs. When offers come in, compare the net amount, the time to close and the chance the buyer backs out, and ask each buyer in writing who pays for title and recording.

On closing day, bring photo ID and keys. The title company will show you the settlement statement, and your lender is repaid from the proceeds before the balance is sent to you. Keep copies of everything you sign.

Before any showing, clear the clutter and fix the small things a buyer will notice first, like dripping faucets and sticking doors. If a buyer's inspector turns up a problem, you can fix it, adjust the price or walk away, so think ahead about which of those you would choose. A written list of repairs you have already made helps the conversation stay factual, and it gives your title agent and any lender a clear picture of the house as it stands today.

Frequently asked questions

Does condo work in Deerfield Beach need a permit?

For most work, yes. The city names water heaters, air conditioner replacement, windows and balcony enclosures as permit items needing a contractor with the right state credentials, and it lists interior painting and new floor coverings as exceptions.

How do I submit a Deerfield Beach permit application?

Online, since December 15, 2025, with in-person applications still accepted at the Building Division in City Hall. Call 954-250-4060 for help.

What fines apply to unregistered vacation rentals in Deerfield Beach?

The city's renewal affidavit lists fines up to $250 per day for a first offense and $500 for repeat offenses, and registration can be revoked.

When are Broward property taxes delinquent?

April 1. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1, so settle any balance before or at closing.

What does recording a Deerfield Beach deed involve?

The state taxes the consideration under section 201.02, and clerk recording charges are billed by the page under section 28.24.

Who handles what in a Daytona Beach sale

County government covers Daytona Beach for property values, tax bills and deed recording. The city itself issues permits, runs rental registration and enforces codes. Sorting out which desk keeps which record will save you many calls.

The house itself points to a route. A well-kept home near the water may do well listed, but a rental, an estate property or a place with heavy repairs is more likely to suit a direct purchase as-is.

  • An agent fits a house that shows well when waiting on a financed buyer is acceptable.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale works for people who handle contracts and disclosure forms without stress.
  • Cash makes sense when time, condition or tenants stand in the way.

Rental registration

Daytona Beach landlords do have to register. The City Commission dropped the old Residential License Program in 2024 and put in a rental registration rule for owners holding fewer than five units. It renews every year and covers long-term rentals, meaning leases of six months plus one day or more.

A voluntary inspection is available, and passing it waives the following year's fee. If you want stays shorter than six months plus one day, phone the Business Tax Office at (386) 671-8140 to learn whether your zoning allows it. The Rental Property Program office is at 125 S. Palmetto Ave.

Selling a rental? Renew the registration first, since a buyer or title agent may want to see it. Note that the program covers long-term leases only, so short stays need zoning confirmation of their own.

Volusia County tax dates

Around November 1 the Volusia tax collector mails bills. You can pay without penalty until March 31.

  • The discount is 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and nothing in March.
  • March 31 is also the deferral application deadline.
  • Accounts turn delinquent April 1, when a minimum 3 percent charge is added.
  • A new installment plan has to be requested by April 30.

After April 30, unpaid accounts are advertised and head toward the yearly certificate sale. The certificate becomes a first lien and, two years on, supports a tax deed application, so pay off any balance by closing day.

The appraiser's exemption deadline is March 1, as elsewhere in the state. Homestead can lower assessed value by up to $50,000.

Permits and code cases

A permit left open, or a pending code case, will probably appear when a buyer does due diligence. City Code Compliance staff look for blighted or substandard housing and push for its repair or removal.

Pull the permit history for your address before you list. Anything done without a final sign-off, whether a new roof, a new room or electrical or plumbing changes, should be cleaned up first. Cash buyers accept the house's flaws, yet the title company still wants liens and open cases paid or accounted for.

Ask the city for any unpaid code charges when you collect payoff figures. They can stay with the parcel and appear in a title search.

Selling with taxes owed

Volusia County runs notices on delinquent accounts three times, in the newspaper and online, after April 30. The advertising and auction listing fees are tacked onto the tax notice, and they cannot be removed after it runs, which is a reason to pay before the deadline.

A bill still open at the annual certificate sale leads the county to sell a certificate against the parcel, and further charges pile up. Redeeming takes guaranteed funds, though the collector also accepts credit or debit cards.

Under state law, the certificate holder can pursue a tax deed once two years have run from April 1 of the issue year. On a homestead, the opening bid counts half the latest assessed value. With a certificate outstanding, ask the tax collector for the redemption total and plan to pay it out of your proceeds.

Deferral works differently. By March 31, homestead owners may submit Form DR-570 to the collector, postponing the tax that exceeds a set share of household income.

Deed tax in Volusia County

When the deed is recorded, the clerk's office takes the tax. It is priced per $100 of consideration under section 201.02, and the state revenue page lists county rates, with Miami-Dade the odd one out.

State rules make everyone on the deed liable, which leaves the contract to decide who actually pays. Section 28.24 recording charges are billed page by page.

Whether it is a warranty, special warranty, quitclaim or trustee's deed, the tax applies. Any such transfer also resets assessed value to just value on the next New Year's Day.

Foreclosure, probate and tenants

Three deadlines come up most often: foreclosure sales, probate and tenant notices.

After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk's sale is set about three to five weeks away, and the high bidder puts down 5 percent. Objections to the bid must come within 10 days.

Probate is the first step for an inherited house. A summary administration is possible if non-exempt assets are $150,000 or under, or the owner died over two years earlier. Creditors who miss the claim deadline lose their claims.

A tenant behind on rent receives a written notice allowing three days. Once the court orders removal, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice. When the house is under lease at sale, record in writing whether the buyer will keep the lease.

Steps from offer to closing

After you accept an offer, a title company examines the record, clears liens and drafts the deed. On your side, collect the lender's payoff letter, your most recent tax bill and any association paperwork. Put in writing who covers the title policy and recording. Weigh each offer against the net an agent listing would leave once repairs, fees and holding costs come out.

Before the signing appointment, read the settlement statement closely, confirm where your proceeds will be sent, and bring photo ID. Hand over keys, garage openers and any gate codes at closing, and keep copies of everything you sign. Do not cancel your homeowner's insurance until the deed is recorded.

If anything in the file is unclear, such as a name that differs between the deed and your tax bill, ask the title agent about it early. Fixing a mismatch before contract is far easier than during a title review, and it keeps a short timeline from slipping. Ask for your closing figures a day ahead so you are not reading them for the first time at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Is rental registration required in Daytona Beach?

Yes, for owners of fewer than five residential units under the 2024 ordinance. The yearly fee is $75 per unit after the first year, and passing a voluntary inspection waives the following year's fee.

When do Volusia County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. A 3 percent minimum charge is added then, and accounts unpaid after April 30 are advertised and can go to the certificate sale.

Can I sell a Daytona Beach house with an unregistered rental?

You can, though registering first is wise. Buyers and title agents may want proof the rental complies.

Who collects the deed tax on a Daytona Beach sale?

The county clerk collects it at recording. Section 201.02 sets it per $100 of consideration, and your sale contract says which side pays.

Does selling end my homestead protection?

Yes. The Save Our Homes cap ends at a change of ownership, and the buyer starts at just value the next January 1. If you are buying another Florida home, the Volusia County Property Appraiser can explain portability.

Melbourne in Brevard County

Melbourne is in southern Brevard County, southeast of Orlando on the east coast, and it straddles the Indian River Lagoon. Most of the city lies on the mainland, while a smaller piece sits on a barrier island across the water, so sellers here hold two very different kinds of property under one city name. The city measures 51.59 square miles, or 33,016.28 acres, as of March 2026, and its 2025 population was 88,499.

  • Get the premium history from your insurer; buyers weigh it.
  • Confirm the parcel is inside city limits before you quote city rules to a buyer.

Permits and a quick sale

A buyer's inspector or lender will ask whether past work was permitted. The city's building section requires permits for many jobs people overlook: carports, garages, fences, sheds, re-roofing, window and door replacement, A/C change-outs, electrical, plumbing, gas piping and generators.

Starting work without a permit can bring a penalty of 100 percent of the usual permit fee, and structures built without one may end up removed. Structures also have to respect setbacks and stay out of easements, and a variance request goes through the Community Development Department.

A residential permit typically takes 5 to 7 working days for approval or a response on a single review. If you are fixing something to satisfy a buyer, count that time in. Owner-builder permits are only available when the property is not for sale or lease for a period of one year, so a house headed to market generally needs a contractor for permitted repairs.

What a Melbourne permit application needs

The online system asks for drawings where they apply, a survey for any new construction or addition, proof of ownership in the form of a deed or tax statement, a description of the work and an estimated construction value.

Permits run on a clock. An application or issued permit goes inactive after 180 days without activity, with another 180 days to reinstate by uploading a letter that gives the permit number, address, reason for inactivity and an expected completion date.

Brevard property tax dates

Brevard's property appraiser assesses the parcel, while the tax collector mails the bill. Florida runs one yearly schedule in every county.

  • January 1: the value is fixed for the year.
  • March 1: last day to file for exemptions.
  • August: the proposed tax notice arrives.
  • November: bills go out with a 4 percent early-pay discount.
  • April 1: unpaid bills turn delinquent.

Have the closing agent prorate the year's bill between both parties, and keep the receipt. Request the unpaid balance, if any, from the Brevard tax collector before agreeing to a closing date.

What happens to my homestead benefits if I sell?

They end on that parcel. The $50,000 exemption ceiling stops applying, and the cap that held your assessed value below market lapses for the next owner, whose bill is based on full just value after the following January 1.

You may be able to carry your cap to a new Florida home. The new homestead must be set up within three years counted from the start of the year in which you left the old home, and the portability form is filed with the homestead application by March 1. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025.

Deed stamps and recording costs

Brevard uses the standard Florida deed stamp, 70 cents per hundred dollars of price. The clerk collects the tax at recording, and each signer of the deed shares liability for it.

Recording is priced per page under section 28.24, and the clerk adds trust fund and technology charges. Quit claim, warranty and life estate deeds are taxable, and a deed from an estate's court-appointed representative is not.

Tenants, probate and foreclosure

Each situation changes the schedule, not the ability to sell. A tenant on a month-to-month lease needs a 30-day notice, and a nonpayment notice runs 3 days excluding weekends and court holidays.

An heir needs authority from the court before signing. Estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt assets, or a death more than two years back, can use summary administration. Florida levies no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004.

In a foreclosure, the court sale is set for a date 20 to 35 days past the final judgment unless the lender agrees to a later date.

Other Melbourne rules that can trip up a seller

Permitted work also covers driveways, parking lots, roofing, irrigation systems, tree removal, signs and land-disturbing activity. If you paved, trimmed or replaced anything major, look for the paperwork.

Plans must be signed and sealed when residential work attaches to the main structure, includes an in-ground pool or has to meet wind load rules, such as a flag pole, satellite dish, aluminum construction or solar panels. Keep copies for the buyer's side.

Contractors applying for permits must show state certification or registration, a Brevard County competency card where required, and proof of workers' compensation coverage or an exemption affidavit. If you hire help to close out a permit, check those credentials.

How to weigh a cash offer

Put the written cash figure beside what a listing would leave you after commission, repairs and the months of carrying costs. Then read the contract for who pays the deed stamp, the title policy and recording.

Skip any buyer who asks for a fee up front. Get the settlement date and the closing agent's name in writing, and ask whether the buyer expects you to finish any open permits before closing. Compare two or three written offers if you can, because terms differ as much as price.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

From offer to closing in Melbourne

A cash sale follows a short path: written offer, signed contract, title search, settlement statement and a signing in front of two witnesses. The title company looks for mortgages, liens, unpaid taxes and open permits tied to the parcel, so clear what you can before the contract date.

Bring photo ID, your payoff letter, your latest tax bill and any permit papers. If the house sits on the barrier island side, also bring flood and wind insurance details. A buyer's agent or lender will ask for them early, and having them ready avoids a late scramble.

After the deed is recorded, the closing agent pays off the lender and sends you the balance. Book final utility readings for the closing day and hand over keys and any warranty papers.

Frequently asked questions

Is Melbourne, FL in Brevard County?

Yes. It is in southern Brevard County on Florida's east coast, southeast of Orlando, on both sides of the Indian River Lagoon.

What is Melbourne's population?

88,499 residents for 2025.

Can I get an owner-builder permit if I plan to sell?

Generally no. The property must not be for sale or lease for a period of one year to qualify, so a listed house usually needs a contractor.

How long does a Melbourne residential permit take?

Residential permits typically average 5 to 7 working days for approval or a response on a single review, and some issue within 3 days.

What deed stamp rate applies in Brevard County?

70 cents per $100, the standard rate for every Florida county except Miami-Dade.

What is the fastest path to a closing in Homestead?

Choose how you will sell, get title and lien paperwork in order, and sign a deed that is witnessed, taxed and recorded in Miami-Dade County. The buyer and the state of your title set the pace, since no one gets to skip recording.

Sellers in South Dade tend to weigh three routes. Listing publicly reaches the most people yet depends on a lender's appraisal. A cash purchase drops the lender and often the repair negotiation, a good fit for a house needing work. Selling to family is permitted, but a transfer for money still owes deed tax, and estate-planning transfers have no separate exemption.

  • Check who is on title, including any owner who has died or moved away.

Housing in Homestead

Buyers here skew young and family-oriented, and renting is common. Population rose from 60,512 in 2010 to 80,737 in 2020, with 86,242 estimated for mid-2025. Only 48.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, which lets rentals edge ahead. A typical owner-occupied house is worth $380,000, and the middle rent is $1,674. Households average 3.21 people. About 68.8 percent of residents use another language at home, so bilingual listings and documents can help.

The city took a direct hit from Hurricane Andrew in 1992, so keep permit history and insurance claim paperwork on hand for the buyer and the title company. Recent public projects include a voter-approved downtown revitalization in 2014, the reopened Seminole Theatre in 2015, a new City Hall in 2016 and the Cybrarium library in 2021, while the Speedway and the air force base, reestablished in 1953, remain big local anchors. Homestead also has designated historic districts and a historic downtown, which means a call to the city comes first if an older building is to be altered.

Selling a former or current rental

Many sellers in Homestead are landlords or heirs who never lived in the house, which shapes both the tax story and what buyers ask.

The county appraiser cautions owners against jeopardizing a homestead exemption by renting the property. An exemption claimed during a rental period can lead to back taxes covering ten years, plus 15 percent annual interest and a 50 percent penalty. Talk to a Florida attorney before you sell.

With a tenant in place, put the lease in the buyer's hands early. Chapter 83 sets 30 days of notice for a tenancy by the month, and an unpaid-rent demand lasts three days, not counting weekends and court holidays.

Deed tax and who must sign

A Homestead deed is taxed under Miami-Dade's own schedule. The base is 60 cents on each $100, and a 45 cent surtax on each $100 sits on top, except when the document conveys nothing but a single-family dwelling. Seventy cents is the figure in every other county.

Because of that exception, the kind of property matters. A single-family house generally avoids the surtax, but a duplex does not qualify. Let your closing agent confirm which treatment applies.

The contract may assign the tax to one side, yet everyone who signs stays liable for it, and the clerk is paid when the deed is filed. Recording starts at $5.00 for page one under section 28.24. The deed itself must be written and have two subscribing witnesses, who may appear by audio-video.

Homestead exemption after a sale

Your exemption stops at closing. Each new owner files alone, and the filing date is March 1. The TRIM notice shows how long late filings are taken, typically until 25 days after it is mailed, and a petition to the Value Adjustment Board may carry a $15 fee.

A ballot measure, Amendment 3, was approved November 3, 2026. If a buyer set up Florida residency by December 31, 2026, the largest non-school exemption becomes $150,000 for tax year 2027, then $250,000 for 2028. People who arrive later follow separate rules, and the school-board piece remains $25,000. The appraiser can say how it affects your buyer.

The first January 1 after closing, the parcel is reassessed at just value, which can make the buyer's opening bill larger than yours. Growth from there is held to the lesser of 3 percent or the CPI change.
