  • Tax certificates: an unredeemed certificate lets its holder ask for a tax deed after two years, counted from April 1 of the issue year. Pay off old balances first.

Florida has no estate tax on a death after 2004.

A checklist for landlords and heirs

Inherited the house, or renting it out? Title comes first. See who is named on the deed, and if an owner has died, learn who may sign for the estate. Next, pull together each lease, rent record and tenant phone number, which any serious buyer will request. Then ask the county Property Appraiser whether a homestead exemption stayed in place during any rental period, since that is where back taxes can arise.

Once you have those answers, line up offers by what you would net. Offers differ in how much time they need. One buyer may keep your tenants and move fast, another may want the keys free and clear. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it sits can spare you repair bills and a lender's schedule.

What a cash sale skips in Homestead

Without a lender, a South Dade cash deal avoids an underwriter's calendar and a bank's repair list. Owners usually notice three differences: fewer showings, less haggling over the inspection report, and a closing day set by agreement. Title work, payoffs and recording stay the same, and so does the deed tax.

Houses with an aging roof, storm damage, tenants or a stalled estate often suit that route. Weigh any cash figure against a listing's likely net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs, and obtain proof of funds and written terms before signing.

From accepted offer to recorded deed

After acceptance the closing agent opens title work and requests a payoff figure from each lender. The agent checks the tax bill for unpaid earlier years, drafts the deed and schedules the two witnesses. Any balance owed to the tax collector comes out of your proceeds at the table.

The deed is recorded at the clerk's office, which also takes the stamp tax. Speed turns on the clerk's queue and on whether your agent files electronically. Title cleanup and recording take time even in a cash sale, so settle on a written timeline before naming a closing day.

Is the deed tax different in Homestead?

It is, since Miami-Dade runs its own schedule. A 45 cent surtax on top of the base rate is skipped when the deed moves only a single-family dwelling.

Can I sell a Homestead house with a tenant inside?

Yes. The buyer steps into the lease, so share it early. Ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days' statutory notice.

Does the buyer get my exemption?

No. The buyer files separately by March 1, and value resets on the change of ownership.

How are unpaid property taxes handled?

They come out of your proceeds at closing. Get the exact balance from the county tax collector, since an unpaid bill turns delinquent April 1.

How long does the deed take to record?

The clerk's office records it and collects the stamp tax. Timing depends on the clerk's queue and on electronic filing by your closing agent.

Kissimmee houses by age

Kissimmee began as Allendale, a small trading post on the north shore of Lake Tohopekaliga, and it is now the Osceola County seat. In 1881 a Philadelphia saw manufacturer, Hamilton Disston, contracted to drain the surrounding land and deepen the Kissimmee River after buying four million acres for $1 million. Growth came in bursts. After Walt Disney World opened in 1971, the city went from 7,500 residents to 15,000 by 1980 and then to 30,000 by 1990. Retirees arrived in the 1950s, and an airport built in the 1940s lifted the population by 38 percent.

The result is a mix of ages on one street. A house from the 1950s ages differently from one built in the 1990s, so write down your build year, roof age and the date of the last wiring and plumbing work before offers arrive.

Code enforcement before a sale

Kissimmee's code enforcement division handles over 5,000 cases a year. The city holds the property owner answerable even when a tenant caused the problem, so settle anything open before a buyer looks.

Typical violations: grass taller than 12 inches on an improved lot, vegetation above 18 inches on an unimproved lot, junk and trash, inoperable vehicles outside a garage, and cars on the lawn past two spaces beside the driveway. Cases left unresolved can reach the special magistrate, who sits in public on the second Monday of each month. When the city performs the corrective work, you receive the bill, and a lien may be recorded if it goes unpaid.

Work cannot begin until a building permit is issued and displayed so it can be seen from the road. If you began a repair, finish it or close out the permit. Anyone renting a short-term dwelling in the city needs a business tax receipt from both Osceola County and the city, renewed each year by September 30, so a vacation rental house should have that paperwork current.

A residential pool needs a barrier at least 48 inches tall with no gaps a small child could squeeze through, and address numbers must be at least three inches high. Both are quick fixes worth doing before photographs.

  • Mow and clear debris.
  • Move inoperable vehicles into a garage.
  • Close out open permits.
  • Pull your business tax receipts if the house is rented short term.

How Osceola County bills and collects property tax

Osceola's tax collector opens collection each November 1, with the gross figure due the following March 31.

Early-payment discounts, Osceola tax collector
Month paidDiscount

December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount

Delinquency starts April 1, when 3 percent is added to the gross amount. With an escrowed loan, the lender requests the bill and you get a copy.

Certificates are sold online by June 1. A certificate is a first-priority lien, not a sale of the land. If one stays unredeemed for two years, the holder may begin a tax deed application, and the clerk then lists the parcel for an online auction. Redeeming on or after June 1 adds a $6.25 fee to the payoff. Value and homestead filings come from the county property appraiser's office, 2505 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway in Kissimmee.

What happens to your homestead and tax savings when you sell?

The exemption belongs to the owner rather than the house, so a sale ends it at that address.

Florida's homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of value. The first $25,000 applies to all taxing bodies and the second slice to non-school taxes only. Yearly assessment growth is capped at the smaller of 3 percent or inflation under Save Our Homes, which explains why a long-held house sits well below market. January 1 after the sale starts a fresh assessment at full just value.

If you buy again in Florida, portability can move part of the capped difference to the new home. You have three years, counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old homestead, and you file by March 1.

The deed, who signs it, and tenants

Deed tax here is the statewide 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, due to the clerk at recording.

The state treats every party to the deed as liable, which leaves the question of who pays to a private arrangement between buyer and seller. The clerk bills recording by the page, beginning at $5.00. Two witnesses are required, and remote video witnessing is allowed.

Tenants in place bring notice clocks: a month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' written notice, and a nonpayment notice runs 3 days with weekends and court holidays left out. If a foreclosure is pending, the clerk's auction is set 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff allows longer, so a sale ahead of that date is what protects your equity.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Kissimmee houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

From signed contract to closing

Once the contract is signed, the closing agent starts title work, requests a payoff letter from every lender and reviews the tax bill along with any open code or permit matters. The deed is prepared, signed before two witnesses and recorded by the clerk. Tax still unpaid for the year is divided between you and the buyer.

A cash buyer has no loan appraisal to wait on, so the schedule rests on title and recording. Get the timeline in writing before agreeing to a closing day, and keep your code enforcement and permit records close by in case the buyer's agent asks. If the house is a short-term rental, add the business tax receipts, and if it has tenants, add each lease and the notice dates.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Osceola County property appraiser's office?

Go to 2505 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Highway in Kissimmee. Record searches, sales transactions and map search are offered, and homestead filings are due there by March 1.

Does Kissimmee code enforcement follow a house after a sale?

Unresolved cases and recorded liens can remain on the parcel. Contact the city's code enforcement division for your address's status. A lien can be filed if the city performs work and the bill goes unpaid.

Does renting the house short term need city paperwork?

Yes. Anyone renting a short-term dwelling within city limits needs a business tax receipt from both Osceola County and the city, renewed each year by September 30. The building division can tell you what fits your address.

When does an Osceola tax certificate turn into a tax deed risk?

Two years after April 1 of the sale year, an unredeemed certificate's holder can apply. The clerk then sets an online auction. Paying off the certificate through the tax collector first ends it.

Can I sell if I inherited the house?

Yes, once someone holds authority to sign. Summary administration exists for small or older estates, and creditor claims end on a fixed schedule. A probate attorney can say which path fits.

Who holds your paperwork

Four offices each keep a piece of your file. The county Property Appraiser describes the parcel, the county Tax Collector sends the bill, the Clerk and Comptroller stores the recorded deed, and the city Building Department holds permits. Once an offer lands, knowing that split saves a lot of repeat phone calls.

You can list the house, sell it privately or deal directly with a cash buyer. A listing reaches the most people but comes with open houses and punch lists. A direct purchase gives up some price for fewer moving parts, and you name the closing date.

  • Print the parcel record before anyone tours the house.
  • Request old permit files and final inspections from the city.
  • Ask each lender for a written payoff figure.

An older city and what buyers check

Boynton Beach started as a small settlement and became the Town of Boynton on April 14, 1920. After a century of growth, you find mid-century blocks next to newer subdivisions, and buyers price the two very differently.

Older houses invite inspection requests. The city runs a permit history service with building plans, site plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for addresses inside city limits. If an earlier owner added a screen room, replaced a roof or changed an electrical panel, that file shows whether the job was closed out. An open permit is far easier to settle before you sign a contract than in the middle of a buyer's inspection period.

For the year a house was built, the city points people to the Property Appraiser, so a buyer's agent will probably look there first.

Can the new HB 803 permit exemption help before listing?

It may help, depending on the job. House Bill 803 took effect July 1, 2026 and created two permit exemptions for single family homes. Boynton Beach set up a request process in its online permitting portal.

The first exemption covers small jobs valued under $7,500. You send the Building Department a written request with a contract or other proof of the work's scope and value. Staff then issue a written determination or tell you to apply for a permit. Cutting one project into pieces to stay under the cap is not allowed.

The city is firm about the limits. Structural, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and gas work still needs a permit at any price, and so does any work on a property in a flood hazard area. Fences and driveways stay under the zoning code. The second exemption covers temporary flood panels or barriers put in by a state-certified contractor, and it also leaves out flood hazard areas. For both, the city says it owes no legal duty to owners or later buyers for exempted work.

  • Described as fine: interior trim, flooring, replacing cabinets, sinks and light fixtures, repairing drywall.
  • Described as still permitted: moving sinks or water heaters, tub to shower conversions, windows, doors, shutters, garage or patio conversions.

Exempt work gets no city inspection, so keep receipts and photos to hand to the buyer.

Common code violations to fix before photos

The city's list of repeat offenders is mostly cheap to correct before you take listing photos.

  • Grass taller than nine inches, or dead sod that has not been replaced.
  • House numbers missing from the building itself. They must be at least four inches tall and contrast with the wall.
  • Peeling paint, damaged fascia, loose awnings or broken screen enclosures.
  • Inoperable or unregistered vehicles, appliances and household items stored outside.
  • Construction debris over three cubic yards, which needs a special pickup from Public Works.

Boats and recreational vehicles may sit on a driveway, in a carport or in the rear yard if a resident owns them, they are registered, and no repair work lasts more than seven days. Nobody may live in a parked RV on private land unless zoning allows it.

Landlords should also know the city bars leasing any residential unit without a business tax receipt and a certificate of use and occupancy for that unit. If you are selling a rented house, confirm both were in place, since a buyer's lender or title agent may ask.

What is the Super Senior exemption?

Boynton Beach and Delray Beach are the only two cities named on the appraiser's exemption chart for a Super Senior exemption. It removes the city's own levies, not the county, school or other bills.

To qualify, an owner must meet the limited-income senior rules, have owned and lived in the home as a permanent residence for at least 25 years, and hold a property with market value under $250,000 at application. A long-time owner who has it should say so plainly to a buyer, because the benefit belongs to the owner and does not pass with the house.

The senior exemption also has a 2026 household income limit. Read it on the appraiser's site before you apply.

Signing the deed

Three statewide rules matter most. A conveyance of land needs a signed writing with two witnesses, and the witnessing may be done over audio-video link. The stamp tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars here, and everyone named on the deed answers for it. And the Clerk collects that tax when the deed is recorded, along with page-based fees under section 28.24.

Ask your closing agent for the draft settlement statement before signing day, since it should itemize all three. Using a quitclaim form does not avoid the tax when money or a mortgage is part of the deal.

Your tax bill and homestead after a sale

The closing agent settles the bill for the year of sale at the table and pays any open balance from your proceeds. The buyer's assessment returns to market value the January after closing.

The savings you built up under the cap follow you only if you file for portability when you claim a new Florida homestead. Renting out the home or moving away ends the exemption, so avoid placing a tenant while you wait to close. Owners with limited income may ask the Tax Collector about the deferral program, which uses Form DR-570.

Getting ready for closing

A short list keeps a quick sale from stalling. Confirm every owner on title can sign. Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any lease. Get payoff letters in writing. Ask the title agent how prorations will be handled. If a buyer's side asks for repairs, answer in writing and keep a copy. After closing, forward your mail and cancel services effective the day the deed is recorded, and keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I see what work was permitted on my Boynton Beach house?

The city's permit history service holds plans, applications, certificates of occupancy and elevation certificates for properties in city limits. Request your address file before you list, and use the Property Appraiser's record for the year built.

Do I need a permit to swap kitchen cabinets before a sale?

Often not, under the city's HB 803 guidance, if the job is under $7,500 and involves no plumbing, electrical, structural, mechanical or gas work. You must file a written exemption request, and flood hazard area properties are excluded.

Can a Boynton Beach landlord sell a rented house?

Yes, but confirm the city business tax receipt and certificate of use and occupancy were in place for the unit. A buyer or title agent may ask for them.

Does the Super Senior exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. It is tied to the owner's 25 years of residence and income filing, so the next owner starts fresh and is assessed at full value after the next January 1.

Who collects the deed stamp tax on a Boynton Beach sale?

The Palm Beach County Clerk collects it at recording, and the sales contract decides which side pays. Ask your closing agent to show the figure on the draft settlement statement.

Selling in Doral

Doral is a Miami-Dade city of roughly 15 square miles, home to approximately 81,182 residents and to more than 100,000 jobs. Its closeness to Miami International Airport keeps people looking for housing. Since you are in Miami-Dade, the county's own deed tax rate applies, and the county appraiser and tax collector handle your assessment and bill.

Plenty of Doral homes belong to a condominium, townhome or homeowners association, and the association can set the pace of a sale more than any buyer does.

  • Listing makes sense when you can sit through showings and wait on a buyer's loan.
  • An as-is cash sale fits a firm move date, a repair bill or a tax deadline.
  • Whichever you choose, reach out to the association first about transfer fees, estoppel letters and approvals.

Doral basics at a glance

Four edges frame the city: the Ronald Reagan Turnpike to the west, the Town of Medley to the north, the Palmetto Expressway to the east and the City of Sweetwater to the south. The airport is about a mile off and Downtown Miami about twelve miles. Commuters touring your house will care about that highway access, so say so.

Condo and townhome neighborhoods

The first neighborhoods, Doral Estates and then Doral Park, went up in the early 1980s. Newer building later spread to Downtown Doral, City Place Doral and Midtown Doral, where many units sit inside condominium or townhome associations. That arrangement changes what a closing looks like. A county building moratorium from 1983 to 1985 protected the well fields, and construction picked up sharply once it ended, so houses in a given neighborhood often share an age.

Ask the association for its estoppel letter early, since it shows what you owe and any fees due at transfer. Missing that letter is a common reason a closing slips by a week. Find out your association's transfer rules before you take an offer. If a board must vote, the buyer waits, and days can pile onto a closing that was supposed to be fast.

Miami-Dade deed tax

No other Florida county uses Miami-Dade's formula: 60 cents on each $100 of price, with a 45 cents per $100 surtax on top. A deed that moves only a single-family dwelling escapes the surtax. The wording stops at single-family homes, so a condo or townhome seller should ask the closing agent how the surtax is handled.

All parties on the deed can be held liable, regardless of which side the contract names as the payer. The clerk collects at recording. Recording itself costs extra under section 28.24, with a first-page amount, a lower amount for each additional page and per-page add-ons.

Property tax dates

November brings the bill, with a 4 percent early-payment discount that shrinks to 1 percent by February. April 1 is the day an unpaid bill turns delinquent, and tax certificates on those accounts are offered by June 1.

  • A TRIM notice from the property appraiser arrives each August. To contest value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • Form DR-501, the homestead application, is due March 1.
  • The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser's exemptions page explains exemptions, assessment reductions and land use classifications.

Ask the Miami-Dade Tax Collector for a payoff figure before you close. Also change your mailing address, or the next November bill may go to an empty house.

Weighing a quick sale against listing

Judge each option on net proceeds, speed and how sure the close is. A listing means showings plus a buyer who needs a loan. A cash buyer drops the loan, but association approval, stamp costs and the closing date still need answers. A simple order of work helps:

  1. Request a payoff statement from your mortgage lender.
  2. If an HOA exists, ask for an estoppel letter.
  3. Confirm whether the tax bill is paid.
  4. Collect each buyer's terms in writing.

If foreclosure is pending, the clerk holds the public sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer.

Checking the property record before you sell

Pull up your folio on the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser site. Owner names should match your deed, homestead should show if you live in the house, and the mailing address should be current.

  • Review the exemptions and assessment reductions listed for your parcel.
  • Ask the association whether any assessments are unpaid, because those can travel with the unit to closing.
  • If you did work on the house, check permits with Community Development.
  • Make sure the legal description on your deed lines up with the folio.

Note which municipality the record names, since that decides who answers permit and code questions. In Doral, that office is Community Development, one department alongside Public Works, Parks and Recreation, Finance and Police.

Carrying your Save Our Homes benefit

Buying another home in Florida? Portability can shift part of your capped benefit to the new homestead, as long as you set it up within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one. File Forms DR-501 and DR-501T with the property appraiser by March 1.

The state's cap chart, revised January 2026, prints 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. Renting the unit or moving out ends homestead, though section 196.061 lets a deployed servicemember rent without abandoning it. Condo owners heading to a different county should ask that county's appraiser how the benefit applies.

What a cash sale looks like from start to finish

Nothing exotic happens in a cash sale; only the lender is missing. An offer arrives in writing and you accept it. A title company searches the record and picks a closing date. Meanwhile you collect payoff letters, association paperwork and your latest tax bill. At the table you sign the deed with two witnesses watching, the agent pays stamp tax, recording fees and any loan, and the remainder is yours. Offers differ in more than price, so line them up side by side and ask each buyer what happens if the title search turns up a surprise. Insist that the closing date and who pays which cost are written down, and never send money or sign over title early.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork to gather first

A tidy folder saves more time than any negotiating trick. Bring your recorded deed, the legal description, the latest mortgage statement or a request for a payoff, and records for work done on the house. Add association contact details, any open violation notices, and leases with deposit records if someone rents the unit. If the owner has died, the title company will want to see who has authority to sign for the estate. Having everything in one place lets the title search begin the day you accept an offer.

Frequently asked questions

When was Doral incorporated?

January 28, 2003, making it one of thirty-four municipalities in Miami-Dade County.

How big is Doral?

The city covers about 15 square miles and has approximately 81,182 residents.

What is the deed tax in Miami-Dade?

The county charges 60 cents per $100 and adds a 45 cents per $100 surtax. A document that transfers only a single-family dwelling does not owe the surtax.

When do Miami-Dade tax bills go delinquent?

On April 1. The discount starts at 4 percent in November and falls to 1 percent in February.

Does Doral's building history matter to buyers?

It can. Building was frozen by the county from 1983 to 1985, and many neighborhoods began as Doral Estates and Doral Park, so nearby homes often share an age band.

Why architecture matters when selling in Miami Beach

The city treats many of its buildings as heritage, and that can limit what a buyer is allowed to change. Miami Beach has the world's largest collection of Art Deco structures, joined by Mediterranean Revival and Miami Modern, or MiMo, designs. The first tropical Art Deco buildings went up in 1933, a few years after the 1926 hurricane forced a round of rebuilding, and a preservation group formed in 1977 to protect the 1930s concentration in South Beach.

Not every block is covered, so the status of one house tells you little about the house two streets over. Find out early whether your lot sits inside a district or carries an individual designation. A buyer planning a renovation will ask, and an answer in hand shortens the negotiation.

Local historic districts

The Historic Preservation Board has designation reports for twenty districts and expansions. Several carry the names of familiar streets and neighborhoods.

Selected Miami Beach historic designation reports
DistrictReport year
Espanola Way1986
Ocean Drive Collins Avenue1986, expanded 1992
Flamingo Park1990, expanded 1992, 2008 and 2009

Individually designated sites include Old City Hall, the Venetian Causeway, the Miami Beach Woman's Club and the 28th Street Obelisk. The city's zoning map and the planning department can tell you which category a given address falls in.

Who approves changes to a historic property?

The seven-member Historic Preservation Board. Its charter powers include issuing or denying certificates of appropriateness, certificates to dig and certificates of appropriateness for demolition inside a district or on a designated site.

  • It reviews new construction, alterations and improvements to designated properties.
  • It prepares guidelines for each site or district that measure whether a proposed change fits.
  • It can recommend restoring property that was altered in violation of the rules.
  • It can grant variances from the land development regulations where hardship is shown.
  • It acts as the city's floodplain management board for applications within its jurisdiction.

The city charter bars weaker preservation standards than those in place on November 6, 2012 unless voters approve. A buyer who dreams of gutting a facade or tearing down a house needs the board's consent, and that uncertainty affects price.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Miami Beach house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Seawalls and the island's flooding risk

Seawalls are the island's first line of defense against tidal flooding, and the cost of upgrading them falls mostly on private owners. Miami Beach has roughly 55 miles of seawalls, with only about 5 miles publicly owned, so around 91% are private.

For a bayside owner the seawall is part of the property a buyer inspects. Inland owners feel the effects too, because bayside walls decide how far high tides reach into the streets.

  • A January 2021 ordinance requires new seawalls at an elevation of 5.7 feet NAVD 1988 and requires failing seawalls to be rebuilt to that minimum.
  • The city updated the ordinance on July 23, 2025 with revised definitions and construction standards for new and existing barriers.
  • Private owners may qualify for a matching grant for upgrades and for PACE financing through the city's Private Property Adaptation program.

What a bayside seller should prepare

Get an elevation reading and a condition report before you list. The city surveyed seawall elevations citywide and built a tool that lets owners check their vulnerability to rising tides, so start there. A recent survey gives a buyer something concrete and answers the first question a bayfront buyer's agent is likely to ask.

If the wall is below the current minimum or failing, you have two honest paths. Repair it and keep the permits, or disclose the shortfall and let buyers price it. Replacement needs approvals from several agencies, including the federal Army Corps, the state, Miami-Dade County and the city, so build that wait into your timeline. A cash buyer used to waterfront work may accept the job as is, while a financed buyer may need the lender to sign off on the plan.

Can a single-family home be rented by the night?

No. The city's Resiliency Code bars rentals shorter than six months and one day in single-family homes, and in many multi-family buildings in certain zoning districts. Qualifying rentals need a city Business Tax Receipt and a Resort Tax account, and section 102-386 requires both numbers in any advertisement.

The city publishes a list of apartment buildings authorized for short-term rental, and reports of illegal rentals go to Code Compliance. If your past income came from stays the code forbids, expect buyers to value the house as a long-term rental or an owner-occupied home.

Miami-Dade deed tax and closing costs

Miami-Dade charges sixty cents on each $100 and layers a forty-five cent surtax on top, a surtax that skips any deed conveying just a single-family dwelling. Every other Florida county charges 70 cents. The liability falls on everyone named in the deed, and payment goes to the clerk's office with the recording.

Mortgage payoffs, any home equity line, the year's prorated property tax and any condo association estoppel round out the usual closing list.

Property taxes and your homestead

The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser sets assessments and the county's tax collector bills. Bills arrive in November with a 4% discount that fades to 1% by February, and unpaid bills turn delinquent after April 1.

Selling a homestead ends the exemption on that parcel, and a new owner is assessed at market-based value from the next January 1. If you are moving within Florida, you may carry the saved amount forward by filing for portability by March 1.

Heirs, tenants and late mortgages

An heir needs a court-appointed representative before anyone can deed the house, and a landlord needs a plan for the tenant. Florida's short-form summary administration is open to estates up to $150,000 outside exempt property, or when the death was over two years ago.

For a tenant, a 3-day written demand covers unpaid rent, a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and after a court judgment the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before restoring possession. Decide early whether to deliver the house empty, and keep every notice and receipt. If the mortgage is behind, ask the lender in writing for the payoff and the court case status, since a sale that pays off the lender before the clerk's auction protects any equity.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Cash sale or listing on the Beach

Compare what each route leaves in your pocket. A listing may bring a higher price, but it adds commission, repair requests from the buyer's inspector, months of carrying costs and the risk that a lender balks at a seawall or a historic restriction. A cash buyer used to older Miami Beach buildings will usually take the house as is.

Whichever you choose, get the closing date, deposit and fee split in writing, and do not sign the deed until the contract is final. Pay no fee just to receive an offer.

Frequently asked questions

When was Miami Beach incorporated?

March 26, 1915. The island had by then been linked to the mainland by a bridge, and hotels and shops followed.

How many Miami Beach seawalls are on private property?

About 91%. The city counts roughly 55 miles of seawall, of which about 5 miles are publicly owned.

What height must a new Miami Beach seawall reach?

5.7 feet NAVD 1988 for new seawalls and for failing ones that are rebuilt, under an ordinance that dates to January 2021 and was updated July 23, 2025.

Does the Miami Beach Historic Preservation Board approve demolition?

Yes, inside a historic district or on a designated site. The board issues or denies certificates of appropriateness for demolition.

Is the Miami-Dade deed tax the same as in other counties?

No. Miami-Dade has its own structure, 60 cents per $100 with a 45 cent surtax that does not reach single-family-only deeds, while the rest of Florida pays 70 cents.

Selling in Largo?

Selling quickly in Largo

You can sell for cash, list with an agent or sell it yourself. A cash buyer shortens the timeline because there is no loan approval and no appraisal gap to worry about.

Listing may bring more money from a financed buyer, though showings, inspection requests and a lender's schedule stretch the process. A house with an aging roof, code problems or an estate attached often moves better to a direct buyer. A well kept house with time on the clock deserves a listing opinion alongside any cash offer.

  • Line up each offer by closing date and the cash you would walk away with.
  • Ask who covers title charges and deed tax.
  • Verify that no lien or tax balance will block the deed.

About Largo and its older houses

Largo was incorporated in 1905 and grew fast after a freeze in 1962 pushed grove owners to sell land to builders. The city now has over 80,000 residents, so much of the housing dates from the postwar and post-freeze building years, with a few older pockets from the citrus era such as Dansville, which began with a 1946 purchase of 80 acres in southwest Largo.

Keep your build year and upgrade receipts handy. A buyer's inspector will ask for the roof date and the age of the air conditioner and the electrical panel. The Largo Public Library and the Pinellas County Historic Preservation Board are places to look for photographs or permit history on an old house.

How Pinellas bills property tax

Bills go out on the last business day of October, payments are accepted from November 1, and April 1 starts delinquency. The Pinellas County Property Appraiser sets values, and the tax collector mails and collects the bills. Up to two owners print on a bill, and address changes go through the appraiser, not the collector. If your mortgage company escrows your taxes, the notice you receive may be informational only.

For the 2026 bills the tax certificate sale is May 28, 2027. Besides paying in full, the collector offers an installment plan for estimated bills over $100, with applications from November 1 through April 30. A partial payment plan takes payments of $100 or more but forfeits early discounts, and homestead owners may apply to defer taxes by March 31, which creates a lien and accrues interest.

Pinellas payment options from the tax collector
Payment optionTerms
Early paymentDiscount period November through February
Installment planFour payments, bill over $100, enroll November 1 to April 30
Partial payments$100 minimum, ends March 31, discounts forfeited
DeferralHomestead owners, lien and interest apply
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Largo house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens when a Largo tax bill goes unpaid?

The sequence can end in a tax deed auction. After April 1 interest and costs are added, and Florida law prohibits partial payments of delinquent real estate taxes.

By June 1 the collector sells a tax certificate on the parcel, awarded to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest, with unsold certificates struck off to the county at 18 percent. After two years the holder can start a tax deed application. The collector mails a warning letter each February to owners at risk, with a deadline of the last business day of March.

Once a deed action begins, all outstanding taxes roll into a single amount plus interest and costs, and only full payment stops it. Personal checks are not accepted for tax deed payments, only cash, wire or certified funds. If any part of your bill is behind, call the Pinellas County Tax Collector before you list and get a written payoff.

Deed tax, recording and short-term rental taxes

The deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp tax, collected by the clerk at recording. Quitclaim deeds, deeds in lieu of foreclosure and contracts for deed are on the taxable list, so a family transfer for value is not automatically exempt. A mortgage on the property counts as consideration. Recording is $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, and two witnesses must see the deed signed.

If you have rented the house to short-term guests, the Pinellas tax collector describes a 6 percent tourist development tax on stays of six months or less, with a 7 percent state sales tax on top for a total of 13 percent. Returns are due even when no rent was collected, and a late return carries a $50 minimum penalty. Settle those accounts before you close.

  • Close or update your tourist tax account if you rent short term.
  • Collect lease copies for long-term tenants.
  • Ask the title company what it needs for the deed.

Tenants and inherited houses

Tenants and estates both add timelines. Pinellas taxes furniture and equipment in rental properties as tangible personal property, billed to whoever owns it on January 1, and any unpaid lien on it survives a sale of the property. Check that those accounts are paid.

A year-to-year tenancy ends on 60 days' notice, a quarter-to-quarter one on 30 and a week-to-week one on 7. A sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before returning possession after a court judgment.

For an estate, Florida has had no state estate tax for people who died after 2004, and the personal representative no longer files the state forms. The heirs still need someone with court authority to sign the deed, so ask a probate attorney or the clerk what the title company will require.

Steps from offer to closing

A typical cash sale starts with an offer and a signed contract. The title company then searches for mortgages, liens and tax balances. You review a settlement statement that shows the payoff, deed tax, recording and any prorated taxes, and then you sign the deed in front of two witnesses.

Bring photo ID, the payoff letter from your lender, your latest tax bill and any lease copies. If a tourist tax or personal property account exists, close it out in the weeks before settlement. After the deed is recorded, the closing agent sends you the balance of the proceeds.

Ask each buyer to state in writing the deposit, the closing date and who pays each fee. Two or three written offers on the same lines are easy to compare, and weak offers stand out fast.

Checklist before you list in Largo

Largo buyers, especially investors, usually want to know three things first: what the roof and air conditioning look like, whether the taxes are current, and whether the property carries any rental accounts with the county. Having those answers on one sheet speeds every conversation.

  • Roof, air conditioner and electrical panel dates, with receipts.
  • This year's tax bill and proof of payment, or a payoff figure from the tax collector.
  • Copies of any lease, plus a note on whether the tenant will stay or leave.
  • Names of every person on the deed, since each must be available to sign.

If a relative lives out of state, plan the signing early. Mobile notaries and the title company can often arrange a remote signing, but two witnesses are still required for the deed.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Largo in?

Pinellas County. The Pinellas County Property Appraiser sets values and the Pinellas County Tax Collector mails the bills.

When do Pinellas tax bills go out?

On the last business day of October, and payment is accepted from November 1. April 1 is the delinquency date.

Can I pay a Largo tax bill by credit card?

Yes, online, with a 2.50 percent convenience fee from the payment processor. eChecks are free. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid by personal check.

What stops a tax deed process?

Full payment of the rolled-up amount, with interest and costs, in cash, wire or certified funds. Installments do not stop it once the action has started.

What is Largo's tourist tax if I rented the house?

It is a 6 percent tourist development tax on rentals of six months or less, plus 7 percent sales tax. Ask the Pinellas tax collector to close the account when you sell.

Selling in Lauderhill

Most buyers care less about the city's profile than about the property itself: its age, its roof, whether it floods in heavy rain, and what the monthly carrying cost looks like. Be ready with utility bills, an insurance summary and the last tax bill, and you will answer most questions in the first call.

  • State whether the house is single-family, a townhouse or part of an association.
  • Confirm school assignment with the district before naming a school in a listing.

Who signs the deed when the owner has died?

First settle who has legal authority to sign. If the owner died holding the house alone, a court usually has to name a personal representative before a title company will close.

Florida allows summary administration for smaller estates, when countable assets stay at or under $150,000, and also once two years have gone by since death (s. 735.201). A house still counts as real property, so Lauderhill heirs normally need some court step. Creditors get a limited window: the later of three months from first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days from service on a known creditor (s. 733.702).

  • Gather the death certificate, the will if there is one, and the deed.
  • Ask the Broward clerk what the probate division requires for a house.
  • Pay taxes and insurance on time until the estate closes.

Estate tax and deed tax on an inherited house

No state estate tax applies. Florida's ended for deaths after December 31, 2004, and filing Form DR-312 or DR-313 has been unnecessary since July 1, 2023.

Heirs sometimes expect closing costs to look like an ordinary sale. They vary with the type of deed and the people who sign it. Before the estate accepts a price, ask the closing agent for an itemized estimate and file it with the estate records.

A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's not-taxable list for documentary stamps. An ordinary sale deed is not: it carries the stamp rate in s. 201.02, seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price in Broward, and the signers share liability.

Homestead and the tax cap after a death or sale

Both reset. Homestead depends on the owner living in the house as a permanent residence on January 1, and renting it out or moving away ends it.

Under Save Our Homes, yearly growth in assessed value stops at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is smaller, and the state's chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale or other change of title, the following January 1 brings a fresh valuation at just value (s. 193.155). Heirs who keep and rent the house should expect a higher bill than the decedent's.

Comparing offers on an inherited house

Put every offer on one sheet with the same lines: price, repairs the buyer expects you to make, who pays the deed tax, who pays recording, and the closing date. An offer that looks high can lose that lead once those lines are filled in.

Ask whether the buyer closes with no financing contingency, whether a deposit becomes non-refundable, and what happens if the estate needs extra weeks for court paperwork. A cash purchase tends to suit a house the heirs do not want to repair, with belongings inside and family out of state. A listing may bring a higher price when the house is clean and the estate can wait.

Photograph each room before anything leaves, and decide in writing who gets which keepsakes. Disagreements among heirs can stall a closing as surely as a missing document. Pick one heir to be the contact for buyers and the title company.

Clearing and preparing an inherited house

Set aside a weekend or two. Walk through with a list and sort contents into keep, donate, sell and discard piles. Lock up personal papers, tax returns, policies and account statements until the estate attorney says what to retain.

Check that utilities stay on, the locks are changed, and the insurer knows the owner has died, since a vacant house can change coverage terms. Mow, remove mail and flyers, and photograph the condition so you can show what the buyer saw.

If the house needs work and no heir wants to manage contractors, an as-is sale shifts that job to the buyer. Get the price in writing and compare it to what a repaired house might bring after months of effort and carrying costs.

How an estate sale moves, step by step

Begin with the court. The personal representative gets letters of administration, then the title company reviews them along with the death certificate and the deed. With those in hand the representative can sign a contract, and a buyer can start a title search.

In parallel, request a payoff figure from the Broward tax collector for any unpaid bill and tell the insurer the house is for sale. At closing the representative signs the deed before two witnesses, the clerk records it, and the proceeds go to the estate, not to any single heir. The estate attorney then guides how the money is split.

Heirs who live far away should send ID copies and signed forms early. A missing signature from one relative is a frequent cause of delay, so confirm every signer's availability before you schedule the closing date with the buyer.

No. The state tax ended for deaths after December 31, 2004.

The state chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. The smaller of 3 percent or CPI sets it, and a sale starts the clock over.

The signers share liability whichever party the contract names, at seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in Broward (s. 201.02).

Which school serves my street?

Get your records ready first

Start with permit records. The city building department regulates a long list of home work, and buyers want proof it was done right. St. Cloud is in Osceola County on the shore of East Lake Tohopekaliga, and buyers weigh that lake setting along with the distance to Kissimmee and the rest of the county.

A quick sale goes best when three things are ready: the deed, the permits for any roof, window, pool or air conditioning work, and a clear idea of the tax bill. Gather them before you talk to any buyer, whether that is an agent, a private buyer or a company offering cash.

Permits the City of St. Cloud requires

A permit is often required before a project starts, and the building department works under the 8th Edition of the Florida Building Code. The city sets the ultimate design wind speed at 140 MPH for Risk Category II buildings.

Demolition, docks, hurricane shutters, screen enclosures and electrical service upgrades are permitted work too. The city does not take cash at its counters, permit fees included.

Wind rules and what buyers ask

With a 140 MPH design wind speed, roofs, window and door units, shutters and screen enclosures are inspected against a wind standard, and replacing them takes a permit. Buyers, insurers and inspectors ask about those items first.

If your roof or windows were replaced, find the permit number and final inspection. If hurricane shutters went in, the city lists them as permitted work as well. A ready file shows that the biggest wind-related parts were done properly, which backs your price and shortens negotiation.

If emergency repairs had to be made fast, the permit application is due by the next working business day, so check that a late permit did not slip through.

Repairs that matter before a sale

Open permits tend to hide behind structural, mechanical and electrical work. When an earlier owner or a contractor did the job, call the building department and ask if the permit reached final inspection.

  • Roof, window and door replacements.
  • Pool, spa and screen enclosure work.
  • Additions, sheds, garages and accessory dwelling units.
  • Solar installations and electrical service upgrades.

The city links to Florida's lien law and to guidance on the dangers of owner-builder permits. Pulled an owner-builder permit yourself? The department can explain how to close it out. Closing gaps invites more kinds of buyers, but a cash buyer may be fine with the house unchanged.

Sheds, accessory units and manufactured homes

Accessory dwelling units, sheds, gazebos, carports, garages, docks, flagpoles and manufactured or modular structures all count as regulated work. A backyard structure that was never permitted is a common surprise in a buyer's review.

If you have one, ask the building department how it was classified and what a retroactive permit would take. Siding or soffit work over 25 percent of a structure needs a permit, while smaller repairs to wood siding and stucco over block do not. Cash buyers can often accept an unpermitted shed or carport, but it may shape their price.

Osceola County property taxes at a sale

In Osceola County, the appraiser fixes each parcel's value as of January 1 and the tax collector mails the bills in November. A capped Save Our Homes assessment is lifted to just value after a sale, which can leave the new owner with a larger bill than yours.

Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Apply to the appraiser by March 1, and make sure the house was your permanent residence on January 1. Anyone who pays early gets a printed discount that steps down from 4 percent in November to 3, then 2, then 1 percent in February.

The August mailing is the notice of proposed taxes. Your closing agent prorates that year's bill between you and the buyer, and the appraiser can tell you which exemptions are on your parcel.

Stamp tax and recording on a St. Cloud deed

Each deed here is taxed by the state at 70 cents for every $100 of consideration, collected by the Osceola County clerk when the deed is filed. Under Department of Revenue rules every party to the document is liable, no matter who the contract says will pay.

Section 28.24 sets the clerk's page fees at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, along with smaller per-page charges. Expect your title agent to list them line by line.

Before accepting a cash offer, ask who pays stamp tax, title insurance and recording, and how many days the buyer needs.

Which offices handle a St. Cloud sale?

Three county offices touch the sale. The property appraiser sets just value every January 1, mails the August notice and decides who qualifies for exemptions. The tax collector issues the November bill, accepts payment, and takes deferral and installment requests. The clerk of the circuit court files your deed and takes the stamp tax.

  • Disagree with your value? You have 25 days from the August notice to petition the clerk.
  • A denied exemption or classification goes to the value adjustment board, and the petition is due 30 days after the denial letter is mailed.
  • Ask the tax collector for a payoff of any balance ahead of closing, so the closing agent can clear it.

These deadlines come around every year, so an appeal made after a sale covers only the tax year still open. Keep the August notice and the exemption papers in your sale folder, because a buyer or title agent may ask to see them.

What to bring to the title agent

A first meeting goes faster with paper in hand. Bring a photo ID, the deed or the names of everyone on it, your latest tax bill, and permit numbers with final inspection dates for the roof, windows and air conditioning. If the house is vacant or inherited, add any court papers that show who may sign.

Mention open permits, an unpermitted shed or a pending dispute over value right away. Surprises found late in the process give a buyer a reason to lower the price or walk, while problems disclosed up front can be priced in and settled.

Steps from offer to closing

Does the City of St. Cloud need to approve a roof replacement?

How long do I have to challenge my assessment?

File a petition with the clerk within 25 days after the August notice of proposed taxes. Appeals of a denied exemption have 30 days from the date the denial letter is mailed.

Yes. The city lists painting, carpeting, cabinets and gutters among work that does not need a building permit. Confirm unusual projects with the building department.

Does the buyer keep my homestead cap?

No. Ownership changes at the sale, so on the next January 1 the assessment goes back to just value. Your buyer applies for a new homestead exemption by March 1.

How can I pay St. Cloud permit fees?

Not in cash. The city does not accept cash at its counters, and staff can explain the other payment methods.

Choosing how to sell in Tamarac

Match the route to your deadline: a listing for the widest market, an as-is investor sale for speed, or a cash offer when you want the fewest steps. Tamarac is a compact Broward County city of about 74,134 people, with 76.2% of homes owner-occupied and a typical owned-home value of $288,600. Most sales are condos, villas and single-family houses on small lots, and buyers compare them closely.

A tidy plan for paperwork matters as much as the buyer you choose. Many long-time owners sell for health, family or estate reasons, so the first steps are often the same: payoff figure, association papers, title check.

Seasonal owners selling from a distance

Tamarac has long drawn snowbirds as well as year-round residents. Owners who go north for the summer often sell from afar. If that is you, line up a local contact who can meet the buyer, a signing method that works remotely, and a plan for the utilities until closing.

Homes from the original era

Houses and villas from the early decades often have small floor plans, shared walls or community amenities, and sometimes an association that still handles exterior work. Buyers will ask what the association covers and what it charges.

  • Collect the association's rules, budget and any pending special assessment.
  • Ask the association how long its approval or estoppel letter takes.
  • Gather records for the roof, windows and air conditioning, since buyers price those first.

A seller with these ready can answer a cash buyer within a day instead of a week. Without them, an offer can sit for weeks waiting on the association.

What a Tamarac seller pays at closing

Broward uses the standard deed rate of $0.70 per $100, since only Miami-Dade differs (Department of Revenue).

  • Deed tax, collected by the clerk when recording.
  • Recording fees under s. 28.24.
  • The seller's share of the year's property tax.
  • Payoff of any loan or lien.

Add association charges and an estoppel letter fee if your community requires them. The contract decides who pays deed tax, but every party stays liable.

Broward County property tax

The Broward County Property Appraiser sets values and exemptions, and the office answers at 954-357-6830 on weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. A buyer does not inherit your capped assessment, since a change of ownership resets it the next January 1.

A homestead cap holds yearly growth to the lower of 3 percent or CPI (Department of Revenue), which is why a long-held Tamarac house can carry a bill far under a new owner's. The calendar is on the state tax page.

Keeping your Save Our Homes benefit

A personal representative must be named before a sale, unless the estate fits summary administration (s. 735.201). Lady bird deeds are a different tool, and the Department of Revenue has advised that one such deed carried no stamp tax on its facts. Have a Florida attorney read your deed.

Owing more than the house is worth

Speak to the lender early. Selling before a court sale lets you choose the buyer and the date. Foreclosure sales follow judgment within 20 to 35 days unless extended (s. 45.031).

Cash buyer or listing?

  • Who pays title insurance and deed tax?
  • Does the written offer match the verbal one?

Steady demand on a small, fixed amount of land means competition for homes, and a seller can use it. Still, an offer is only worth what reaches you at the table.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer has no loan to be approved, so the lender's appraisal and underwriting steps drop out and a sale cannot collapse because financing fell through. The rest of the process stays: title search, payoff of liens and mortgages, a signed deed, and recording with the Broward County clerk.

Cash buyers also tend to take a house as it is. Skipping repairs, staging and showings is the real saving of time, and the offer reflects it. If your community has an association, remember that the buyer's closing still waits on the association's paperwork, so order it the day you accept an offer.

Steps from offer to closing

  1. Accept an offer and sign the contract, naming who pays title insurance and deed tax.
  2. Request the association's estoppel letter and sale documents.
  3. The title company searches the records for liens, mortgages and ownership problems.
  4. Collect payoff figures from the servicer and, if you deferred taxes, from the tax collector.
  5. Sign the deed with two witnesses, and the clerk records it.

Most delays come from one of three things: a slow association, a missing owner signature, or a lien nobody knew about. A title search early in the week takes care of the third, and a quick call to every owner on the deed takes care of the second.

Records to hand a buyer

A buyer will want to see what you have, and a seller who answers fast usually gets a better offer. Pull together the recorded deed, your latest Broward County tax bill, proof of any exemption, the association's rules and budget, and invoices for the roof, windows and air conditioning.

If you hold a homestead exemption, say so, and remind the buyer that the exemption does not transfer. They file their own application by March 1, and the assessment resets after the sale. Telling them early avoids a surprise when their first bill arrives and looks higher than yours.

Quitclaim deeds and two owners

Land deeds need two witnesses, and every owner must sign. Settle any missing signature before the closing date.

Four calls to make this week

Start with four calls, in this order.

  1. Your mortgage servicer, for a payoff figure.
  2. Your association, for its sale requirements and fees.
  3. A title company, for a preliminary look at liens and ownership.
  4. Two or three buyers, for written offers you can compare.

Doing these in one week gives you a full picture of the net you can expect, and it keeps any deadline from sneaking up on you.

Can I sell for cash in Tamarac if the house is in a homeowners association?

Yes, but the association may require an application or estoppel letter. Request the documents early because the buyer cannot close without them.

Will Broward County tax bills change after I sell?

Yes, for the buyer. The assessment resets after a change of ownership.

What deed tax rate applies in Tamarac?

It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, the standard rate outside Miami-Dade. The contract decides who pays, but all parties remain liable.

Can I sell while behind on the mortgage?

Yes. Until a court sale is confirmed you can sell and pay the lender at closing.

Does selling end my homestead exemption?

The exemption ends for that property. You can reapply on a new Florida home by March 1, and you may be able to carry over part of your capped value through portability.

Quickest ways to move an Ocala house

An Ocala seller in a hurry has three realistic paths: take a cash offer, list with an agent at an aggressive price, or sell straight to a buyer you know. Just 52.1% of homes in the city are lived in by their owners, which tells you landlords and investors are active here.

  • Cash purchase: nothing waits on a lender appraisal, so you steer the closing date, and the buyer takes the house in its current state.
  • Agent listing: the biggest audience, at the price of showings, repair haggling and a commission.
  • Direct sale: the whole price is yours, but you draft the paperwork, and a title company normally runs the closing.

Some older Ocala houses sit in locally regulated historic districts. Learn early whether yours does, so you can price and negotiate around it. Ask each bidder in writing who pays for title work and the deed stamps, and confirm the date you will hand over keys.

Ocala housing figures

An estimated 71,753 people live in Ocala as of mid-2025, 12.7% more than in 2020. The figures below are citywide survey estimates (2020 to 2024 unless noted). Read the home value as a midpoint only, because a renovated bungalow and a dated rental can sit far apart on the same street. Your street, lot and condition set your price, and a broker's price opinion or an appraisal gets closer.

Ocala's historic core

A Thanksgiving Day fire in 1883 wiped out the center of town, and rebuilding in brick and other fire-resistant materials earned Ocala the nickname Brick City. The oldest houses stand within a few blocks of the courthouse square, which is why many now belong to the Ocala and Tuscawilla Park Historic Districts. If your house is in that part of town, mention it in the listing, since some buyers want a historic home and others want to avoid the review process. Either way, they will ask, and a clear answer from you saves a round of questions during the inspection period.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Ocala house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Historic district rules

If the house is inside the Ocala or Tuscawilla Park district, yes: exterior work needs a Certificate of Appropriateness first. Ocala lists four historic districts. Those two are both local and national, while Downtown Commercial and West Ocala hold only a national listing, so local review covers just the first pair.

Applicants file through the city's eTRAKiT portal a full month ahead of the Historic Preservation Advisory Board meeting, and the city charges nothing to apply. The packet includes a signed form, manufacturer specifications and drawings for windows, doors, siding, roofing and fencing, a site plan if relevant, proof of ownership and, for new construction, plans no larger than 11 by 17 inches showing all four elevations. The board gathers most months on the first Thursday at four in the afternoon, at City Hall, 110 SE Watula Ave.

Sellers should know two things. First, the certificate has to come before any other permit, and a building permit pulled without one is invalid. Second, work done without approval can bring fines under the city code. To check your parcel, email historic@ocalafl.org with the address, and pass the answer to any buyer planning exterior changes.

Property tax bill and proration

The owner on January 1 is assessed for the whole year, which is why the November bill is divided at closing. Exemption applications go to the Marion County property appraiser by March 1. Billing and collection belong to the tax collector, and paying in November earns 4 percent off, a discount that shrinks one point per month until February.

Anything unpaid is delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates reach auction by June 1. On your settlement statement, find the proration line to see what passes between you and the buyer.

The Save Our Homes cap, set at 2.7 percent for 2026, slows the climb of a homestead's assessment. It belongs to the owner. When the house sells, the county resets it to full just value, and your exemption lapses once you leave.

Florida deed tax and recording fees

Under section 201.02 the deed carries documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Mortgages and other encumbrances on the land count toward consideration, even if the buyer does not assume them. The state can collect from any signer no matter what the contract says, and the clerk takes the money at recording. Page-based recording fees start at five dollars for the first page, and extra names and technology surcharges are added.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ocala houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Foreclosure or a tax deed on the horizon

Once a judge enters final foreclosure judgment, the clerk auctions the house 20 to 35 days later, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait. The winning bidder owes a 5 percent deposit, and a 10 day window for objections starts at the certificate of sale. A homestead owner who may be owed surplus should reach the clerk inside that window.

A tax deed moves more slowly. The certificate holder can apply two years after April 1 of the issue year, and a homestead opens at the amount owed plus half its latest assessed value. If you receive a notice, take it to a lawyer before signing an offer. Selling before the auction or tax deed date lets you pay the debt from the proceeds and keep any equity, so move quickly once you have a notice in hand and ask the title company to confirm the payoff amount in writing.

What to do before you accept an Ocala offer

  • Find out from city staff whether your parcel sits in the Ocala or Tuscawilla Park local district.
  • Gather payoff letters from each lender or lienholder.
  • Check last year's bill for a homestead exemption and any special line items.
  • Compare offers by what lands in your account after the deed tax and recording fees.
  • Ask the closing agent to explain the proration of the year's property tax.

Keep the payoff letters, the latest tax bill and any historic approval paperwork in one folder, since both the title company and the buyer will ask. With a cash buyer there is no appraisal or lender approval, so once the title search clears you can close on your own timeline. At signing the deed is witnessed, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. If heirs or co-owners are involved, line up everyone's signature and identification ahead of the signing date.

Frequently asked questions

Can an Ocala house in poor repair still sell?

Yes. Cash buyers and investors take houses in rough shape, and conventional buyers can negotiate credits. Inside the Ocala or Tuscawilla Park district, though, any exterior fix needs the historic approval first.

What does a Certificate of Appropriateness cost in Ocala?

Nothing. Submit through eTRAKiT a month before the board meets, since the certificate must be in hand before any other permit.

Will my Marion County homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. It ends when you stop living in the house. The buyer files their own by March 1 if the house is their home on January 1, and the county reassesses at full just value.

When does the 4 percent discount on a Marion County tax bill apply?

Pay in November, when bills go out, and you get 4 percent off. After that it steps down: 3 percent in December, 2 in January, 1 in February. April 1 starts delinquency.

How do I sell a house I inherited in Ocala?

Start with the probate route. A probate lawyer can say whether summary administration, which Florida reserves for smaller or older estates, fits your case.

Where to start with a fast Delray Beach sale

Because Delray Beach lies in Palm Beach County, county offices produce your tax bill and handle deed recording and tax certificates. Three questions drive a quick sale here: the condition of the house, what you owe on it, and where the property tax calendar stands.

The city describes its growth from a small farming village into a community of nearly 70,000 residents, built around a historic downtown on Atlantic Avenue. Homes close to downtown are older and may carry deferred upkeep. Newer parts of town usually need less. Financed buyers may want repairs; cash buyers frequently accept the property exactly as it stands.

  • An agent listing suits an owner who can sit through showings and a lender's schedule.
  • An as-is cash sale answers pressure from repairs, a move date or a tax deadline.
  • A renovator is the likelier buyer when the work would scare off a mortgage lender.

Two halves, one city

Linton was the first name. After crop freezes and a land payment default it became Delray in 1898, and it took the name Delray Beach when two municipalities merged on May 11, 1927. Land west of the canal had incorporated in 1911, and land east of the Intracoastal in 1923.

The mainland and barrier island halves still feel different: beachside living east of the waterway, inland neighborhoods to the west. A bridge across the canal first linked them in 1911. Homes vary enormously in age and in condition, and on an older parcel a long ownership chain can hide a mortgage nobody formally released. Have your title company look for stale easements and unreleased liens.

Historic downtown and renovation buyers

Downtown centers on Old School Square and Atlantic Avenue, and buyers who like that setting often shop within walking distance. The 1913 school building is now the Cornell Museum of Art and History, while the 1925 high school is the Crest Theatre.

Does your house stand in or beside a historic area? Planning staff can tell you what rules govern exterior changes, and renovation-minded buyers will want that answer before they commit.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Delray Beach house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Palm Beach County tax dates

More than 600,000 bills go out from the county tax collector by November 1. You can pay from that date through March 31, after which the tax is delinquent and carries penalties and interest. The appraiser's Notice of Proposed Taxes arrives each August.

Discount by payment month

  • Florida law pushes a weekend or holiday due date to the next working day.
  • No online payment is possible for delinquent tax, and a postmark does not count as proof that you paid.
  • If the house has sold but the bill still came to you, a Property Sold Form from the tax collector sends it to the right person.

The county's property tax page describes an installment plan and a homestead tax deferral. Phone the collector before listing to see whether either applies to you.

Deed tax and recording

The state's deed tax runs 70 cents for each $100 of consideration (section 201.02). Everyone on the deed is liable regardless of who agreed to pay it. Miami-Dade stands apart with a rate of its own, but Palm Beach County does not, so the standard figure applies here.

Under section 28.24 the clerk may bill $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, plus trust fund and technology charges. Two deeds are listed as exempt: a spousal homestead deed where a mortgage is the only consideration, and a divorce deed covering the marital home.

Some older owners use lady bird deeds. In October 2020 a Department of Revenue advisement found that a particular one owed no documentary stamp tax, since the life tenants kept full powers. Because it turns on its own facts, have a title attorney look at yours first.

Listing or quick sale

Three yardsticks help: what you net, how long closing takes, and how likely the deal is to collapse. A listing brings in more buyers but also showings, an appraisal and loan conditions. Selling for cash lets you pick the closing date and usually removes repair requests.

  1. Obtain a written mortgage payoff.
  2. Find out if this year's property taxes have been paid.
  3. Learn from each buyer who covers stamps, title and recording.
  4. Request the closing statement before the day itself.

If a foreclosure is under way, the clerk's sale is held 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless the plaintiff gives more time.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Delray Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Moving within Florida

Portability is the tool. Start a new Florida homestead inside three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, and the Save Our Homes difference may reduce what the new house is assessed at. Both Form DR-501T and Form DR-501 are due March 1.

You lose homestead by renting the property, by moving out permanently, or by ceasing to be a Florida resident. An extra exemption may be available to owners 65 and older where local ordinance provides one and income is under the limit, so the county appraiser can tell you if Delray Beach has it.

From accepted offer to closing

When you accept an offer, the title company searches the records, writes the deed and agrees a date with you. Take photo ID, keys and any garage or gate openers. Read every line of the settlement statement, and check how the money will reach you. Your lender gets paid first, taxes are prorated, and you receive the rest after recording.

It helps to pack and clear the house before closing, and to photograph its condition on the day you hand over keys. Switch utilities only on the agreed date, and keep your own insurance running until the deed is recorded.

A folder of records speeds everything, and it keeps surprises from showing up late in the process. Include the deed, your most recent mortgage statement, the most recent tax bill, any permit paperwork and warranties for the roof or appliances. Write down known problems with the house and the dates of past repairs, because buyers and inspectors ask about them. If several people own the house, make sure each one will be available to sign, or arrange a signing for those who live elsewhere. Heirs and co-owners in particular should agree in advance on the asking price, the lowest offer they will take and who speaks for the group when a buyer calls. Put that agreement in writing so nobody has to guess later.

Retain a copy of every page. A seller who is also buying should request closing figures early, so the next lender has what it needs.

Frequently asked questions

When did Delray Beach become a city?

The City of Delray Beach was formed on May 11, 1927, when the Town of Delray Beach and the City of Delray united. They had been incorporated separately, in 1923 and 1911.

What was Delray Beach called before?

It started as Linton, named in 1895 for a congressman in the settlement group. Residents changed it to Delray in 1898 after freezes damaged crops.

When are Palm Beach County property taxes delinquent?

April 1. Bills are payable from November 1 through March 31, and delinquent taxes cannot be paid online.

Is there an early payment discount in Palm Beach County?

Yes: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with none in March.

Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Delray Beach?

The contract decides who pays, but all parties are liable. The statewide deed rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

A Weston owner can go through an agent, a cash buyer or an investor, and the choice mostly comes down to how much time and certainty you need. Most Weston homes sit inside a homeowners' association, so a buyer's timeline often depends on association paperwork as well as financing.

  • Cash sale: no lender appraisal, so closing can be quick once the title is clear and any association documents are in hand.
  • Agent listing: a wider buyer pool, with showings and a loan approval period.
  • Investor sale: the buyer accepts the property in whatever shape it is in.

Write the price, closing date and who covers each closing charge into the contract. Then request the association's payoff or estoppel figures early, since an unpaid assessment can hold up the settlement.

A planned community

Weston began as a planned development, not an old town. Its 15,000 acres were assembled in the 1950s, a regional approval in 1978 first allowed more than 25,000 dwelling units, and later amendments cut the figure to 17,000. The Indian Trace Community Development District followed in 1981 to finance and manage water and sewer mains, water bodies and arterial roads. The first homes were finished in Windmill Ranch and Country Isles in 1984.

That makes Weston houses comparatively recent, and it means association rules and the district's roads, lakes and utilities are part of what a buyer is evaluating. Residents voted to form their own city, and the Legislature approved the local bill on May 5, 1996. The result is a city that controls its own zoning and permits. Ask the city, not the county, about setbacks, additions and pools, and give buyers the same instruction in writing.

Homeowners' association paperwork

Very likely your sale involves one. Most residences in Weston are in a private development governed by an association, and City Code requires each association to register annually with the City Clerk's Office by the first workday in April.

In gated or private communities the common areas are private property, so the association maintains the infrastructure, roads and landscaping inside. Trees on association property and street trees cannot be removed without a city permit. The city maintains most of the water bodies, though some lakes are privately owned.

  • Ask your association or management company for the current assessment status before you list.
  • Collect the governing documents a buyer will request.
  • Confirm whether any lake, drainage or tree work is pending on your lot.

Homeowners who draw irrigation water from a lake or canal need the consent agreement the city publishes, and the city takes questions at 954-385-2000. A buyer who wants to keep that irrigation should ask you for the agreement.
