Permits for work before you sell

A permit problem can surface at the worst moment, when a buyer's inspector walks the yard. Call Weston's Building Code Services and Planning and Zoning staff before any exterior work, and ask what applies to the specific job. Tree removal is the clearest rule: street trees and trees on association property cannot come down without a city permit.

Florida enacted a 2026 exemption for some small projects under $7,500, but it has limits. Electrical, plumbing and structural work still need permits, so assume a permit is needed until Weston staff tells you otherwise.

If you finished a patio, pool deck or addition without a permit, ask the Building Department what it would take to close it out before a buyer's inspector finds it. Cash buyers may accept the risk, but expect them to reduce the offer for it. Keep any final inspection approvals and contractor invoices for permitted work, and hand them over with the rest of your closing folder.

Broward County property taxes and your sale

The county sends the bill, and the state calendar sets the dates.

Broward property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Property assessed at just value
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
NovemberBills sent; 4 percent early-pay discount
FebruaryDiscount drops to 1 percent
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
June 1Tax certificates sold on unpaid items

When you request a payoff figure, also ask the Broward County tax office for the current bill and any delinquent balance.

For homesteaded owners, Save Our Homes limits yearly assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The cap ends when the property changes hands, which resets the property to just value the next January 1, so a Weston buyer can face a higher bill than you paid. An owner-occupant buyer can claim up to $50,000 of homestead exemption through Form DR-501, filed with the county appraiser by March 1. The exemption is lost if the home is rented or stops being the owner's permanent home.

If you will buy another Florida home, portability can move some of your accumulated savings to the new homestead when it is established within three years.

Deed and recording costs

Broward County pays Florida's standard deed tax, $0.70 for each $100 of price. Only Miami-Dade has a separate rate. Everyone on the deed is liable, whoever the contract says will pay.

The clerk charges $5.00 to record the first page and $4.00 for each later page, plus trust fund and technology charges. The final amounts appear on your title agent's settlement statement, which you should compare with the contract before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Weston houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Gathering your documents

Weston buyers expect a complete packet. Pull your deed and survey, the association's governing documents and fee schedule, and proof that assessments are current. Add permit records for any pool, patio or addition, and the irrigation consent agreement if you draw from a lake or canal.

Request the association's figures in writing and note when they were issued, since buyers and title agents will want recent numbers. If any tree, lake or drainage work is pending on your lot, say so before the buyer finds it. Candor early keeps a cash offer from shrinking late in the process. If the association needs time to produce its documents, tell the buyer the expected date so the closing schedule reflects it. Delays here are common and rarely fatal, but surprises are.

What a cash sale skips in Weston

With no loan involved, nobody orders a lender appraisal or waits on underwriting. Where an association exists, the slowest step is usually the paperwork it supplies, so request it the day you accept an offer.

Then a title agent hunts for liens and drafts the settlement statement. You sign the deed, and the clerk records it. Read every line of the statement first, and ask how and when your proceeds will reach you. If a mortgage is being paid off, the statement should show the payoff amount going to your lender, and any unpaid association balance should appear as a deduction too. Ask the title agent to explain any line you do not recognize before you sign anything.

Frequently asked questions

Do most Weston homes belong to a homeowners' association?

Yes. Most residences in Weston are in a private development governed by an association. Ask yours for assessment status and governing documents before listing.

When did Weston become a city?

The State Legislature approved the local bill enabling incorporation on May 5, 1996. Weston grew from a planned community that began with the 1978 Indian Trace approval.

Can I remove a tree from my Weston lot?

Trees on association property and street trees cannot be removed without a city permit. Call the city before any tree work.

Is there a deed tax when I sell in Weston?

Yes. Florida's deed tax runs $0.70 per $100 of price and is collected by the clerk.

When do Broward County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent that day, and certificates are sold by June 1.

Ways to sell a Sanford house

A Sanford homeowner has three basic paths: hire a listing agent, find a buyer alone, or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands. Putting the house on the market tends to bring the highest price when it is in good shape. Cash suits a place that needs work, has renters inside, or must close by a certain date.

Sanford is the Seminole County seat, so the property appraiser, tax collector and clerk are all close by. Ordering a lien search, a payoff figure or a certified deed copy takes little travel. Whatever route you pick, the sale ends with a signed deed, recording and Florida stamp tax.

  • Agent: exposure to the most buyers, and someone else runs showings and haggling.
  • Owner-direct: you keep the commission and take on the contract and paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: speed and certainty in place of top price, with no lender or appraisal to wait on.

Older homes and inspections

Sanford sits on the south shore of Lake Monroe, and its older neighborhoods carry a river-town layout. Houses in those parts of town may have aging plumbing, wiring or foundations, and a buyer's inspector will find them. If that describes yours, settle early on fixing, giving a credit, or selling untouched.

Buyers also notice location. A lakefront downtown with a RiverWalk draws walkers and downtown diners, and the airport sits on the former naval air station site. When you describe the house, mention how close it is to the RiverWalk, downtown and the airport, since out-of-town buyers recognize those points.

Seminole County Property Appraiser

The appraiser's office in downtown Sanford sets assessed values, takes exemption applications and posts parcel and deed data. Walk in at 1101 E. 1st Street on a weekday between 8 and 5, or phone customer service at 407-665-7506. Exemption or fraud questions go to 407-665-7512.

The 2026 tax roll counts 181,187 real property parcels in the county, 138,250 of them residential, with a market value of $92 billion against a taxable value of $60 billion. The gap comes from exemptions and assessment caps.

A constitutional amendment passed on November 3, 2026 and touches the state's property tax system. Phone the office and ask what it means for your parcel before you set a sale timeline.

Property taxes and deed tax at sale

On a Sanford deed, the state charges 70 cents for every hundred dollars of price, and any mortgage balance is counted in that base (s. 201.02). Payment happens through the closing agent at recording, and every name on the deed remains on the hook until the tax is paid (Revenue's stamp tax page). Put the payer in the contract.

Bills go out in November (taxpayer guide). Before closing, get your parcel's balance from the Seminole County Tax Collector. Whatever is still owed is deducted from your sale proceeds. Payments are accepted at the counter, by mail or online.

The appraiser also holds parcel splits, combinations and plat recordings until 2026 taxes are paid, so settle that first if you plan to divide a lot. Once the house sells, the assessment is reset to just value, so the new owner's bill is not a copy of yours.

Homestead filing

Homestead applications are due March 1, 2027. Pre-filing for the following year opens March 2 and runs through December 31. Your buyer must file separately for their own exemption, so point them to the appraiser.

If you hold a homestead now, check what the appraiser shows on file. A stale exemption can confuse a closing statement.

Inherited, rented or behind on payments

  • Inherited house: an estate worth under $150,000 apart from exempt property, or a death more than two years back, may qualify for the faster summary administration (s. 735.201). Creditor claims are barred three months after the first notice or 30 days after service, whichever comes later (s. 733.702).
  • Rented house: ending a weekly tenancy takes 7 days' notice, and a monthly one takes 30 (s. 83.57).
  • Payments behind: after the court enters judgment, the clerk holds the sale 20 to 35 days later unless the lender allows more time (s. 45.031).

The Seminole County Clerk offers free property fraud alerts, and the appraiser recommends them, especially for an empty inherited house. If any of these situations fits you, start the conversation with a title agent early, since liens and estate steps set the timeline.

How closing works, step by step

A closing moves from contract to recorded deed in a few steps, and a cash sale drops the lender and appraisal steps. A title agent or closing attorney runs the logistics.

  1. Contract: price, closing date, and who pays deed tax and recording.
  2. Title search: surfaces mortgages, judgments and liens, which get paid from proceeds.
  3. Signing: land conveyances need two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01), and those witnesses may appear by audio-video link.
  4. Recording: the deed goes from the closing agent to the Seminole County clerk.
  5. Owner update: the appraiser changes the parcel owner after the recorded deed is processed.

Deed linking can lag when the clerk's records system is down, so an unchanged owner name online right after recording is no cause for alarm.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer pays without bank financing, so the loan approval, buyer appraisal and underwriting delays drop out. Title still has to be clean, the deed still has to be signed, and any mortgage or lien still gets paid off at the table.

The usual trade is price. Because the buyer accepts the house with its flaws, you avoid repairs, clean-outs and staging. For a house with deferred work, tenants or a looming deadline, many Sanford owners weigh that speed against a higher listing price that may take months.

  • Request a payoff letter from your lender before comparing offers.
  • Ask every buyer who covers deed tax, recording and title charges.
  • Get the closing date and the move-out condition in writing.

Records and tools for sellers

The appraiser's site offers parcel and deed searches, plus free downloads of its data in Excel, Access and several GIS formats, updated daily. A custom data pull takes 10 business days, and fees may apply.

The site also links a First-Time Florida Homebuyer Guide and a Department of Revenue guide to the property tax system, handy to pass along to a buyer. Before listing, go down this list:

  • Read the owner name and mailing address on your parcel record.
  • Confirm the exemption listed matches how you actually use the house.
  • Sign up for fraud alerts through the clerk's office.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I get a parcel record for my Sanford house?

From the Seminole County Property Appraiser, which has an office at 1101 E. 1st Street in Sanford and posts parcel data online. Customer service is 407-665-7506.

Is Sanford in a county with a special stamp tax rate?

No. Seminole County uses the standard 70 cents per $100 on deeds, the same as every Florida county besides Miami-Dade.

Can a house in an older Sanford neighborhood sell as-is?

Yes. Cash buyers regularly buy older houses as-is, and a financed buyer will rely on an inspection and appraisal instead.

When do I have to file for homestead on a new Sanford house?

File with the county appraiser by March 1. Early filing for the next year is allowed from March 2 to December 31.

What happens to my taxes after I sell?

On the next January 1 the Save Our Homes cap resets because ownership changed, and the assessment returns to just value. Your buyer's bill may look different.

Selling a house in Port Orange

Port Orange is a Volusia County city along the Halifax River, with an estimated 66,395 residents in July 2025. Sellers here tend to be long-time owners, downsizers or heirs, and they usually choose among three paths.

  • Agent listing: best for a house ready to move into, when you can wait on the buyer's lender.
  • Sale by owner: fits someone comfortable setting a price and handling disclosures and contracts.
  • Cash sale: fits deferred work, an estate on a timeline or a firm move-out date.

Choosing a path starts with a short checklist of what you know about the house: the age of the roof and air conditioner, any water or insect damage, open permits, and who lives there. Buyers will find these items in an inspection or a title search anyway, so telling them first builds trust and avoids a late price cut.

A cash buyer closes as quickly as the title company can clear the record. A listing adds showings, an inspection and the lender's timeline. Match the route to the house's condition and the date you have to be out.

Most homes here are owner-occupied. A typical value is only the midpoint of a wide spread, so a riverfront home and an inland ranch sit far apart. Recent sales on your own street tell you more.

Homes near the Town Center

In eastern Port Orange, a 271-acre redevelopment district covers 300 parcels. The city created the Town Center on December 15, 1998, and its plan favors mixed-use buildings and public access to the water. It has five Special Character Districts: Riverwalk, Causeway, Down Under, Dunlawton Village and Ridgewood Avenue.

Live in or near one? The city's planning office can give you the adopted redevelopment plan, which shows what is hoped for nearby. Buyers who want river access or walkable errands will ask about it. In your description, give the distance to Dunlawton Avenue, the river and the beaches, because local buyers measure by those.

Homestead exemptions and Amendment 3

Volusia County's 2026 homestead exemption reaches $51,411: $25,000 against all millages plus $26,411 against non-school millages. A constitutional change, Amendment 3, passed on November 3, 2026.

Starting January 1, 2027 the non-school exemption can reach $150,000, and from January 1, 2028 it can reach $250,000. School taxes stay at $25,000. Assessment growth on non-homestead property falls from a 10 percent cap to 5 percent. A person who becomes a Florida resident on or after January 1, 2027 begins at $50,000 and earns the larger amount over four years.

After a sale Florida resets a property to just value, so the buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours. Volusia's property appraiser can explain how your parcel is treated, since follow-up legislation may refine the details.

  • End your exemption if you move out before March 1.
  • Expect the next owner to file their own.
  • Keep your TRIM notice, which lists exemptions and any capped value.

Taxes owed at closing

If taxes are still owed when you sell, the title agent pays the balance from your proceeds, so the buyer gets a clean record and you do not write a separate check. Ask the Volusia tax collector for the exact figure in writing before the closing date. The bill is prorated between you and the buyer for the part of the year each of you owned the house.

Your closing statement should also show the deed stamp tax, recording fees and any lien payoffs. Compare it with your contract several days ahead, and ask the title agent to explain any line you do not recognize before you sign. Keep a copy of the signed statement with your tax records.

Water accounts and tenants

Port Orange holds the owner liable for utility charges unless the account is formally in a tenant's name. Each time a renter leaves, water service reverts to the owner and is turned off, and each request to start or stop water carries a $40 service fee.

Between renters, the owner pays monthly water availability fees, and the account must have a deposit on hold. Leases must be signed and witnessed, and a management agreement is required when an agent handles the rental.

A final reading matters. Schedule it for the day the keys change hands so you are not billed for the buyer's usage, and keep the last statement with your closing papers.

With a rented house, take care of these before closing.

  • Confirm whose name is on the water account and settle any final balance.
  • Send the tenant's lease and any management agreement to the buyer's title agent.
  • Remember that Florida law bars cutting utilities to a tenant without legal authority (section 83.67).

Heirs and recording a deed

Section 735.201 allows summary administration for a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less, or if the owner died more than two years ago. Creditors lose their claims after the later of three months from first publication or 30 days from being served, if they had to be served.

No stamp tax applies to a personal representative's deed under a probated will, but a quit claim deed is taxed. Most other deeds bear 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade, which the clerk collects at recording from any liable party.

Delinquency for unpaid taxes begins April 1, and section 689.01 requires two witnesses on the deed. Out-of-state heirs should ask the Volusia clerk which authority papers the title agent needs, since that paperwork controls the closing date.

From offer to closing

Allow a few days for the paperwork even when the offer is firm. The title agent needs time to confirm payoffs, and the clerk needs time to record. If you are an heir or the seller lives out of town, ask whether the deed can be signed before a notary near you, with two witnesses present as the statute requires.

  1. Pull together the payoff letter, newest tax bill, any lease and water account details.
  2. Compare written offers for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent runs the record search, requests payoffs and drafts the deed.
  4. Two witnesses watch you sign.
  5. The clerk records the deed, and your proceeds follow.

Cash drops the buyer's appraisal and loan approval, the steps that usually stretch a listing. The water account, the tax proration and any lien payoffs remain. Ask every buyer who pays for the title policy and how long the offer holds, and get each answer in writing. Compare at least two offers before you commit.

Frequently asked questions

Is a cash sale a fit for a Port Orange house needing repairs?

Often. Cash buyers purchase as-is and skip lender appraisals, but the title still has to be clear.

When did voters approve the new homestead amendment?

On November 3, 2026, with effect from January 1, 2027.

Does a buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?

No. The sale resets the property to just value the next January 1, except in cases like transfers between spouses.

Can heirs sell before probate ends?

Only if someone has authority to sign. A personal representative or court order usually decides that, so check with the Volusia clerk and an attorney.

What happens to my city water account when I sell?

The owner stays responsible unless the account is in a tenant's name, and each start or stop request costs $40. Call the utilities office before closing.

Selling choices for an Apopka owner

Owners here usually choose among three routes: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash offer on the house as is. Each trades time, effort and net proceeds in a different mix.

Listing suits a tidy house when a few weeks of showings are fine. Cash suits a place with repairs looming, an estate behind it, or a renter inside. All three end at the Orange County recording desk.

  • With an agent: showings and lender timing set the pace.

Apopka at a glance

Apopka sits about twelve miles from Orlando in northwest Orange County, with a population of 56,727. The city is second in size in the county, behind only Orlando.

A lot of Apopka buyers work somewhere else in the Orlando area. Only 21 percent of residents both live and work in Apopka, and the average commute is 31.6 minutes. Describe the drive toward Orlando when you talk to buyers, because road access can weigh as much as the address itself. For a house inside the city limits, permit and code questions go to city staff rather than the county.

Orange County taxes after an Apopka sale

Two county offices matter: the appraiser who values the parcel and the tax collector who bills it. Values are fixed each January 1. After a sale, a homestead is reset to full market value the following January, which can leave the buyer's bill above yours.

On the appraiser's site you'll find a tax estimator aimed at buyers and sellers, plus a property search with sales and foreclosure records by address. Check both before you name a price, because buyers can pull the same record.

  • Homestead relief reaches $50,000 of value and requires an application to the appraiser by March 1.
  • Save Our Homes holds a homestead's yearly assessment rise to inflation with a 3 percent ceiling; the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A property without homestead can rise at most 10 percent in assessed value per year.
  • Pay your November bill early for 4 percent off. The discount falls each month to 1 percent in February, and April 1 makes a balance delinquent.

Ask the title company how this year's taxes will be divided with the buyer, and read that line before you agree to it.

Recording a deed in Orange County

The Comptroller charges $10 for the opening page of a deed and $8.50 for each extra page, plus $1 for every name past the fourth. On top of that, outside Miami-Dade, Florida deed tax is 70 cents on each $100 of price.

The tax is due at recording, and every party to the document is liable for it, whoever agreed to pay. A deed sent by mail usually waits 7 to 10 business days. E-recording is usually finished within 24 hours. The quickest option is walking a deed into the office at 109 East Church Street.

Two details trip up sellers. A deed without two subscribing witnesses may not be recognized by the property appraiser for tracking ownership changes. Also, the comptroller doesn't give legal advice or supply deed forms. A Florida attorney or your title company should prepare the deed. After closing, your lender's satisfaction of mortgage is recorded in the same Official Records, where a name search shows liens and judgments. The comptroller won't issue a letter saying a property has no liens.

Foreclosure or an inherited house

Both run on statute clocks, and a private sale is still possible if you move early. Following a foreclosure judgment, the clerk sells the property at auction within 20 to 35 days unless the plaintiff agrees to wait. The highest bidder leaves 5 percent down.

For an inherited Apopka house, Orange County probate papers can't be viewed online, because Florida law keeps those document images off the comptroller's website. A short-form summary process exists for estates up to $150,000 and for owners dead more than two years. A deed from a court-appointed representative is on the state's non-taxable list.

A renter in the house

A landlord owed rent serves a written notice giving three days, not counting weekends and court holidays. Thirty days of notice ends a month-to-month tenancy; a year-to-year tenancy needs 60.

Certain cash buyers will purchase a house with a renter still in it. Read the lease and ask a Florida attorney how it affects the sale. A tenant who contests the case on grounds other than payment has 5 days to deposit the rent with the court. Following a judgment, the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice.

Practical steps to sell

  1. Look up the parcel and its tax estimate on the county appraiser's site.
  2. Gather the deed, mortgage payoff figure, HOA details and any open permits from the city.
  3. Work out your net for each route, agent, solo sale or cash buyer, after taxes and recording charges.
  4. Pick a title company and request the closing statement early.
  5. File the deed at the Orange County Comptroller and send the appraiser your new mailing address.

Give each step more time than you think it needs, and start with the slowest items first. A payoff letter can take days to arrive, and an HOA may need a few weeks to return its paperwork. Ask for each in writing and keep copies together in one folder.

Disclosing what you know

It's wise to tell buyers about known problems that aren't easy to see, such as leaks, past water damage or unpermitted work. Write these down before the first showing and share them early. A buyer who hears about an issue at the start rarely walks away over it, while one who finds it at the last minute often does.

If you aren't sure what counts, ask your title company or a Florida attorney. In a cash sale, the buyer may buy as is, but honest answers still protect you after closing.

Before closing day

Plan for a final walk-through with the buyer if the contract calls for one, and agree on what stays with the house. A few days before closing, review the draft settlement statement line by line. Confirm the payoff amounts, the tax split and every fee, and ask the title agent to explain anything unfamiliar. Bring a government photo ID and any keys, garage openers and codes you'll hand over.

With cash, no lender appraisal or underwriting sits between you and the closing table. The deed, the tax proration and the recorded payoffs are handled just as they would be in a financed sale.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays doc stamps on an Apopka deed?

Whichever side the contract names, though the state can pursue any party to the deed. The rate outside Miami-Dade is 70 cents on each $100 of price.

When does Orange County reassess a house after I sell it?

The next January 1. A change of ownership resets a homestead to market value as of that date, and the new owner has until March 1 to file for homestead.

How fast will Orange County record my deed?

By mail, between 7 and 10 business days. E-recording is usually done within 24 hours, and walking it in is the fastest way.

Can I sell an inherited Apopka house without probate?

Not always. Where the estate is small enough or the owner died over two years ago, summary administration is available, and a personal representative's deed is not subject to doc stamp tax. Ask a Florida attorney which path fits.

What do I owe if property taxes are unpaid at closing?

Get a balance from the Orange County Tax Collector before closing. After April 1 an unpaid bill is delinquent, and certificates on unpaid items are sold by June 1.

A planned community

Palm Beach Gardens was planned from the start. On March 20, 1959, John D. MacArthur announced a plan to develop about 4,000 acres for 55,000 people. His first-choice name, Palm Beach, was refused, so he settled on Palm Beach Gardens to match his garden-city concept.

Streets and construction were routed around mature trees such as banyans. That heritage explains the tree canopy, waterways and master-planned grid that buyers notice on a drive-through, and it is also why the city cares so much about landscaping.

Permit rules to check first

Open permits and unpermitted work tend to surface during a buyer's inspection. Roof replacement, electrical, plumbing, mechanical work, window and door replacement and additions all need a permit, filed through the city's online system with plans, contractor details and a survey.

Work done without a required permit violates the Florida Building Code and city rules. The city lists these consequences: a stop-work order, higher fees and penalties, mandatory inspections with possible repairs or removal, project delays and complications in future property transactions. A county flood-hazard designation covers every municipality in Palm Beach County, so the exemption for single-trade permits under $7,500 does not apply in Palm Beach Gardens.

Trees and landscaping before you list

A Certified Arborist is on staff, and tree removal falls under Section 78-328 of the city code. A dead tree, palm or shrub should be replaced within one month. Brazilian pepper, Australian pine and melaleuca are prohibited, and planting beds need three inches of mulch. All types of organic mulch are allowed, xeriscape is encouraged, and dead branches should be trimmed before hurricane season.

After notice, an owner who leaves a violation uncorrected can be sent to the Special Magistrate, with fines and liens possible. Walk the lot before the photographer arrives so no banned plant or dead tree shows up in a buyer's inspection report.

The city follows the South Florida Water Management District watering schedule for Palm Beach County. To confirm a lot is inside city limits, and therefore under city code, check the municipality field on the appraiser's site.

A seller may mention these programs to a buyer who plans repairs. The Single-Family Home Improvement Grant is for owner-occupied, homesteaded houses within city limits, with household income capped at 120 percent of area median income and liquid assets at $50,000. It covers items such as roofs, windows, doors, garage doors, driveway overlays and exterior paint.

A separate Multifamily Improvement Grant, funded by the Workforce Housing Fund that comes solely from developer contributions, aims at condominium, apartment and townhome communities selected by age.   • A veteran with a permanent disability, 65 and over: a homestead discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Deferral: a March 31 application to the tax collector, available to permanent residents 65 or older.

County offices and the tax side of a sale

The county handles the tax side. The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets value and the Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends the bill. The collector distributes over $4 billion in property taxes a year, runs six service centers and requires a reservation for in-person visits.

The state deed tax is $0.70 per $100 of price, and the clerk adds recording charges that open at $5.00 for page one. Value disputes and denied exemptions each have a short petition window printed on the notice. If you are moving within Florida, ask about portability. The amendments in chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 roll.

Liens, lenders and unwanted occupants

Each has its own clock. A foreclosure sale follows a final judgment within a short statutory window, and a homestead owner should ask the clerk about surplus funds right after the sale. An unpaid tax certificate can ripen into a tax deed application after two years.

For a stranger living in a house, Florida offers a sheriff complaint, but false statements risk triple the fair rent plus fees. A tenant needs the written notice process instead. Heirs pay deed stamps and closing costs on an inherited house but no state estate tax for deaths after 2004. Look in on a vacant seasonal or inherited house often.

What to bring when you meet a buyer

Bring the deed or your last closing papers, a list of permits for any roof, window or electrical work, and the latest tax bill. If an association governs the community, add its contact details and the dues. A buyer paying cash still wants a clean title search, so clear any lien before the contract is signed. Walk the lot first for dead plants or banned species so the inspection has nothing to flag.

Which county appraises Palm Beach Gardens homes?

Palm Beach County. The county property appraiser values the house and the county tax collector bills it. The appraiser's municipality field confirms whether a lot lies inside city limits.

When was Palm Beach Gardens founded?

The founding announcement came March 20, 1959, when John D. MacArthur announced plans for about 4,000 acres. It is a planned community, so its roots are more recent than those of many Florida towns.

How much are deed stamps in Palm Beach County?

The standard Florida rate: $0.70 per $100 of price, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded.

Can I skip a permit for a small repair in Palm Beach Gardens?

Do not assume so. The exemption for single-trade permits under $7,500 does not apply here, and unpermitted work can bring a stop-work order, extra fees and trouble in a later sale.

Can a senior defer property tax in Palm Beach County?

Possibly. File Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31. A permanent resident 65 or older may defer the part of the bill above 3 percent of household income.

Before it became a suburb, Wellington was farmland that needed draining, and the Everglades still form its southwestern edge. The Acme Drainage District was created in 1953 to drain and protect more than 16,000 acres, and the village has since improved drainage to prevent flooding.

Lenders and insurers sometimes want an elevation certificate or a flood zone determination, and a seller who has them ready answers faster. Collect the survey, any paperwork from a past flood claim and the dates of roof and drainage work. If your lot borders a canal, say which one.

A cash sale moves along a short path. Hand over your survey, association documents and tax bill. The buyer reads them and sends an offer, often within days. Next a title agent looks for liens and drafts the settlement statement, you sign the deed, and the clerk records it and collects the tax.

Much of Jupiter's appeal is outdoors and river-based, and listings near these places can say so. The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse and Museum offers climbing tours of the 1860 lighthouse, run by the Loxahatchee River Historical Society. Dubois Park has 18.69 acres, 1,200 feet of beach front, a guarded swimming lagoon and the DuBois Pioneer Home, a listed historic property. Loxahatchee River Battlefield Park covers 680 acres, and John D. MacArthur State Park has 325 acres at the north end of Singer Island with kayaking, fishing and snorkeling. The Loxahatchee River Center adds aquariums and programs about the river.

Inlet Village, the area around the lighthouse, worked as a fishing village and port from the mid-1800s into the early 1900s, with a long wharf feeding the Celestial Railroad and St. Martin's Episcopal Church built there in 1899. The town's Community Redevelopment Agency, created in 2003, manages the coastal and Intracoastal strip from Inlet Village south to Ocean Way. If your house lies in that strip, ask the town what plans could affect a buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Is Jupiter a city or a town?

A town. Recording, assessment and tax collection all go through Palm Beach County.

When must a Jupiter buyer apply for homestead?

By March 1 of the tax year, provided they own the house and live there as of January 1. A missed March 1 waives that year's exemption.

Is the Palm Beach deed tax different?

No. It is the standard 70 cents per $100. Only Miami-Dade differs.

Do my Save Our Homes savings stay with the house?

No. A change of ownership resets value, though portability may carry savings onto a later Florida homestead once you file with the appraiser.

Who handles exemption changes?

The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser. Call 561.355.2866 or write to myexemption@pbcpao.gov for ownership or use changes.

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Sell Your Winter Haven House for Cash

Selling in Winter Haven?
We buy Winter Haven houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Which sales routes are open to a Winter Haven homeowner?

A homeowner in Winter Haven has three ways out: engage a listing agent, find a buyer yourself, or accept cash. They differ in speed and in how much effort lands on you. Putting the house on the market exposes it to the most buyers but invites showings, inspections and a lender's schedule. Cash usually closes faster and can work with the house as it is.

  • Listing agent: suits a house in good shape and an owner who can wait for a financed buyer.
  • Private sale: no commission, though contracts, disclosures and title work fall to you.
  • Cash buyer: works for houses needing repairs, inherited property, or anyone who needs a firm closing date.

The deed, recording and tax steps are the same on every route, and the same Polk County offices keep the records. Get each offer in writing and compare what you would net.

Lakes, docks and flood questions

The Chain of Lakes City has 50 lakes inside or touching its limits, and a house near the water draws water-related rules and buyer questions. The lake system has two navigable chains, 8 lakes in the North Chain and 14 in the South Chain, plus 13 more public lakes inside the city that are not linked for boat travel. The city sits at the top of the Peace River Watershed, with water flowing on toward Charlotte Harbor.

Lakefront owners should ask the building division what documents a dock, seawall or low-lying lot needs. The division publishes a dock requirements sheet and employs a flood plains manager. Lenders frequently want to know the flood zone, so gather any elevation or flood papers you have.

Housing in Winter Haven

Housing here ranges from older lake cottages to newer subdivisions, a mix that grew out of the citrus and tourism years. The city sits on the I-4 corridor between Tampa and Orlando, which shapes who shops for homes here. Cypress Gardens opened on Lake Eloise in 1936, and LEGOLAND Florida later opened on the same site.

An older cottage may have additions or repairs from several decades, so the permit trail matters more than the age on the deed. Before you list a cottage, gather receipts for the roof, wiring and plumbing, and any notice of commencement for past projects. Buyers near the lakes also like to know what is allowed on the shoreline, and a clear folder lets you answer quickly. Cash buyers read the same folder to decide how much to deduct for repairs, so a complete one tends to improve the offer.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Winter Haven house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Permit and paperwork snags

The most common snag is an open or unfinished permit. The Building and Permitting Division, at 490 Third Street NW, can look up what exists for your address, and its phone is 863-291-5695. Permit history for 2025 and older is searchable through the eSuite portal. Accela handles newer applications, plan review status and inspection scheduling, and inspection requests for 2026 permits can also be sent by text to the number the city prints.

  • Ask the division whether any permit at your address is still open or lacks a final inspection.
  • Locate approved plans, contractor invoices and any notice of commencement for past work.
  • Keep roof, pool and driveway paperwork together: the city lists a re-roof affidavit, swimming pool safety requirements and a driveway connection application among its forms.
  • Check demolition or dock records if either was ever done.

Fixing a paperwork gap before closing is usually cheaper than negotiating around it afterward.

Polk County property tax and your sale

In Polk, one office values your home and another mails the bill, and the closing statement has to settle that year's tax. Value is fixed on January 1, and a proposed notice shows up in mid-August. Bills in November give a 4 percent discount, one point less each month through February, and an unpaid bill is delinquent on April 1. Title companies typically split the tax by days of ownership.

Homestead is the big one. It can lower assessed value by up to $50,000, which saves about $750 a year on average, depending on millage. Applications are due March 1. Nothing carries over to a new house on its own, so you file again at the new address.

Expect the buyer's first bill to run higher than yours, because a transfer lets the appraiser reassess at full market-based value.

Exemptions that change at sale

A sale can end or change several benefits you may hold.

  • Homestead, with the Save Our Homes cap on yearly assessment growth. The limit follows CPI up to 3 percent, and the state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Portability: a new Florida homestead can inherit up to $500,000 of that benefit, claimed on the DR-501T with the new application.
  • Polk's limited-income senior exemption, adopted at the full $50,000 for residents aged 65 and up under an income ceiling the appraiser publishes.
  • Widow or widower and disability exemptions of $5,000 each, plus veteran exemptions.

Call the Polk appraiser at 863-534-4777 to learn how a pending sale touches each benefit.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Winter Haven houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deed tax and recording fees

Two charges attach to a Winter Haven deed: the state's documentary stamp tax and the Polk County clerk's recording fee. The tax runs 70 cents on every $100 of price. Anyone who signs the deed is liable, whoever the contract says pays. The clerk takes the tax at filing. Under Section 28.24(13), recording starts at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each additional page, with trust fund and technology add-ons. A title company can give you the full Polk total.

Who to contact in a Winter Haven sale

Closing step by step

After an offer is signed, the title company looks for liens, open permits and unpaid taxes. The closing agent then drafts a settlement statement covering deed tax, recording fees, your portion of the year's property tax and any lender payoff. You sign, the clerk records the deed, and you receive your proceeds. A cash buyer needs no mortgage approval or appraisal, so title work and open permits decide the timing. Ask your title company early for a list of anything that could slow things down, and settle it while you still have room in the schedule. If a permit is open, ask the division how to close it before the title search turns it up.

Frequently asked questions

Which Winter Haven sale route closes quickest?

Cash is generally fastest, since there is no mortgage approval or appraisal to wait for. Title work and open permits still affect timing, so look at those first.

Must lake or dock issues be fixed before a Winter Haven sale?

Not necessarily, but paperwork helps. Ask the city's building division, which posts dock requirements and has a flood plains manager, what is on file for your lakefront address.

Does my Polk County homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. The buyer applies on their own, and even you would file anew after moving to another Polk home.

Who pays the deed stamp tax on a Winter Haven sale?

Florida holds all signers liable, so your sale contract decides who covers it. The rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price.

Where do I check for open permits on a Winter Haven house?

Call the city Building and Permitting Division at 863-291-5695. Its eSuite portal covers 2025 and older permits, and the Accela portal covers newer ones.

Sell Your North Miami House for Cash

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in North Miami?
We buy North Miami houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Fast sale options in North Miami

A homeowner here can accept cash, list with an agent or go it alone, and the deadline plus the state of the house point to the right one. Whichever you choose, the deed, title search and Miami-Dade recording are identical. Repair cost, waiting time and your final take are what move.

  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies, a negotiable closing date, house taken as is.
  • Agent listing: a larger pool of buyers, with showings, an inspection period and a lender's schedule.
  • Owner sale: no listing fee, but the contract and buyer screening are yours.

Ask for two written offers and compare what you would keep after costs. Offers that look close can end far apart once repairs, stamp tax and carrying months are counted.

North Miami in brief

North Miami is a suburban city in northeast Miami-Dade County, about ten miles north of downtown Miami. The city counts more than 64,000 residents, which makes it the sixth largest in the county, and it incorporated on February 5, 1926. Biscayne Bay lies along the east side, and the Biscayne Bay Campus of Florida International University is nearby. Oleta River State Park and the Museum of Contemporary Art at MOCA Plaza are local landmarks.

Homes near the water and the university draw different buyers than homes inland, and renters and investors are a steady part of the market.

Local rules to check before you sell

Code compliance is the first office to call. It sends violation notices to the owner of record and not the tenant, which makes any open violation at your address your job to clear before closing.

Rentals are tightly limited. Advertising a rental for less than three months is prohibited, and so is renting for three months or less or renting more than four times in a twelve month period. If your house has hosted short stays, buyers will raise it, so stop them before you list.

  • Ask code compliance whether the address has open violations or an unfinished inspection.
  • Keep the right-of-way in front of the lot maintained, since owners are responsible for it.
  • Do not divide a single-family home into units without permits from the city's Building Department.
  • Ask whether a certificate of use or business tax receipt is attached to the property.

The code compliance phone line is on the city website. A call before you list costs less than hearing about a problem from the buyer's title company. If a violation is open, ask what it takes to close it and how long that usually runs, then weigh fixing it against selling as is at a lower price.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your North Miami house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Taxes and fees at a North Miami closing

The biggest state charge on a deed is the documentary stamp tax. Miami-Dade runs its own schedule of 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and a document conveying only a single-family dwelling skips the surtax. The rate in the rest of Florida is 70 cents.

Closing items on a North Miami deed

The statute adds small extra charges per page, so the title company's settlement statement shows the final recording total. Mortgage payoffs, association fees and prorated property tax come out of your proceeds at closing.

County tax bill and homestead

Assessed value is locked in on January 1, and November brings the tax collector's bills. The Miami-Dade appraiser's homestead page sets March 1 as the application deadline and accepts late filings until the cutoff on the proposed tax notice, usually 25 days after mailing. Renewal receipts do not go to properties with a change of ownership, deeds by warranty or quitclaim included.

The exemption belongs to the owner and does not stay with the house. A new buyer applies on their own, and the sale moves the assessed figure up to market level on the next January 1.

Amendment 3 and homestead exemptions

Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year. For owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, it raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028. From 2029 the amount is adjusted for positive consumer price index changes, and the school board portion stays at $25,000.

Newcomers are treated differently. Someone who becomes a Florida resident after the start of 2027 may start with up to $50,000 against non-school taxes, and generally reaches the higher amount in the fifth year of holding a homestead. That five-year rule is subject to federal constitutional limits and to implementing legislation.

Do not quote a buyer's future tax bill in a listing. Send buyers to the county appraiser's homestead page and phone number and let them confirm what applies to them.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Miami houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited or tenant-occupied houses

Yes to both, with strings attached. For an inherited house, the title company wants to see who may sign: probate letters, or proof the property passed outside probate. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's list of documents that owe no stamp tax.

With a tenant, hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. Some cash buyers accept the tenant and others want the unit empty at closing. North Miami limits short rentals, so confirm any short-stay use was lawful before you describe it.

Moving the house to a relative first can add cost, since quitclaim deeds are on the taxable list and may change how the county treats ownership.

What is a sensible timeline for a sale?

Clean title lets a cash sale close in as little as a couple of weeks. Add a lender and the appraisal and loan approval stretch the schedule. Allow time for payoff letters, an association estoppel and clearing any permit or violation.

  • First week: gather the deed, tax bill, payoff and association papers.
  • Next: pick an offer and a closing date.
  • Then: title search, lien and violation clearing, signing appointment.
  • Closing: signing before witnesses or a notary, then recording.

A contract with a firm date and a plain list of seller repairs prevents the most common slips. If anyone on the deed lives far away, ask the closing agent about remote signing arrangements early so the date does not slide.

Frequently asked questions

What is the stamp tax rate on a deed in North Miami?

Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and the surtax is not due when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Your title company can give the figure for your deed.

Can I rent the house short term while it is listed?

No. Rentals of three months or less are prohibited, as is renting more than four times in twelve months. Check with code compliance before any short stay.

Does the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?

No. The buyer applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the sale resets assessed value to market level the next January 1.

Who is responsible for a code violation notice at my address?

The city addresses the notice to the owner. A tenant should speak with the landlord, but plan to clear the violation before closing.

What is Amendment 3 and when does it start?

Voters approved it on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year, raising the non-school homestead exemption for eligible owners.

About Margate

Margate is in Broward County. It was created as the Town of Margate on May 30, 1955 and took city status in 1961. The city covers about nine square miles with 30 miles of canals, sits 7.5 miles from the Atlantic and is roughly 20 minutes from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport and Port Everglades. It provides its own police, fire and emergency medical services, water, wastewater and stormwater service, and it has 19 parks and recreational facilities.

  • Margate runs its own water and sewer, so request a final meter reading from the city at closing.
  • Canal frontage and distance to the coast are worth stating in a listing.
  • A buyer from outside Florida may ask about insurance, so gather your policy details.

Selling after a foreclosure suit starts

A Margate owner can still sell before the court sells the house for them. The lender files suit in Broward County and has to win a final judgment before the clerk sets any auction, which usually leaves more time than people expect.

After judgment the auction falls no later than 35 days and no sooner than 20 days out, unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031). Notice runs for two consecutive weeks, the winning bidder posts a deposit, and 10 days of objection time follow the certificate of sale. Under s. 702.10 a lender can seek a faster order to show cause, but a granted homestead exemption on the latest roll creates a presumption of owner occupancy, which keeps a Margate homeowner on the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

Surplus money after an auction

Whatever remains after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The judgment carries a notice about it, and homestead owners are told to check in within 10 days.

File your claim before the clerk reports the money as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your terms usually leaves more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and hands you the balance.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Margate house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Early-payment discounts on Margate tax bills

Bills arrive in November, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Paying early earns a sliding discount.

Early-payment discounts on a Broward tax bill

Relief exists for owners who are short of cash. A homestead owner can defer part of the bill by filing Form DR-570 by March 31 following the assessment year. The deferral covers the amount above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent when the permanent resident is 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

Tax certificates and tax deeds

Skipped taxes lead to a certificate auctioned by June 1, with bidders competing to accept the lowest interest in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The certificate holder is barred from pressing the owner for payment during the first two years, counted from April 1 of the year of issue.

After that, a tax deed application can be filed for a $75 fee (s. 197.502). The clerk runs the auction, and on homestead land the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value. Before listing, ask the Broward tax collector whether any certificate is attached to the parcel.

What to gather before talking to a buyer

Round up the papers a buyer will ask about first so the offer matches the house's true condition. Missing paperwork is a frequent reason closings run late.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • Your newest tax bill, plus a note of any certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

Florida requires a land transfer to be written and signed in front of two witnesses, and witnessing may happen by audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Plan signing early when an owner lives out of state. For exemption questions, call the Broward County Property Appraiser at 954-357-6830.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Margate houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Which offers suit an owner in a hurry?

A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and repairs become the buyer's job.

Get the closing date, the payoff and each fee on paper first. Ask whether the deposit can be refunded, who picks the title company, and how a request for more time would be handled. Comparing two or three written offers with the same lines filled in helps you spot the weak ones fast.

If you plan to stay a few weeks after closing, ask for a short rent-back in writing, with a daily rate and a move-out date. Take photos of the house at handover so both sides agree on its condition.

Services for older sellers and retiree buyers

The Northwest Focal Point Senior Center serves adults age 60 and older in the city and county, with transportation, an eldercare advocate, home energy assistance and meals. An older owner selling to move closer to family can ask the center what help is available before the move, and retiree buyers may ask about these services too.

The city also has a fire department rated ISO Class I and a Community Redevelopment Agency created in 1996. Keep your listing description plain and let a buyer confirm the details with the city.

From signed contract to funds in hand

After you sign, the title company runs a search for mortgages, liens and any tax certificate. You then review a settlement statement showing payoff, deed tax, recording and any prorated taxes. At signing the deed is witnessed, recorded with the clerk, and the balance is sent to you.

If your mortgage is in default, give the title company the lender's contact information and any court papers so the payoff can be confirmed. Sell before the auction date and you keep control of the price and the timing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting a Margate house ready

Start outside. Margate's canals and tree-lined streets make curb appeal matter, so trim hedges, clear gutters and pressure wash the driveway. Inside, fix leaks, stains and sticking doors. Buyers from out of state often ask about the roof and the air conditioning, so note their ages and keep the receipts.

If you plan to take a cash offer as is, you still gain by listing the problems you know about. A buyer who sees a clear list can price the repairs without padding the offer for unknowns.

Frequently asked questions

What is the gap between foreclosure judgment and auction?

The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031).

Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?

Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?

No. A deed application cannot be filed until two years have run from April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what clearing it would cost.

How does the Florida tax deferral work?

The owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector, deferring the part above 5 percent of last year's household income.

Who provides water and sewer in Margate?

The city provides water, wastewater and stormwater service, so a closing should include a final utility reading.

The Coconut Creek market in Broward County

Coconut Creek had an estimated 58,626 residents in mid-2025, up from 52,909 in 2010 and 57,833 in 2020. Owner-occupied homes had a typical value of $309,600 over 2020 through 2024. Owners occupy 64.8% of the housing. Rent at the midpoint is $2,102 a month, so owners of rental units can set that income against what a sale would bring.

Check whether your home belongs to a homeowner or condominium association. Its rules can add steps to a sale, and the vacation rental affidavit on the city's site refers to notice to a mandatory association.

Vacation rentals and a sale

The city's vacation rental page says its regulations do not prohibit vacation rentals or limit how long or how often a home is rented. They exist to protect neighborhoods and life safety, and every vacation rental must register and obtain a Vacation Rental Certification.

If you hold one, tell buyers up front. The certification counts toward what a rental earns, and a buyer who wants one must file a fresh application. The city lists these details:

  • Application or registration fee: $250. Renewal: $250. Re-inspection: $40.
  • Registrations expire annually and must be renewed before September 30.
  • Fire safety and code compliance inspections come before the first certificate, under Ordinance No. 2021-003, by appointment.
  • Packet items: a Florida DBPR transient public lodging license, Florida Department of Revenue sales tax registration, a Broward County business tax receipt and Broward tourist development tax registration.

The city also offers a notarized-letter option for owners whose booking sites collect taxes. Ask the city's business tax office for the current form.

Landlords: what to do before selling a rented house

Start with the lease. Ending a tenancy that renews monthly requires notice of at least 30 days. A tenant behind on rent is owed a 3 day written notice, counted without weekends or court holidays. The state's eviction statute lays out the notice and the court steps, so follow them if a tenant must leave before closing.

If the tenant stays through the sale, the rent keeps flowing and no gap opens between occupants. Put the lease, the security deposit amount and the rent ledger in the contract package.

Broward deed tax and recording fees

Deeds in Broward pay the same 70 cents per $100 of price charged across the state, with Miami-Dade the lone exception. The base includes any mortgage or encumbrance, assumed by the buyer or not. The Broward clerk collects at recording, and the state can pursue every person on the deed whatever the contract says.

Statute prices recording on its own: $5.00 buys the first page, each later page is $4.00, and other per-page fees are extra. Ask the closing agent to list every one.

Homestead and tax dates

Every parcel is assessed as of January 1. To receive a homestead exemption of up to $50,000, apply by March 1 and show the home was your permanent residence on January 1. The first $25,000 reaches every tax. The second $25,000 applies only above $50,000 of value and only to non-school taxes.

Under Save Our Homes, assessed value grows each year by 3 percent or inflation, whichever is less. A sale sends the parcel back to just value the following January 1. November brings the bills, with a discount starting at 4 percent and shrinking to 1 percent by February. April 1 marks delinquency. A mid-year closing means the title company splits the tax with the buyer.

Foreclosure or an inherited house

Foreclosure here is a court matter. The clerk runs the auction 20 to 35 days after final judgment, or later with the lender's consent, and a sale before then pays the lender out of proceeds. Heirs selling an estate home may use summary administration when non-exempt assets total $150,000 or less, or when the owner died more than two years ago.

Either case rewards an early call to the servicer, a Florida attorney or the probate clerk. A cash buyer can work around those dates, yet the court sets the schedule.

What if property taxes go unpaid?

Delinquency starts April 1. The tax collector then sells certificates on the unpaid bills by June 1, and bidders offer the lowest interest rate they will accept, in quarter-point steps. For two years after April 1 of the issue year, the holder may not seek money from the owner.

Following that period a tax deed can be requested for a $75 application fee, and the clerk conducts the sale. A homestead's opening bid includes half of its assessed value. Delinquent taxes get paid from closing proceeds. Ask the title company for an exact payoff.

Florida tax breaks that may apply

Seniors aged 65 or older may qualify for an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000, if a local ordinance provides it and household income is under the limit. A 10 percent or greater disability, with an honorable discharge and Florida residency, brings a $5,000 cut in assessed value. A total and permanent service-connected disability may earn a full homestead exemption.

Homestead ends when you rent the home or move out, though a servicemember may rent without losing it. Ask the Broward property appraiser which exemptions sit on your parcel before closing.

Moving day and what follows

Once you have a contract, plan the handoff. Schedule your move for a day or two before closing so the house can be cleaned and photographed empty. Arrange to end service on trash, internet and any lawn or pool care, and notify the association if you have one. Ask the title agent exactly when funds will be released, and keep a copy of the signed deed and settlement statement for your records. If you sold a rental, give the tenant's contact and deposit details to the buyer in writing so nothing is lost in the transfer.

Before a quick Coconut Creek closing

Quick sales still need paperwork. Open permits and code violations can delay a closing, so ask the Building Division and the code office about your address. If you have an association, contact it early, because approvals can run longer than a buyer expects. Pull together your deed, latest tax bill and payoff letters. Weighing cash against a listing? Take commission, repairs and holding costs off the listing number and choose whichever result suits your deadline. Before signing day, review the title agent's draft settlement statement line by line.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Coconut Creek house that has a vacation rental certification?

Yes. The certification belongs to the current owner, and a buyer planning short-term stays has to register separately. Check the city's annual September 30 renewal date and your fee status before closing.

Do I owe the city anything before I sell my Coconut Creek home?

Call the Building Division about open permits and the code office about open violations, since both can hold up closing.

How quickly can a cash sale close here?

Usually faster than a listing, because no lender or appraisal is involved. HOA approval, title work and lien payoffs can still add days.

Who pays Broward deed tax on a sale in Coconut Creek?

The state holds every person on the deed liable, and contracts typically assign it to the seller. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

What happens to my Coconut Creek tenant if the house sells?

The lease generally carries on unless it ends or the proper notice is served. A tenant renewing monthly is owed at least 30 days of notice.

Fastest way to sell in Sarasota

A cash offer closes soonest in Sarasota, since no lender approval, buyer appraisal or round of repair haggling stands in the way. Listing the house takes longer but shows it to more buyers, and that can lift the price.

Buyers here weigh bay access, flood and wind exposure, and the age of the house. The owners in the biggest hurry often hold a house they inherited, one that is overdue for repairs, or a rental with someone still living in it. Each situation has its own rules, covered below.

  • Cash purchase: the quickest close, bought as-is, at a negotiated figure.
  • Agent listing: more prep work, a wider market.
  • Private sale: the contract and closing paperwork are yours to run.

Old plats and your lot

Sarasota grew through recorded plats. Newtown, near downtown, started on April 20, 1914, when its original plat was filed with Manatee County with 96 building lots, and a first addition on August 6, 1914 added 74 more. Lot lines, easements and setbacks on an old plat decide what a buyer may build or add.

If you have an old survey, keep it with the sale papers. If not, a title agent can tell you what the recorded plat shows for your lot.

Sarasota County Property Appraiser

The office is at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota, phone 941.861.8200. It sends a TRIM notice each August, and you can pull a copy of yours through the property search on its website. The site also links Hurricane Evacuation Levels, which buyers sometimes ask about for a specific address.

It also urges owners to enroll in the Clerk's free fraud alert, which sends an email whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name.

Tax calendar for a Sarasota seller

Florida property tax calendar as it applies in Sarasota County
EventTiming

Bills mailed; 4 percent discount for payingNovember
Discount drops to 1 percentFebruary

The calendar comes from the state's taxpayer guide. If you sell and then buy again within Florida, part of a Save Our Homes benefit can move to the new house, but only inside the filing window (Save Our Homes guide).

On the next January 1 after a sale, the parcel goes back to just value. Do not give a buyer a tax estimate built on your current bill.

What the deed transfer costs

A Sarasota County deed carries state stamp tax of 70 cents on each hundred dollars of price, with an existing loan added into the figure (s. 201.02). The state can pursue anyone on the deed, but the sales contract usually names one side to pay.

The clerk's recording charge is set by s. 28.24 and shows up as a separate line at closing. The stamp tax does not apply to a spousal homestead deed whose only consideration is a mortgage, or to a deed in a divorce that transfers the marital home (stamp tax page).

Inherited, rented or in default

  • Inherited: a modest estate ($150,000 or less, exempt items aside) or a death over two years ago can qualify for summary administration (s. 735.201). No Florida estate tax applies to anyone who died after 2004.
  • Tenant: nonpayment of rent starts with a three-day notice that leaves out weekends and court holidays (s. 83.56). A breach the tenant can fix gets seven days.
  • Default: after a judgment, the clerk's sale comes 20 to 35 days on, and whoever bids highest leaves a 5 percent deposit (s. 45.031).

Selling ahead of that auction leaves price and timing with you. Surplus from an auction is claimed through the clerk.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sarasota houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Preparing the house and paperwork

Gather the deed, survey, latest tax bill, permit finals and any insurance claim records. Coastal buyers press hard on flood and storm history, so be ready to explain past water or roof damage.

  1. Request a payoff statement from every lender or lienholder on the property.
  2. Check with the Sarasota County Property Appraiser on whether homestead is active.
  3. Sign up for the Clerk's fraud alerts if the house will sit vacant.
  4. Ask your title agent which documents the Sarasota County recording office wants.

Doing these four things early cuts surprises whether you list or take cash. Bring copies to your first meeting with the title agent, along with a photo ID and the names of everyone on the deed.

Storm risk questions from buyers

Insurers and buyers both want to know your address's hurricane evacuation level, which the county publishes. Check yours ahead of listing, so your answer is ready.

Roof age, window protection and past claims usually follow. Permit records for roof and window work help, as do the product approvals and installer paperwork from those jobs. A permitted, documented roof is easier to insure and to price. A house with gaps in its records can still sell, usually to an investor who plans repairs after closing and builds that cost into the offer.

  • Pull permit finals for roof, windows and electrical.
  • Collect insurance declarations and any claim letters.
  • Write down any past water intrusion and the repair that followed.

What a cash sale skips

With a cash buyer there is no loan to approve, so the bank's appraisal and underwriting steps vanish and the closing date depends mostly on title work. Liens and mortgages still get paid from your proceeds, and the deed still has to be signed and recorded.

Cash buyers expect to take a Sarasota house as it stands, so you can skip repairs, cleaning and showings. What you give up is some price. Compare a cash figure with what a listing might bring after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs, then choose.

  • Ask for the offer in writing, with the closing date and who pays closing costs.
  • Have your payoff statements ready before you accept.
  • Tell the title agent early if the house has tenants, an estate in progress or a pending foreclosure.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Which office handles which record?

Several offices touch a sale, and a call to the wrong one can burn a few days. In Sarasota County, the appraiser, tax collector and clerk of the circuit court are elected county officers, separate from city hall.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and the TRIM notice, at 2001 Adams Lane.
  • Tax collector: sends the November bill, collects payment, and sells certificates when an account goes unpaid.
  • Clerk: files the deed, takes the stamp tax at recording, and conducts foreclosure and tax deed auctions.
  • City of Sarasota: planning, historic preservation and building matters inside city limits.

Keep each office's name and number in one folder. A title agent can fill gaps, but the owner is usually the first person asked when a record looks wrong.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I find my Sarasota TRIM notice?

On the Sarasota County Property Appraiser's website. Search for your parcel and click the TRIM button. Notices are mailed each August.

Does Sarasota County charge a different deed tax rate?

No. Sarasota County uses the usual 70 cents per $100, and Miami-Dade is the lone exception in the state.

Can I sell a Sarasota house that needs major repairs?

Yes. Cash buyers purchase as-is. A financed buyer may require repairs, because the lender's appraisal has to support the loan, so condition decides which buyers can close.

Whom should I contact about a Sarasota parcel record?

The county property appraiser, at 941.861.8200 or 2001 Adams Lane.

Do I lose my Save Our Homes benefit when I sell?

On that house, yes, because the assessment goes back to just value on the next January 1. Portability can move part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead if you meet the filing rules.

Which sale route fits a Bradenton owner in a hurry?

Start with your deadline. An agent listing can reach the highest price but requires prep and showings. Selling by owner saves a commission and costs time. A cash company gives up some price in exchange for a firm closing date.

Your house is in Manatee County, on the Manatee River, which means three county offices handle most of the file. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions, the Tax Collector bills you, and the Clerk records the deed. City permits are separate, so ask your agent or closing company which departments must sign off.

  • Decide whether you can wait through a listing cycle.
  • Decide whether repairs are worth doing before a sale.
  • Check for liens, back taxes or unpaid utility balances.

Neighborhoods that draw buyers

The river and downtown do most of the work. The Bradenton Riverwalk runs 2.03 miles between the Green and DeSoto bridges along the Manatee River, with a lighted path, fishing, a skate park, a playground and a splash pad. It stays open around the clock, while other city parks open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Near downtown is the Village of the Arts, between 9th Street West and 14th Street West and between 9th Avenue West and 17th Avenue West. It holds more than 275 properties, a blend of early twentieth-century bungalows, Florida Cracker homes and later additions, and a monthly Artwalk runs on the first Friday weekend. Sellers of small older homes there can lean on that identity in a listing.

Manatee County Property Appraiser dates

The county follows the statewide calendar. Use the table below to plan the year around a sale.

Annual dates for Manatee County owners
MonthEvent
January 1Date of assessment
March 1Deadline for homestead, low-income senior, widow and widower, non-profit exemptions and agricultural classification

The deadline to petition on value is printed on the TRIM notice itself, so read it when it arrives. Value appeals are separate from exemption denials, which follow the July timeline.

Homestead and Save Our Homes

A homestead exemption can reach $50,000. The first slice of $25,000 counts against every levy. The second slice of $25,000 leaves school taxes alone and begins above $50,000 of assessed value. Once you are in, Save Our Homes keeps yearly increases to the smaller of 3 percent or inflation.

Your buyer starts without the cap, since a new owner means the property goes back to just value a year later. If you purchase another Florida home, portability can move part of your accumulated savings along, capped at $500,000 of the gap, provided the new homestead begins inside the three-year window.

Leasing the house ends homestead. A move-out followed by a rental changes your exemption on the next roll.

The tax bill at closing

Tax bills come in November and carry a discount that shrinks from 4 percent to 1 percent by February. Anything paid after March 31 is late.

If your closing falls somewhere between November and March, expect the closing agent to split that year's bill between you and the buyer. The Manatee County Tax Collector can tell you what was billed and whether a discount applied. Unpaid taxes lead to certificate sales by June 1, so clear any balance at closing to keep the title clean.

How do I compare offers on a Bradenton property?

Judge each one by what reaches your account and how likely the deal is to close. A list price means little until you subtract commissions, repairs, carrying costs and weeks of waiting, and a cash figure deserves the same math.

  • Count the months you would keep paying the mortgage, insurance and utilities while a listing sits.
  • Price the repairs a lender-backed buyer would demand after an inspection.
  • Request proof of funds from cash buyers, or a loan commitment letter from financed ones.
  • Find out the closing date, and whether it can slide if moving takes longer than planned.

Two offers at the same price can end up thousands apart once those items are counted. Ask a title agent to draft a mock settlement statement for each before you choose.
