Deed charges at a Bradenton closing

In Manatee County a deed carries 70 cents of stamp tax per $100 of consideration, the same rate used everywhere in Florida except Miami-Dade. The state can collect from anyone named on the document, so the closing agent normally pays it at recording.

Recording charges come on top. Section 28.24 sets them page by page. The Clerk of the Circuit Court can quote a total for your exact document.

  • The tax reaches warranty, special warranty, quit claim and trustee's deeds alike.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure is taxed as well.
  • Have the closing agent total both lines before signing day.

Preparing the house and the file

A seller with a tidy file closes faster. Before accepting an offer, collect your deed, recent tax bills, payoff statements and any warranty or inspection records. Walk the house and make a list of known problems, such as a leaking roof or an older air handler, so you can disclose them honestly and price the sale to match. If a repair is cheap and obvious, finishing it can raise an offer more than it costs, but skip large projects when a cash buyer will take the house as it stands. Keep copies of everything you sign.

Selling an inherited home

Heirs can sell once someone gains court authority to sign for the estate. Summary administration under section 735.201 is a shorter court process. It fits estates under $150,000 in non-exempt assets, or cases where the owner died over two years ago.

Creditors face a cutoff too, tied to publication of the notice to creditors or service on a known creditor. Florida has no estate tax for deaths after December 31, 2004. A deed from a court-appointed personal representative is not taxable. Speak with a probate lawyer before you advertise or sign anything.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Tenants and lender trouble

To end a monthly tenancy, give notice at least 30 days before the rental month ends (section 83.57). For unpaid rent the notice is three days, with weekends and court holidays left out (section 83.56). Check the lease before promising a buyer an empty house, and file a copy of each notice you serve.

If a lender has already sued, a final judgment sets a public sale not less than 20 or more than 35 days out, under section 45.031. The winning bidder posts a deposit, and objections have a short window after the certificate of sale. Talk with a Florida attorney and the county clerk about surplus funds and timing.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Bradenton and which county handles my taxes?

Bradenton lies on the Manatee River in Manatee County. The county Property Appraiser sets value, and the Tax Collector mails bills in November.

What is the homestead deadline for Manatee County?

March 1 of the year the exemption should apply. The same date covers the low-income senior, widow, widower and non-profit exemptions.

Can I appeal my Bradenton property value?

Yes. TRIM notices go out in August and a 25-day appeal period begins at mailing. The exact deadline for a Value Adjustment Board petition is printed on the notice.

Does a sale change the assessed value?

For the buyer, yes. New ownership resets the property to just value on the next January 1, and their Save Our Homes cap starts fresh once they claim homestead.

How much time passes before a foreclosure sale?

Expect a sale date 20 to 35 days after final judgment, later if the plaintiff agrees. Confirm specifics with your attorney.

Ways to sell in Bonita Springs

When time matters in Bonita Springs, a cash buyer is the usual answer. A listing has to wait on open houses, inspections and whoever is financing the purchase. Many owners in town are dealing with storm repairs, a seasonal second home or an estate, and each of those pushes you toward a different route.

  • Cash buyer: accepts flaws as they stand, and you negotiate the closing day.
  • Agent: broader exposure, with repair and lender dates built into the schedule.
  • Solo sale: you run the contract and the recording yourself.

Lee County's property appraiser, tax collector and clerk each hold part of your file, so begin with the property record for your address. Bonita Springs became a city by vote in 1999, and homes range from older streets to golf course communities. Say plainly how old your house is and what has been updated, and keep permits and repair records ready for the buyer.

Selling a house damaged by Hurricane Ian

If your house was damaged, report it to the Lee County Property Appraiser. The new value is set as of the January 1 after the event, and the damage is factored in. Owners can email hurricaneupdate@leepa.org or use the reporting link on the appraiser's hurricane page.

Residential owners can apply for a partial tax refund depending on the extent of damage and whether the property could be used, with details in section 197.319 of the Florida Statutes. A rebuild that changes the property significantly will likely raise its value, while one similar to the old house should have a minimal effect. Permits are still required under each jurisdiction's process, and the FEMA 50 percent rule applies to substantial repairs. Before spending on a house you mean to sell, ask the city building office which rules reach your job.

For many parcels the appraiser issues a tax roll value letter that helps owners apply the FEMA 50 percent rule, which compares repair cost with the value of the structure. Vacant land, many commercial properties and condominiums may get no letter. There are deadlines for starting repairs if you want to keep a homestead on a damaged house, so email exemptions@leepa.org before deciding between repairing and selling.

  • Condominiums get no tax roll value letter, because the appraiser does not split land and building value for a whole complex.
  • Condo owners can work with their association on a private appraisal of the entire complex.
  • While repairing, do not register to vote or get a driver license elsewhere, or the homestead exemption could be jeopardized. Changing your mailing address is fine.

Lee County property taxes and a sale

Lee County values each parcel on January 1 and sends bills in November. After a sale, the next owner's assessment goes back to market the following January. Homestead relief reaches $50,000 and needs an application filed by March 1. Under Save Our Homes, assessed value may rise each year by the smaller of inflation or 3 percent. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

Lee County tax calendar for sellers
StepWhen it happens
Value dateJanuary 1 each year

Deed tax and recording

Florida's deed tax on a Lee County conveyance is 70 cents for each $100 of price. Each signer can be held to it by the state, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Statute sets the clerk's recording fees by the page. The deed itself must carry two subscribing witnesses. A deed from a court-appointed representative is left off the state's taxable list, and a spouse's homestead deed is exempt where a mortgage is the only consideration.

Inherited, rented or in foreclosure?

Every one of these cases is governed by a state timetable. An estate of up to $150,000, or one opened over two years after the death, may qualify for the shorter summary process, which can speed an heir's sale.

A landlord with a tenant behind on rent may serve written notice giving three days, not counting weekends or court holidays. Foreclosure sales are set 20 to 35 days after judgment.

Unpaid taxes lead to certificate sales by June 1, and a holder may seek a tax deed two years on. Get a payoff figure from the Lee County Tax Collector before you set a closing day.

  2. Ask your lender for a payoff and the tax collector for your balance.
  3. Check city permit records for open or unpermitted work.
  4. Weigh each route by the money left after taxes and recording fees.
  5. Sign the deed in front of two witnesses, then have the Lee County clerk record it.

A title agent usually handles the search and the settlement statement. Review that statement before signing day and ask about every line you do not recognize. If an offer depends on repairs, get the scope and the deadline in writing so a missed date does not turn into a dispute at the table.

Papers to gather first

Sellers who show up with documents in hand get quicker answers from buyers and title agents. Pull together your deed, the latest tax bill, any insurance claim file from storm damage, receipts for repairs and photos of finished work. If a contractor did the job, keep the invoice and any final inspection record. Seasonal owners who live elsewhere should also line up a way to sign remotely or name someone with written authority, because a closing date that depends on a plane ticket is easy to miss.

Closing day logistics

Plan your final week around three jobs. First, schedule utility shutoffs for the day after the deed is recorded, so the buyer is never left without service during the walkthrough. Second, hand over keys, garage openers, gate codes and any warranty paperwork for appliances or the roof. Third, confirm where your proceeds will be sent and who will wire them. Take dated photos of the empty house after you move out, which protects you if a buyer later questions its condition.

What a cash sale skips

Because a cash buyer needs no lender appraisal or loan approval, the weeks normally spent on underwriting fall away. Title work, payoff letters and tax balances still apply, and so does the deed signing. Get proof of funds, a closing date in writing and a clear split of fees from any buyer. Set the offer next to a listing estimate that already subtracts repairs, holding costs and commission, then choose the one that suits your deadline.

Is Bonita Springs in Lee County?

Yes, and the Lee County Property Appraiser values its parcels. Voters made it a city in 1999.

Do I need to tell the appraiser about hurricane damage?

Yes. Value follows the home's condition on the January 1 after the event. Residential owners may also apply for a partial refund under section 197.319.

Can I keep my homestead while repairing a storm-damaged house?

Yes, if you tell the appraiser you intend to repair or rebuild and make it your permanent residence. Avoid actions like registering to vote or getting a license in another county or state.

What is the doc stamp rate in Lee County?

It is 70 cents for each $100 of price. The state can look to any party on the deed, whoever the contract assigns it to.

Does my homestead exemption stay with the house?

No, it leaves with you. The buyer applies by March 1 for a new one, and the parcel is reassessed at market the January after the sale.

How fast can a Pensacola house sell for cash?

A cash sale of a Pensacola house can close in the time the title search and deed take, since no lender sits between you and the buyer. A listing instead waits on loan approval, an appraisal and a repair list from the buyer's inspector.

Pensacola is the Escambia County seat on Florida's panhandle coast, with a 2020 population of 54,312. Naval Air Station Pensacola anchors the local economy, and duty orders send families in and out on fixed dates. A seller leaving town for new orders often values a certain closing day over a top bid, and a cash sale lets you pick that day. Salt air and storm season wear on older houses here, so any buyer will look hard at the roof, windows and drainage.

  • Pick cash if a bad roof, plumbing or storm damage would worry a loan underwriter.
  • Pick a listing if the house shows well and you can wait out the buyer's financing.

Historic review districts

Check before you list. An Architectural Review Board looks at work in the city's historic, preservation and aesthetic districts, and Pensacola set up its first preservation ordinance and district lines in 1968.

What do buyers look for in Pensacola neighborhoods?

Downtown is the draw. Palafox Street is a Great Street with locally owned shops, restaurants and gallery nights, and the bayfront gives walkers and cyclists a path along the water. Parks near downtown include Plaza Ferdinand, Alabama Park and Plaza DeLuna. Pensacola Beach lies across the sound on Santa Rosa Island, with Fort Pickens and the Gulf Islands National Seashore nearby.

Buyers moving for the base, a hospital job or retirement all weigh the same basics, so open your listing or your cash-offer conversation with the features of your own street.

  • Walk to Palafox and the bayfront: strong draw for downtown houses.
  • Historic districts: charm, with design review on exterior changes.

Property tax dates and your closing

Values are fixed on January 1 each year, which means a summer closing leaves buyer and seller splitting a bill that has not been mailed yet. The county tax collector mails that bill in November, and the early-payment discount starts at 4 percent in November, then slides down to 1 percent by February.

Homestead status changes the picture. If you live in the house, you may exempt up to $50,000 of value by turning in Form DR-501 before March 1. Save Our Homes then limits yearly increases to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower, and the state chart puts the 2026 figure at 2.7 percent. The buyer is assessed at full market value starting the next January. Your own cap follows you only if you port it to another Florida homestead.

  • Property appraiser: value and exemption decisions.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, and the April 1 date when unpaid bills turn delinquent.

Closing charges on a Pensacola deed

Two charges hit the deed. The state taxes the transfer at 70 cents for every $100 of price, and a buyer's assumed mortgage counts toward that price. The clerk then bills $5.00 to record the first page and $4.00 for each page after it, with a few small per-page add-ons set by statute.

Everyone who signs the deed answers for the stamp tax, so the contract should name who pays it. Request the full settlement statement several days before closing and compare each line with your contract.

What if my Pensacola house has liens, a foreclosure or an unpaid estate?

Selling may still be possible. A court sets the foreclosure auction 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to wait, so a private buyer who closes fast can pay the lender off before that date. A small estate, $150,000 or less, can use summary administration, and creditors get a fixed window to file claims.

A Florida attorney can tell you which route fits your situation, and ask the Escambia County clerk how to record the deed once authority is in place.

If the house belongs to an estate, the person with court authority signs the deed, and the title agent will want proof of that authority before closing. Heirs who live out of town can usually sign by mail with a notary, which saves a trip to Pensacola. For a lien, the payoff letter shows the exact amount, and it comes out of your proceeds at the table, so you never write a separate check.

From offer to funds: the steps

  1. Send the address, mortgage balance and any tenant or lien details.
  2. Review the written offer, paying attention to repair terms and the closing day.
  3. A title agent combs the county record for liens and requests lender payoffs.
  4. Sign the deed in front of two witnesses.
  5. The clerk records the deed, then your proceeds are released.

Collect at least two offers, and hold on to your signed settlement statement. Put three questions to every buyer: how long the offer stays open, who pays for the title policy, and whether the price can drop after an inspection. Get the answers in writing, since that protects you if the closing date slips.

Before the first call, pull together your mortgage statement, newest tax bill, insurance claim history and a list of everyone living in the house. A cash buyer works faster with those in hand, and a title agent can start the record search the same day.

What a cash sale skips is worth listing. You do not stage the house, host open houses or wait through an appraisal that may come in under the price. You also avoid a buyer's repair demands after the inspection. What you still handle is the lien payoff, the tax proration and the deed signing, and those take the same few days on any Pensacola sale, cash or not. If the house is storm damaged, tell the buyer what is wrong and share any insurance claim paperwork so the offer reflects the real condition.

Frequently asked questions

Must I fix my Pensacola house before selling?

No. Cash buyers purchase as-is and lower the offer to cover needed work. If you are inside a historic district, ask the city which exterior jobs need board review.

Who handles the tax bill on a Pensacola property?

The tax collector mails the bill and the property appraiser sets the value. Check the balance with both offices before closing.

Do my homestead savings pass to the buyer?

No. The sale resets the value to market the next January 1. You can take your savings to a new Florida homestead through portability.

Why do deed taxes depend on my loan?

Because Florida adds a mortgage on the property into the price used for stamp tax, whether or not the buyer takes it over.

Is Pensacola in a flood or storm area?

The city is on the Gulf coast, so buyers ask about insurance and roof age. Ask your insurer for your policy history before you list, and keep the roof age and any past claim dates handy for the buyer's questions.

Is your mailing address inside Clermont city limits?

The city tells owners to search the address on the Lake County Property Appraiser site, open the Alternate Key and read the millage group. A plain number marks unincorporated Lake County, and letters such as GR or MI mark Groveland or Minneola.

The answer decides which building department issued your permits, which codes applied and which tax bill you will split at closing. Confirm it first, then request permit records from the right office.

Permits before you list

The city's Building Services FAQ says almost everything may need a permit, with exceptions such as replacing kitchen cabinets, flooring and painting. A homeowner can pull their own permit only for a residence they own and occupy, and they sign an owner-builder affidavit. The city also warns that a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself may be a red flag.

Buyers and their inspectors compare visible work to the record. A few items from the FAQ:

  • Fences need a permit, including repair and replacement. Height cannot exceed 6 feet behind the building line or 4 feet in front of it.
  • Tree removal needs a permit costing $25 regardless of how many trees, with a site plan of canopy, understory and palm trees.

Who owns which pipe?

The city draws a firm line. Your responsibility for water begins where the line meets the city-owned water meter, and for sewer it begins where your lateral joins the city main in the street. A leak or blockage on your side is your cost, and one on the city's side is the city's.

Homes with water pressure of 80 psi or more need a pressure-reducing valve under building codes, and the homeowner owns and maintains it. A failing valve or lateral turns up in inspections, so test yours before you list.

Florida deed tax and your tax bill

Lake County deeds bear the state's tax at 70 cents on each $100 of price. Whoever signs can be held liable, and the clerk collects when the deed is recorded. Your closing agent can show the figure before you agree on a price.

Value is set on January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, and a November payment earns 4 percent off. Once the house sells, the homestead value resets to full just value the next January 1. Falling behind on the mortgage

Foreclosures here run through the courts. Once final judgment is entered, the clerk schedules a public auction within 20 to 35 days, and the high bidder posts 5 percent. Leftover funds go to whoever claims them before the clerk reports them as unclaimed.

Lenders who want the faster order-to-show-cause route meet an obstacle on owner-occupied homes, because a homestead exemption on the latest tax roll creates a presumption that the owner lives there. If you sell before the auction, the payoff comes from the proceeds and equity may be left for you. Questions about timing belong with a Florida attorney or your servicer.

How does probate affect an inherited Clermont home?

An heir cannot sell until a court gives someone authority, normally a personal representative. Summary administration, a lighter court process, can apply to a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less, or to one where the owner died over two years back. A representative's deed under a probated will is among those that owe no deed tax.

Creditors have until three months after the first published notice, or 30 days after a known creditor is served, whichever ends last. Florida collects no estate tax for deaths after 2004. Agree on dates with the probate clerk and a title company before accepting an offer.

Offers, showings and closing day

When several buyers respond, line up their offers side by side. Look past the headline price to the closing date, any contingencies and who covers which costs. Schedule showings in blocks so your household is not disrupted all week, and keep valuables out of sight. On closing day, bring photo ID, your keys and garage remotes, and confirm in advance how and when your proceeds will arrive. Afterward, hold on to the final settlement statement and a copy of the recorded deed for your tax records.

Preparing paperwork for a quick close

Gather the deed, recent tax bills, lender payoff letters, permit records and any lease before you take calls from buyers. Have each buyer write down the price, closing date and the split of costs. An aging roof or unpermitted work should be disclosed early. A cash buyer can accept the property as-is and price the problem in. Often within a few weeks, because a cash buyer skips underwriting and the appraisal. Title work and liens can still set the pace. Get the offer and the closing date in writing.

Must a Clermont seller show a permit history?

A permit history is not required to list, but open permits can delay closing. Call Clermont Building Services to learn whether any permit at your address is unfinished and what inspections are needed.

What if my Clermont house has an old roof or unpermitted work?

An as-is sale is allowed, and cash buyers take houses that way. Disclose what you know, and expect a buyer to price in the repair or permit cleanup.

Who pays the Lake County deed tax?

Most contracts assign it to the seller, but the state can collect from any signer. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, so put the allocation in writing.

Does my homestead exemption survive a sale?

It ends with the sale. The buyer applies by March 1 for their own, and the parcel goes back to just value the following January 1.

Who buys a house fast in Pinellas Park, FL, and how?

A cash buyer in Pinellas Park makes an offer that does not hinge on a mortgage, so closing waits only on the title company's clean record. Putting the house on the market with an agent stretches things out: the buyer's bank must sign off on the loan, and an appraiser must agree with the price.

Pinellas Park was planned and built fast. F. A. Davis bought 12,800 acres on the peninsula in 1890, a developer arrived around 1909 or 1910 to start a cane sugar town, and Pinellas County was split from West Hillsborough in 1913. Houses here arrived in waves across a hundred-plus years, so age and condition can change from one block to the next.

Before you pick a route, decide what matters most: top price, a fixed closing day, or avoiding repairs. A house with old plumbing, a worn roof or a stalled estate often suits a cash buyer. A tidy house on a busy street may do better with an agent and a few weeks of showings.

Drainage and water

Water control was a founding project here. The first town newspaper, in March 1915, described a drainage district covering 14,000 acres with planned canals toward Boca Ciega and Tampa Bay. Buyers today still ask how a lot handles heavy rain, and your insurance history is the best answer you can hand them.

Say what you know about flooding, leaks or standing water, and hand over any past claim paperwork. Candor early prevents a late request for a price cut and covers you if questions surface after closing.

In your listing or offer call, name the nearest cross streets, and mention Park Boulevard if you are close to it. Stick to facts you can document.

Closing costs when you sell in Pinellas Park

The deed triggers a state documentary stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of the price, and a loan on the property is folded into that price. Recording is separate: the clerk takes $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each additional page, with minor statutory add-ons.

The tax is a shared liability of the signers, which is why the sales contract should assign it. Your title agent lists every charge, and any lien payoff is subtracted from what you receive.

If you are moving to another Florida homestead, portability can transfer part of your capped savings, provided the new homestead begins within three years.

If you owe back taxes when you sell, the title agent pays the balance out of your proceeds at closing and the account is cleared. You need not catch up first, but you should know the amount so the offer math is honest.

Can I sell if foreclosure or probate is involved?

Often yes. After final judgment, the clerk's auction is typically 20 to 35 days away unless the lender allows longer, and a private sale that closes first can wrap up the case on better terms. Have a Florida attorney confirm who has the right to sign the deed. Heirs can also expect the title agent to want proof of that authority before setting a closing date.

Steps from offer to payout

Most deals follow the same line, with the title agent coordinating.

  1. Collect your payoff letter, tax bill, survey and any lease copies.
  2. Compare written offers on price, closing day, repair terms and who pays which fee.
  3. Let the title agent order the record search and resolve liens.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses watching, which Florida's conveyance statute requires.
  5. The county clerk records the deed and collects the stamp tax, and then the agent pays you.

Take your own copies of everything signed. A Pinellas Park house that sat in a family for decades can carry old recorded items, such as easements or unreleased mortgages, and the title search is where those show up. Clearing them early keeps the closing date from slipping.

Before the signing, walk the house with your closing agent's checklist in hand: keys, garage openers, any warranty papers and the final utility readings. Leave the house in the condition the contract describes, since a buyer can delay funds if the walk-through turns up something new.

If you plan to buy another Florida home soon, tell your title agent so the homestead and portability paperwork is ready before the March 1 filing date.

What a cash sale leaves out: the appraisal, the buyer's loan approval and the round of repair haggling after an inspection. What it keeps: title work, payoff letters and the witnessed signing. Budget a few days for those no matter who the buyer is. Ask for the offer in writing, and ask how the buyer arrived at any repair deduction so you can check the math yourself. Compare at least two offers before you sign anything.

What happens to a tenant when a rental sells?

A tenant's lease, or a month-to-month arrangement, stays in force until it is lawfully ended. Under Florida's notice rules, unpaid rent gets three days, a lease breach gets seven days to fix it or leave, and a month-to-month tenancy needs 30 days to end. If a tenant contests anything other than payment, rent must be deposited with the court within five days or those defenses are lost. After a judgment, the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice.

Spell out the tenant's rights in the sale contract so the buyer knows exactly what comes with the property. A tenant who stays means giving the buyer the lease and deposit records before closing. A tenant who must go means finishing the notice process first, because an empty house is simpler to price and to close.

Frequently asked questions

What should I bring to a first call with a Pinellas Park cash buyer?

Does water history change what I disclose?

What is the stamp tax on a Pinellas Park deed?

Choosing a sale route in Ocoee

A seller in Ocoee can go cash, list with an agent or sell without one. Repairs, deadlines and how much of the price you want in your pocket decide it. The city lies in Orange County, so you answer to the county's tax bill and to a city fire assessment printed on that same bill.

  • Cash sale: a good match for a leaking roof or a closing date that cannot move.
  • Agent listing: a good match when the house shows well and you can wait through showings and loan approval.
  • Sale by owner: fits a seller willing to draft the contract and arrange the deed personally.

On any route, get the unpaid portion of the year's tax and fire assessment spelled out in writing at closing.

Ocoee's fire assessment

Ocoee adds a yearly non-ad valorem fire assessment to property tax bills to pay for fire protection, and it is one of the amounts split between buyer and seller at closing. An ordinance adopted on August 6, 2013 authorizes it within city limits, and it shows up on the bill mailed each November.

Taxes follow property value, while a special assessment follows the benefit a property receives from the service. Residential parcels are measured by dwelling units and non-residential buildings by square footage. The city's equivalent dwelling unit is 2,423 square feet, the size it treats as the average house, and each residential dwelling unit counts as one unit.

How the Ocoee fire assessment works
DetailWhat the city sets
AuthorityOrdinance No. 2013-010, adopted August 6, 2013
BillingOn the property tax bill mailed in November
Payment windowNovember 1 through March 31
Residential measureOne equivalent dwelling unit per dwelling unit
Equivalent dwelling unit size2,423 square feet
Early-payment discountSame discounts and penalties as ad valorem taxes
QuestionsCity Clerk's Office, (407) 905-3105

The city holds a public hearing each August at City Hall, 1 N Bluford Avenue, to set the final rate. Go by the line item on the current bill, not last year's number. The city mails a separate notice about the assessment and says plainly that it is not a bill. For parcel questions, the same clerk's office line is the place to start.

Fire protection, insurance and property values

Ocoee ties the assessment to its fire protection classification with the Insurance Services Office, known as ISO, which it wants to preserve. Stronger fire service can support higher property values and lower insurance rates, while weaker service can push values down and premiums up. Special assessments can only pay for fire protection, unlike general taxes.

A buyer will look at the insurance quote right next to the asking price, so get your own homeowner's declarations page and be ready to share the premium and coverage. If you received a renewal notice recently, keep it with the rest of your papers. The city's notice was written to explain a proposed increase, so check the current bill for the amount that applies to your parcel.

Orange County tax dates around a closing

The Orange County Property Appraiser sets your house's value as of January 1, and the tax collector mails the bill in November. Where your closing falls in the year determines how that bill is shared with the buyer. A tax estimator on the appraiser's website is meant for people planning to buy or sell, and it lets you preview the next owner's bill before you name a price.

  • By March 1 you file for any exemption.
  • In August a proposed-tax notice comes in the mail, and you have 25 days from it to petition on value.
  • November brings the bills, with a discount for early payers that gets smaller every month through February.
  • April 1 is the delinquency date, and certificates are sold by June 1.

Up to $50,000 of homestead exemption is available, stacked in two layers. Selling ends yours, and the next owner has to apply again.

Your capped assessment and the buyer

The cap does not pass on. Because a sale counts as a change of ownership, the assessment jumps back to just value and the buyer's opening bill can be far above yours. Buying another Florida home? Portability may let you carry part of your cap along, as long as the new homestead is established within three years of the January 1 of the year you left the old one. The portability form goes in with the exemption application, so talk to the property appraiser before you sign the next contract.

Building and zoning questions

The City of Ocoee takes development and building applications through its website, where building applications sit under Apply and development projects and annual budgets sit under Find. To see what construction is planned near your listing, begin with the development projects page. A buyer's agent will probably look there too.

Planning and Zoning meets on the second Tuesday of the month, and the City Commission sits on the first and third Tuesdays. Individual meetings are sometimes canceled, so confirm on the city calendar before you plan a visit. The home page also carries quick links for irrigation restrictions and sidewalk repair lists, which are the sort of things a new owner asks about on moving day.

Inspections tend to uncover unpermitted work. A porch, garage conversion or addition built without a permit is worth a call to the city's building staff before you list, to learn what it would take to close it out.

When a lender has sued

Foreclosure here goes through a judge, and the auction follows the final judgment by 20 to 35 days, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait. The high bidder puts down 5 percent. Bids above the debt produce surplus money, and homestead owners should ask the clerk about it within 10 days of the sale.

Selling before the auction lets you pay the lender from the proceeds and pick your own closing date.

Stamp tax on an Ocoee deed

Each deed carries stamp tax of $0.70 per $100 of consideration, and every signer is answerable for it. The Orange County clerk of courts collects the payment when the deed is recorded. Page-based recording fees and smaller per-name and technology charges come from section 28.24, and the settlement statement totals them.

Steps once you accept an offer

Expect the title company to hunt for liens and unpaid taxes, so collect payoff letters, your latest tax bill with the fire assessment line and any permit paperwork. The closing agent can explain how the fire assessment and property tax are split, and you can confirm it on the settlement statement. Cash buyers skip the appraisal and loan approval, the stages where financed deals often slow down. At signing you execute the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. If anyone on the title lives out of town, raise remote signing options early.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Ocoee fire assessment a tax?

It is a special assessment, and the city separates it from property tax. Taxes follow property value, while the assessment follows the benefit a property receives from fire protection. It still appears on the same November bill.

Who covers the fire assessment at an Ocoee closing?

The contract and the closing statement settle that. Most sales prorate the year's bill between seller and buyer, so look for the assessment line on your settlement statement and ask the closing agent how it was divided.

Where do I take questions about an Ocoee assessment notice?

Phone the City Clerk's Office at (407) 905-3105. The letter the city mails about the assessment is neither a bill nor a fine.

Does my Ocoee homestead exemption survive the sale?

No. The exemption follows your permanent residence and is lost once the home stops being that residence. File a new application on your next home by March 1.

Do I owe Florida estate tax on an inherited Ocoee house?

No. Florida's estate tax ended for deaths after December 31, 2004, and since July 1, 2023 personal representatives no longer file the old state forms. Probate steps and creditor deadlines still apply, so ask a probate attorney.

How a Fort Pierce owner can sell

Three paths are open: hire an agent, look for a buyer on your own, or accept cash from someone who takes the house in its current state. How soon you need to move and how long the repair list runs will point you to one.

  • Market listing: the biggest audience, with weeks added by showings and lender steps.
  • Going alone: you steer price and terms and carry the paperwork.
  • Cash purchase: fewer strings and a flexible date, at a price below what a fixed-up listed house might bring.

Line up the offers by what reaches your account after liens, tax and recording. The headline figure hides those costs.

Fort Pierce housing numbers

Fort Pierce is the St. Lucie County seat on the Indian River Lagoon, with an estimated population of 51,737 and incorporation dating to 1901. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $250,800 and the median gross rent is $1,217. Owners live in 49.5 percent of units, so close to half the homes are rentals and landlords are active buyers. Median household income is $47,072, which tells you price sensitivity is high and many buyers will need financing that tolerates an older house.

Investors weigh that rent against that value when they decide what to offer, and they usually ask about condition, tenants and insurance before price. Indian River State College also brings students and staff into the rental and starter-home market.

Why the waterfront matters

Houses near the lagoon face wind, water and salt, and buyers look hard at the roof, windows, drainage and any flood history. Water views appeal, but they also raise the questions an inspector and an insurer will ask. A cash buyer and a lender both start with the same paperwork.

  • Gather permit records for roof or window work. A short folder of invoices, dates and contractor names can answer an inspector's first questions before they are asked.
  • Keep insurance and repair invoices together.
  • Ask the county where your house sits on flood maps.

Deed tax and recording costs

Florida charges 70 cents of deed tax on each $100 of consideration, and the clerk bills separately to record. Under section 201.02(1)(a), a mortgage on the property counts as consideration even if the buyer never assumes it. The state also treats every party to the document as liable, whoever agreed to pay.

The recording amounts come from s. 28.24(13), and trust fund and technology charges are added. Your title agent shows the exact total on the settlement statement.

Property taxes and homestead around a sale

Taxes follow the January 1 assessment, so the bill issued in November covers the entire calendar year even if you sell in spring. In August the appraiser mails a notice of proposed taxes. To contest value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days. November payments earn a 4 percent discount. April 1 is when an unpaid bill goes delinquent, and by June 1 certificates are sold on those accounts.

Homestead needs DR-501 on file by March 1. Once you sell, the next January 1 resets the assessment to just value. Ask the St. Lucie County tax collector for the balance through your closing date.

Inherited, behind or rented

Each case has a state timeline you can plan around.

  • Inherited: a shortened probate called summary administration may fit smaller or older estates (s. 735.201).
  • Foreclosure: a public auction follows judgment within a short, fixed window (s. 45.031).
  • Tenant in place: a monthly tenancy ends only on 30 days' written notice before a period closes (s. 83.57).

Acting early gives you more choices than waiting for the sale date or the notice window to close. A deed needs two witnesses under s. 689.01, so plan the signing with a title agent.

Paperwork that speeds a closing

Delays at title usually come from missing records, not from the buyer, so have the trail ready.

  • The deed, or probate papers that show who may sign.
  • Written payoff figures from each lender or lienholder.
  • Permit records for roof, window, electrical or addition work.
  • Leases and rent history if someone rents the house.
  • Your latest TRIM notice and tax bill.

Ask the clerk for a lien search and the tax collector for a balance. Then go through the purchase agreement line by line to learn who pays each closing item. A fair offer states the price, the closing date, any repairs the buyer expects and who covers the doc stamp tax and recording fees.

A cash sale step by step

Acceptance sets the title company to work: it searches the record, orders payoffs and picks a closing date. You sign the contract, then the deed in front of witnesses. Loan balances and closing charges are deducted from what you receive. With no appraisal and no lender underwriting in the path, cash closings can move quickly. Be wary of any buyer who wants money from you first, and ask for every promise in writing.

Comparing offers fairly

Two offers with the same headline number can leave very different amounts in your pocket. Ask each buyer to list who pays the deed tax, the recording charges and the title policy, whether repairs will be demanded after inspection, and when the money moves. Check how long the offer stays open and what happens if something unexpected appears in the title search. A buyer who answers these questions plainly and in writing is easier to trust than one who promises the moon and leaves the details for closing day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

If foreclosure papers arrive

Do not set court papers aside. A foreclosure follows a schedule, and an owner who acts early has more choices than one who waits for the auction date. Get a written payoff from your lender so you know what a sale must cover, speak with a Florida attorney, and contact buyers while there is still time to close. If a sale pays off the loan, the case ends and any equity is yours. After an auction, ask the clerk how surplus funds are claimed.

Closing day

The title agent walks you through the settlement statement. Read each line, question anything unfamiliar and confirm the payoffs match the letters you collected. After the deed is signed and recorded, hand over keys and any garage remotes, and expect your proceeds by wire or check. Update your mailing address afterward so tax and insurance mail reach you, and keep a complete copy of the signed documents in a safe place for future reference and tax records.

Frequently asked questions

Is Fort Pierce a good place to sell quickly?

Demand is there, though buyers watch price closely. With median household income at $47,072 and median value at $250,800, a clean, fairly priced house moves fastest.

Which local figure should I check for my house?

Treat the $250,800 median for 2020 to 2024 as a rough yardstick at most. Your own house could be far from it, so collect written offers and recent comparable sales.

Who bills property tax in Fort Pierce?

Offices of St. Lucie County do. The appraiser sets value, the tax collector mails the November bill, and the collector can tell you the balance through your closing date.

Does a Florida deed need witnesses?

Yes, two subscribing witnesses are required under section 689.01, and they may watch by audio-video link.

Can an heir sell an inherited Fort Pierce house quickly?

Often, once title is cleared. Estates of $150,000 or less can use summary administration, and a deed from a personal representative owes no doc stamps.

Titusville sits along the Indian River in Brevard County, and its housing grew up around Kennedy Space Center. Before inviting offers, find your deed, the newest tax bill and a payoff letter from your lender, if you have a mortgage. That packet lets each buyer judge the house on the same facts.

Flood, water and older-house questions

The city rests on a dune ridge above the Indian River Lagoon, with Merritt Island and Cape Canaveral to the east and wetlands of the St. Johns River watershed to the west. Water, drainage and flood questions therefore come up in many sales.

Spanish Revival houses from the 1920s land boom and older riverfront homes still stand around town. If you own one, say so. Character and age cut both ways: some buyers pay extra for it, and others subtract the repairs. Regular rocket launches have also made the city a draw for space workers, and a buyer relocating for a job at the Cape often wants a short closing. That is one reason a seller with clean title can ask for speed.

  • Ask the Brevard County Property Appraiser for your parcel's flood zone before you list.
  • Keep elevation certificates, roof records and permits together for buyers.

Papers to gather for an older house

A buyer who sees dated records trusts the house more, and an investor can price repairs without guessing. Photograph period details such as stucco, tile roofing or original millwork, since a buyer who wants character will notice them.

  • List the year of the roof, panel and plumbing, if you know them.
  • Keep any termite or moisture reports in one folder.
  • Note any additions built without a permit, and ask the building department how to close them out.
  • Ask planning staff which zoning district covers your lot.

Call the building department to learn whether your address has open permits or code cases, because an unresolved item can stall a closing at the last minute. On a big lot, an investor may wonder about other uses, and the city is the one to answer that. For guest rentals, check the city's current code before telling anyone the house can run as a vacation rental.

The sale ends that protection, and the buyer starts at full just value the following January 1, so their bill may run well above yours. Buying again in Florida? Every one of these has a deadline. Courts schedule a foreclosure sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, with a 5 percent deposit from the top bid. A short probate path exists for estates of $150,000 or less, or when the owner died over two years ago.

Unpaid property tax turns delinquent on April 1. Certificates go up for sale by June 1, and two years later a buyer can apply for a tax deed.   5. The clerk records the deed and takes the deed tax.

A cash buyer brings no lender review, so timing hinges mostly on how clean the title is. Owe back taxes? The title company can ask the Brevard tax collector for a payoff and pay it out of your proceeds at closing.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer does not need a mortgage approval, so the deal avoids the lender's appraisal and the repair demands that sometimes follow it. You also skip staging, open houses and the weeks of waiting between a showing and a contract.

The trade is price. An investor builds repair costs and risk into the offer, so expect a figure under what a polished retail listing might reach. Compare the two honestly, counting the mortgage payments, insurance and tax bills you carry during a longer sale.

Before you sign anything

Read every offer for who pays which closing charges, whether the buyer may walk away after an inspection, and when you hand over keys. Ask a Florida attorney or title company to look at the contract if anything is unclear. Never sign a deed until you have seen the settlement statement and know what lands in your account.

If anyone is living in the house, sort out the move-out date in writing. If a relative co-owns the property or an estate is still open, every owner or the personal representative has to be ready to sign, or the closing will slip.

The Brevard County clerk of the circuit court records deeds and other land documents for the city.

Probably not. A change of ownership resets value on the next January 1, and your homestead does not pass to the buyer.

Yes. Ask the title company for a payoff figure from the Brevard tax collector, and tell it right away about any tax certificate on the house.

The city's permits page lists every permit it issues, and the City Services Directory covers anything you cannot find there. Building staff can tell you whether any permit on your address was never closed out. Better to hear that from them this week than from a buyer's title agent mid-contract.

The Development and City Projects page tracks traffic calming and large construction, so scan it for work planned near your block. Agendas and public notices are posted under City Meetings.

Deed tax and recording fees

Miami-Dade charges 60 cents for every $100 on a deed. The county adds a 45 cents per $100 surtax too, though a transfer of nothing but a single-family house escapes it. You can read the base rate in s. 201.02, and anyone whose name is on the document can be held responsible for it, regardless of what your contract assigns.

  • The clerk takes payment the moment the deed is filed.
  • Recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each after it (section 28.24), plus trust fund and technology charges.
  • Two people must witness your signature (section 689.01).

An itemized closing statement lets you check every one of these charges ahead of signing day.

Property taxes when you sell

Someone buying a Gables homestead you have held for decades can face a much bigger bill than yours, since the sale pushes assessed value up to just value.

  • Save Our Homes limits annual increases to 3 percent or the inflation figure, whichever is smaller.
  • Up to $50,000 comes off taxable value under homestead, with a March 1 filing date.
  • Leasing the house to a tenant ends the exemption.

Billing is the tax collector's job, not the appraiser's, and paying in November earns a discount that starts at 4 percent. Assessment questions can go to the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line, 305-375-4712.

If the house has a mortgage default, a tenant or an estate

Three situations, three separate timetables. Following a foreclosure judgment, the court auction is set 20 to 35 days later, so closing privately beforehand may save the equity you hold. If an estate is selling, the personal representative's deed is listed as non-taxable.

  • Small estates, meaning $150,000 or less of non-exempt property, can take the summary route in s. 735.201.
  • A month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' notice (s. 83.57).
  • Missed rent begins with a written demand giving 3 days.

A free Clerk of Court alert warns you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name, which helps if the house sits empty or came to you by inheritance.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Coral Gables houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps after you accept an offer

After you say yes, the deed is drafted, signed in front of two witnesses and recorded by the Miami-Dade clerk. Audio-video witnessing is allowed, which lets an owner in another state sign from home.

  1. Request a payoff statement from your lender and collect permit records.
  2. Find out whether your homestead status stops at closing.
  3. Have the title agent explain the split of this year's tax bill.
  4. Read the settlement statement slowly the day before.
  5. File away your copy of the recorded deed.

Planning to buy again in Florida? The portability form goes in alongside the application for the new homestead.

Senior and veteran exemptions

Relief for older owners and for veteran owners rides on the homestead, so it stops when you sell. The Miami-Dade appraiser lets owners file widow and veteran disability exemptions online.

  • A veteran over 65 with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Tax deferral requests are due at the tax collector by March 31.

Holding one of these? Ask the appraiser how it is treated at closing and whether it can be claimed on your next home.

What a cash sale skips

Cash removes the lender from the picture. No appraisal, no underwriting queue, no repair list handed down by a loan officer. Title still has to be clean, though, so liens, unpaid code charges and open permits get settled before or at the closing table.

That suits a house with postponed maintenance, a tenant living in it, or a seller racing a move date. If the place is in good condition and you have time, a retail buyer may bring a better price. Collect at least two offers and ask each buyer for proof of funds and a written closing date.

Bring photo ID, keys, garage openers and any warranty papers to closing. The title company shows you where to sign, and your proceeds arrive by wire or check once the deed is recorded.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork to collect first

Preparation trims days off almost any sale. Put the deed, the newest tax bill, a lender payoff figure and permit records in one folder. When heirs or co-owners are involved, settle early who has the authority to sign.

Judge each offer by what lands in your account, how long closing takes and how likely the buyer is to back out. A listing exposes the house to more people but brings showings and financing conditions. Whoever you pick, get in writing who covers title, recording and deed tax. If a buyer asks for a longer inspection window or a lower price after the first walk-through, decide ahead of time what you would accept, so a rushed moment does not make the decision for you. Keep every message with a buyer in one place in case a question comes up later.

Frequently asked questions

How much is a typical Coral Gables house worth?

The typical owned-home value is $1,089,900 for 2020-2024. Your own house could land well above or below that.

Does a historic designation affect my sale?

It can, if the house is on the city's historic register. Ask city staff about your address before you promise a buyer any renovation.

Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Coral Gables deed?

Whoever the contract names, though everyone on the deed shares liability. The surtax skips a document moving only a single-family dwelling.

Will my property taxes follow me to a new home?

Partly. Portability can move some homestead savings to a new Florida home if you qualify, using Form DR-501T.

Where do I ask about my assessment?

Call the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712 or book an appointment through the appraiser's website.

Selling in Winter Garden?
We buy Winter Garden houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Fastest ways to sell in Winter Garden

A cash or investor purchase is usually quickest, with a short agent listing as the alternative. A Winter Garden owner chooses between a buyer who accepts the property in its present state and a retail buyer who will want an inspection, a loan and sometimes repairs.

  • Cash offer: little fine print, and the closing day is often yours to pick.
  • Agent sale: wider exposure, though showings and a lender's review usually take longer.
  • A house in the historic core: buyers will probably ask about design rules first.

The older core carries design rules, so line up documents early: surveys, permit records, any Notice of Commencement for past projects, and your association's contact details if one applies. Missing items can slow a closing, so gather them before signing a contract. Have the contract say who pays the deed tax, title search and recording, and compare offers by what lands in your account.

Older neighborhoods and what buyers ask

Winter Garden sits on the south shore of Lake Apopka. It was first settled in the 1850s and grew after the railroad arrived in the 1880s, and the oldest surviving buildings date from about 1890. With few exceptions, the historic buildings date between 1915 and 1940. East Winter Garden grew in the early twentieth century as the African American community around Center Street, with turpentine and citrus packing houses providing work.

If your house lies in or close to either area, say so up front. Some buyers value original details, and investors look at how much work the structure needs. The city has a designated Historic East Winter Garden Neighborhood map, so ask the city whether your street falls inside it. Maxey Community Center on Klondike Avenue and Mildred Dixon Community Center on South West Crown Point Road are nearby amenities that can matter to buyers.

Historic Downtown design rules

Houses inside the overlay can be affected. The city created an Architectural Review and Historic Preservation Board in 2009 and adopted Ordinance 10-05 to set a Historic Downtown Architectural Overlay for the district.

Permits to check before listing

Pull the permit history on any addition, roof, fence, driveway or pool. Florida requires a permit for most projects, except items like replacing cabinets, floor coverings and painting. Work started without the proper permit faces code enforcement and fees of up to three times the regular permit fee.

  • Zoning permits submitted online include fences, turf, pavers, concrete, driveways, trees and backyard chickens.
  • Projects over $5,000 ($15,000 for air conditioning) need a Notice of Commencement recorded with the Orange County Comptroller.
  • The base fee is $30 for a project up to $1,000, and fees generally track project cost.
  • Owner-builders must sign their application at the counter, where staff notarize it at no charge.

House Bill 803 (2026) exempts some single-family home projects under $7,500, and the city offers a guide and request form. Use it to check a small job before you start, and keep the approved request with your closing files.

Keep invoices for permitted work as well. A buyer's agent often asks who did the roof, the air conditioning and the electrical, and when. A tidy folder of permits, final inspections and contractor names answers quickly and supports your asking price. Thursday opens an hour later than the other weekdays, and the permit counter closes before the building office does. Questions go to 407-877-5136.

Orange County property taxes when you sell

The bill comes from Orange County, on a schedule Florida sets every year. Value is fixed as of January 1, bills are sent in November, and anything unpaid goes delinquent on April 1. Paying early saves 4 percent in November, shrinking to 1 percent in February.

Unpaid items are sold as tax certificates by June 1, and after two years the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed. Make sure no balance is owed well ahead of closing, and let the closing agent prorate the current year.

If the house is homesteaded, the exemption, capped at $50,000, depends on permanent residence and ends if the home is rented. A new owner applies separately by March 1, and the Save Our Homes cap resets after the sale, which can make the buyer's bill very different from yours. Show last year's bill if you want to illustrate the pattern, and point buyers to the Orange County Property Appraiser about their own exemptions.

Closing and recording costs

Under Section 201.02 the deed tax is $0.70 for every $100 of price. Winter Garden lies outside Miami-Dade, so no special surtax applies. All parties to the document carry liability, no matter who the contract assigns to pay.

Section 28.24 lists the clerk's per-page recording charges and add-on fees. The closing agent can quote the exact total for your deed.

A Florida deed has to be written and signed before two witnesses, and the statute permits witnessing by audio-video technology. Ask your closing agent how the signing will work so it does not stall the sale.

Selling a house with unpermitted work

Yes, though an inspection may flag the work. Call the Building Department to learn how an old project gets closed out, or accept a price that reflects the problem. Cash buyers often take these houses as they stand and deduct the cost of fixing or permitting.

Do not hide it. Lenders and insurers sometimes ask about additions, and a buyer who learns late usually demands a bigger discount than one told at the start. Collect plans, photos and contractor names that show when the work happened. If the work is old and the contractor is gone, the Building Department can tell you what records exist, and that history may be enough to settle a buyer's concern without a new permit.

From signed offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company looks for liens, open permits and unpaid taxes, and the closing agent drafts a settlement statement. It should list the deed tax, recording charges, your share of that year's property tax and any lender payoff. Then you sign with two witnesses present, the clerk records the deed, and your proceeds follow.

With cash there is no lender review. A financed purchase needs an appraisal and loan approval, and that is where delays tend to begin on an older house.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need approval to change a house in Winter Garden's Historic Downtown overlay?

Call Planning and Zoning at 407-877-5156 before you start. A review board advises on construction, demolition and renovation in the district, and the overlay sets standards for major improvements.

What happens when work skips a Winter Garden permit?

Code enforcement can act, and fees can reach three times the regular permit fee. Ask the Building Department how to close out an old project.

When do Orange County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Certificates on unpaid items are then sold by June 1.

What is the Florida deed tax rate?

Seventy cents for each $100 of price, paid through the clerk when the deed is recorded. Miami-Dade follows different rates.

Can I sell a Winter Garden house that has unpermitted work?

Yes, though an inspection may flag it. Ask the Building Department about closing the permit, or negotiate a price with a cash buyer that reflects the issue.

Ways to sell a house in Altamonte Springs

An Altamonte Springs owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a direct offer from a buyer willing to leave repairs undone. All three finish the same way, with a signed deed, a title search and a recorded transfer in Seminole County.

Altamonte Springs is a Seminole County city with newer apartments and retail around Uptown Altamonte. Even so, the condition of your house, any repairs it needs and whether tenants live there will do more to set your timeline than the street will.

A direct offer may mean a lower price, in return for speed and fewer moving parts. Listing exposes the house to more buyers, though you take on showings, repair requests and the risk of a loan that never funds. Put each offer on paper and compare what you would actually take home after costs.

Permits and inspections

Selling itself needs no permit, yet half-finished work has a way of turning up when a buyer's inspector visits. Permits run through the city's Building and Fire Safety Department and Civic Access, its online portal.

Contractors use the portal for permits without plan review, for status checks and for booking inspections. Jobs that need plan review go in on paper, by mail, or on a USB flash drive the city keeps. If you rented the house out before selling, ask the City Clerk whether a business tax receipt applies.

Property tax when you sell

The county, not the city, values your parcel and mails the bill, with the city among several taxing bodies. Each August, the county appraiser's TRIM notice shows taxable value, proposed millage and budget meeting dates.

Setting rates isn't the appraiser's job, and the collector mails final bills by November 1. Pay in November for a 4 percent discount, with the reward shrinking to 1 percent by February. Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. For questions about value, classification or exemptions, call the appraiser at 407-665-7506.

To dispute value, petition the county's Value Adjustment Board, which the county clerk runs, no later than 25 days after the notice is mailed. A buyer's first bill often runs higher than a long-time owner's, because a sale resets homestead value.

Florida transfer taxes and recording costs

The biggest transfer cost in Florida is deed stamp tax, at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. The clerk collects it at recording. Each party to the deed stays answerable to the state, whatever the contract says.

The contract assigns the payer. A mortgage on the property counts as consideration even when the buyer doesn't take it over. Recording charges follow state law and the clerk's own schedule, so ask the Seminole County clerk for current figures.

  • The clerk's recording fee.
  • Back taxes and liens, settled from your proceeds.

Our Florida property tax guide explains discounts and caps.

Recording the deed in Seminole County

Your deed is filed with the Seminole County Clerk of Court, who records it and takes in the stamp tax. The appraiser then updates ownership, and the next TRIM notice goes to the new owner.

Before closing, the title agent should find any mortgage, lien or judgment filed against you. Ask for a written payoff list and the clerk's current fee schedule, since the county sets its own recording charges.

With tenants in the house, list their deposits and prepaid rent in the closing paperwork.

Foreclosure or an inherited house

A foreclosure and an estate each have their own timetable, and either can still end in a sale. Once a Florida court enters a foreclosure judgment, the clerk holds the public sale 20 to 35 days out, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait.

The top bidder puts 5 percent down. With no objection inside 10 days, the clerk issues the certificate of title. Any surplus is claimed through the clerk. A sale you make before that date puts the price in your hands.

For an inherited house, a simpler summary administration is available when the estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner died more than two years ago. No Florida estate tax applies to deaths after 2004, and a personal representative's deed under a probated will carries no deed stamps.

Selling with tenants

A lease may continue after the sale. An investor buyer won't mind, but someone who wants to move in will. A month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, while a year-to-year one needs 60.

Unpaid rent brings a 3-day written notice that doesn't count weekends or court holidays. Other lease breaches carry a 7-day notice. Once a judgment is entered, the sheriff carries out a writ after posting 24 hours' notice.

Read the lease before you promise a closing date, and disclose it early to any buyer.

Gather the signed lease, the deposit amount and the rent ledger, and give copies to the title agent. If the tenant plans to stay, ask the buyer for that in writing. If the tenant must leave, put the move-out date in the contract so no one is surprised at closing.

City services that change hands with the house

The city's home page links to services you'll want to move or stop.

  • Trash and recycling, to set up or end service when ownership changes.
  • Online payments, for city bills and fees.
  • Permits, through the Civic Access portal.
  • Agendas and minutes, if a zoning or code item affects your street.
  • A disaster resource guide, useful for buyers moving from out of state.

County offices still handle tax and recording. Those pages answer the everyday questions that arise before you hand over keys.

Steps for a straightforward sale

Whatever route you pick, a few habits keep the sale tidy. Start by pulling together your deed, latest mortgage statement and any permit records. Ask your title agent exactly which papers they need from you, and by what date. Ask for every offer in writing, then compare the amount you'd net once taxes, recording fees and payoffs come out, not the headline price.

Before signing, read the contract for who pays each closing cost, the closing date, and what happens if an inspection finds problems. A direct cash purchase skips lender appraisals and many financing delays, yet the title search, deed recording and tax settlement still happen.

Confirm where the proceeds will go and how you'll receive them, and ask when you must hand over keys and remove belongings. Cancel utility service only after closing is confirmed. Hold on to copies of everything you sign, plus the final settlement statement.

No reliable number can be given without looking at your house. Get written offers or an appraisal, and compare what each leaves you after costs.

Seminole County values and bills the parcel, and the city is one taxing authority. The appraiser does not set rates.

Do I need a permit to sell my house?

Not just to sell. Unfinished permitted work can still surface in an inspection, so call Building and Fire Safety at (407) 571-8433.

It's 70 cents per $100 of consideration. The contract names the payer, but the law reaches every party.

Can I sell with a tenant in the house?

Yes. The lease usually continues, and a month-to-month tenancy ends only with 30 days' notice.

Which desks handle a DeLand sale

County offices do the paperwork, not city hall. DeLand sits in Volusia County, so the Property Appraiser, the Tax Collector and the Clerk are the three desks that touch a sale. The city describes itself as a high pine meadow of rolling hills beside the St. Johns River, and that setting shapes the housing.

A seller in a hurry usually weighs three routes, each trading time against price differently:

Older and newer houses

DeLand mixes old and new because it grew in stages. Houses near the original center can have vintage plumbing, wiring and roofs, while later subdivisions sit on bigger lots. A mortgage buyer may insist on repairs, whereas an investor used to old stock tends to price the work and move on.

The center of town grew around the courthouse and a historic commercial street, and the city publishes design guidelines for downtown buildings. Houses within walking distance of that district appeal to people who want older construction near shops. Farther out, annexation has added newer subdivisions, and there you compete with recent builds, so a polished listing may outperform a rushed cash deal. Near the center the reverse can hold: a buyer comfortable with old wiring and plaster may close faster than a mortgage buyer facing an inspector's list.

Volusia dates that affect your closing

The collector starts taking payments November 1 and expects the whole amount by March 31, and April 1 marks delinquency. Closing agents prorate the year around these dates, so they decide whether you owe something or are credited.

Homestead and what follows you

Longtime owners have the most savings at stake. The state's Save Our Homes guide explains the details, and the Volusia appraiser can estimate your portable amount.

Recording costs for a DeLand deed

Two separate charges apply. Section 201.02 puts the stamp tax at seventy cents on every hundred dollars of price, and each signer on the deed is answerable for it, whatever the contract says about who pays. The Volusia clerk collects it at filing.

Filing fees follow section 28.24: $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each later page, plus technology and modernization add-ons per page. Your title agent adds them up.

Foreclosure, probate and tenant trouble

Each situation runs its own clock, and a private sale can still close ahead of a court.

  • Probate: a personal representative's deed carrying out a probated will is not taxed for stamps, and small estates can use summary administration up to $150,000.
  • Tenants: unpaid rent draws a three day notice that skips weekends and court holidays, and a periodic lease ends only after thirty days' written warning.

How a quick sale usually moves

You describe the house, receive an offer, choose a date, and a title company clears title and files the deed with the Volusia clerk. To keep it moving:

  • Gather the mortgage payoff letter, your latest tax bill and any association paperwork.
  • Update your mailing address with the appraiser, which offers an online change form, so the November bill reaches you.
  • Weigh every offer against your probable proceeds from an agent listing once repairs, fees and holding costs are subtracted.
  • Agree in writing on who pays the stamps and the title policy.
  • Check the payoff and proration lines on the closing statement before signing.

Ask every buyer how they pay, how long they need and whether repairs are a condition. Offers differ, so compare more than one.

At the table, expect to sign the deed in front of the required witnesses and review the settlement statement with the closer. Your mortgage payoff comes out first, then the tax proration and any agreed fees, and the rest goes to you. If you are leaving town before closing, ask the title company whether signing can be arranged remotely, and leave a working phone number where you can be reached for last-minute questions from the title agent.

City rule changes

The city's website announces that DeLand is updating its Land Development Regulations and points to a dedicated update site. Those rules govern lot use, setbacks and building standards, so an owner planning an addition, a second unit or a lot split should ask the planning desk about the current text before promising anything to a buyer.

Older homes in or near the historic core need extra care, because downtown design guidelines already shape how buildings look. Confirm any open permits or unfinished work on your parcel, since the next buyer's financing and inspection will surface them.

Check your parcel record first

Before naming a price, pull your parcel from the Volusia Property Appraiser's records and check the legal description, owner names and exemptions. Fixing a name mismatch before a contract is far easier than during title review. The tax bill lists the county, school board and city separately, and the collector can explain any line that is unfamiliar.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a DeLand house that has unpaid property taxes?

Yes. The title company requests a payoff from the collector and settles the balance out of your sale money. Delinquent parcels face a certificate sale beginning by June 1, so closing sooner helps.

Who pays the deed stamp tax on a DeLand sale?

Your contract assigns it, though everyone on the deed is jointly liable. The statute sets it at seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price.

Will I lose my homestead benefit if I sell in DeLand?

The exemption stops with your ownership and the buyer files their own. Saved assessment growth can travel onto a replacement Florida homestead by portability, provided you claim it on time.

How soon does a Volusia foreclosure sale follow judgment?

Typically three to five weeks. The top bidder leaves a 5 percent deposit, and a private buyer who closes first spares you the auction.

Does Volusia reward early payment of property taxes?

Yes. November payments get 4 percent off by November 30, and the discount drops a point each month until February. March 31 is the last day for the full amount.

Selling in North Miami Beach?
We buy North Miami Beach houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How fast can a North Miami Beach house sell?

Speed comes down to who the buyer is, how they pay and what the title search finds. With cash there is no lender in line, so you control much of the schedule. Listing brings more bidders along with showings, an inspection window and loan approval.

  • Cash offer: no lender appraisal, a closing day you can often pick, usually as is.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus repairs, showings and a longer wait.
  • Owner sale: no commission, and the contracts and disclosures are on you.

This is a tight, built-out city. About 46,236 residents share roughly 4.84 square miles, and just 52.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Expect offers from families, investors and people planning to rent.

North Miami Beach for a home seller

North Miami Beach is an older, fully built suburb in northeast Miami-Dade County. Its founder planned a "perfect city" in 1917 with 80 foot residential streets and 100 to 125 foot business thoroughfares, and today's street grid still follows that plan. Rock mining in the early 1900s left behind lakes, including Maule Lake and the lakes in the Sky Lake neighborhood, so some homes sit beside water that was once a quarry.

Buyers know Greynolds Park and the Ancient Spanish Monastery on West Dixie Highway. State Road 826, also called North Miami Beach Boulevard, and the 163rd Street shopping center anchor the commute, and the average commute is 30.1 minutes. Condos, townhouses and houses near the park can price very differently, so ask for comparable sales on your own block.

Housing numbers for the city

Typical values here are moderate, renters are a large share and households run big. These are survey estimates for the whole city, not an appraisal of one property.
