Closing costs on a North Miami Beach sale

The largest deed charge is Florida's documentary stamp tax, and Miami-Dade is the one county with its own schedule. The stamp tax page sets out the Miami-Dade figures, including how a single-family deed is handled, and your title agent will run the number.

Every signer on the deed is answerable to the state, yet the sales contract decides who actually pays, so nail that down before accepting anything. Section 28.24 lets the clerk add recording fees on top.

  • Stamp tax: figured by the title company on the sale price.
  • Recording: charged by the clerk at filing.
  • Payoffs for a mortgage, lien or late tax: taken from your proceeds.
  • This year's property tax: divided by closing date.

County tax bill and your homestead

The assessed value is set on January 1 and bills come from the tax collector in November, with a discount for paying early. Selling ends your homestead exemption. A buyer who will live there files a fresh application by March 1. The county appraiser's homestead page warns that an unreported change in status can lead to ten years of back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent annual interest, and it lists renting the property among the risks.

Save Our Homes slows the yearly rise in a homestead's assessed value, yet a title transfer resets the figure to just value the following January. A buyer's first full bill can therefore land well above yours. The state's Save Our Homes guide covers the details.

Repairs, permits and code problems

Open repairs do not block a sale. Permits and violations, though, stay with the address, so find out what is outstanding before you list. North Miami Beach runs permits, inspections and code violations through its eDMS online portal, where you can search records, check violations and request inspections.

Unpermitted work is the usual surprise at this stage, and it often comes from earlier owners rather than from you. A porch enclosure, converted garage or added bathroom can stall a financed sale because the appraiser and insurer ask about it. Cash buyers often accept that risk, then lower the offer to cover it.

  • Look up the address in the portal for open permits and violations.
  • Collect receipts for the roof, windows, electrical and plumbing.
  • Order a lien search before you sign a contract.
  • Keep lease dates handy if a tenant lives there.

If a permit turns up open, call the city to learn what inspection is missing, then decide whether to close it out yourself or sell as is at a lower price. A cash buyer will usually tell you the same day which choice they prefer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Miami Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a rental or inherited house

Both rentals and inherited homes can be sold. A tenant can stay through closing, and an heir can sell as soon as someone holds authority to convey. Buyers want proof of who may sign, so gather the lease, the death certificate or the court papers early.

Short-term rentals add a local layer. The city's application list includes a short-term rental registration for owners who list on platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO. Ask the city for the current rules before you advertise, because a buyer who plans to keep that use will ask whether the registration transfers.

Quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed are on the state's list of taxable documents, so handing a house to a relative before a sale is not automatically free of tax.

What steps lead from offer to closing?

Most of the waiting happens inside the title company's work, so the order of steps matters more than speed on your end.

  • Gather the deed, a mortgage payoff, your association contact and the newest tax bill.
  • Weigh a cash offer, a listing price and your net after costs.
  • Sign a contract that names who pays stamp tax and which repairs you will do.
  • Wait for the title company to clear liens, open permits and unpaid taxes.
  • Sign the deed before witnesses or a notary and hand over keys.
  • The clerk records the deed and collects the tax.

Condominium and association properties add an estoppel letter and sometimes board approval, so request those early. Ask the association what its fee for that letter is and how many days it needs, since that timing can set your closing date. If a tenant is staying, some cash buyers will honor the lease and others want the unit empty at closing, so ask before you agree on a date.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays stamp tax on a North Miami Beach home sale?

The purchase contract assigns the cost, although the state holds every party on the deed liable. Miami-Dade follows its own schedule, so ask the title agent for the figure on your deed.

Will the buyer get my homestead exemption?

No. Your exemption ends with the sale. The new owner applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the property is reassessed at just value the following January.

Can I close with open permits on the house?

Yes, though a title or permit search will show them. Expect a lower cash offer or a request to close the permit first. Look up the address in the eDMS portal before you list.

How do I weigh a cash offer against a listing?

Add up costs honestly, including carrying costs while the house sits unsold. Work out what you would keep on each route after commission, repairs and carrying costs, then compare the totals side by side.

Can I sell with a tenant living there?

Yes. The lease generally continues, so give buyers the terms early. Some cash buyers take the tenant, others want the unit empty by closing.

Haines City basics for sellers

Haines City is in northeast Polk County, west of Orlando and east of Tampa. Population is slightly over 23,000, and the city counts itself among the quickest growing in central Florida. Shoppers can arrive from either metro area, and Polk County's offices stand behind every tax bill you will deal with.

City hall is at 620 East Main Street, phone 863-421-3600. Permit questions go to the Building Division, and that same office handles the Business Tax Receipt program, which matters when the house has been a rental or a home business.

Permits and contractors

Plan review and inspections for residential and commercial work inside the city run through the Building Division, which tracks every permit from application to final sign-off.

Ask the division for any open permit on your address before a contract exists. Roofs, water heaters, air conditioners, additions and pools come up most. A buyer's lender may balk at a job with no final inspection, and closing it out is easier now than mid-contract. Staff can also say whether a Business Tax Receipt is tied to the parcel.

  • Ask for the permit list for your address.
  • Finish any permit that lacks a final inspection.
  • Keep invoices from contractors who did the work.

Unpaid Polk County taxes

Once April 1 passes after the assessment year, an open Polk bill carries 3% interest plus an advertising charge. By June 1 the office sells a tax certificate against the parcel at auction.

Polk County Tax Collector steps for an unpaid bill
Date or stageWhat happens
April 1Taxes become delinquent, with 3% interest and an advertising charge
By June 1Certificate sale held online; bidding starts at 18% and is bid down
After two yearsThe certificate holder may apply for a tax deed
Tax deed saleClerk of the Courts auctions the property; the owner of record can still pay what is owed before the sale

A certificate expires after seven years. Paying the full balance ahead of the deed sale lets you keep the house, and a sale that closes in time can retire the lien out of your proceeds.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Haines City house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead and senior exemptions

Owners who live in the house as a permanent residence on January 1 can claim Polk's homestead exemption, worth up to $50,000 off assessed value. The average saving runs about $750 a year, though the actual amount moves with the millage rate. Applications are due in early March each year, and a late filing can still be heard until the petition deadline in September. The appraiser's office at 863-534-4777 gives the current dates.

  • Residency proof: four forms of Florida residency identification for each resident, with a Florida driver license required.
  • Senior exemption: up to $50,000 once you are 65, provided household income is $36,614 or less. Polk allows the whole amount.
  • Twenty-five year exemption: offered on the county's general millage only, with just value under $250,000.
  • Widow or widower and disability: $5,000 each.
  • Portability: up to $500,000 of Save Our Homes benefit can move to another Florida homestead.

Tax calendar through the year

January 1 is the valuation date. Around mid-August the appraiser mails the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, known as the TRIM notice, and a value petition goes to the clerk within 25 days of it. November brings the bills, with an early-payment discount that gets smaller each month until the gross amount is due.

Owners who want installments sign up with the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year. A rental in Haines City has its own limit: assessed value on that parcel cannot rise more than 10 percent a year. A homestead is capped at the lower of 3 percent or inflation.

Selling and your tax cap

After closing, the next January puts the buyer at just value, and your exemption leaves with you. A move to another Polk home means a fresh application, plus form DR-501T if you want the cap benefit to follow.

November bills mean a spring closing happens before that year's tax is paid. Get the balance from the Polk County Tax Collector ahead of time so the title agent can prorate it.

Deed tax and recording

The deed tax in Polk is the ordinary state rate, 70 cents on every $100 of the price, and it is paid through the Polk clerk when the deed is recorded. Recording fees follow section 28.24, with added per-page charges. Your closing agent adds these up on the settlement statement, so ask for that number early.

Disability and military exemptions

A $5,000 reduction is available for a service-connected disability rated 10 percent or more. A combat-related disability exemption is open to honorably discharged service members who are 65 or older and homestead-qualified. A total and permanent rating can exempt a homestead completely, and sometimes a surviving spouse inherits that exemption.

Buyers who close between January 1 and November 1 may get a prorated first-year refund, requested with a worksheet and proof of tax payment. Owners who use a wheelchair or are legally blind can qualify for a separate exemption with an income limit. Appraiser staff at 863-534-4777 can tell you who qualifies.

Trusts, agreements for deed and renewals

A trust-owned house qualifies when the owner holds equitable title or a beneficial interest, and the appraiser may request a copy of the trust. A buyer under an agreement for deed can qualify too, provided the agreement is recorded with the Clerk of the Court. A plain purchase contract does not convey equitable title.

After approval, exemptions renew every year without a new application, and only a denial brings a letter. Owners should report life events that change eligibility, since losing an exemption has specific causes the appraiser publishes. If a servicer wants proof of homestead, save or print the parcel detail page as a PDF. The appraiser writes no letters.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting your house ready to sell

Take these steps in order. Get the permit list from the Building Division. Then call the Polk County Tax Collector for the balance and any earlier years still owed. Next, choose the route: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or a cash buyer who accepts the house in its current shape. Last, collect the recorded deed, mortgage payoff details and any lease, so a buyer can see a clean file right away.

If the house has tenants, hand over the lease early. If it is a rental, tell the buyer which assessment cap applies, since the rental limit differs from the homestead one. If an owner has died, someone with legal authority must sign, so confirm who that is before you accept an offer. Each of these items is small on its own, yet any one of them can push a closing date back a week or more.

With a signed contract, the title agent clears liens, prorates the year's tax and sends the deed to the clerk for recording. A cash sale can close as soon as that work is done, while a financed sale also waits on the lender.

Frequently asked questions

When was Haines City incorporated?

The Town of Haines City was incorporated on February 23, 1914. The city's first meeting was held on January 5, 1925.

When do Polk County taxes become delinquent?

April 1 of the year after assessment, when 3% interest and an advertising charge are added. An auction of the certificate comes by June 1.

What homestead exemption can a Haines City owner claim?

Up to $50,000 off assessed value on a permanent residence. Dates shift yearly, so phone 863-534-4777 before you file.

Who runs permits in Haines City?

The Building Division, which also runs the Business Tax Receipt program. Reach it through city hall at 863-421-3600.

Should I repair a Haines City house first?

Not necessarily. Start by asking the Building Division which permits remain open on the address.

Selling in North Lauderdale: what to know first

North Lauderdale is a Broward County city that grew from farmland into a mostly residential community. It was 90 percent farmland when it incorporated in 1963. Most housing dates from the decades since, so roofs, wiring and air conditioning are the items buyers tend to question.

One local rule matters more than most: the city requires an inspection and a residential rental license before an owner may offer a home for rent. If you rented the house yourself, or if your buyer is an investor who plans to rent it, that rule comes up fast.

The 2004 annexation and your records

The 2004 annexation of the Broadview and Pompano Park area added about 12,000 residents, the busy State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station. A few neighborhoods were unincorporated county land until then, so their older records and permits may sit with Broward County instead of the city. If your house is in that part of town, check both offices for permits.

The fire department became a full-service fire and EMS department in 2002 and now lists more than 40 firefighter-paramedics. Station 44, begun in 1991, sits near the middle of the city, and Station 34, finished in 2008, serves the east side. Mutual aid agreements with Broward County and neighboring cities cover the rest. Keep your insurance declarations page handy for buyers who ask about coverage.

Rental license requirements

No one may offer residential units for rent unless the community development department has inspected the building and the owner of record holds a residential rental license, which is a local business tax receipt. A buyer who plans to rent the house has to plan for that step.

Residential rental license charges by unit type

Other charges include a $65 initial application fee, a business tax receipt fee of $11.60 per unit and a $20 renewal fee. Call the city for the current schedule before you quote any of these to a buyer. An owner who receives no rent can file the city's affidavit of no residential rental compensation.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your North Lauderdale house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The business tax receipt calendar

Receipts run on a fiscal year. Sales begin July 1 for the period from October 1 through September 30 of the following year, every receipt expires on September 30, and none is issued for more than one year.

  • Renewals are completed at City Hall before September 30. Penalties apply for each month late.
  • Operating without a receipt carries a penalty of 25 percent of the tax due.
  • A receipt may be transferred to a new location within the city or to a new owner on the sale of a business.

The business tax receipt desk at 954-724-7069 is open Monday through Thursday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. A first-time applicant needs a certificate of use from the building code services department before applying, a step investors sometimes overlook when they buy a rental.

Plan the closing around these dates. If you hold a receipt for the house, tell the city about the sale so renewal notices stop and the new owner can apply for a fresh license.

What a rental inspection checks

The city lists standards for exterior, interior and outside property conditions. Passing them is required for the rental license, and an investor buyer will run the same checklist on your house.

  • Exterior walls must be free of holes and loose boards, and repainted when 25 percent or more of an exposure is discolored or peeling.
  • Roofing and guttering must keep water out, and windows and doors must be weather tight.
  • Electrical wiring, plumbing and heating and ventilation must be in safe working condition.
  • Pools and patios must be clean and screened enclosures intact.
  • Storm water must drain without running onto other properties.

Fixing a few of these before you list can speed a sale. A buyer who sees an easy rental inspection is more likely to offer without a long repair negotiation.

Deed tax and property tax dates

A Broward County deed carries the standard 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp rate, paid to the clerk at recording. The state holds every party liable whichever one agrees to pay, so the sales contract should assign it.

  • Property is assessed each January 1, and homestead applications are due by March 1.
  • The Notice of Proposed Property Taxes arrives in August, with 25 days to file a petition.
  • Bills go out in November. The discount shrinks from 4 percent to 1 percent by February, and April 1 begins delinquency.
  • A sale resets a homesteaded assessment to just value on the next January 1.

The Broward County Property Appraiser handles exemptions, and its customer service line, 954-357-6830, takes exemption questions countywide.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy North Lauderdale houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What are the ways to sell a North Lauderdale house quickly?

Owners here usually weigh an agent listing against an investor purchase. A listing may bring a higher price from a financed buyer but needs showings, an appraisal and repairs. A cash sale shortens the timeline and often lets the buyer take on the rental license and repairs, with the price reflecting that.

If you are behind on the mortgage, the court must enter a final judgment before the clerk's public sale, which then happens 20 to 35 days later unless the lender allows more time. An heir who needs to sell may qualify for summary administration when the estate is $150,000 or less, and creditors have until the later of three months after notice publication or 30 days after service to file claims.

Compare written offers, ask who pays for title work and doc stamps, and raise the buyer's rental license plans early in the conversation.

Closing day checklist

Before closing, collect the deed, a payoff figure from your lender, your latest tax bill and any rental license paperwork. The title company searches for liens and unpaid taxes and tells you what must be cleared. If the house was rented, find out from the city whether any inspection or license issue is open, since an investor's title agent may ask. You sign the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. A cash sale lets you skip lender appraisals and loan approval, which is where financed deals usually lose time. Agree in writing on who pays for any repairs the buyer's inspector finds, and set the date you hand over keys. If a tenant lives there, give the buyer the lease so the term and rent are clear before the contract is final.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a rental license to sell a North Lauderdale house?

No, the license is for owners who offer units for rent. If you rented the house, ask the city about any open inspection or license issue before closing.

Can a house with exterior wear still sell to an investor?

Yes, but investors know the rental inspection standards and may bid lower for visible wear, old wiring or a failing roof. Fixing those items first can widen your buyer pool.

What did the 2004 annexation add?

About 12,000 residents, the State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station, in an area that had been unincorporated Broward County.

Where can a buyer file a business tax receipt application?

At North Lauderdale City Hall at 701 SW 71 Avenue, where applications and fees are processed. The business tax receipts line is 954-724-7069.

Does the Florida deed tax change in Broward County?

No. Broward uses the standard 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid through the clerk at recording, and all parties to the deed are liable.

Fast sale options in Oakland Park

You can accept a cash offer, list with an agent or run the sale yourself, and the trade-off is speed against price. A cash buyer can often close on your date and take the house as is. Listing puts the house in front of more people, at the price of showings, repair requests and a lender's calendar.

  • Cash offer: few contingencies, quick closing, a price that reflects repair risk.
  • Agent listing: usually the highest price, with commission and a longer wait.
  • Owner sale: no listing fee, but you handle the contract and the buyers.

If you have rented the house short term, settle that question first, because the city regulates short-term rentals and a buyer will ask whether yours is registered.

About Oakland Park

Oakland Park is a dense Broward County city of roughly 48,000 people on about 8.1 square miles, north of Fort Lauderdale. Blocks are tight, single-family streets sit beside condominiums, and investors are regular buyers. It was incorporated on July 1, 1929, and subdivisions and condominiums filled in during the 1960s and 1970s, when the city became both a commercial and industrial hub and a bedroom community for Fort Lauderdale.

That mix of older single-family blocks, small commercial corridors and condominiums is what a buyer sees today. Collect at least two written offers before you decide, and ask each buyer which closing costs they will cover.

Short-term rentals in Oakland Park

Nightly rentals are legal here with registration and inspection, and those requirements add real cost for anyone selling a house that has been used that way. The city adopted its rules in 2018. A short-term rental is a unit rented to guests more than three times a year for periods under 30 days, or one advertised as regularly rented to guests.

Ownership changes trigger a new initial registration fee, which means your registration does not pass to the buyer. If you hold one, tell the buyer up front and expect them to compare it with their own plans for the property.

Checking permits and inspections

Search any address in the city's online permit portal to see its permits and inspection results. Permits opened before November 1, 2019 and after it live in separate search systems, so check both if the house is older.

Owners connected to a permit can apply, view plan review comments, and schedule or cancel inspections through the same portal. The Building Division is at 1100 Park Lane East and posts weekday office hours on its permit page. Late-stage delays usually trace back to an old roof permit, a window job or an addition that never got a final inspection.

  • Run the address through both permit systems.
  • Look for permits that never received a final inspection.
  • Ask contractors for closing paperwork and warranties.
  • Tell cash buyers about unfinished work, since they price it in.

Pull registration and inspection records as well if guests ever stayed in the house. Buyers like to see them. A short-term rental hotline and a sheriff's office non-emergency line take complaints, so unresolved ones can also surface in a buyer's research.

Broward taxes and closing costs

Deed stamp tax in Broward follows the statewide schedule on the Department of Revenue page, since only Miami-Dade differs. The state can look to any signer for payment, so the contract needs to say who covers it. The clerk takes the tax as the deed is recorded and adds page-based recording charges under statute section 28.24.

On the Broward County Property Appraiser's homestead page, residency is fixed as of January 1. Timely 2027 filings close March 1, 2027, and September 20, 2027 is the final day for a late 2027 exemption. Your exemption does not outlast the year of sale, and renting the home out can forfeit it. A spring buyer should file for the following tax year.

The basic exemption saves roughly $673 to $1,020 for 2026, depending on the city's millage rate. Additional exemptions exist for seniors, widowed persons and people with disabilities, so a buyer who qualifies may carry a lower bill than you do. The sale itself resets the assessed value to market level.

Estate sales and the closing process

Heirs can sell an inherited house as soon as the person signing holds legal authority. Expect the buyer's title company to ask for the court papers or for proof that the property passed outside probate. Quitclaim deeds are on the Department of Revenue's taxable list, while a personal representative's deed under a probated will is shown as not taxable.

  • Gather the deed, payoff statement, latest tax bill and association contact.
  • Compare cash offers against your net from a listing.
  • Put in writing who covers deed stamp tax and any repairs.
  • Let the title company search for liens, open permits and tax balances.
  • Sign before two witnesses or a notary so the clerk can record the deed.

Witnessing can happen over audio-video technology in Florida, so heirs in other cities do not have to travel. Ask the title company to schedule the signing once payoffs and liens are cleared, and confirm which documents each heir must bring, such as photo identification and the court papers that give them authority.

What a cash sale skips and what it does not

Before you accept any offer, add up what you owe and what you will keep. Start with the mortgage payoff, any association balance, the property tax bill for the year and, if the house was a short-term rental, any unpaid city fees or fines. Ask the title company for an estimated settlement statement early so the number is not a surprise at the table. Keep copies of any city fee receipts, inspection reports and registration papers in one folder so a buyer's agent can see them without a scramble.

With cash, nothing waits on a lender's appraisal or loan approval, and many buyers accept the house with its repairs and its open permits. The title search, the deed, the stamp tax and the recording still happen, and any lien or unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds. Ask each buyer for a written offer that states the closing date, who pays closing costs and whether they will take the property with an unfinished permit. If the house has a short-term rental registration or a tenant, say so at the start, since either one changes what a buyer will pay.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Oakland Park house if I rent it by the night?

Yes, but disclose it. The city requires registration, an inspection and fees, and a change of ownership requires a new initial registration fee. A first violation carries a $250 daily fine.

What stamp tax applies in Broward County?

Broward follows the statewide schedule on the Department of Revenue page. Your contract decides who pays, and the clerk collects at recording.

Do I need to fix open permits before I sell?

You can sell with them, but they can slow a lender-backed buyer and trim a cash offer. Search the city portal by address, covering both the older and newer permit systems.

Does my homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. Your exemption ends with the year of sale, and the buyer files a new application by March 1.

When does late filing for a 2027 exemption end in Broward?

September 20, 2027 is the last day, and state law allows no later filing for any reason.

A regional branch of the county appraiser operates inside Cutler Bay, on the second floor of the South Dade Government Center at 10710 SW 211 Street. Walk-in hours run weekdays, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Call 305-232-3810 or book online.

Billing and collection belong to the county tax collector, and this office does not set rates. Appeals go to the Value Adjustment Board, which can still change a value. The Online Exemptions tool accepts widow and veteran disability filings.

Deed tax and recording costs

Deeds in this county carry a tax of 60 cents on every $100. A surtax of 45 cents per $100 is layered on top, but a transfer that conveys just a single-family house skips it. The base rate is set out in s. 201.02, and each person who signs is liable for payment.

  • The clerk collects the tax at recording.
  • Page one costs $5.00 and each later page $4.00.
  • Two witnesses must watch you sign, and they can do so by audio-video link.

You can also register with the county Clerk of Court and Comptroller for a free alert, delivered within 24 hours, any time a deed or mortgage is recorded under your name.

Homestead and the Save Our Homes cap

Your taxable value stays below market while you own the house, thanks to a cap equal to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. The state's chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. The cap does not survive a sale.

  • The homestead exemption removes up to $50,000 of value, and school taxes get the first $25,000 of it.
  • On the next January 1, the new owner is assessed at just value.

If a tenant, an heir or a lender is involved

  • Heirs generally need a personal representative before anything can be signed. Estates of $150,000 or less may take the short route.
  • If a lender sues, the court sale is held 20 to 35 days after judgment.
  • Someone holding a tax certificate must wait two years from April 1 of the issue year to apply for a deed.

Ask a Florida attorney or the clerk which of these applies to you.

Property tax dates and the closing split

The state calendar is simple. Values are set January 1, exemption filing ends March 1, notices come in August, bills in November, and unpaid tax is delinquent from April 1. A petition on value must reach the clerk within 25 days of the notice.

A spring or summer closing leaves a whole November bill unpaid, and you and the buyer share it. Look for the proration on the settlement statement, then check it against the collector's record for your folio.

Senior and veteran benefits that end at sale

Each of these Florida benefits is attached to the house, so find out from the appraiser how it applies before you list.

  • Owners 65 and older may qualify for an additional exemption, up to $50,000, if the local ordinance permits it and household income is within the limit.
  • A veteran past 65 with a permanent disability from service can get a discount matching the VA percentage.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember rated at 10 percent or more receives $5,000 off.

With 16.9 percent of residents at 65 or older, many local owners may be affected.

Renting versus selling

Rent of $1,978 makes holding the house as a rental tempting. Landlords live with the notice rules above, and the tax bill can climb once homestead protection is gone. Weigh the repair calls and empty months before you commit.

If you do sell, note that 63.5 percent of residents aged five and up use another language at home and 64.0 percent are Hispanic or Latino. Listing text in two languages, plus a translated outline of your terms, will reach more buyers.

Getting the file ready

Put the deed, newest tax bill, lender payoff figure and permit records in a single folder. Review the town's Property Registration page too. Take dated photos of the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanical systems, so your description of the house is backed by pictures. Once offers come in, find out who covers title and recording and how each buyer will pay. Read the proration lines carefully on the settlement statement before you sign.

It also pays to think about moving day. Decide when the house will be empty, who will hold the keys, and which utilities need to be switched off or transferred. Leave garage openers, manuals and warranty papers for the new owner, and keep your own copies of the closing documents. Ask the title company when funds will reach you so you can plan the next purchase or rental around that date. If a buyer asks to move in early or to stay behind after closing, put the terms in writing with exact dates before you agree

The typical owned home is valued at $472,700 for 2020-2024.

Slightly the other way. The 2025 estimate of 44,750 is 1.5 percent under the 2020 base.

Does the surtax apply to my Cutler Bay deed?

No, if the document moves only a single-family dwelling. The 60 cents per $100 base tax still applies.

Where can I get help with an exemption?

Visit the county appraiser's Cutler Bay branch at the South Dade Government Center, or use its online exemption filing.

Who sends my tax bill?

The Miami-Dade tax collector, each November, with 4 percent off for paying that month.

How Greenacres owners sell

Greenacres sellers can go through an agent, handle the sale personally, or accept cash from someone who will deal with the repairs. Speed, repair cost and certainty rarely all point the same way.

  • Agent listing: wider reach, paid for with showings and a lender's calendar.
  • Direct sale: you hold the price and the paperwork.
  • Cash: few conditions, flexible timing, repairs priced in.

Collect written bids and work out what each would put in your hands once payoffs, tax and recording are paid.

Greenacres in brief

Greenacres is a compact city in central Palm Beach County, about six square miles. Developer Lawrence Carter Swain platted half the townsite in 1923 and began selling lots in 1925 for $225 with $45 down, aiming at working families. The city was incorporated in 1926 as the Town of Greenacres City, lost its charter after a petition in 1944, regained its rights in December 1945 and reincorporated in 1947.

Today about 44,736 people live here, and the city is dense, with 7,407 people per square mile. That working-family history still shows in the housing: family-sized homes on small lots.

Housing figures

About two thirds of homes here are lived in by their owners (66.5 percent for 2020 to 2024), at a median value of $291,000. Rent runs $1,756 at the median, and monthly owner costs median $1,865 with a mortgage and $672 without. Households average 2.90 people, and 15,249 households were counted.

Talking with buyers

Conversations in this city often happen in more than one language. Provide documents in clear form, use a translator or a bilingual closing agent if the buyer asks, and keep offers in writing. A plain purchase agreement prevents misunderstandings that cost time at title. Buyers who commute along the coast also like to hear about road access, so mention the nearest major roads and shopping.

Recording a Greenacres deed

A deed in Palm Beach County is taxed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at recording. Under section 201.02(1)(a), a mortgage on the property is part of the consideration. Each party to the deed carries liability for the tax, whoever promised to pay it.

Recording is billed by the page under s. 28.24(13): $5.00 for the first and $4.00 for each after it, with trust fund and technology charges on top. Look for the totals on your settlement statement.

Tax dates and homestead

Assessed value is fixed each January 1, and the county appraiser mails a notice of proposed taxes in August. A challenge to that value is a petition to the clerk, due within 25 days. The November bill carries a 4 percent discount that declines to 1 percent in February, and April 1 begins delinquency. File homestead and other exemptions by March 1.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value, and the extra $25,000 slice skips school taxes.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly assessed growth at the smaller of 3 percent and inflation.
  • Once you sell, the following January 1 resets the assessment to market-based value.

Phone the tax collector for the exact balance and file the written figure with your closing papers, so you can check the settlement statement against it.

Inherited, foreclosed or rented

State law sets a timeline for each of these.

  • Inherited: summary administration, a streamlined probate, covers estates that are small or long past death (s. 735.201).
  • Foreclosure: the clerk auctions the property soon after final judgment, and bidders post a deposit (s. 45.031).
  • Tenant: a monthly tenancy needs 30 days' notice (s. 83.57).

About a third of Greenacres units are renter-occupied, so tenant questions come up often. Share the lease with any buyer at the outset.

What to line up before closing

Missing records delay more closings than buyers do, so gather them early.

  • The deed, or trust or probate papers that show who can sign.
  • Payoff statements from every lender.
  • Permit and repair records for roof, electrical and air conditioning work.
  • Lease copies and rent history for tenants.
  • The newest TRIM notice and tax bill.

A deed needs two subscribing witnesses under s. 689.01, so schedule the signing with your title agent.

How a cash sale unfolds

When a written offer is accepted, the title company looks for liens and back taxes, asks for payoffs and picks the closing date. You sign the contract, and later the deed in front of two witnesses. Payoffs, stamp tax and recording come out of the proceeds, and the rest goes to you. With no appraisal or loan underwriting, a cash closing can move fast. Ask the buyer to commit the date and the cost split to paper, and do not pay anyone before closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Listing or cash: weighing the trade

Listing can bring a higher number, but it asks for patience through showings, inspection requests, a buyer's loan and carrying costs while you wait. Cash gives you speed and certainty and leaves repairs to the buyer, so the price reflects that work. A tidy house with a flexible date may do well on the market. A house needing work, with a tenant or a lender deadline, often fits a direct sale better. Ask for at least two written offers and rank them by net proceeds.

If an inheritance or unpaid taxes complicate things

Talk to the clerk's probate office or a probate attorney about who may sign for an estate, and send the title company any court papers the moment you have them. If taxes are owed, the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a written figure early. Neither problem has to stop a sale, but both are easier to solve with weeks of lead time than with days. Starting those calls before you accept an offer also lets you give a buyer a realistic closing date from the beginning.

Closing day

The title agent goes over the settlement statement with you. Read every line, ask about any charge you do not recognize and confirm that payoffs match your letters. After the deed is signed and recorded, hand over keys and remotes and expect your proceeds by wire or check. Afterward, update your mailing address with the property appraiser and keep copies of what you signed, including the final settlement statement.

Is Greenacres mostly owner-occupied?

Yes, at 66.5 percent for 2020 to 2024, which suggests most buyers plan to live in the house.

What is the median home value in Greenacres?

$291,000 for 2020 to 2024. It is only a rough guide, because a house with a new roof and one needing work can sit far apart. Ask for written offers on your own property.

When was Greenacres incorporated?

In 1926 as the Town of Greenacres City. It lost its charter in a 1944 petition, was reinstated in December 1945 and reincorporated in 1947.

Who pays doc stamp tax on a Greenacres deed?

The statute makes every party liable. The contract decides who actually pays, and the closing agent collects at recording.

When must I file homestead after buying in Greenacres?

Send DR-501 to the county property appraiser by March 1 of the tax year. You must own and live in the home as of January 1.

  • An agent listing reaches the widest pool of buyers. About 33.5% of residents are past 65, so expect many offers from retirees.
  • A direct sale saves the commission and leaves the contract, disclosures and recording to you.

First confirm that the property is inside city limits, because unincorporated Volusia County addresses follow different rules.

Local housing numbers

The city had an estimated 44,692 residents in July 2025, a 3.7% gain over the 2020 base.

Since 90.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, listings tend to come from long-term owners, and many of those houses carry decades of accumulated repairs. A buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as it stands saves such a seller from a repair list.

Flood zones and your sale

Lenders and insurers use FEMA flood maps to decide whether flood insurance is required. The city says every property lies in a flood zone of some kind. High-risk zones include A, AE, AO, V and VE. Zone X is a minimal-risk area that does not usually require flood insurance, although flooding can occur anywhere.

Before listing, look up your zone through the links on the city's floodplain pages and ask your insurance agent for a quote. A buyer's lender will ask for it, and a surprise on the quote can delay or end a closing. The Halifax River and part of the Tomoka River run through the city, which is why the question comes up so often.

Renting the house instead of selling

Long-term rental, meaning a lease over six months, is permitted in all residential districts. The city does not regulate it, so no business license is needed. Short-term rental, meaning transient lodging on a lease under six months, is not a permitted, conditional or special exception use in residential zoning districts.

The B-4, B-6 and B-7 commercial districts allow transient lodging, but those operators need a local business tax and must follow state lodging rules, with locations approved by the Site Plan Review Committee. A house in a residential district cannot be run as a vacation rental, and a buyer who hoped to do that will pay accordingly.

Permits and paperwork before closing

  • Fences and driveways require permits, and the city asks for a survey showing the location.
  • Tree permits come from the Neighborhood Improvement Department at 386-229-7250.
  • A zoning confirmation letter costs $35 per address or parcel and is requested by email at comdev@ormondbeach.org.
  • A notice of commencement is required when work exceeds $5,000, or $7,500 for replacing an existing heating or air conditioning system, under section 713.13 of the Florida Statutes.
  • The Volusia County Property Appraiser's site shows your tax district: 201 is Ormond Beach and 200 is unincorporated northeast Volusia.

In 2014 the city also took jurisdiction over properties along North US Highway 1 from the Tomoka River bridge to the Volusia-Flagler County line, under an agreement with the county. If you own there, the district number tells you which government handles permits and code enforcement. Gather your permit records, survey and any zoning letter before you list, since title companies and buyers often request them.

Property taxes when the house sells

The Volusia County Property Appraiser values each parcel as of January 1. Bills reach owners in November, with early-payment discounts that shrink month by month. Exemption applications are due March 1, and unpaid bills turn delinquent on April 1.

Homestead can trim taxable value by up to $50,000, and Save Our Homes slows how quickly the assessment climbs. Many Ormond Beach owners stay for years, so the capped assessment can sit far below market value, and a sale ends that cushion for the buyer. If a prospective buyer asks what the bill will be, send them to the Volusia County Property Appraiser for an estimate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ormond Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling an inherited or family-transferred house

Florida has a streamlined summary administration for some smaller or older estates. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable for deed stamps. A quitclaim deed is taxable, and it also counts as a change of ownership for assessment unless an exception applies.

A lady bird deed, also called an enhanced life estate deed, gets different treatment. A 2020 revenue advisement found that, on its facts, such a deed transferred no present beneficial interest and drew no stamp tax. The ruling is fact-specific, so have an attorney review your deed first. Under section 689.01, a conveyance of land must be written and signed before two witnesses.

Stamp tax on the deed

Florida taxes the deed itself at $0.70 per $100 of consideration, and each party to it answers to the state whichever side the contract says will pay. The Volusia County clerk collects the tax at recording and adds recording fees that scale with page count. The closing agent can give you the exact total.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens the file and searches the record for liens and unpaid taxes. If the house has open permits or an unrecorded owner change, that is when it surfaces. Sign the deed before witnesses as the statute requires, pay off any mortgage from the proceeds, and the clerk records the deed. With a cash buyer the sequence is the same, minus the lender's appraisal and underwriting.

Bring a photo ID, your deed or last closing paperwork, and the payoff statement if a mortgage remains. If the house is inside a flood zone, hand over the insurance declarations page so the buyer can compare it with their own quote. Tell the closing agent early about any open permit, tenant or estate paperwork, because each one adds a step and a delay if it comes out late.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use my Ormond Beach house as a vacation rental?

Not in a residential zoning district. Short-term rental, defined as a lease under six months, is not a permitted, conditional or special exception use there. Leases longer than six months are allowed and need no city business license.

How do I tell if my address is in the City of Ormond Beach?

Search your address on the Volusia County Property Appraiser's site and read the tax district. District 201 is within Ormond Beach, while district 200 is unincorporated northeast Volusia and falls under county jurisdiction.

What does a zoning confirmation letter cost?

The city charges $35 per confirmation. Send the street address or tax parcel ID with the fee to comdev@ormondbeach.org. Buyers and title companies sometimes request one.

Is every house in Ormond Beach in a flood zone?

Yes, every property is in some FEMA flood zone. Zone X is a minimal-risk area that usually does not require flood insurance, while A, AE, AO, V and VE are high-risk. Your insurance agent can confirm what your lender will require.

Does my homestead exemption go to the buyer?

No. Yours ends when the house stops being your permanent residence, and the buyer applies by March 1 for a new one. The county reassesses at just value after the change of ownership.

How can I sell my Plant City house quickly?

The fastest route in Plant City is a cash purchase. The buyer needs no loan, so closing depends on the title search and a signed deed. A listing goes through showings, an inspection and the buyer's mortgage underwriting before it gets that far.

Plant City sits in northeast Hillsborough County, about 25 miles east of Tampa and just west of Lakeland, with a population estimate of 45,331. Many buyers ask about the drive first, because the city lies between Tampa and Lakeland and close to I-4. Put your cross streets and drive times in your listing or your first conversation with a cash buyer, and say how far the house sits from the rail lines and main roads, since trains and highways bring noise.

Decide early whether speed or price matters more. A seller with a closing date in mind, such as a job move or an estate deadline, usually leans toward cash. A seller with time to spare and a house in good shape may net more through a listing, though repairs and buyer financing can still slow it down.

  • Cash fits a house needing a roof, kitchen or foundation work.
  • A listing fits a move-in-ready house and a flexible calendar.
  • Occupied homes and estate property need extra paperwork in both cases.

City utilities and your closing

The city owns and operates its water, wastewater and solid waste service, so a buyer who asks about utilities gets one provider to call. Ask the city for a final water reading before closing, and ask whether a code case or lien is open on the parcel.

Keep your last few water, power and trash statements together, because a buyer may ask for them and a title agent may need proof of the account holder. If you are moving out before closing, schedule the final readings for the last day you hold the keys so you are not billed for the buyer's usage.

Open items surface during the title search anyway, so finding them first lets you clear them on your schedule instead of the buyer's. A cash buyer will usually subtract a known problem from the offer, while a surprise found late can delay funds.

Newer homes nearby

The city encourages light, clean industry and has over 2,000 acres of privately owned industrial parks. Jobs nearby give buyers a reason to look at houses inside the city rather than only in Tampa's suburbs. New homes are also being built, and your house competes with them.

  • Compare your asking price with newer construction nearby.
  • Point to features a new build lacks: mature trees, larger lots or an established street.
  • Be ready to explain the age of the roof, air conditioner and plumbing.

A cash buyer weighs the same factors, then subtracts repair costs from the offer. Ask for the offer in writing and ask how the repair estimate was built. If a figure looks high, request the line items and get a second contractor's number before you agree.

Closing and recording charges in Hillsborough County

The state's deed stamp tax runs 70 cents on every $100, collected by the Hillsborough clerk when the deed is recorded. Page fees come on top: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each one after. Any mortgage on the house is counted in the price. Name the payer in the purchase contract.

Ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement early, then check each line against your contract.

Property tax dates and exemptions

Hillsborough County property tax steps

If you live in the house, you can exempt up to $50,000 by applying before March 1, and a separate cap limits how quickly the assessed value of a homestead can rise. The cap ends for that property when you sell. If you own farmland or other classified land near the city, ask the property appraiser whether the March 1 classification continues for the buyer.

When taxes go unpaid, the county sells a certificate to the investor who bids the lowest interest rate, and after two years that investor may apply for a tax deed. A delinquent balance paid out of your sale proceeds removes that risk.

Does a stranger or former tenant occupy the house?

In Florida, a tenant and an unlawful occupant are handled under different rules. For a person with no tenancy, no family tie and no invitation, section 82.036 lets an owner file a sworn complaint with the sheriff, who serves a notice to vacate. False statements risk damages equal to triple the fair market rent plus costs and fees.

For a tenant, the clock is shorter or longer depending on the problem: three days for unpaid rent, seven days for a lease violation that can be cured, and 30 days to end a month-to-month tenancy. Adverse possession is not quick. Section 95.18 requires seven years of possession plus payment of taxes and a filing with the property appraiser.

Sort occupancy out before you sign a cash contract so the buyer receives the house as agreed.

Steps to close a Plant City cash sale

  1. Collect your payoff letter, tax bill and any lease.
  2. Choose an offer and sign the contract.
  3. The title agent pays off liens and taxes.
  4. Sign the deed while two witnesses watch.
  5. The Hillsborough clerk records it, and you get paid.

Before you accept any offer, confirm the buyer can close on the date you need, ask who pays for the title policy, and learn whether the buyer expects you to leave the house empty or to leave appliances.

Keep copies of the contract, settlement statement and recorded deed in one folder, since a later tax filing or insurance question may need them.

Foreclosure and probate run on their own tracks. In a foreclosure, the court sale lands 20 to 35 days after final judgment. An estate of $150,000 or less can use the summary process. Heirs, even those living out of state, should ask the Hillsborough court which papers show who may sign.

On signing day, bring a photo ID and expect to sign the deed, the settlement statement and any affidavits the title agent prepared. Two witnesses must be present for the deed, and the title office usually supplies them. After funds are confirmed you hand over keys and garage openers, and the clerk's recording finishes the transfer.

A cash sale lets you skip staging, open houses and the wait for a buyer's appraisal. The title work and the signing still happen, so plan for a few days of paperwork even when the offer is firm.

Frequently asked questions

What should I ask a Plant City cash buyer before signing?

Find out who pays for the title policy, how soon funds arrive, whether an inspection can change the price, and what happens to appliances or belongings left behind. Have every answer in writing.

Which county handles my Plant City deed?

Hillsborough County. Its clerk records the deed and collects the stamp tax.

Does Plant City have its own utilities?

Yes. The city operates water, wastewater and solid waste service, so one city account covers those.

Can squatters take my house after seven years?

Only if they meet section 95.18, including paying taxes and filing with the property appraiser. In the meantime, you can use the sheriff process in section 82.036.

Do I need two witnesses on a Florida deed?

Yes. Section 689.01 calls for a signed writing with two subscribing witnesses, and audio-video witnessing is permitted.

What are your options for a quick sale in Lake Worth Beach?

Three paths are open to a Lake Worth Beach owner: a cash sale, an agent, or a sale handled alone. Cash tends to close first, since no mortgage underwriting sits between signing and the closing table.

Hurricane season is part of life in this city, and its resident page covers evacuation zones, outage reporting and storm preparation. A worn roof or storm damage can stall a financed sale, whereas a direct buyer just builds the repair into the price.

  • Cash buyer: no repairs, no showings, and a closing day you choose.
  • Agent: wider exposure, more steps.

Historic districts and small lots

The city names six historic districts: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park.

College Park grew mainly in two bursts, 1925 to 1928 and 1945 to 1949. The Northeast and Southeast Lucerne districts sit north and south of Lake and Lucerne Avenues, with the commercial Old Town of about 16 acres between them. South Palm Park covers roughly 60 blocks southeast of Old Town, next to Bryant Park and the Intracoastal Waterway.

The city runs a design review process for historic districts. Ask planning staff whether your address is covered before a buyer plans new windows, fencing or an addition. Platted lots here were deliberately small, since the original lot sales were tied to farmland purchases west of town, so a buyer planning an addition will ask about lot size. Have your survey ready.

  • Confirm the district and any review needed.
  • Keep permits and approvals for past work.
  • Ask about fence rules, which the city publishes in a permit guide.

A short note on the city's layout

Settlement began after the Homestead Act of 1862, and the railroad reached the area from West Palm Beach in 1896. The platted townsite was first called Lucerne, but the post office found that another Florida town already used the name, so it became Lake Worth, and incorporation followed in 1913. A 1912 survey laid out 55 miles of streets, about as many miles of alleys and 7,000 residential lots. Because lot sizes drive questions about additions, locate your lot survey before you list and keep it with your permit records.

Closing your account with city utility customer service is one task. Confirming that no permits or violations are open on the parcel is another, and a buyer's records search will surface them if you do not.

Palm Beach County's tax collector publishes a tax bill explainer. Taxable value is assessed value minus exemptions, multiplied by each taxing authority's millage, and non-ad valorem assessments, such as Solid Waste Authority fees based on property type, are added on top. Ask for a recent bill so you can see which pieces will be prorated.

  • Schedule the utility shutoff or transfer.

How Palm Beach County tax bills work for a seller

The county property appraiser mails proposed-tax notices each August. By November 1 the tax collector has sent more than 600,000 bills to the addresses on file with the appraiser.

You can pay from November 1 through March 31, and delinquency begins in April. If you have already sold, hand the bill to the new owner or file the Property Sold Form. A delinquent bill cannot be paid online, and a postmark stops proving timely payment.

An installment plan is also available. Enrollment runs from November 1 to April 30 each year, and the estimated tax must exceed $100. Payments follow the preceding year's tax and fall due in June or July, September, December and March. Miss the first one and you are dropped from the plan.

What happens to the Save Our Homes cushion when you sell

The cushion does not go with the house. Closing is a change of ownership, so the buyer begins at full just value the next January 1.

Documentary stamps in Palm Beach County run at the ordinary 70 cents per $100 of consideration, without the Miami-Dade variation.

The clerk takes the payment when the deed is filed, and the state makes each party to the deed answerable for it. Estate planning transfers have no special exemption. A 2020 advisement concluded that a lady bird deed with the life tenants' full powers retained carried no present beneficial interest and was not taxed on those facts, so take your own deed to an attorney. Deeds need two witnesses.

Behind on the mortgage in Lake Worth Beach

A sale before the auction lets you pay the lender and keep whatever equity is left.

Following a foreclosure judgment, the clerk schedules an auction 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff agrees to more time. The high bidder puts down 5 percent, and a homestead owner hoping for leftover funds should check with the clerk inside 10 days. Selling on your own before the auction date sidesteps all of it.

  • Obtain a payoff letter.
  • Calendar every court deadline.
  • Speak with an attorney or a court self-help resource.
  • Compare a cash offer with a short listing.

From accepted offer to closing

After you accept an offer, a title company or closing agent searches title, requests a lender payoff letter and drafts the deed. It is signed before two witnesses and filed with the county clerk, who collects the stamp tax. The year's property tax is prorated between you and the buyer, and any balance still owed is paid from your proceeds.

While that moves along, close your city utility account and hand over permit records, historic district approvals and your survey. A cash buyer can often close faster, yet title and recording steps remain, so ask for the timeline in writing and confirm who is paying for the title policy and the deed tax.

How many historic districts does Lake Worth Beach have?

Six: College Park, Old Lucerne, Old Town Commercial, Northeast Lucerne, Southeast Lucerne and South Palm Park. The city's planning staff can confirm your parcel.

What should I do with my tax bill after I sell?

Send it on to the buyer, or complete the tax collector's Property Sold Form. Confirm the proration with your closing agent.

Can I still pay a delinquent bill online?

No. Once a bill is delinquent it cannot be paid online, and a postmark no longer proves timely payment.

Who pays the deed tax in Palm Beach County?

The purchase contract decides, but the state holds both sides liable. The rate is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration.

Can I sell a house I inherited?

Someone with court authority must sign the deed. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is among the deeds the revenue department lists as not taxable. A probate attorney can say whether a shorter summary process applies.

Hallandale Beach in brief

Hallandale Beach is a compact, oddly shaped city at the southern tip of Broward County. Its outline goes back to a 1947 deal that allowed annexation from Federal Highway east to the ocean, with the oceanfront north of Beach Boulevard going to Hollywood. The city covers 4.55 square miles, 4.21 of them land.

A 2020 headcount found 41,217 people in 17,573 households. Homes are packed close together here, so before you tell a buyer what could be built or added, ask the city which zoning and redevelopment rules apply to your parcel.

Permits and the online portals

The Building Division offers two websites. ePermitsOneStop is shared by the city and Broward County, so plans get reviewed by both at once. HB Self-Service is where you pay fees, check on a permit and book inspections. Searching by address or parcel brings up permit history, and no account is needed.

Run that search on your own house before listing. Any permit that never reached a final inspection should be closed, and the Building Division can explain how. Roofs, windows, electrical work and balcony enclosures are what buyers' inspectors chase most. This city took direct hits from the 1926 hurricane and from Hurricane Katrina in August 2005, so older homes often draw questions about roofs, windows and past claims. Keep claim paperwork next to the permit list.

Who collects the tax bill?

Broward County Records, Taxes and Treasury sends the bill and supports the Value Adjustment Board, the body that hears disputes over exemptions, classifications and values. Visit the Recording Office at 115 S. Andrews Ave, Room 114, Fort Lauderdale, or call 954-831-4000 or 3-1-1 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. The Value Adjustment Board sits at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale.

Exemptions and the assessment cap

  • Homestead: the first $25,000 reduces all taxes, and a further layer of up to $25,000 reduces non-school taxes on assessed value above $50,000.
  • Save Our Homes: assessed value may climb each year by the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, and it resets by itself when the home sells.
  • Renting: the exemption stops once the unit is leased or no longer your permanent home.
  • Portability: the benefit can move with you to a new Florida homestead, provided you set that up within three years.

When you sell, your cap goes away. The Broward Property Appraiser can tell you how the parcel will be reassessed for a buyer, and the new owner's bill will likely be higher than yours. Buyers who estimate their own taxes can land far from your current figure, so hand them your tax history up front.

Redevelopment area

Ordinance No. 96-25, dated December 27, 1996, created the Hallandale Beach Community Redevelopment Agency. The district stretches from Pembroke Road in the north to the Dade-Broward County line in the south, and from Interstate 95 in the west to NE 14th Avenue and its canal in the east.

A house inside those lines may be affected by a redevelopment plan. Phone the city's planning staff and learn what a future owner may build. Such plans can touch park access, traffic and nearby streets, and having an answer ready helps a buyer feel comfortable.

Documentary stamps and other closing costs

Broward charges the regular doc stamp rate of 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, due to the clerk when the deed is recorded. Miami-Dade's higher rate and surtax stay out of the picture. Buyer and seller are both liable to the state, whatever the contract says about who pays.

Recording fees follow section 28.24 and are counted by the page. Condominium and homeowners associations must provide an estoppel or payoff letter, which can add days before closing. Ask for it the moment you have a buyer.

Tenants, estates and missed payments

A tenant in the house changes your schedule. A month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' notice, and a 3-day notice starts the process for unpaid rent. Once a landlord wins in court, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice and then puts the landlord in possession.

When an owner has died, summary administration may fit a small estate: the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or the decedent has been gone more than two years. A foreclosure sale lands 20 to 35 days after judgment. Your closing agent or a Florida attorney can say which path matches your situation.

How to challenge your assessment

If the value on your proposed tax notice looks too high, you have 25 days from the mailing to file a petition with the clerk. The Broward Value Adjustment Board hears these cases at 1801 NW 49th Street, Fort Lauderdale. Questions can go to 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444.

Do this before you sell, since a lower assessment helps you through proration and helps your buyer see a fair history. Bring the notice, recent sale prices near you and photos of any condition problems.

Whatever value ends up on the roll, the tax collector bills from it in November, and your closing agent prorates that bill between you and the buyer as usual.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal or loan underwriting, so the usual wait for a bank's sign-off disappears. Repairs are priced into the offer instead of negotiated after an inspection, and you do not host open houses. Title work, payoff letters, association paperwork and recording still take days, so ask for a written timeline and a named closing agent.

If the house has open permits or a lien, tell the buyer at the start. A lender-financed buyer may insist on fixing those first, while a cash buyer can often close with them open and handle the cleanup after, which is worth comparing against what a listing would net after repairs.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you take offers

Start with records: the deed, the latest tax bill, the permit history, and loan payoff details. A condo or HOA home also needs the association paperwork. Then compare routes. An agent listing draws the most showings, a cash buyer can drop lender conditions, and a private sale leaves the paperwork to you.

With any route, insist on terms in writing and a date when funds reach you. Afterward your closing agent drafts the deed, collects the stamp tax, files with the clerk, and divides the year's property tax between you and the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Hallandale Beach in?

Broward County. The area belonged to Dade County until Broward was formed in 1915.

Do I pay documentary stamp tax in Broward?

Yes. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, and the clerk collects it at recording. Miami-Dade's rate does not apply.

How do I check my permit history?

Open the HB Self-Service portal and search by address, parcel number or inspection number. Finalized documents can be viewed with no account.

Where do I file a property value challenge?

File a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the proposed tax notice. The Broward Value Adjustment Board hears it, and 954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444 can answer questions.

How much notice does a month-to-month tenant get?

30 days. For unpaid rent, a landlord starts with a 3-day notice.

What is a quick way to sell in Royal Palm Beach, FL?

Royal Palm Beach owners usually pick between two quick paths: an investor who accepts present condition, or a competitively priced listing with paperwork ready at the first showing. The listing reaches more people; the investor gives a firmer date.

The village is a municipality, but the property appraiser and the clerk who records your deed belong to Palm Beach County. Sellers lose time on small items such as an expired permit or an unfiled homestead change, so the sections below list checks worth doing first.

  • Gather the deed, any survey, and recent permit and inspection records.
  • Request a payoff letter from the mortgage holder.
  • Decide whether the house sells occupied or empty.

Trees, lakes and canals

Royal Palm Beach serves about 40,000 residents in the central part of Palm Beach County, roughly 10 miles west of the Atlantic Ocean. The village designates its entire area a bird sanctuary and has been a Tree City USA since 1990.

For a seller, the trees and parks matter in practical ways: the village has a vegetation removal permit, and a house with mature landscaping or a lake easement may come with its own rules. Because the village sits inland, buyers touring a house here are weighing canals, lake easements and drainage rather than beach access. The village's forms include easement, lake easement maintenance and canal alert items for that reason.

Village forms and permits that come up before a sale

The village's Forms, Permits and Applications page is the best checklist for work on a house you are about to sell. It lists the documents the building and planning staff use, and several of them show up in buyer inspections.

What if the house has an open permit or a code complaint?

Ask the village building division to look up the address. The village has a request to administratively close a permit, a permit extension application and a code enforcement fine mitigation request form, so each situation has a set procedure.

A permit that was never finaled can surface when a buyer's inspector or lender pulls records. Closing it before listing is usually faster than negotiating it after you have an offer. A cash buyer will often take the house with whatever permit history exists and adjust the price, which can be the simplest path when the work is large.

  • Open permit: ask about closing, extending or finaling it.
  • Code fine: the village offers a fine mitigation request form and an agent authorization form.
  • Palm Beach County impact fees: the village links a county impact fee form for new construction questions.

Transfer tax and recording costs

Palm Beach County has no special deed rate, so the standard 70 cents per hundred dollars applies. Any loan staying on the property is counted in the price used (s. 201.02).

The clerk's per-page recording charge sits under s. 28.24, and your title agent will list both amounts at closing. The contract says who pays, though anyone on the deed remains answerable to the state.

Property taxes and homestead

Values lock in on January 1. The county tax collector mails bills in November, and paying that month earns 4 percent off, with the discount dropping a point each month until February. Unpaid bills turn delinquent on April 1.

Selling counts as a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value the next January 1. If you will buy again in Florida, portability can carry part of a Save Our Homes benefit to the new homestead. Ask the appraiser about the three-year window and Form DR-501T.

Renting out the house ends homestead for that period. Confirm which exemption sits on your parcel with the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser before signing.

  • Inherited: a deed from a personal representative under a probated will is listed by the state as untaxed.

On closing day you sign the deed with two witnesses, review the settlement statement and hand over keys. The Palm Beach County clerk then records the deed, and your proceeds are released. A cash sale skips the buyer's appraisal and loan approval, so title and payoffs set the timeline.

Ask the title agent for a dated list of deadlines so you know which one controls.

What to gather before talking to buyers

Start with the paperwork that answers a buyer's first questions: the recorded deed, a survey if you have one, the last tax bill, and any permit finals for roof, windows, pool or shutters. The village's checklists for those items show what staff expect, so you can tell quickly whether your records are complete.

Next, find out whether a homeowners association or lake or canal easement applies to the lot. An association can add its own approval and fee steps that lengthen a closing. Finally, request a payoff letter from your lender. With those four pieces in hand, a cash buyer can price the house in a day or two, and a listing agent can write accurate disclosures.

  • Recorded deed and survey
  • Latest tax bill and homestead status
  • Permit finals and warranties
  • Payoff letter and association contact

Proving the work was done right

The village publishes a Single Family Home Checklist, a Planning and Zoning Pre Review Checklist and a Home Improvement Guidelines sheet on working with contractors. Reading them shows what staff look for on a finished house.

It also has forms for a Private Provider request and results guideline, which some owners use when a private firm does the inspections. If your records mention a private provider, keep the results with the sale papers.

  • Waiver and Release of Lien forms, partial and final, prove a contractor was paid.
  • The Final Acknowledgement form closes out a job.
  • An Elevation and Drainage Certification Compliance form applies where grading matters.

Buyers rarely read these forms themselves, but their inspectors and title agents often ask whether lien releases exist for recent work.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records my Royal Palm Beach deed?

The Palm Beach County clerk records it. The village does not record deeds, though its building division holds permit records that buyers ask about.

Is the stamp tax different in Palm Beach County?

No. Only Miami-Dade has a different rate, so the 70 cents per $100 deed rate applies in Palm Beach County.

Can I sell if the village has a code fine on the house?

Yes. The village offers a fine mitigation request form, and a payoff or lien search at closing will show any balance. Ask the village code enforcement office for the current status.

Does a tree come down without village approval?

Often not. The village has a Vegetation Removal Permit, so ask the village before cutting anything on the lot.

How long does a homestead exemption last after I sell?

It ends with the sale. The new owner has to file their own application by March 1, and the property goes to just value the next January 1.

Selling an Oviedo house quickly

A quick sale is realistic if you price for speed or accept an offer from an all-cash purchaser who agrees to buy the house in whatever shape it is in. A listing with an agent usually brings more offers. A direct sale cuts showings, repairs and the wait on a buyer's loan.

Oviedo is a mostly residential city in Seminole County, with larger family homes than much of the region. Owners of well-kept houses can test the open market, and owners of dated or worn houses often prefer a straight cash sale.

The 2025 population estimate of 41,317 is only 3.2% above the 2020 base, so growth is steady and not a boom. Pricing near the $454,000 midpoint for owner-occupied homes, and showing clean permit records, helps a house stand out.

City rules that come up before a sale

  • Canopy trees: taking one down needs a city permit, but palms, fruit trees and understory plants such as crape myrtle do not.
  • Clearance over public space: branches must stay 14 feet 6 inches above roads and 8 feet 6 inches above sidewalks, and shrubs near the right-of-way should stay at 3 feet or less.
  • Bear management area: trash stays secured except on pickup days, cans may go to the curb at 5 a.m. or later, and pet food, bird feeders, fruit trees and unclean grills count as attractants that must be secured.
  • Lot surveys and wetlands: the city does not hand out survey or wetland data for private lots, so a buyer who wants them hires a surveyor or environmental professional.

The Building Department works from the Annex Building at 320 Alexandria Boulevard, phone 407-971-5755. If you replaced a roof, added a room or changed wiring, ask what the permit file shows before you list. Open permits are a common cause of stalled closings.
