Power and utilities

Your electric company depends on which side of the C.R. 419 Econlockhatchee River Bridge the home sits. The city does not run street lights or electric service itself. Areas east of the bridge, including The Sanctuary, Riverside and Live Oak Reserve, are served by Florida Power and Light. Most of the rest of the city is served by Duke Energy.

Water, reclaim and sewer accounts run through the city, so schedule the account change for closing day. For after-hours street, tree or stormwater trouble, Public Works lists 407-722-4706, and for water, reclaim or sewer trouble the number is 407-256-5026. Seminole County handles mosquito control through an online request or 407-665-5542.

The city's FAQ page also carries precautionary boil water guidance: boil tap water before preparing food, or use bottled water, and let it cool before use. An address lookup tool on the city site shows whether a property lies inside the city or in unincorporated Seminole County. Check it, because city and county rules differ.

Seminole County property taxes at sale

Two county offices handle the tax side: the Property Appraiser sets values and the Tax Collector sends the bills. The appraiser's office is at 1101 E. 1st Street in downtown Sanford, and customer service answers at 407-665-7506.

The 2026 roll holds 181,187 real property parcels, 138,250 of them residential, with $92 billion in market value against $60 billion in taxable value. The gap comes from exemptions and caps, and it is why a sale can raise a bill.

  • The assessment date is January 1.
  • A homestead's assessed value can climb by the lower of 3 percent or inflation, and the state chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Once title changes hands, the value goes back to just value the following January 1, which can leave the buyer with a larger bill than yours.
  • Homestead filing closes March 1. Pre-filing for the 2027 exemption is open from March 2 through December 31.
  • If you buy again in Florida, form DR-501T lets you port part of your cap savings to the new house, filed within three years.

Voters approved a property tax constitutional amendment on November 3, 2026. Call the appraiser's office to learn what it means for an exemption you hold.

Deed recording cost

The deed tax in Seminole County is the state rate, $0.70 on each $100 of price, and the clerk collects it when the deed is filed. A mortgage the buyer assumes is counted in the price. The state holds every party to the deed liable, whoever agreed to pay.

Recording is billed apart from the stamps, beginning with $5.00 for the opening page under the clerk fee statute. Request an itemized estimate from your closing agent, because extra pages and names change the total.

Selling an inherited or rented house

If the owner died, a small estate (under $150,000 in non-exempt assets) or one opened more than two years after death can use summary administration, with the file kept by the Seminole County Clerk. When a personal representative signs the deed under a probated will, no stamp tax applies. Florida's state estate tax ended for deaths after 2004.

If tenants live there on a month-to-month basis, notice must reach them 30 or more days before the end of the rental period. When rent goes unpaid, a written three-day demand comes first, and weekends and court holidays do not count. In an eviction suit, a tenant raising any defense other than payment has five days to deposit the rent owed with the court or lose those defenses. Many cash purchasers will accept a tenant already living there, and your title agent can say how that shifts the closing date.

What to have ready for a cash buyer

Collect the deed or your last closing papers, the permit file for any roof, room or wiring work, and the lease and rent records if a tenant lives there. Know which utility serves the house and which accounts will move at closing. Ask your agent or title company for a short list of what the buyer will request, so nothing is chased after the contract is signed. A buyer who sees tidy records can make an offer faster, and the title agent can order the lien search sooner. If the house sits in the bear management area, mention how trash is secured so the buyer knows the routine.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a city permit to remove a tree in Oviedo?

Only for canopy trees. Palms, fruit trees and understory plants such as crape myrtle can come out without a permit, but a canopy tree needs one from the city.

Whom should I call about a street light at my Oviedo home?

Your electric provider, not the city. East of the C.R. 419 Econlockhatchee River Bridge that is Florida Power and Light, and west of it Duke Energy. Give them the address and pole number.

When does the Seminole County homestead window close?

March 1. Pre-filing for next year's exemption is open from March 2 through December 31.

Will the buyer keep my capped assessment?

No. A sale resets assessed value to just value on the next January 1. You may move part of your savings to a new Florida homestead within three years.

Who owes the stamp tax on an Oviedo deed?

The statute makes every party liable, and the contract decides who actually pays. The state charges $0.70 on each $100 of price.

Sale routes for an Aventura owner

In a condominium town, the building adds a step to every route: an agent, a private deal or a cash buyer. The city describes itself as an upscale condo community with large, well-known condominium and apartment buildings.

Before choosing, gather your association's documents and ask what approvals a buyer needs. Cash skips lender rules, though an association may still screen the buyer.

  • Through an agent: financed buyers and association approvals.
  • Directly: you arrange the contract and closing agent.
  • For cash: a closing day that suits your move.

Aventura in brief

Aventura covers 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County, and it was incorporated in 1995. Downtown Fort Lauderdale and Miami are about 20 minutes away, and Aventura Mall, restaurants and theaters are close by.

Put those drive times in the listing. Buyers tend to weigh waterfront access and commute together.

Miami-Dade property tax and an Aventura sale

The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser values property but doesn't send tax bills or set taxes. Questions about a bill go to the Miami-Dade Tax Collector. The appraiser's office takes calls at 305-375-4712, and applications for widow and widower exemptions and for veteran disability exemptions can be filed online.

The yearly sequence is steady. The appraiser releases estimates of taxable value on June 1, sends a preliminary certification to the taxing authorities on July 1, and certifies the roll in the fall. Because values reflect January 1 conditions, a change of ownership shows up in assessed value on the next January 1 and in the bill that follows.

Request this year's balance from the Tax Collector so the closing statement lines up with the roll. Keep the August notice of proposed taxes with your closing papers, since it shows how each taxing authority proposed to set its rate.

Who does what for an Aventura owner
OfficeRole

State homestead rules

Homestead relief reaches $50,000 of value for owners who applied by March 1. Save Our Homes keeps annual assessment growth at or under inflation, never above 3 percent, and the state's 2026 figure is 2.7 percent.

Any change in title resets the property to market value on the next January 1, so your buyer's first bill may look much higher than yours. Portability can carry part of your savings to a new Florida homestead set up inside a three year window. Renting the unit or moving out ends the homestead, so avoid a long rental between listing and closing.

Other benefits may matter to you or to your buyer. An ordinance may give owners 65 or older an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 within an income limit. A disabled ex-servicemember may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value, and a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage. Ask the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser which of these apply to the unit.

Bills arrive in November, discounted 4 percent at first and 1 percent by February, and unpaid ones go delinquent April 1.

Deed tax in Miami-Dade

Miami-Dade stands apart on deed tax: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that doesn't apply to a document moving only a single-family dwelling. Other counties charge 70 cents.

Every party to the deed answers to the state for the tax, so the contract should name who covers it. The surtax exception is worded for single-family dwellings, so ask the clerk or your closing agent how a condominium unit is treated before you price the sale. Recording charges at the clerk are set by statute per page. Deeds need two subscribing witnesses.

A Department of Revenue advisement found that one lady bird deed conveyed no present beneficial interest and so carried no deed tax. It rests on its own facts, so get advice before using one.

Protecting yourself from deed fraud

The Miami-Dade clerk runs a no-cost alert system that emails you within 24 hours of a deed or mortgage being filed under your name. Separately, the appraiser's compliance staff accept homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

Owners of a vacant unit should enroll and keep a current mailing address on file.

The appraiser has offices in downtown Miami and at the South Dade Government Center in Cutler Bay, and appointments can be booked online. Bring the deed and any exemption paperwork if you need a record corrected before closing.

Checks before accepting an offer

Start with the building. Ask the association for its financial statements, pending assessments and approval rules, then compare the price against what the appraiser shows for the folio. The property record lists assessments, exemptions and sales, and the appraiser's tax estimator tutorial explains how a buyer can estimate a bill.

  • Payoff letters from every lender or lien holder on the unit.
  • Proof of exemptions you hold, since a sale ends the homestead on that unit.
  • The contract clause naming who pays deed tax.
  • The Tax Collector's balance for this year.

A few other situations change the timeline. A renter behind on payments can be served a written three day notice that skips weekends and court holidays. After a foreclosure judgment the auction follows in 20 to 35 days. A small estate, one at or under $150,000, can use summary administration. Talk to a Florida attorney early if any of these applies.

Working with your association

For a condo, the association is a third party to your sale. Ask the manager what documents a buyer will request, such as financial statements, rules and a statement of dues owed, and how long each takes. Some boards want to meet or screen a buyer, and a few set move-in rules or fees.

Tell your buyer about any pending or planned assessment before the contract is signed. Surprises here are a common reason deals stall. If dues are behind, plan to clear them at closing so the buyer receives the unit free of unpaid balances.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens the file. Send it your deed, association contact and loan payoff information right away. If the association requires approval or a statement of dues, request it the same day, because associations often take longest to reply.

Before closing, read the settlement statement for the payoff, tax credit, deed tax and any dues owed to the association. When did Aventura become a city?

Aventura was incorporated in 1995. It covers 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County.

Selling in Winter Springs?
We buy Winter Springs houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Selling a Winter Springs house: where to start

Your sale paperwork passes through three Seminole County offices, because Winter Springs lies in that county: the clerk files the deed, the appraiser decides what the home is worth for tax, and the collector mails the tax bill.

Most of the city is suburban, with neighborhoods dating to the 1970s and later, a Town Center near State Road 434 and Tuskawilla Road and shoreline along Lake Jesup. Your choices are an agent, a for-sale-by-owner listing or a cash offer. Many streets sit in planned subdivisions, so gather homeowner association rules, dues and any pending assessments before a buyer asks for them.

  • If an HOA governs your street, order its payoff letter early.
  • Confirm that past renovations were permitted.
  • Check your homestead status with the county appraiser.
  • Know your payoff amount if a mortgage remains.

Lake Jesup is shallow, about six feet deep in most places. A house near the shore or on low ground will draw flood zone and insurance questions, so dig out any elevation certificate and claims history for the buyer's lender.

Town Center and neighborhood selling points

Winter Springs built its Town Center as a mixed-use district, opened in 2002 at what the city describes as its geographic heart. It was planned on an old-town Florida model and includes a 54,000 square foot Publix and 61,000 square feet of specialty retail and office space.

Buyers who want a walkable retail center or the water are a different crowd from those who prefer a quiet interior street. Speak to both in your listing by describing the real distance to shopping, trails and the water instead of making general claims. Because the city covers more land than any other in the county, streets differ widely. Write about your own block: house age, lot size, and how near you are to the lake or the shops.

The Town Center is at the corner of State Road 434 and Tuskawilla Road, which means buyers will ask about traffic and commute times. Have real answers ready. A new wastewater treatment plant is also under construction, a project that spans several years. Ask the city utilities office whether any assessments or service changes touch your street.

Property tax bills and early-payment discounts

One office values the home and a different elected office collects the money.

Value is fixed on January 1 and the exemption filing deadline is March 1. In August you get a proposed-tax notice. Bills go out in November, and paying that month saves 4 percent. Each later month cuts the discount by one point until it reaches zero in March. After that the account turns delinquent on April 1 and fees for advertising and collection are added. An installment plan exists but needs an application, so phone the collector for the form and cutoff.

The closing agent divides the year's tax between you and the buyer and pays off anything unpaid from your proceeds. A sale resets the assessment, so your buyer starts at full value the next January 1. Your capped amount stays yours only if you carry it to a new Florida homestead through portability.

Recording charges for the deed

Expect the Seminole clerk to bill $10.00 for page one of any recorded document and $8.50 for every page after that.

The state also levies a deed stamp tax, 70 cents per $100, which the clerk collects when you file. All parties share liability under the statute, so the sales contract should name who pays. Each name past four in the index costs another $1.00.

What filing a deed costs at the Seminole clerk
ChargeAmount
First page recorded$10.00
Pages after the first$8.50 each
Names past four in the index$1.00 each
State stamp tax on a deed70 cents per $100
Copies$1.00 a page

Deeds sent through the clerk's electronic portal usually post within 24 to 72 hours.

Timeline for selling a Winter Springs house

Two things set the pace: title work, and how fast the buyer's loan clears if there is one.

Plan backward from the day you want to close. Do the title search and lien payoffs first. A buried judgment or an open permit is what most often makes a Florida closing slip. The county's Official Records index covers deeds, mortgages, liens, notices of commencement and satisfactions, and your title company searches it under your name and address.

  • Week one: gather the deed, survey, HOA documents and permit records.
  • Next: request payoff figures from the lender, tax collector and HOA.
  • Then: choose the offer, sign the contract and order title.
  • At closing: sign the deed, which Florida requires to carry two subscribing witnesses, and let the title company record it.

Leave your insurance in force until the deed is recorded, then cancel.

Selling with taxes or HOA dues behind

Settle the balance before closing, because unpaid taxes follow the property, not the owner.

An open bill after April 1 can be sold to an investor as a tax certificate. The investor may apply for a tax deed two years after April 1 of the certificate year, and the clerk then auctions your home with no court case. You would lose the house, so call the tax collector early if you are behind.

  • Get a payoff number covering taxes, interest and any added fees.
  • Request a written HOA balance covering dues and assessments.
  • Tell your title company about any lien, judgment or code case you know of.

Closing agents routinely pay such items from the sale funds, so owing money does not by itself block a sale. A cash buyer can often close fast and skips lender appraisal and underwriting, which helps against a deadline, although the same payoffs still come out of your proceeds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Winter Springs houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to bring to the first meeting

Whoever you sell to, a short folder of papers speeds everything. Bring your deed or the closing statement from when you bought, a recent tax bill, the latest mortgage statement, the HOA contact and any permit or insurance records. If you have a survey, include it.

With those in hand, the title company can order its search right away and quote payoffs in week one, which keeps the rest of the timeline on track.

A few questions are worth settling before you sign anything. Does the buyer want possession at closing or later? Who covers the deed stamp tax? Will the buyer's agent or lender need a repair credit, an HOA estoppel letter or a flood certificate? Put the answers in writing in the contract so nothing surprises you at the table. If you are moving to another Florida homestead, tell the appraiser about it too, since portability of your capped assessment depends on that filing.

Frequently asked questions

Is Winter Springs in Seminole County?

Yes. The county clerk takes the deed for recording and the county tax collector mails the bill.

What does the Town Center mean for a seller?

It opened in 2002 and has a large Publix plus retail and office space. If your home is close, describe the real walking or driving distance in your listing.

What is the recording charge for a deed in Seminole County?

Recording runs $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for each later page. The deed stamp tax is a separate 70 cents per $100.

What discount do I get for paying Seminole County taxes early?

The discount starts at four percent for a November payment and falls monthly to one percent in February. Delinquency begins April 1.

Does a buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap in Winter Springs?

No. The cap ends with the sale and the buyer is assessed at full value the next January 1. You can port up to $500,000 of your benefit to a new Florida homestead.

Selling in Riviera Beach?

Selling a house in Riviera Beach

Waterfront living defines Riviera Beach, a compact Palm Beach County city of about 39,357 people as of July 2025. The Port of Palm Beach lies inside its limits, and the city covers both the mainland and part of Singer Island. A seller typically picks from three routes.

  • Hire an agent and wait for a conventional buyer.
  • Find your own buyer and sell directly.
  • Take a cash offer for the house in its current state, closing when you choose.

Lots, ages and styles are mixed, so the condition of the house and its exact location drive the price more than any citywide number.

Housing in Riviera Beach

Riviera Beach market snapshot, 2020 to 2024
MeasureValue
Population estimate, July 202539,357
Owner share of occupied homes62.2%
Middle value, owner-occupied units$354,500
Middle gross rent$1,702
Middle household income$68,060
Households13,927

In this dense city, 62.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so almost two in five households rent. Lease and deposit records are worth keeping ready, because many houses change hands with a tenant inside.

Palm Beach County homestead rules for sellers

The first layer of a homestead exempts $25,000 of the opening $50,000 of assessed value from every tax. A second layer skips school taxes and tops out at $25,722 for 2025. Your January 1 status decides eligibility, and the application is due by March 1.

The office renews exemptions each year without a new form and mails a receipt card at the end of December. If you sell, or if marriage, divorce, death or a change in use alters ownership, tell the property appraiser by phone or email. A buyer starts with a new application.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller, and after a sale the property goes back to just value. Amendment 3 won approval on November 3, 2026, and the Palm Beach office can explain the larger exemption that starts in 2027.

You can file online through E File, at one of five service centers or by mail, and ownership-change calls go to 561.355.2866. Have Social Security numbers for every owner and spouse, a Florida driver's license and a second proof of residence ready.

  • Report a move-out so the exemption ends cleanly.
  • Ask about portability if you are buying another Florida homestead.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Riviera Beach house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Back taxes and tax certificates

An unpaid bill is delinquent from April 1. The county tax collector then auctions a certificate on it, no later than June 1, to the investor willing to take the lowest interest rate (section 197.432). Bids drop in quarter-percent steps.

The investor holding the certificate can start a tax deed case once two years run from April 1 of the issuance year, with a $75 fee (section 197.502). On a homestead, one-half of the latest assessed value gets added to the opening bid. A public auction follows at the clerk's office. The winner deposits the larger of 5 percent or $200 and has 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays, to pay the rest.

A certificate on your house is a reason to sell before the deed process begins, because that can protect your remaining equity. Get the redemption total from the Palm Beach tax collector rather than guessing.

Deeds, recording and landlord points

To end a month-to-month tenancy, a landlord must give at least 30 days' notice ahead of the end of a monthly period (section 83.57). Once a court enters judgment, the sheriff posts 24 hours' notice before carrying out the writ (section 83.62).

Stamp tax on the deed runs 70 cents for each $100, and the clerk collects it when recording. Everyone who signs is liable for it. The recording fee under section 28.24 is $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional one, plus technology charges.

  • Have the closing agent calculate lien payoffs and the tax proration.
  • Collect leases and deposit records to pass to the buyer.
  • Line up the two witnesses the deed needs.

Selling with tenants in the house

Selling does not cancel a lease. A tenant with time left stays unless a lawful notice or an agreement ends the tenancy, and the buyer takes the house with that lease. Let the tenant know in writing that a sale is coming, and schedule showings at reasonable hours with notice.

A buyer who wants the house empty should say so early. Some cash buyers will wait for the lease to end or pay for a move-out, and either arrangement belongs in the contract. Back rent is handled at closing, and your title agent can show you how. Pass along the lease, the deposit amount and any management agreement so nothing surprises the buyer.

Compare the rent actually paid with the lease before you sign. A cash buyer may lower the price for a below-market rent, and a buyer planning to live there may ask for the house vacant.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Riviera Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Marketing a house near the port or Singer Island

It does. The port is part of the waterfront identity, and the waterfront marketplace draws visitors headed for the cruise ships. Houses near the water or the marinas are judged on views, boat access and insurance costs. Inland houses are judged on lot size, roof age and distance to the bridges.

Seasonal storms shape how buyers look at a coastal city. Expect questions about the roof, shutters or impact windows, and the date of your last insurance claim. If you replaced anything after a storm, keep the permit and the final inspection record, since a buyer's insurer may ask for them before binding coverage.

Pull your flood zone information, insurance policy and permit records together before you talk price, so a buyer can weigh ongoing costs as well as the sale price. Sellers who document these early usually face fewer renegotiation requests after inspection.

How a cash sale proceeds

  1. Give the buyer the address, your mortgage balance and the names of occupants.
  2. Study the written offer for price, repair terms and closing day.
  3. The title agent searches the record and orders payoff letters.
  4. Sign the deed with two witnesses watching.
  5. The clerk records it, then your proceeds are released.

Prepare a payoff letter, your newest tax bill, any lease and your insurance declarations page before the first call. Then put three questions to each buyer: how long the offer lasts, who pays for the title policy, and whether an inspection can change the price. Write down the answers.

On the day of the closing, plan to bring a photo ID, review the settlement statement line by line and sign the deed in front of the two witnesses. Leave keys, garage openers and any gate cards with the closing agent. Once the clerk records the deed, the transfer is done and your money is released. Hold on to every page you signed, because the property appraiser or your own tax preparer may ask for them later.

Since nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal, title work sets the speed of a cash sale. Store the signed settlement statement and recorded deed with your tax records.

Frequently asked questions

Is a tenant-occupied Riviera Beach house sellable?

Yes. Until its term runs out or proper notice ends it, the lease stays in force, so give the title agent the lease, deposit records and any management agreement.

Does the buyer keep my Palm Beach homestead exemption?

No. Your buyer must apply separately, and you should tell the property appraiser about the sale.

What is the stamp tax rate on a Riviera Beach deed?

The state rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, which applies everywhere but Miami-Dade, with all parties to the document liable.

When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Certificates on unpaid items are offered for sale by June 1.

Is a cash sale quicker than listing here?

Usually, because no bank appraisal is required. Clear title, a witnessed deed and recording still come before funds.

Selling in Parkland

Parkland sits in Broward's northwest corner, and its buyers usually want acreage, quiet streets and newer construction. Its boundaries are State Road 7 on the east, the Everglades on the west, the Sawgrass Expressway on the south and Loxahatchee Road on the north.

A cattle farmer founded the city in 1963 after buying over 1,000 acres of Everglades land with his father, then sold plots off his ranch. Roads stayed unpaved into the 1980s, and some areas still feel rural. Growth since then runs from under 100 residents on 420 acres to nearly 38,000 on more than 8,000 acres.

Many lots are large, a few back onto horse or trail corridors, and the age and look of the homes change from street to street. Investors paying cash tend to focus on roof, drainage and permit history rather than finishes, so collect those records first.

Sale routes for a Parkland owner

You can list with a broker, go it alone, or take a direct cash purchase. Your calendar and repair budget usually decide.

  • Brokered listing: reaches the most buyers, but means prep, showings and waiting on a loan.
  • Private sale: no commission, but pricing, the contract and disclosures are on you.
  • Direct cash purchase: fast and as is, at a price that reflects repair and resale risk.

Compare offers by the amount left in your pocket once repairs, taxes, fees and carrying costs are paid, and read the whole contract first. A newer roof and clean permits help on all three routes.

Permits in Parkland

Building permits and occupancy certificates come from the Building Department inside City Hall at 6600 University Drive, phone 954.753.5447. The office keeps Monday to Thursday hours, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Contractors now apply through the city's online portal and must re-register with new insurance and license documents. Fees changed starting October 1, 2025 under a city resolution, so request the current schedule from the department before you plan repairs.

An unclosed permit for an old roof, window or addition can hold up a closing. Find out what the department has on file for your lot before you market the house.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Parkland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property taxes and your sale

Florida sets the calendar and Broward offices follow it. January 1 is the valuation date, March 1 is the exemption deadline, and bills arrive in November.

  • Early payment pays: 4 percent off in November, then one point less each month through February.
  • A bill still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.
  • A permanent residence can get up to $50,000 of homestead exemption if it was occupied that way on January 1.

Once the house sells, it is reassessed at just value the next January, and the new owner may owe much more than you. Leave your own bill out of the sales pitch. The Broward property appraiser's number is 954-357-6830.

Deed transfer charges

Deeds in Broward carry a documentary stamp tax at a single rate. The contract may name who pays, but under state rules everyone on the deed remains liable.

Florida deed and recording charges
ChargeRate
Doc stamps on the deed$0.70 per $100 of price
Doc stamps on a mortgage35 cents per $100 borrowed
Recording, page one$5.00, then $4.00 for each added page
Names past the fourth$1.00 each

The clerk collects at recording. Your closing agent can put these rates against your real price in a written estimate.

Inherited house or behind on payments

Both follow set legal steps. For a modest estate, summary administration is open when non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or when the death was more than two years ago.

After a foreclosure judgment, the auction is set roughly three to five weeks out, though the lender can agree to a later date. Money from the sale above the debt may be claimable, and homestead owners are told to ask the clerk within 10 days. A sale beforehand can protect equity, so speak with an attorney and your lender.

  • Gather the deed, your newest tax bill and all lender letters.
  • Ask the Broward clerk's office which filings touch the property.
  • Request a payoff statement before weighing offers.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Parkland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When a tax bill goes unpaid

April 1 starts delinquency, and by June 1 the county sells certificates against the unpaid tax. Once two years pass from April 1 of the issue year, the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed and pays $75 to do it.

The tax collector then identifies who must get notice: the titleholder, lienholders and any contract for deed buyer. Selling before an application is filed keeps your options open if you are behind. Request a current payoff figure from the Broward tax collector's office.

  • A homestead owner over 65 may defer part of the bill on Form DR-570, due March 31.
  • To prepay in installments, apply by May 1.
  • Whether to accept a partial payment is up to the collector.

Family transfers and quitclaim deeds

Stamp tax applies to a quitclaim, and for Save Our Homes it is a change of ownership unless an exception, such as a transfer between spouses, fits. Handing the house to a relative before a sale can lift the tax base and add stamp tax.

A lady bird deed is treated differently: a revenue advisement found no present beneficial interest passed on the facts it reviewed. See an attorney before you record any of these.

Parks, trails and horse access

Parkland has 11 parks with trails for families, dogs and horses, a library, and a Native American midden more than 1,000 years old. Buyers who want room like trails and horse access, so say so if your lot backs onto one. Check park and school boundaries yourself before advertising them.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a house with a tenant

When rent is unpaid, the landlord serves a written 3 day demand that skips weekends and court holidays. Other curable lease problems get a 7 day window.

Ending a month by month tenancy takes 30 days' notice. Read the lease before selling an occupied house, since a sale does not cancel it. Show buyers the lease and rent history early, and warn the tenant before any showing or inspection.

What to have ready before you list

Pull together your deed, the newest tax bill, notes on the roof and drainage, and the permit file from the Building Department. Ask your lender for a payoff statement if you still owe. Clear records let a cash buyer move fast, and the closing agent can start title work as soon as you sign. An open permit should be closed out or disclosed, not left for the inspector to find. Walk the lot too: with larger parcels, buyers look hard at fencing, drainage swales and any outbuilding, and a short list of what is permitted and what is not saves arguments later.

Frequently asked questions

Which office runs the tax timeline for a Parkland home?

The state sets the calendar and Broward offices apply it: value on January 1, exemption filing through March 1, bills in November, delinquency from April 1.

Does paying cash remove doc stamp tax in Parkland?

No. The stamp tax is $0.70 per $100 of price however you pay, and all parties on the deed are liable. Decide who covers it in the contract.

Can I sell a Parkland house with open permits?

You can, but it complicates things. The Building Department at 954.753.5447 can tell you which permits are still open on your lot, and buyers and title companies will look.

What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?

It ends at the sale. The buyer is assessed at just value beginning the following January.

How soon can an inherited Parkland house be sold?

That depends on the court path. Estates with non-exempt assets up to $150,000 can use summary administration, while larger or contested ones need formal administration, so see a probate attorney.

How a Leesburg sale works

Leesburg is in Lake County, and the city runs its own electric, gas, water and wastewater utilities. A sale therefore involves city utility accounts as well as county tax records. Whether you plan to list, sell alone or take a cash offer, sort out both sets of paperwork early.

  • An agent listing works for a sound house and a long runway.
  • A by-owner sale needs you to run showings, contracts and disclosures.
  • A cash buyer suits a house where repairs, renters or liens drive the schedule.

About Leesburg

Leesburg is Lake County's oldest city, incorporated on July 12, 1875. It takes its name from Calvin Lee, whose brother Evander Lee settled the area in 1857. The city commission form of government dates to the 1922 charter, and Venetian Gardens on the lakefront began as a project in 1938. Buyers drawn by water access or events often start near the lakefront and downtown, so say how far your house is from both.

Storms, cold snaps and water limits

Storm history comes up in inspections, insurance quotes and buyer questions. The city closed city facilities for Hurricane Helene and Hurricane Milton in September and October 2024 and earlier for Hurricane Ian in 2022. Lake County issued a countywide burn ban in March 2025, and the city has handed out sandbags ahead of storms.

In early 2026 a historic freeze led the city to post cold-weather tips, a good reminder to check pipes, irrigation lines and older heating systems before showings. In May 2026 a Phase III Extreme Water Shortage notice came from the St. Johns water district, so ask the city and the district what lawn and irrigation limits apply when you list.

Put storm repair receipts and insurance claim papers in a single folder. A cash buyer will price whatever repairs remain, and a financed buyer's lender may ask for proof of the fixes. Add a few sentences on how the house fared.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Leesburg house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Lake County offices, exemptions and key dates

The county property appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and a separate county tax collector sends bills and takes payment. Value is set January 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and bills come in November.

A homestead exemption can reach $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school taxes, and a second layer of up to $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 and only to non-school taxes (s. 196.031).

Dates for a Leesburg homeowner
DateWhat to do or expect
March 1Exemption filing deadline
March 31Homestead tax deferral application (Form DR-570)
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
May 1Leesburg fire assessment exemption applications due

The city posts its fire assessment exemption notice each winter. Ask the city how the assessment is handled on a sale so it does not surprise either side.

Protecting your title from deed fraud

The Lake County Property Appraiser warns that scammers record phony deeds to appear as owners, then take money from people who believe they are renting or buying.

The Lake County Clerk of the Court runs a free alert that e-mails you when anything is filed in the official records under a name you monitor, for as many as 5 names per address. Owners of vacant Leesburg houses and heirs who live elsewhere benefit most. Sign up before you list so any strange filing against the property reaches you quickly.

Can back taxes cost me a Leesburg house?

A bill left unpaid goes delinquent on April 1. By June 1 the county sells a certificate against it to an investor. That investor must wait until two years after April 1 of the issue year before pressing the owner.

Then the investor can apply for a tax deed by paying a $75 fee (s. 197.502). If the land is homestead, the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value plus what is owed. Request a full statement of amounts due from the Lake County tax collector before you list.

A homestead owner with a tight budget can file Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year to defer the portion of the bill above 5 percent of last year's household income. The threshold is 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

Permits and road projects

Leesburg announced in August 2025 that building permit fees would rise in October, so a renovation you planned to permit may cost more than older figures suggest.

The Florida Department of Transportation has run work on US 27 from CR 33 to Middlesex Road and on SR 44 at South Street. Buyers drive a street before they bid, so a project near your address can come up in negotiation. Ask the city about open permits on the address, and give any past owner-built work to the buyer in writing.

What to fix before showing a Leesburg house

Tour the house the way a buyer would, curb to back fence. Start with fixes that cost little: loose handrails, stained ceiling tiles, dripping faucets and broken screens. Pull together utility bills, storm repair receipts and warranty papers.

Test smoke alarms and check the electrical safety of older wiring before listing. A clean inspection report helps hold your price, and it shows buyers you kept up with the house. Because Leesburg's utilities are city-run, schedule the final reads for water, gas and electric around your closing date.

  • Smoke alarms tested and batteries replaced.
  • Roof, plumbing and electrical panel dates written down.
  • Irrigation timers set to the rules in force.
  • Final utility reads booked for the closing date.

From offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes. You then review a settlement statement and sign the deed. On the closing date, move the city electric, gas and water accounts to the buyer and file your last bills with the sale papers. A buyer's agent will usually ask when each meter was read.

If a tenant lives in the house, tell the buyer in writing whether the lease stays or ends. Bring ID, the payoff figure from your lender and the names of everyone on the deed to the signing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Weighing a listing against a cash offer

Write both options down as the cash you would keep. For a listing, start with the expected price, then take away the agent's commission, repairs a buyer's inspector will request, and the months of insurance, taxes and utilities you pay while the house sits on the market. For a cash offer, subtract only the fees the contract hands to you.

A sound, updated house with time to wait often does better on the market. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant or a lien tends to move faster to a buyer who closes as is. Ask for the deposit, the closing date and the title company in writing, and never pay a fee just to receive an offer.

Frequently asked questions

When was Leesburg incorporated?

July 12, 1875, about a dozen years before Lake County was formed.

Who values my Leesburg home for tax purposes?

The Lake County Property Appraiser sets value each January 1 and rules on exemptions, while the tax collector sends bills. Exemption claims are due March 1.

Can I monitor for fraudulent deeds on my property?

Yes, through a free Lake County Clerk of the Court e-mail alert covering up to 5 names per address.

When do unpaid property taxes become delinquent?

On April 1. A certificate is then sold by June 1, and its holder may seek a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502).

Which utilities does the city of Leesburg run?

Electric, gas, water and wastewater, so utility transfers at closing go through the city.

How fast can an Estero house sell?

When nobody needs a lender's sign-off, an Estero sale moves at the speed of the title work. Payoffs, liens and co-owners who have to sign from another state are the usual slow spots.

Estero is a village in Lee County, formed on December 31, 2014, with roughly 20 square miles inside its limits. The village runs its own government, yet assessment, billing and recording all go through county offices. Your deed gets recorded with the county clerk, and the tax collector sends your bill.

If a homeowners association governs your street, find out right away whether it must issue a payoff or approval letter. Waiting on that letter can stretch a closing by several days.

Design standards and older records

Growth surged around 2001 and 2002, and community groups responded by writing architectural and landscaping guidelines that continue to shape the area. The Coconut Point Mall district is the best-known example. Buyers sometimes ask what those standards mean for exterior changes.

Did you add a screened porch, replace a roof or repaint outside the usual palette? Round up the permits and approvals so everyone reads the same clean record. Settlement here goes back well over a century, which makes old surveys and easements worth reviewing before you list.

Homestead after you sell

Lee County's appraiser wants exemption applications in by March 1 and hands out no retroactive relief. The 2026 exemption has two layers: $25,000 that reaches every tax, and up to $26,411 more that skips school taxes, measured on assessed value above $50,000.

Your homestead ends with the sale, so the buyer files a new application. If you are moving elsewhere in Florida, portability may carry part of your capped benefit along when you apply by March 1.

  • Renting the house out before closing can forfeit homestead for that year.
  • Buyers who close after January 1 should file before the following March 1.
  • Exemption staff at the appraiser's office can confirm what your record shows before you close.

Senior exemption and county dates

Owners who are 65 or older, with limited household income, can claim an extra exemption. Lee County lists the Village of Estero among the governments that approved it, at $50,000 and up to $250,000, matching the figure for all Lee County millages. At least one applicant must reach 65 by January 1 of the assessment year, which can matter if your buyer is an older owner-occupant.

Lee County dates for sellers and buyers

Income papers for the senior exemptionJune 1
Proposed tax notices mailedAugust

Unpaid taxes delinquentApril 1

Missing income papers on March 1 is no reason to skip the application. File, then send the papers by June 1.

What the Save Our Homes reset means for a buyer

Under Save Our Homes, a homestead's assessment can climb each year only by the lower of 3 percent or inflation. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. That cushion belongs to the owner, not the house, so a sale sends the property back to just value on the next January 1.

So a buyer's first tax bill may exceed yours by a wide margin, especially if you have owned for many years and your assessment lags the market. Say so early and the buyer will not feel misled.

Closing costs and deadlines

The stamp tax on a Lee County deed is the state's 70 cents per $100, and everyone on the deed is on the hook for it. Page-based recording fees under section 28.24 are billed by the clerk when the deed is filed.

Notices of proposed taxes show up in August and bills in November, and an unpaid bill goes delinquent April 1. A fall or winter sale means the closing agent must split the year's bill, so ask how that will be done. A sensible checklist:

  1. Request payoff letters for each loan or lien.
  2. Ask the association for an estoppel letter if one exists.
  3. Check the tax status with the Lee County Tax Collector.
  4. Schedule the deed signing with two witnesses present.

Selling an inherited Estero house

An inherited house generally sells after a court, or the estate's paperwork, gives someone authority to sign. A smaller estate may qualify for a shorter court process, and a probate attorney or the Lee County Clerk's probate office can say which route fits. Florida collects no state estate tax on deaths after 2004, so the costs are mostly court steps, creditor deadlines and the deed.

Heirs living out of state can still sell. Name a local person to handle signings, or set up a remote signing with the title company, and send documents ahead so nothing waits on the mail.

What a cash sale skips, and what remains

A cash buyer removes the appraisal, the loan underwriting and most repair negotiation. Three tasks stay. The title company still searches for liens and open permits. Any mortgage still gets paid from your proceeds. The deed is still signed, witnessed and recorded. Ask the buyer to put the closing date, the cost split and the treatment of anything left in the house in writing, and refuse any request for money from you before closing.

Compare offers side by side by what you would actually receive after payoffs, stamps, recording and unpaid taxes, not by the headline number.

Documents to gather before closing

Paperwork in hand is the cheapest way to protect a quick closing.

  • Your recorded deed and the property's legal description.
  • The newest mortgage statement, or a request for a payoff.
  • Permits, approvals and any open code or association violations.
  • Association contact details, if one governs the house.
  • Leases and deposit records for a rented house.

The title company will ask for most of this anyway. Assembling it first can save days.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Closing day, step by step

Closing is less dramatic than people expect. The title agent reviews the settlement statement with you line by line, and you should question any charge you do not recognize before signing. You sign the deed and the closing paperwork, hand over keys and any garage remotes, and the agent records the deed with the county clerk. Loan payoffs and the stamp tax come out of your proceeds, and the remainder is paid to you by wire or check.

Walk through the house one final time just before closing, take meter photos for your records, and keep copies of everything you sign for your own files. Then change your mailing address so tax mail and any refund reach you, and tell the homeowners association, if there is one, that the house has sold.

Frequently asked questions

Is Estero a city or part of Lee County?

Estero is a village, created on December 31, 2014, and it lies inside Lee County. County offices still handle your tax roll, tax bill and recording.

When must a new owner apply for homestead?

By March 1 of the year the exemption should start. Lee County grants nothing retroactively, so file soon after moving in.

Can Estero owners get the senior exemption?

Yes, owners 65 and older with limited household income can. The amount is $50,000 and up to $250,000, applications are due March 1 and income papers can follow by June 1.

Is a lawyer needed to sell an inherited Estero house?

Not always. Smaller estates may qualify for summary administration, but title companies often want court paperwork or proof of a personal representative's authority, so ask a probate attorney.

What does the deed stamp tax cost in Estero?

Lee County uses the state's 70 cents for each $100 of consideration. The clerk collects it when the deed is filed.

The bay, flood zones and your sale

Panama City sits on St. Andrews Bay in the Florida Panhandle. The bay wraps much of the city and shelters the harbor of the Port of Panama City complex. Moisture and salt air shape what buyers inspect first: roofs, window seals, siding and anything near the water.

Bay County tells residents to look up their address on its evacuation zone map, and the zones may differ from what people assume. The county's floodplain ordinance was updated to federally required standards with new flood maps, and the county keeps a copy of the updated flood zones in its map gallery. Ask which map your parcel sits on before you describe flood risk to a buyer. A seller who knows the evacuation zone and the flood map status of the lot can answer the questions insurers and buyers raise early.

Buyer interest near the water

The water is the draw. The city has public boat ramps at St. Andrews Marina, Downtown Marina, Carl Gray Park, Snug Harbor and Bob George Park, and two city marinas on the Intracoastal Waterway take vessels up to 130 feet. Downtown holds the Center for the Arts, and St. Andrews, Downtown and Millville are tied together by a mural trail.

Give your distance to any of these in plain miles, since a buyer will check it on a map. Bay County also funds road and utility projects through a half-cent surtax and posts an interactive project map, so you can point a buyer there instead of guessing which streets are slated for work.

Permit history to pull

Pull every permit, final inspection and certificate for work done on the house. The city requires a permit before a project starts, including reroofing, decks, carports, sheds, remodels and changes to electrical, plumbing, mechanical, structural, irrigation or insulation systems.

The duty to confirm permits rests on the owner or the owner's authorized agent. A permit goes invalid if work does not begin within 6 months of issuance or stops for 6 months after it starts, and an extension must be requested in writing with a fee. Work has to stay exposed for inspection until approved.

The city issues a certificate of occupancy for a structure and a certificate of completion where occupancy does not apply, such as a reroof or system alteration. Building Services is at 501 Harrison Ave., phone 850-872-3025. Some projects need approval from other agencies too, such as the Florida Department of Environmental Protection.

Non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater and solid waste ride on the same bill and also become delinquent April 1. Changes to a name, address, location or assessed value go through the property appraiser. If an escrow servicer pays your bill, ask it to request the original notice so you get a copy.

Paying or asking questions in person

The Bay County Tax Collector runs offices in Panama City at 850 W. 11th St., Panama City Beach at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Lynn Haven at 700 Florida Ave. and Callaway at 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy. Renewal kiosks sit inside the Publix stores on W. 23rd St. and on Panama City Beach Parkway.

  • Bring the tax notice or the property address. Only Bay County property tax is taken at these counters.
  • Delinquent payments must be made with certified funds: cash, cashier's check, money order or card.
  • Appointments can be booked online for each office.

Homestead after a sale

Homestead does not stay with the house. The exemption belongs to the resident owner, and a sale lifts the capped assessment back to full market-based value at the start of the next year, so a buyer can open with a bigger bill than yours.

A permanent home can lose up to $50,000 of taxable value, with school taxes touched only by the first $25,000. The Bay County property appraiser takes applications until March 1. If you are moving within Florida, portability can carry your capped savings to the next house, provided you set up that homestead inside three years.

Voters considered Amendment 3, a constitutional change on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would raise the non-school homestead exemption if 60 percent approved. Ask the property appraiser what the outcome means for your parcel.

Bay County also requires registration, reporting and inspection for vacation rentals in the unincorporated areas. That is worth knowing if your house has been used for short stays and the new owner wants to continue.

Deed charges at a Bay County closing

Florida's deed tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, and all parties to the deed stay liable for it. The clerk takes it at recording.

Recording fees open at five dollars for page one and four dollars for every later page, then add a trust fund charge and a technology charge per page. A mortgage the buyer assumes counts toward the consideration, so the closing agent adds it to the total.

Inherited, rented or behind on taxes

Each case has its own clock. Florida offers a shortcut for modest estates and a short written demand for unpaid rent, so ask a lawyer which route fits.

If tax stays unpaid, the county sells a certificate against the parcel and an investor can eventually seek a tax deed, which is why a payoff matters. Collect the payoff letter, the lease or the court file before you weigh an offer.

Steps from offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens, unpaid taxes and open permits, and the closing agent prepares the deed and the settlement statement. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which removes the longest wait. Bring a photo ID, the payoff letter if a mortgage remains, and permit papers for any roof or system work. Settle utility accounts for closing day, and leave keys and any warranties for the buyer. Ask the closing agent how and when your proceeds will arrive.

If the house has storm or water history, gather repair invoices, insurance claim papers and any elevation or flood zone documents, since a buyer's insurer will want them before binding coverage. Sellers with a tenant should add the lease and rent ledger. When the file is complete, the title company can often clear the house faster, and a cash buyer can set a closing date that fits your move.

How is Panama City located on the bay?

Panama City sits on St. Andrews Bay in the Florida Panhandle, and the bay wraps much of the city. Look up your address on the county evacuation zone map and check your flood zone before you list.

When are Bay County property taxes due?

Notices go out on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31. Taxes unpaid after that become delinquent on April 1.

Which permits should I check before selling in Panama City?

Check permits for roofs, decks, sheds, remodels and electrical, plumbing, mechanical and structural work, plus any certificate of occupancy or completion. Call Building Services at 850-872-3025.

Does the Bay County Tax Collector have an office on Panama City Beach?

Yes. It has an office at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, along with offices in Panama City, Lynn Haven and Callaway.

Can homestead carry over to a house I buy next?

Partly. Portability can transfer the Save Our Homes difference to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years, and you file for it with the new county's property appraiser.

Selling with a tenant in the house

You can, but the lease keeps running after a sale contract is signed. A buyer either takes the unit with the tenant in it or waits for the landlord to end the tenancy through the notice steps in Chapter 83.

Notice lengths depend on the problem. Missed rent draws a 3-day demand (weekends and court holidays do not count), and a lease violation the tenant can fix draws 7 days to cure. Florida foreclosures run through the courts, so you usually have time to sell before a judgment sale. After judgment, the clerk sets the auction between 20 and 35 days out unless the lender agrees to longer (s. 45.031).

Talk to your servicer and the closing agent about a payoff statement, and ask whether a short sale or an investor purchase fits your balance. Open every letter from the lender and the court, and write the response date on a calendar. Silence is the costliest choice, because deadlines keep running whether or not you answer. A housing counselor or a legal aid office can read the papers with you before you decide anything.

Getting the house ready to show

Start with what buyers notice from the curb: the roof line, the yard, the front door and any peeling paint. On an older house, buyers ask about the age of the roof, the electrical panel, the plumbing and the air handler. A one-page list of what was replaced and when answers those questions before they become negotiating points.

Clear out clutter and walk each room with a notepad. Note stains, soft floors, door-frame cracks and anything that smells of damp. Florida humidity punishes closed-up houses, so run the air conditioning and open the blinds before every showing.

Listing versus investor offer

Write each path as a net figure. For a listing, take the expected sale price and subtract the agent's commission, the repairs a buyer's inspector will demand, carrying costs for each month on the market, and closing costs. For an investor offer, subtract only what the contract assigns to you.

Then compare timing. A listing may take months and can fall through at financing or appraisal. An investor sale can close within a few weeks, but the price is lower. Ask any buyer to put these terms in writing, and read every line before signing.

  • Price, deposit and whether it is refundable.
  • Closing date and who picks the title company.
  • Who pays for repairs found in inspection.
  • What happens to any security deposit held for a tenant.

From signed contract to closing day

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a search on the parcel. It looks for mortgages, judgments, unpaid taxes and anything recorded against your name. Clear what you can early, because a surprise lien is the most common reason a closing slips.

You will see a draft settlement statement before signing. Check the payoff, the prorated tax, recording charges and any fee the buyer expects you to cover. Bring photo ID and the names of every owner on the deed, since each one signs. If an owner lives out of state, arrange the signing ahead of time.

On closing day the deed is recorded with the Broward clerk, the lender is paid off and the remainder goes to you. Book final readings for utilities and hand over keys, garage openers and any warranty papers.

About four square miles, centered on State Road 7 (US 441) at Oakland Park Boulevard.

Can I sell while a tenant lives in the house?

Yes. The lease stays in force, so the buyer takes the house with the tenant or waits for a lawful notice process to end the tenancy (s. 83.56, s. 83.57). Put your chosen route in the sales contract so the title company and the tenant both know the plan.

Will the buyer inherit my capped assessment?

No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value the following January 1 (s. 193.155).

When do Broward tax bills go out?

In November. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, so ask the Broward tax collector for an exact balance before closing.

Who polices Lauderdale Lakes?

Can a Dunedin house sell quickly for cash?

Yes. With no loan approval and no lender appraisal in the way, a Dunedin sale can close as fast as the title search and payoff letters permit. What actually slows sales is the house: repairs, a tenant, an estate or a lender's deadline. Selling directly also spares you an inspection-driven repair list to argue over.

Dunedin is on the Gulf side of Pinellas County, north of Clearwater and St. Petersburg, and has more than 35,000 residents. It is a walkable town with a Scottish name and Scottish street names, which draws buyers who want to live near downtown, second-home owners and investors. A cash buyer can serve any of them without asking you to stage anything.

Homestead in Pinellas County after a sale

The Pinellas County Property Appraiser prints the homestead benefit as $51,411 off assessed value. The first $25,000 applies to every tax on the bill. The remaining $26,411 covers value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves out school taxes.

That exemption ends when you sell. A sale, renting the property, any change of ownership or moving out all stop it. If the buyer closes after January 1, your homestead may still appear on the August notice, and the credit comes off on December 31. The buyer then files an original application by March 1 to start their own.

The assessment cap does not follow the house either. The next January the state resets the assessment to full market level. If you are buying elsewhere in Florida, ask about portability, which carries part of your capped benefit to a new homestead established within three years.

Fixed costs of a Dunedin sale

The state and county charges are set by law, so you can see them before you list. The largest is usually the deed stamp tax, 70 cents for every $100 paid, which applies in every county except Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable for it, although the contract normally lands it on the seller.

The Pinellas clerk also bills a per-page recording fee under section 28.24, with technology and trust fund add-ons. Ask the clerk for the total on your particular instrument.

What a new owner brings to file for homestead

The appraiser's office wants proof of residency for every owner, spouses included. That means a Florida driver license and auto registration, a voter card or permanent resident card where one applies, and Social Security numbers for all owners and spouses, even when only one spouse is on the deed.

An owner who holds a residency-based exemption elsewhere will be denied. The office asks for proof that the other exemption was removed, or the latest tax bill on any property owned elsewhere, within 30 days of applying.

  • File online or in person at one of the appraiser's offices.
  • Owners who had homestead last year and still live there get a receipt in early January.
  • Tell the office if you stop qualifying, for example after renting the home out.

Pass this list to your buyer. A quick, correct filing keeps their first tax bill predictable.

Signing and recording the deed

A Florida deed must be in writing and witnessed by two people, and section 689.01 allows witnessing over audio-video technology. The closing agent normally drafts the deed and takes it to the clerk. The usual order:

  1. Sign the sales contract and open a title order.
  2. Clear liens, loan payoffs and any open permits the search turns up.
  3. Sign the deed before two witnesses.
  4. Pay stamps and recording fees to the clerk.
  5. Let the appraiser update the tax roll afterward.

Estate sales differ. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is untaxed, while quitclaims and deeds given to a lender do carry stamp tax.

Taxes or the mortgage behind

Act before the legal clock runs out. Tax bills arrive in November with a 4 percent discount that falls to 1 percent by February. Unpaid taxes are late from April 1, and certificates on them go to auction by June 1.

Foreclosure moves through the courts. Once final judgment is entered, the clerk sets a public sale 20 to 35 days out unless the plaintiff consents to a delay, and the winning bidder puts down 5 percent. Selling first can retire the loan and leave any equity with you. After a sale has already happened, the clerk can explain how surplus funds are claimed.

Cash sale or listing?

Compare what lands in your account, not the headline price. A listing may reach a higher number, but it adds showings, repair negotiations, financing risk and months of carrying costs. A cash purchase moves fast and the buyer accepts the house as is.

Run the closing statement for each route: loan payoff, stamps, recording, unpaid taxes and the repairs you would otherwise fund. For recent nearby sales, search the Pinellas Property Appraiser's public records or ask a local agent. Written terms from every buyer make the comparison honest, and a request for fees from you before closing is a reason to stop and talk to an attorney.

If a tenant lives in the house

A tenant does not block a sale. The lease still binds both sides, and Florida sets minimum notice periods for ending a tenancy, so read the lease before you promise a buyer an empty house. Tell each buyer about the tenancy at the start, and keep the lease, rent history and deposit records together for the title company.

Getting ready before you accept an offer

A few errands done in advance keep a direct sale from stalling. Locate your recorded deed and legal description. Ask your lender for a written payoff. Gather permit records for any repairs, and settle or at least disclose open permits. Pull the latest tax bill from the Pinellas Tax Collector. If the house is rented, find the lease and deposit records. When an estate is involved, work out early who has authority to sign, because a title company will insist on seeing it.

With those items in hand you can answer a buyer's questions in a day, which matters when the whole appeal of a cash sale is speed. Afterward, remember to cancel insurance and move utilities only once the deed has recorded, so the house is never uncovered mid-sale.

The contract usually puts it on the seller, though the state makes every party to the deed liable. The clerk collects the flat 70 cents for every $100 paid.

Will the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?

No. It ends with the sale. The new owner files with the Pinellas appraiser by March 1, and any leftover credit on a notice comes off December 31.

Can I sell with a tenant living in the house?

Yes. The lease still binds the parties, and Florida sets minimum notice periods for ending a tenancy, so read the lease first.

What happens to my Save Our Homes savings?

The buyer does not get them, because the assessment resets to full market level the next January. You may move your own benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability.

Which office records the deed?

The Pinellas clerk's recording office, and the closing agent usually files it.

Servicemembers and former servicemembers have separate routes. Getting a New Smyrna Beach house ready to sell

New Smyrna Beach is a coastal Volusia County city with an old downtown on the Indian River, and the age of the housing is the first thing a buyer or inspector weighs. Part of the city is a federally listed historic district and other parts are post-war neighborhoods, so repair and exterior-change rules differ from street to street.

The city's Development Services Department covers planning, engineering, building and code compliance, which means most permit, zoning and violation questions go through one office. Before you list, check for open permits, find out whether the house is in a historic district, and ask code compliance if a case is open on the address.

Historic districts and older homes

The New Smyrna Beach Historic District joined the national register on April 26, 1990. It covers about 100 acres of commercial and residential blocks built between 1885 and 1935, with 313 contributing and 97 non-contributing buildings when it was nominated. The district is a two to six block wide band along the North Indian River, running roughly from Riverside Drive on the east to U.S. Highway 1 on the west, and from Ronnoc Lane on the north to Smith Street on the south. Most buildings are wood frame vernacular homes and masonry commercial buildings.

  • A separate Coronado National Register district also exists.
  • The city runs a historic property plaque program and a historic preservation grant program.
  • A property tax exemption for historic properties is part of its preservation pages, so ask the planning office whether your home could qualify.

If yours is an early twentieth century wood frame house, put its age, roof and wiring updates in the listing. Buyers will ask.

Code compliance

Enforcement here starts with complaints. Officers look into a possible violation, decide what needs correcting and work with the owner to fix it. A case that cannot be settled at staff level goes to a Code Compliance Board of citizen volunteers or a special magistrate.

Common concerns are substandard structures, high grass and weeds, trash, open storage, junk vehicles and front yard parking. An empty house is easy to flag, and the city has an abandoned and vacant property registration form on its code compliance page. That is worth knowing if you inherited a house and left it sitting.

  • Call 386-410-2870 to schedule time with a code officer.
  • A lien amnesty application is among the city's forms, so ask whether a past fine can be reduced.
  • Since July 1, 2021, state law bars officers from investigating anonymous tips unless there is an imminent threat to health, safety or sensitive resources.
  • The city posts a short-term rentals brochure for owners who rent by the night.

A buyer's title search will turn up recorded code liens. Resolve them before closing or have the closing agent pay them from your proceeds.

Fire service, insurance and flood paperwork

The city has its own fire department, with 64 certified firefighters, paramedics, EMTs and administrative staff. It runs four fire engines, a tower truck, two full-time ambulances and a fire rescue boat, and it answered 7,177 calls in 2025. All four aging fire stations were replaced after voters approved an $18.3 million general obligation bond in 2004, and the Central Fire Station sits at 1400 State Road 44.

In a coastal city, buyers ask about insurance and flood zone early. Pull your insurance declarations and any elevation certificate before you list so you can answer the same day.

What buyers ask about an older home

Four topics come up first with older coastal houses: the roof, the electrical panel, plumbing and insurance. Because most buildings in the historic district are wood frame, termite history and moisture damage are fair questions too.

  • Open or closed permits for additions, porches and window replacements.
  • Whether the property sits in a National Register district or has a historic plaque.
  • Any recorded code lien, and whether a lien amnesty application was filed.

Having these answers ready cuts inspection time and shrinks the price cushion a buyer adds for unknowns. For an estate property, filing the vacant property registration where it applies and keeping the yard cleaned up helps keep code compliance out of the sale.

Taxes and fees at closing

Volusia County uses the statewide base deed stamp rate of 70 cents on each $100, the figure that applies everywhere in Florida except Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable, and the clerk collects the tax at recording.

How can I sell a New Smyrna Beach house on a short timeline?

You can list, sell directly, or accept an investor's bid, and repairs, timing and your loan payoff steer the choice. A listing reaches the most buyers but adds showings, inspection negotiation and loan approval time. An investor's cash purchase removes the financing step and lets you pick a closing date, though the buyer discounts for condition and speed.

  • Check the age and condition of the roof, electrical panel and plumbing while you work out an asking price.
  • Get each bidder's answer in writing on title charges and stamps.
  • Confirm there are no open permits or code liens.

If your lender has started foreclosure, the court sets the sale between 20 and 35 days after final judgment unless the lender agrees to more time. For an inherited property, summary administration is the shortened court process available for estates with a non-exempt value under $150,000, or for deaths more than two years back.

From accepted offer to keys

The title company does most of the work after you sign. It searches for liens and unpaid taxes, and you supply payoff letters, the deed, your latest tax bill and any historic-district or permit paperwork you have. Expect questions about the roof and insurance as well. At closing you sign the deed in front of witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. Cash sales skip the appraisal and loan approval, so the schedule is mostly the title search. Settle with the buyer in writing who pays for repairs found in the inspection, and agree on the date you hand over the keys.

Frequently asked questions

Is my New Smyrna Beach house in a historic district?

It is if it falls inside the National Register district between Riverside Drive, U.S. Highway 1, Ronnoc Lane and Smith Street, or in the Coronado district. Ask the city's planning office to check your address.

Does code compliance need to sign off before I sell?

No general sign-off is required, but unpaid code liens will appear in a title search. Call code compliance at 386-410-2870 to ask about any open case.

What is the deed tax rate in Volusia County?

Seventy cents on each $100, the base rate used across Florida outside Miami-Dade. All parties are liable, so the contract should say who pays.

Can I still sell a vacant New Smyrna Beach house?

Yes. Register it on the city's abandoned and vacant property form if it applies, keep the yard maintained and clear any code case before closing.

Does the property tax bill change after a sale?

It can. A homesteaded property's assessment resets to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's first bill may be higher than yours.

Selling in Miami Lakes: the basics

Miami Lakes is a planned town in northwest Miami-Dade County, and the planning shapes how its houses sell. Population is near 31,240, spread over roughly 6.5 square miles, with about 4,720 businesses inside the town limits. It sits 16 miles north of Downtown Miami and about 10 miles from Miami International Airport, which is the commute story most buyers hear first.

The town runs from NW 170th Street and the Palmetto Expressway on the north to NW 138th Street on the south, and from NW 57th Avenue (Red Road) on the east to Interstate 75 on the west.

Because so much of the town sits inside one master plan, a seller here usually runs into a homeowners association, a lake or canal frontage question, or a special taxing district earlier than sellers in older grid suburbs do. Sort out which of those apply to your address before you talk to any buyer.

What the master plan means for your house

The original plan covered 3,000 acres of former dairy land and produced winding streets, cul-de-sacs, 23 lakes, parks and separate business parks. Buyers see all of that on a drive-by, so curb appeal, tree condition and the state of the swale count for more than usual. Light industrial and office parks take up about 13 percent of the town, and lakes and canals about 11 percent.

  • Housing ranges from medium-density multifamily to large waterfront single-family homes, with many lakefront townhouse communities.
  • Most of the town is low density, with a Town Center and parks spread between neighborhoods.
  • The town's businesses employ about 30,000 people, and only 12 percent of those workers live in Miami Lakes.

If your home is a townhouse or sits in an association, ask for the current dues, any pending assessments and the estoppel procedure early. Those papers take time, and a buyer's lender will want them.

Drainage, guarded districts and town projects

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue answers calls here, mainly from the Miami Lakes station and the Miami Lakes West station, which together handled about 89 percent of responses in fiscal 2025. There were 3,546 emergency calls to the town that year.

Drainage work is the item an owner is most likely to notice. Finished projects include Canal Bank Stabilization Phase III and the Francesca Mary and Loch Lomond drainage improvements. Many neighborhood jobs are still under way, among them Royal Oaks additions and West Lakes Phase IV. If your street is on a project list, tell the buyer what was done and ask the Town for the project status in writing.

A house inside one of the Town's special taxing districts carries extra costs, such as automated gate arms and guardhouse work, and buyers tend to raise them. Pull the district charge from your tax bill so you can answer without guessing.

The Town also runs the FreeBee on-demand ride service, which gave more than 28,564 rides in the year, and it launched a Vision Zero plan for road safety.
