What a Miami Lakes listing can highlight

Fiscal 2025 gave sellers several facts a listing can lean on. Emergency response times ran under 6.5 minutes, and the Town ranked among the top three safest cities in Miami-Dade County in a Niche report. Police figures show a 45 percent drop in auto thefts and a 73 percent drop in residential and commercial burglaries. The fiscal year ran October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025, so date any number you quote.

  • Parks: Royal Oaks Park fields, K9 Cove, a marina on the C8 canal and pocket parks renovated with new benches and signs.
  • Recreation: more than 1,800 registrants in youth and adult leagues, tennis and pickleball programs, and an archery program.
  • Events: a Fourth of July celebration and Main Street Live in the Town Center.
  • Transit: free on-demand FreeBee rides within town limits.

Deed stamp tax and recording fees

Florida charges a documentary stamp tax on deeds, and Miami-Dade is the one county with a different schedule. The state holds everyone named on the document liable, whichever side agrees to pay, so the contract should say who covers it.

Miami Lakes has many lakefront townhouses and multifamily units, so ask your closing agent which line fits your property type. The clerk takes the tax at the moment the deed is recorded and adds page-based recording fees under section 28.24.

Property tax bill

Property tax comes on its own bill. The Town's annual performance report charts millage for Miami-Dade municipalities, and the Miami-Dade tax collector can give you the current Miami Lakes rate. A web-based millage calculator from the Town lets residents compare this year's taxes with last year's. The Town's rate is just a piece of the total, since the county, school board and special districts each add theirs.

Have the closing agent split the year between you and the buyer, and hold back money for the November bill when it is not out yet at closing. Expect the buyer's first bill to run well above yours.

Florida tax dates and homestead rules

Miami Lakes homeowners pay county, school, Town and special district charges on one November bill. The calendar comes from the state: values are fixed as of January 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and bills land in November with an early-payment discount that shrinks from 4 percent to 1 percent by February.

  • Homestead applications reach the Miami-Dade appraiser by March 1, on Form DR-501.
  • Homestead status ends if you rent the home out or move away.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly assessment growth on a homestead. After a sale the assessment jumps to market-based just value at the next first of January.
  • To contest a value, file with the clerk within 25 days of the August mailing. Unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1.

What is the fastest way to sell in Miami Lakes?

You can hire a broker, sell it yourself, or take a cash bid from an investor. Each route gives up something different for speed. Lakefront and gated-district homes tend to draw financed buyers, while a dated interior or a deferred drainage problem can favor an as-is investor.

  • Agent listing: most exposure to financed buyers, with repair requests after the inspection.
  • Owner-marketed sale: no listing fee, but you write the contract and handle showings and disclosures.
  • Investor bid: fewer contingencies and a closing date set by you, at a discount for speed.

A cash sale avoids the lender's appraisal, the loan approval and most repair haggling. The title search, the deed and the stamp tax still happen. Collect offers in writing, ask every bidder who pays for title work and stamps, and let an attorney or closing agent review the contract first.

From offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the title company hunts for liens, open permits and unpaid taxes. Have ready the deed, a mortgage payoff figure, the latest tax bill, the association's contact details and any special taxing district paperwork. At the signing table you execute the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the tax.

With a tenant in place, hand over the lease so the buyer sees the term and the rent.

Behind on payments or inherited?

Foreclosure in Florida goes through a judge. After final judgment the clerk schedules a public auction 20 to 35 days out, though the lender can agree to wait longer. The top bidder puts down 5 percent, and objections to the bid are due ten days after the certificate of sale. Selling privately ahead of that auction lets you keep any equity.

Heirs can use summary administration, a shortened court process, when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less or the owner died more than two years ago. Creditors lose their claims after the longer of three months from first publication or 30 days from service. Florida collects no estate tax return for deaths after 2004.

Someone living there unlawfully who is not a tenant can be removed by the sheriff after the owner files a verified complaint under section 82.036, if the statute's conditions are met. For a leaseholder behind on rent, a three-day written notice comes before any eviction suit.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a Miami Lakes sale take to close?

With clean title a cash deal can finish in a few weeks. A financed buyer adds inspection, appraisal and lender steps. A title defect, a lien or a slow association approval can hold up either one.

Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Miami Lakes deed?

Your contract assigns the cost, but the state treats all parties to the document as liable. Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and a deed for only a single-family dwelling skips the surtax.

Does a sale reset my property tax assessment?

Yes. The new owner starts at full market-based value as of the next first of January and gets none of your Save Our Homes cap. Transfers between spouses and some transfers at death are exceptions.

Is a home inside a guarded Miami Lakes district harder to sell?

It can be, since buyers see the district charge and any gate or guardhouse costs. Ask the Town and the Miami-Dade tax collector for current amounts before you set a price.

Who files the deed after a Miami Lakes sale?

Your title company usually submits it to the Miami-Dade court clerk, who takes the stamp tax and page charges in the same step.

At roughly 7.81 square miles, the city is compact, and a single city hall, appraiser and clerk of court cover nearly every step.

Old blocks tend to have old systems. Insurers and inspectors start with the roof, panel, plumbing and windows, and an untouched house is where selling as-is fits best. If your home is on that list or beside a listed property, call planning and zoning about exterior changes before you discuss renovation with any buyer.

Short-term rentals and long leases

Renting for short stays requires a city certificate. The Vacation Rental Certificate application goes through the city's Planning and Zoning Division, and the website walks owners through it.

For longer leases, chapter 83 of the Florida Statutes sets the rules statewide.

  • Rent that runs late is met with a written three-day demand that skips weekends and court holidays.
  • Tenants paying month to month get thirty days' notice before the term closes.
  • Removal of an occupant is the sheriff's job, once a judge has ruled and a writ has issued.

A tenant is not a barrier to selling. Certain buyers will close with the occupant still living there, so raise that idea before starting an eviction you might not need.

Unfinished work and permits never closed are the usual trouble. Records for your address are available from the city's Community Development Department.

Documents and a walk-through

Round up your deed, your latest Broward tax bill, permit records, a lender payoff statement and your insurance declarations page. If an association governs the property, add its rules and a current balance statement.

Broward County works to the state's tax schedule: January 1 valuation, an August notice of proposed taxes, and bills mailed by the tax collector in November.

Selling ends your Save Our Homes cap. On the next New Year's Day the buyer is assessed at just value, so your old bill usually understates theirs.

Staying in Florida? Portability may let part of your capped benefit follow you, provided the new homestead begins within three years of the first January 1 after you left the old one. Form DR-501T goes in with your DR-501 by March 1.

On closing day

The title company prepares the settlement statement, collects the signed deed and files it with the Broward clerk. Expect to show photo ID, sign where indicated and hand over keys and any remote controls. Your lender is repaid first from the proceeds, then any taxes, fees and prorations are deducted, and the balance is wired or mailed to you.

Read each line before you sign, and ask the closer to explain anything unfamiliar. If something looks wrong, say so before the deed is recorded, because corrections get harder afterward. Keep a copy of every document you sign.

If the house is inherited or in default

For an inherited house, probate comes first, since the personal representative needs court authority to sign a deed. Summary administration, a shorter route, covers estates worth $150,000 or less and deaths over two years back.

Once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the clerk sets a public sale for 20 to 35 days later, unless the lender agrees to wait. Closing a private sale first pays off the loan and leaves any surplus to you.

Unpaid taxes follow their own timetable. A certificate holder may ask for a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year. When the sale opens, your title company can quote the payoff.

Do I need to close an old permit before listing in Dania Beach?

The Broward clerk records it, and the title company usually handles recording and the state's deed tax at closing.

When do Broward early-payment discounts end?

February is the last discount month, at 1 percent. After that the full amount is due, and unpaid bills are delinquent from April 1.

Can a Dania Beach house be sold with a tenant inside?

Yes. The buyer may accept the lease, or you can give thirty days' written warning on a monthly tenancy. Changing the locks yourself is not allowed.

Yes. A transfer of ownership returns assessed value to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's bill can run well above yours. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the property appraiser about portability.

Where Casselberry sits and what buyers notice

Casselberry is at the southern end of Seminole County, about ten miles north of downtown Orlando. Interstate 4 is five minutes away, State Road 436 and U.S. 17-92 cross the city, and commute time is often the first thing a buyer weighs. Put drive times and road access in your listing.

The city covers approximately 8 square miles, so neighborhoods are small and close together. Lakes are a draw, and the larger ones include Lake Howell, Lake Kathryn and the Triplet Chain of Lakes, so name the nearest one in your listing. If a buyer asks about schools, point them to Seminole County Public Schools to confirm attendance zones for your address instead of promising one. Seminole County, not the city, assesses, bills and records property, which keeps the paperwork in one place.

Seminole County Property Appraiser dates

A short list of recurring dates governs every Casselberry owner's year.

Property tax calendar for Seminole County
DateEvent

March 1Deadline to apply for homestead exemption or agricultural classification

January 1 through March 1 is the regular filing window for the current tax year. A filing made between March 2 and December 31 counts as pre-filing for the next year.

When the tax bill is due and when it turns late

Bills go out from the Tax Collector in November. Pay that month and take off 4 percent; the discount falls by a point each month, reaching 1 percent in February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 is when unpaid taxes turn delinquent.

The state also offers an installment prepayment plan, which requires an application to the tax collector by May 1. Partial payments before delinquency are accepted at the collector's discretion. The Seminole County Tax Collector can explain how either would work on your parcel.

Look at each year's bill before you list. A buyer's title agent will, and a surprise costs time.

Trusts and lady bird deeds before a sale

Both are possible, but talk to an attorney about the tax effects first. In one revenue advisement, a lady bird deed on the facts presented moved no present beneficial interest, so no documentary stamp tax was due. That was one advisement on one set of facts, and it is not a rule for every deed.

The same agency adds that no specific exemption covers deeds moving Florida real property for estate planning. Its taxable list includes quit claim deeds and contracts for deed. Moving title usually counts as a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception fits, such as a transfer between spouses.

If a family member's name must come off title before a sale, the usual signing rule applies: a writing with two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01.

How much has the Save Our Homes cap allowed lately?

Recent caps have tracked inflation closely. The chart revised in January 2026 lists 3.4 percent inflation and a 3.0 percent cap for 2024, 2.9 percent for both in 2025, and 2.7 percent for both in 2026. Because the cap is whichever is lower, 3 percent or the inflation change, a long-held Casselberry homestead can be assessed well below market.

That gap is the savings a seller carries. At sale the buyer's assessment resets to just value. You, if you buy again in Florida, may port part of that gap to the new house. The portability form travels with the new property's homestead application, due March 1, and the new house must be your permanent residence by January 1.

  • Gather your last three tax bills to see how the assessed and just values compare.
  • Confirm that the homestead exemption is still active on the latest roll.
  • Keep a copy of the portability form with your closing file.

Checklist for the weeks before closing

The title agent runs most of this, but you speed things up by having documents ready.

  • Order a payoff from your lender and ask whether a prepayment charge applies.
  • Check with the city for open permits on additions, sheds or roof work.
  • Confirm that every owner on title can sign, or that a legal representative has authority.
  • Ask the title agent how the November tax bill will be split at closing.
  • Cancel or transfer water, sewer and garbage service, which the city provides as municipal utilities.

Once signed, the deed goes to the county clerk to be recorded. The new owner then has until the next March 1 to file for an exemption of their own. Keep your settlement statement with your tax papers for the year.

What about tenants, inheritance and missed payments?

For a rented house, the notice depends on the problem. Nonpayment needs 3 days' written notice, which skips weekends and court holidays. A curable lease violation gives the tenant 7 days to cure, and an incurable one gives 7 days to vacate. When a landlord wins in court, the sheriff posts a 24 hour notice before returning possession.

An inherited house usually needs probate authority first. A shorter court process, summary administration, is open if the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the owner has been dead more than 2 years. Deaths after 2004 carry no Florida estate tax.

An owner behind on the mortgage faces a foreclosure sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A sale before that date leaves you more control over terms.

Getting the house ready on a short clock

A quick sale rewards small, inexpensive moves. Clear the yard and garage, fix anything that leaks or will not open, and take clear photos in daylight. Keep a folder with your deed, recent utility bills, appliance manuals and any repair receipts, so a buyer can see the house has been looked after. If a roof, air conditioner or plumbing job is unfinished, say so up front. A buyer who learns about it from you can price it; one who discovers it late tends to walk away or ask for a steep discount.

When more than one person owns the house, settle early who will sign and where each of you will be on closing day.

Offers and next steps

List or sell for cash, the test is the same: how much you keep, when you close and how likely the deal is to fall apart. Check funds or loan paperwork, read any repair terms twice, and ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement on your favorite offer. Raise questions about it days ahead, not at the signing table. Also decide in advance how long you can wait. A seller with a firm move date is better placed to turn down a weak offer, and one without a date should say so up front so the buyer's schedule fits yours.

Frequently asked questions

Is Casselberry in Seminole County?

Yes. The city lies in the county's southern end. County offices handle your assessment, tax bill and recording.

When do I apply for homestead in Seminole County?

By March 1. January 1 to March 1 is the regular window, and applications filed between March 2 and December 31 count as pre-filing for the next year.

What discount applies if I pay early?

Pay in November for 4 percent off, then the discount drops one point a month to 1 percent in February. March has none, and April 1 starts delinquency.

Does a lady bird deed avoid the deed tax?

Not always. The state agency reached that result on one set of facts where the owners kept full powers, so get an attorney's read on yours.

It is 25 days after the mid-August TRIM mailing. The notice itself states the filing deadline.

Sell My House Fast in Rockledge, FL: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Sell Your Rockledge House for Cash

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Rockledge?
We buy Rockledge houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Which selling routes fit a Rockledge house?

A Rockledge owner can list with an agent, line up a buyer without one, or take a cash offer for the house in whatever shape it is in. The house's condition and your deadline point to the right choice.

Listing puts the house in front of the most people, but repairs, showings and a financing failure are your risks. Cash gives up some price for speed and certainty. Every route finishes the same way, with the deed filed at the Brevard County Clerk of Courts and Florida stamp tax paid on it.

Start by collecting the deed, a mortgage payoff letter, your newest tax bill, any survey and permit records for big jobs. Buyers, agents and title agents all ask for these.

  • Listing: most exposure, most preparation.
  • Private sale: you manage pricing, showings and contracts.
  • Cash purchase: bought as-is, faster close, often a lower figure.

City services around a sale

Rockledge is a city in Brevard County on Florida's Space Coast. The city has its own building department, finance division, code enforcement and public works, which means most questions about your address end up at one city hall.

Road work near a house can affect showings and buyer traffic. Barton Boulevard is getting roadway improvements, and work on Fiske Boulevard intersections is scheduled from April 2026 into fall 2026. The city's news page will tell you whether your street is affected. The city also publishes collection schedules and a special pick-up request form, which is handy when you are clearing a house before a sale.

If a violation has been filed against your address, the code enforcement board is where it gets heard, and the board posts its agendas on the city's agenda center.

Permits for work already done

A residential permit needs a signed, notarized application with a written scope of work, and an owner who does the job personally also files an Owner/Builder Affidavit. Inspectors and buyers usually check permit records for roofs, windows, air conditioning and additions, so find out which of your upgrades were permitted.

Flood zones and the 50 percent rule

Under Section 30.20 of its Land Development Regulations, any development in the floodplain needs a building permit. To learn your flood zone, phone the Building Department at (321) 221-7540, option 2.

If you repaired a damaged house before selling, the substantial improvement rule applies. Once rebuilding, additions or improvements cost 50 percent of the building's market value or more, the entire building must meet new-construction standards, and a damaged house at that level may have to be raised above the base flood elevation. The property appraiser's assessed value is not used for this test, and an independent appraisal may be required.

  • Before you list, ask the building department whether the address has open or expired permits.
  • A notice of commencement is recorded with the Brevard County Clerk of Courts for projects of $5,000 or more.
  • When a repair estimate approaches half the building's value, speak with the city first.

Florida transfer tax on the deed

A Florida deed is taxed at 70 cents for each hundred dollars of price, with any mortgage on the property added into that price. The state holds every signer liable regardless of who agreed to pay, and the clerk takes the tax when the deed is recorded.

Recording adds a few dollars a page under s. 28.24, and your closing statement shows the real total. A quitclaim to a relative still can be taxed, since quitclaims and deeds in lieu are on the taxable list.

Property tax calendar

The Brevard appraiser sets values as of January 1, and bills come from the tax collector in November. Paying early saves 4 percent that month, down to 1 percent by February, and April 1 begins delinquency.

Homestead applications close March 1. Amendment 3 brings sizable homestead changes, and the Brevard appraiser's office can explain how they reach your parcel. After you sell, the Save Our Homes cap no longer follows the house, and the next owner is assessed at full just value from the following January 1.

A buyer's first bill rarely matches yours, so do not present your bill as what the buyer will pay.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Rockledge houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What if the house has liens, tenants or an estate attached?

  • Behind on the mortgage: once a foreclosure judgment is entered, the clerk auctions the house in 20 to 35 days (s. 45.031). A sale that closes first leaves any equity with you.
  • Renters: ending a monthly tenancy takes 30 days of notice before a period closes (s. 83.57). If the tenant will stay past closing, write that into the contract.
  • Estate: summary administration is open to a small estate, $150,000 outside exempt property or less, and to one where the owner died more than two years ago (s. 735.201). Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004.

What to ask the city before listing

The building department holds the permit file for your address, so call it first. These questions head off surprises at the inspection stage.

  • Is any permit open, expired or missing a final inspection?
  • Does a tree permit apply? Rockledge requires four trees to remain on the lot after a removal.
  • Does the lot lie in a flood zone, and does the 50 percent improvement rule apply to recent repairs?
  • Was a notice of commencement recorded for work of $5,000 or more?
  • Is there an open code complaint? The city has a code violation complaint form and a code enforcement board that meets on its calendar.

Keep notes as you go: the name of the staff member you spoke with, the date, and what was said about each permit. If a buyer or title agent asks later, you can answer quickly, and a cash buyer will often price the house more firmly when you hand over a clear permit history. Open items do not always block a sale, but they do change who bears the cost of fixing them, so settle that in writing before the contract is signed.

Clearing a house before closing often means bulk trash. The city lets residents request a special pick-up through a form on its site, and its collection schedules page lists regular pickup days.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Rockledge house with an unpermitted addition?

Yes, but expect questions. Buyers and title companies look for permit history, and the city's building department can tell you what is on file for the address. Cash buyers often take unpermitted work as-is, while financed buyers may ask you to resolve it first.

Who records the deed on a Rockledge sale?

The Brevard County Clerk of Courts records it. The clerk also collects documentary stamp tax at recording, and the closing agent usually handles both.

Does the city's 50 percent rule apply if I only repaired a little?

No, it applies when improvement or repair costs equal or exceed 50 percent of the building's market value. Below that threshold the ordinary permit requirements apply. Ask the building department how it measures value for your house.

When is the homestead application due?

Every March 1, filed with the county property appraiser, and the house must be your permanent home by the preceding January 1. Rockledge sits in Brevard County, so the Brevard office takes the application.

Will a cash sale change what I owe in transfer tax?

No. Documentary stamp tax depends on the consideration on the deed, not on how the buyer pays. All parties to the document are liable by statute, and the parties decide in the contract who pays it.

Choosing how to sell in West Melbourne

Owners in West Melbourne have three realistic options: a standard agent listing, a cash purchase, or an investor who wants the house with no repairs. Speed and price pull in opposite directions on each. What you pick depends on how the roof and major systems look, how soon you need funds, and any debt attached to the title.

  • Agent listing: usually the highest sale price, but showings, repairs and waiting on a buyer's mortgage add weeks.
  • Cash buyer or investor: fewer contingencies and timing you can often pick, though the price tends to run lower.
  • Sale after a repair push: worth it only when the work is cosmetic and cheap, because permits and inspections take time.

No matter who buys, write the terms down and decide who covers the deed tax, title search and recording. Those costs are negotiable in Florida, so put the answer in the contract instead of leaving it to a handshake.

West Melbourne homes and what inspectors look at

West Melbourne is in Brevard County, and the city grew quickly after it was created in 1959, from 3,050 people in 1970 to 25,924 in 2020. A lot of the housing stock was built during those fast-growth decades, which is why inspectors tend to focus on roofs, air conditioning and electrical work. Cash buyers usually reduce their offer for such items instead of asking you to repair them.

Water comes from the City of Melbourne and reaches customers through lines and meters the city owns, while a private contractor runs the wastewater plant. If your home is on city sewer, the closing agent will want a final utility reading and a clear account. A property on a septic tank is a different case, so tell any buyer early which system serves the house.

Sewer tie-in inspections are scheduled Monday through Thursday only. If an earlier owner hooked up to sewer, request the permit record from the Building Department. It shows buyers the connection passed inspection.

Building Department and permit questions

Work done without a permit tends to come up once a buyer's inspector or lender starts asking. Starting a project that needs a permit without one can bring code enforcement proceedings.

A recent Florida change, House Bill 803, allows certain permit exemptions for small home improvement projects under $7,500 on single family homes, duplexes and townhomes outside flood zones. Electrical, plumbing, structural work (including exterior doors, windows, roofing and sheds), mechanical and gas work still need a permit regardless of cost. You have to request an exemption in writing before the work starts.

Can a buyer rent out a West Melbourne house?

Yes, but the city expects a business tax receipt for rentals. A separate rental application is linked from the city's Business Tax Receipts page, and a business must hold a receipt showing the owner has registered and paid local tax.

Penalties apply unless renewal payments arrive by September 30. New owners must submit a fresh application with the deed or a bill of sale, and a buyer of a house with tenants should plan on that. The Finance Department answers questions at 321-327-6614 or 321-327-6616.

Landlords should hand the buyer the current rental receipt and let the tenant know about the sale. If either side wants the house empty at closing, put that in the contract.

Brevard County property taxes

One Brevard County bill carries every levy on a West Melbourne parcel. The Property Appraiser decides value. The county commissioners, school board, city and other bodies set millage, where one mill means one dollar for every thousand dollars of value. The Tax Collector's office number is (321) 264-6969.

The bill is mailed to the last address on record, and lenders who escrow usually ask for it directly. If nothing arrives, you still owe the tax and should request the amount before it goes delinquent.

  • Assessments are set as of January 1, and homestead requires the house to be your permanent residence by that date.
  • The exemption lasts only while you live there and do not rent it out.
  • For the next owner, value resets to just value the following January 1, so your tax figure will not simply carry over.

Delinquency starts April 1. Because bills come after the year ends, the closing agent prorates that year's tax between you and the buyer, and you should see the split in writing.

Closing costs on a West Melbourne deed

Deeds in Florida carry a documentary stamp tax of $0.70 per $100 of price. Whoever the contract says will pay, all parties to the document remain liable, and the clerk takes the money at recording.

Under Section 28.24, recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each one after it, with a $1.00 and 50 cent trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge. The itemized statement from the closing agent shows the actual total.

A cash offer does not erase these costs. It changes who negotiates them, so compare offers by net proceeds on the final statement and not by the headline number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy West Melbourne houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What if you owe taxes or the title is cloudy?

Back taxes create a lien problem but not a dead end. A title company finds any tax certificate or lien on the house and pays it from your proceeds at closing, so you can still sell.

Disclose known problems to buyers early. An investor can often work around a title issue or an unpermitted addition, but a surprise found late can kill the deal or lower the price.

Steps from offer to closing

Most quick sales follow one pattern. First you gather your deed, a payoff figure and recent tax bills, then accept an offer. The buyer may inspect, and a title company looks for liens and open permits. A settlement statement lists each charge. After you sign, the clerk records the deed and you receive what is left once payoffs and taxes are covered.

Cash buyers skip the lender's appraisal, the point where financed deals usually slow down. Ask about the closing date and deposit up front, and whether closing can happen before the next tax bill arrives.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my West Melbourne house as-is?

Yes. Inspections can bring repair requests from a lender or retail buyer, while a cash buyer taking it as-is typically folds condition into the price. Ask the Building Department about any open permits first.

Is there a local transfer tax in West Melbourne?

The state deed tax is $0.70 for each $100 of price, taken by the clerk at recording. Look over the draft settlement statement for any other charge.

Are permits needed for minor fixes made before listing?

Often. House Bill 803 can exempt a few small jobs under $7,500 on single family homes outside flood zones. Electrical, plumbing, roofing and other structural work still need permits, and any exemption must be requested in writing first.

What happens to my rental receipt when I sell?

Your buyer applies for a new business tax receipt and attaches the deed or a bill of sale. The city Finance Department, at 321-327-6614, can walk you through it.

When are Brevard County property taxes delinquent?

On April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. At closing, the year of sale's bill is split between buyer and seller.

Crestview prices and growth

Homes in this Okaloosa County city cost much less than the national average. A typical owned home is valued at $277,900 for 2020-2024, while the U.S. figure is $332,700.

Newcomers keep arriving. The city had 20,978 residents in 2010 and 27,134 in 2020, and the newest estimate reads 31,193, or 13.8 percent more than the 2020 base. Middle household income is $65,480, so what local buyers can offer is limited.

Housing costs at a glance

Which Okaloosa office does what

Three elected county offices matter. The property appraiser decides what your parcel is worth, the tax collector sends the bill, and the circuit court clerk files your deed. The sheriff and the supervisor of elections hold the other two elected county posts.

Values are set as of January 1, and the appraiser also decides exemption claims. The collector takes care of deferrals, installment plans and certificate sales. At recording, the clerk gathers the deed tax. Phone each one for current forms, hours and fees tied to your parcel.

Deed tax and recording charges

The Revenue Department's page shows 70 cents for each $100 as the rate Okaloosa uses, and s. 201.02 sets it. Whichever party promises to pay, every party on the document stays liable.

  • Filing starts at $5.00 for the first page, then $4.00 a page, with add-on charges.
  • Each name after the fourth costs another $1.00.
  • The deed needs two witnesses.

Quitclaim deeds are taxable. If a homestead moves between spouses and the only consideration is a mortgage, it may be exempt.

Homestead rules and the next owner's bill

An exemption of up to $50,000 comes off taxable value for a homesteaded Crestview house, with $25,000 of it applying to school taxes. Leave the house, rent it out or sell it, and the exemption is gone.

While you own it, the Save Our Homes cap holds increases to the lesser of 3 percent or CPI. A fast-growing city can push market value past that cap, so the buyer's first bill may be a shock. Property with no homestead is limited to 10 percent a year. Any sale or foreclosure sets just value again the following January 1.

What if there is a tenant, an heir or a lender?

Florida attaches a timetable to each case.

  • Tenants: 3 days after a rent demand, 7 days after a lease violation, 30 days to close a month-to-month arrangement.
  • Estates: a short-form administration is possible at $150,000 or under, and creditors get three months after first notice.
  • Foreclosure: the auction comes 20 to 35 days after judgment, with a 5 percent deposit and 10 days for objections.

A person with no lease at all gets different treatment. The owner can file a sworn complaint with the sheriff, but a false statement exposes the owner to damages of triple the fair market rent.

Tax calendar

Okaloosa keeps to the statewide yearly rhythm.

  • January 1: the date values are fixed.
  • March 1: exemption applications close.
  • August: proposed-tax notices are mailed.
  • 25 days after the notice: final day to petition on value.
  • November: bills arrive, and paying that month saves 4 percent, dropping to 1 percent in February.
  • April 1: late.

Your closing agent will split the year's bill with the buyer, so ask how that will be shown on the statement.

Selling with taxes owed

Accounts left unpaid go out as certificates by June 1, bought by whoever bids the lowest interest rate. The certificate holder must wait until two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply for a deed, and that application costs $75.

A homestead at a tax deed sale starts bidding at what is owed plus half of the assessed value. The high bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, either 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger. A closing that pays off the balance ends the problem far sooner.

Life estate deeds and family transfers

A gift of title to a relative usually counts as an ownership change, unless a narrow exception like a spousal transfer fits. The Revenue Department also treats quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed as taxable.

In 2020 the Department of Revenue issued an advisement about a so-called lady bird deed. On those facts the deed moved no present beneficial interest, and no doc stamp tax applied. Since the answer rested on specific facts, show any such deed to a Florida attorney before counting on it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Records to gather before listing

  • Deed logistics: two witnesses, recording with the Okaloosa clerk, and the 70 cents per $100 stamp tax divided as your contract says.
  • A written reply from the tax collector about any deferral or installment plan on your account.

Having this folder ready lets buyers move faster, and it keeps you from scrambling when a title agent calls with a question.

How a direct sale usually unfolds

You describe the house, a buyer makes an offer, and you agree on a closing date. A title company then searches the record, clears any problems and files the deed. Expect to sign a purchase contract, a deed and a settlement statement.

Before you sign anything, read who pays for the title policy and recording, and ask whether the buyer needs any repairs done first. If you have a mortgage, the payoff is taken from your proceeds at the table, and what remains is sent to you after the deed is recorded. Compare more than one offer, and ask each buyer how long they need and how they will pay.

Sellers who are moving on

Some Florida veteran exemptions can apply to Crestview owners. They follow the home you live in, so ask the appraiser how yours will be handled when you sell. Many sellers also have children at home, since 28.3 percent of residents are under 18, and they often need the closing date to line up with a new purchase.

Buying again? Get your financing lined up before accepting an offer here. Ask the buyer whether the closing date can bend, and if you need a few extra days in the house afterward, write the arrangement down with an end date.

Quickly. The 2025 estimate of 31,193 is 13.8 percent above the 2020 base.

Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Crestview?

Yes, the deed tax is 70 cents per $100 and all parties are liable. The sales contract decides who pays.

Who can tell me my current property tax bill?

The Okaloosa tax collector bills each November, and the appraiser explains the value behind it.

Can an heir sell a house before probate ends?

Usually not until the personal representative has authority. Ask a probate lawyer or the clerk about the right track, such as summary administration for smaller estates.

Which way of selling suits a Venice owner who needs speed?

Venice owners can sell for cash, list on the open market or find a buyer on their own. Flood exposure often decides which one works, because elevation and repair history shape what buyers and insurers will accept.

  • Cash buyer: fewer conditions and a closing date you choose, at a price that absorbs the buyer's risk.

Your route also affects how soon the buyer's insurance quote arrives, and on an older coastal house a slow quote can hold up a closing. Venice sits on the Gulf side of Sarasota County. Its planned downtown, restored 1927 train depot and fishing pier give buyers a sense of where a house stands in the city's layers: older streets near downtown, newer annexations toward the interstate. Say which one yours belongs to when you write the listing or pitch a cash buyer.

Hurricane history and your house

Storm history now comes up in almost every conversation about a Venice house. Hurricane Ian in 2022 did more than $10 million in damage in the city. Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024 flooded the Golden Beach neighborhood and destroyed the South Jetty.

Water or wind damage raises three questions from any buyer: what was repaired, by whom, and whether the permits closed. A complete folder shortens negotiation.

  • Invoices and contractor names for every repair.
  • Permit records showing each one closed.
  • Dated photos from before and after the work.
  • Insurer letters and any flood claim history.

The Sarasota County Property Appraiser's website links a Hurricane Evacuation Levels reference. Look up the level for your address and mention it in your listing notes, since out-of-town buyers often ask about it before they ask about price. A house left unrepaired can still sell. Describe its condition honestly, and expect an offer that reflects the work left to do.

The 50 percent rule

Venice limits repair spending in flood hazard areas. Once restoration or renovation costs reach half of the structure's pre-damage market value, with labor counted, the rule applies and the work must meet current flood standards.

The Florida Building Code adds a foot of freeboard above base flood elevation to reach design flood elevation. Anything built below that level, such as a garage or enclosure, cannot be living space. The owner signs a non-conversion agreement before a Certificate of Occupancy issues, and Sarasota County Public Records holds the recorded copy for later buyers.

Deed stage costs

Sarasota County charges the usual state stamp rate on the deed, and the clerk takes it along with recording fees at filing. Everyone on the deed shares liability. Ask the title agent for a combined total before accepting an offer, since a mortgage that stays on the house counts toward the price.

Owners can also join the Clerk's free fraud alert, an email notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded under a registered name. A seasonal resident selling from out of state benefits most.

Property taxes after a Venice sale

The seller's exemption ends at closing. The buyer's value is reset the next January 1, so the capped growth the seller enjoyed (2.7 percent for 2026 on the state chart) goes away. Plan on a buyer's bill that looks different from yours.

Tax bills go out each fall, and owners can enroll with the collector to get future bills by email. A Florida constitutional amendment on homestead taxes helps both sides to understand what is coming: the 2026 bill must be paid as issued, voter-approved changes first reach the 2027 bill, and school taxes plus non-ad valorem charges such as fire protection and solid waste remain on the notice.

Planning to buy again in Florida? Phone the appraiser at 941.861.8200 about moving part of your savings to the next home, a claim with a March 1 deadline.

Foreclosure or probate

Both situations run on court clocks, so talk to a Florida attorney early. A foreclosure sale follows judgment within a window set by statute. Heirs of a Venice house may qualify for a shortened probate route, depending on the size and age of the estate. The state's estate tax does not apply to deaths after 2004.

If you want to choose your own buyer instead of leaving the outcome to a court, a private sale before the auction date is the way to do it. A title company can show what liens, if any, must be paid from the proceeds.

For an inherited house, collect the death certificate, the will if there is one and any insurance policy on the property. Whoever has legal authority to sell, usually the personal representative, must sign the deed. Without that authority, no buyer's title company will close, so settle that question first.

How a Venice sale moves from offer to closing

Most quick sales follow the same path, and each stage has a Venice twist.

  1. You gather permits, invoices and any flood or insurance letters.
  2. A buyer makes an offer, usually after walking the house and checking its flood zone.
  3. The title agent searches the record for liens and for the recorded non-conversion agreement, if the house has one.
  4. The agent prepares a settlement statement showing deed tax, recording fees and your share of the tax bill.
  5. You sign the deed, and the clerk records it.

A buyer who needs a mortgage or a new insurance policy adds time at the third and fourth steps. A cash buyer can often skip both, which is why cash closings on coastal houses finish sooner when the paperwork is in order.

Who issues permits for work on a Venice house?

The city's Building Division handles permits, flood questions and reports of unpermitted work, and its number is (941) 486-2626. Check for open permits before you list. An unclosed permit on a house with storm repairs is one of the most common reasons a buyer asks for a lower price or a delay.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a storm-damaged Venice house without repairing it?

Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as they stand and price in the repairs. Keep permits, photos and insurer letters, and ask the Building Division whether the 50 percent rule might apply.

What is a non-conversion agreement in Venice?

It is a document in which the owner promises that space below design flood elevation, such as a garage, will not become living area. The city requires it before a Certificate of Occupancy and files it with county records.

How much is the state deed tax on a Venice sale?

Seventy cents per $100 of price, the rate everywhere but Miami-Dade. The clerk collects it at recording and every party to the deed is liable.

Does my homestead exemption pass to a Venice buyer?

No. It ends with the sale, and the buyer's value resets on the next January 1. You may carry part of your capped savings to a new Florida home through portability.

Who should I call about permits?

The city's Building Division at (941) 486-2626. Ask about open permits before you list, and report any unpermitted work there.

We buy Winter Park houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What shapes a house sale in Winter Park

Winter Park is an Orange County city of more than 30,000 residents just north of Orlando, known for stately trees, parks, brick-lined streets and the Park Avenue shops. Many houses stand under mature canopy or near water, which draws buyer attention to roofs, drainage and tree health.

Owners may market the home, sell privately or accept a cash bid, and the paperwork side is the same for each: a deed, a recording with the county, and a clear tax and permit record.

  • Pull any permit history before you list.
  • Check whether protected trees on the lot affect work you planned.
  • Confirm homestead status so the closing tax split is right.

An old city and its houses

The town was platted in 1881 as a planned winter resort and chartered in 1887, with a street grid, a park by the railroad tracks and a lakeside hotel site. Rollins College began its first term in 1885. Central Park anchors downtown and hosts the Sidewalk Art Festival, which the city says draws over 250,000 visitors a year.

That age shows in the housing. A house in a historic part of the city may have additions from several decades, each with its own permit trail. Check the age of roofs, wiring and plumbing before you list, and gather whatever records you have. A buyer or investor will price what the records do not explain. If a repair was done by a contractor, keep the invoice and the final inspection. If the work was done years ago and the paperwork is gone, ask the city's building office what it has on file for the address. That answer can settle a buyer's question faster than guessing, and it tells you whether anything needs to be closed out before an offer.

Ground movement and insurance history

A sinkhole west of Denning Drive nearly swallowed a city block in 1981, and the city has since stabilized and landscaped the edge so it looks like a small lake. Buyers sometimes mention it when Florida sinkholes come up. One past event does not describe any single lot, so a seller with concerns about ground movement should rely on inspection records and, if wanted, a geotechnical report.

For buyers and lenders, the useful paper is the insurance history, any engineer or inspection reports, and records of foundation repairs. Keep those with the closing file.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Winter Park house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tree rules

The city treats its canopy as an asset. The urban forest holds over 75,000 trees on private and public land, with over 25,000 along rights of way. Protected trees on single-family lots still need permits unless Florida Statute 163.045 overrides the city, and work on trees in the public right-of-way or on city land needs city approval.

The city is reviewing its residential tree-removal program, so confirm current requirements with Urban Forestry before you cut anything.

  • Before cutting any tree ahead of a listing, find out whether it required a permit.
  • Should a buyer intend to remove a large tree, tell them to call Urban Forestry at 407-599-3325.
  • Ask the city's building office about permits on any past addition or demolition.

Steps to follow before closing

Start with records, then taxes, then the deed, and leave the timeline flexible for title questions. The city lists a demolition application and a tree-removal application among its permitting resources, so past teardown or landscaping work is worth confirming.

  1. Request your permit history from the city building and permitting office.
  2. Check your parcel record on the county appraiser site for exemptions and the current assessed value.
  3. Ask the tax collector for the current bill and whether it is paid.
  4. Gather inspection, repair and insurance records for the roof, pool and foundation.
  5. Choose how to sell, then compare the net proceeds from each written offer.
  6. Sign the deed before the notary or witnesses your title company arranges: Florida requires two subscribing witnesses on a conveyance of land.

If a mortgage or lien remains, the title company pays it out of sale funds and records the satisfaction.

Orange County property tax and a Winter Park sale

The Orange County Property Appraiser values the home while the county tax collector sends the bill, so your sale has to account for the year's bill. January 1 sets value and March 1 closes exemption filing. A proposed-tax notice comes in August, and a challenge to value must reach the clerk within 25 days of it. November bills allow a 4 percent early-pay break that steps down to 1 percent by February, and April 1 marks delinquency.

Winter Park values run well above many Florida cities, so the Save Our Homes cap matters. Past the first homestead year, yearly growth in assessed value is held to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and the state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. A buyer starts fresh, because a conveyance restarts assessment at full value on the next January 1. Request the exact payoff figure from the Orange County tax collector before you close.

Deed tax and recording

Two charges follow a deed here: a state stamp tax and a per-page recording fee. Section 201.02 sets the deed rate, and every signer is liable, whatever the contract says about payment. Orange County sits outside Miami-Dade, so that county's separate surtax is absent. Recording charges come from section 28.24(13), and your title company can total them.

How a quick sale works

A buyer who pays cash skips the appraisal and loan review, so the schedule depends mostly on title work and your records. Once you accept an offer, the title company checks for liens and open permits, drafts the settlement statement and arranges the signing. The clerk records the deed, and proceeds follow.

In a city with mature trees and older additions, the likeliest delays are an unclosed permit or an unanswered tree question. Clear those first and the rest tends to move on its own. If you owe a lender, ask for a payoff letter early. If you share ownership with a relative or an estate is involved, make sure every owner is ready to sign, because one missing signature can hold up closing. Finally, ask the title company how and when you will receive your proceeds so you can plan the next step.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Winter Park house with an unpermitted addition?

You can, but it will likely surface in a buyer's inspection or a records search. Ask the city's building office what is on file, and expect to resolve or disclose it before closing.

Is a tree removal permit needed in Winter Park?

For protected trees on single-family lots, yes, except where Florida Statute 163.045 overrides the city. The city is reviewing its residential program, so call Urban Forestry at 407-599-3325 before any cutting.

Is there a separate city tax bill in Winter Park?

No. One bill covers all taxing bodies. County offices value and collect, so the Orange County tax collector sends it each November.

Does the Save Our Homes cap pass to a Winter Park buyer?

No, the buyer is assessed at full value after the transfer. You can carry part of the benefit, up to $500,000, to your next Florida homestead.

How old are Winter Park's neighborhoods?

The city was platted in 1881 and chartered in 1887, so some areas are well over a century old. Check the age of roofs, wiring and plumbing in any older house you plan to sell.

About Palm Springs, Florida

This Palm Springs is a village in central Palm Beach County, not the California desert city. It was chartered by the 1957 legislature on about 700 acres of pastureland with a dairy barn and no residents. By August 1958 the first section opened with some 800 homes on paved, landscaped streets.

The village now has about 28,000 residents and a mix of single-family homes, townhomes, apartments and condominiums. A 1960s ranch, a townhouse and a condo each sell to a different buyer, and condo or townhome sellers should line up association paperwork early.

Corridors and redevelopment

The village runs along Congress Avenue south to Lake Worth Road, west to Military Trail and north along the east side of Military Trail to Forest Hill Boulevard. It extends east toward Florida Mango Road and south along it to 10th Avenue North. Congress Avenue and Lake Worth Road anchor the commercial areas.

A Community Redevelopment Agency works on older commercial areas, streetscapes and walkability. Redevelopment is a selling point for some buyers, so ask the village what projects are planned near your street.

Property tax dates

Your bill follows one yearly cycle: the county values the house on January 1 and mails bills in November.

Homestead exemption

Your permanent home can qualify for as much as $50,000 in exemption, applied for on Form DR-501 by March 1. Under Save Our Homes, assessed value grows each year by the smaller of 3 percent or CPI, and the state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

After a sale the buyer begins at just value. Owners of many years are often surprised how much higher the buyer's bill can run. Have a lender or agent estimate it instead of quoting yours to a buyer.

Deed recording charges

The deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on every $100, and the statute includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property in the amount taxed.

  • Recording with the clerk costs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after it.
  • Names past the fourth cost $1.00 apiece.
  • Extra modernization and technology charges apply per page.

The closing agent adds these up. Transfers made for estate planning get no special stamp exemption.

Repairs and permits before you sell

A house from the late 1950s or 1960s may need a new roof, wiring, plumbing or windows before an insurer or lender relaxes. Investors can take on that risk. A buyer with a loan may ask you to do the work first.

Ask the village building office what permits exist for earlier work, and keep invoices and inspection records. Permits that were never closed usually come out during title review.

Tax certificates and tax deeds

A bill goes delinquent April 1 and a certificate is sold by June 1. The certificate holder cannot press the owner for payment for two years after April 1 of the issue year, and applying for a tax deed costs $75.

The clerk runs the auction. The winning bidder puts down a nonrefundable deposit of $200 or 5 percent, whichever is larger, and pays the balance within a day, skipping weekends and holidays. A sale before the auction removes the risk.

  • A homestead with under $250 delinquent goes to the county and not to auction.
  • Notice of a tax deed goes to the titleholder, any mortgagee and any contract for deed buyer.

Vacant houses and occupants

When strangers are in a house and there is no tenancy, no family tie and no court case, the owner can sign a complaint asking the sheriff to remove them. A false statement in it can cost the owner damages, including triple the fair market rent.

A claim of adverse possession requires seven years of possession and tax payments, and moving in on that theory before the return is filed is trespass. Check on a vacant house often and keep it locked.

Selling a house with tenants

A landlord may mail a notice, hand it over, e-mail it where the statute allows, or leave it at the unit if the tenant is away. A lease cannot waive these rules.

After a ruling for the landlord, the sheriff posts 24 hours of notice and then returns possession. A tenant defending on any ground besides payment has 5 days to deposit rent with the court or forfeit those defenses. Month-to-month tenancies end on 30 days' notice, and a lease that stays in place will shape the offers you get.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps from offer to closing

A land deed must be written and signed with two witnesses, which your title agent arranges along with recording. Before that point, you compare offers and pick a buyer.

  • Put in the contract who pays doc stamps and recording.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter if a mortgage remains.
  • Check the tax roll for liens and exemption status.
  • Be available for a walkthrough if the buyer brings an inspector.

Call the Village of Palm Springs for questions about permits, code compliance and rental rules on your street.

Inherited homes and houses behind on payments

State rules fix the steps for inherited homes and houses behind on payments. A small estate (under $150,000 non-exempt) may use summary administration, and unpaid rent begins with a 3 day notice. A foreclosure auction follows the judgment by 20 to 35 days. If payments are behind, call your lender early. Selling before the auction can let you keep equity that a foreclosure sale would take.

What to bring when you meet a buyer

Have the deed or your last closing papers, the most recent tax bill, a payoff figure if a mortgage remains, and a list of repairs and permits from the past years. For a rental, add the lease and rent records. A buyer who sees these up front can make a firm offer and the title agent can start sooner. Walk the house yourself first and note anything an inspector will find, such as an old roof or aging wiring, so you can price it into the sale or tell the buyer plainly. If the village or the county has sent any notice about the property, bring that too, and pay or resolve it before you sign so it does not hold up the closing.

Condos and townhomes

For a unit inside an association, ask for its sale rules and estoppel paperwork the day you decide to sell. Some associations must approve the buyer, and that step can push back closing. Cash buyers usually clear it quickly, yet the forms are identical, so begin before you accept an offer. Know your monthly dues and any special assessment, because buyers ask for both.

Is Palm Springs, FL the same as the California city?

No. It is a village in Palm Beach County chartered in 1957, with about 28,000 residents.

When do Palm Beach County tax bills arrive?

In November, under the state calendar. Taxes unpaid after the year turns become delinquent on April 1.

Is there a state tax on the deed in Palm Springs?

Yes. Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk at recording.

Can I challenge my assessment?

Yes. Petition the clerk within 25 days of the TRIM notice, which arrives in August.

What if my condo has association approval rules?

Request the association's sale rules early, because approval timing can move the closing date.

Before you sell a Sebastian house fast

Picking among a realtor, a private sale and a cash buyer starts with two questions: when do you need to close, and what does the house need? Sebastian sits on the Indian River Lagoon in Indian River County, and the population is about 27,352. Roughly 85.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and a typical owner-estimated home value is $317,000, so compare recent nearby sales before you pick a price.

Most of the work is paperwork. The clerk records deeds, the tax collector bills each parcel, and the building department keeps permit files. Knowing who holds what saves days.

  • Request the permit history from the city's building department.
  • Find out whether a homestead exemption sits on the parcel.
  • Keep the deed, any survey and recent repair invoices in one folder.

Older homes in a slow-moving market

About 89 percent of residents live at the same address a year later, so homes change hands slowly. Houses held for decades often still have older finishes and older permit files, and buyers will look for both.

Much of the city was platted from a 1957 purchase of 1,345 acres by a Miami developer to start Sebastian Highlands. Houses from that era may be due for a new roof, air handler or water heater, which is why many owners here look at cash offers.

Permits that can slow a sale

Open or expired permits are the most common snag. Check with the city building department at 1225 Main St., phone 772-589-5537. Applications go through the MGO portal or by email, with uploads capped at 30MB.

An owner-builder can use the portal, but the first application must be made in person, a rule the city ties to Florida law. Inspections are booked through the portal at least one day ahead. The city offers free video inspections for air conditioning replacement, electrical panel change-outs and plumbing water heater or re-pipe work, which helps when nobody is home to let the inspector in.

  • Ask whether any permit on your address is still open.
  • If a roof, air conditioner or water heater was replaced, find the permit and final inspection.
  • If work was done without a permit, tell the buyer or buyer's agent up front, not at the inspection.

Cash buyers will usually take a house with unpermitted work and price it in. Closing out permits first can raise what a conventional buyer will pay.

Property taxes at a Sebastian closing

The Indian River County property appraiser values each parcel as of January 1, and bills go out in November. When the house transfers, a capped assessment resets to just value, so a long-time owner's low bill rarely follows the house. August brings the notice of proposed taxes.

Paying early earns a printed discount of 4 percent in November, dropping a point each month to 1 percent in February. At a late-year closing, your title agent splits the bill by days of ownership.

Homestead exemption

The exemption removes up to $50,000 of taxable value, though only the first $25,000 counts for school taxes. You apply by March 1 and must live in the house permanently as of January 1. Renting it out ends the exemption.

The exemption follows the owner, not the house, so your buyer files their own application. Call the county property appraiser to learn what your parcel carries.

Recording fees and stamp tax on the deed

Who chooses a cash sale in Sebastian?

Cash suits owners who value speed or condition over top price. With so many homeowners and a large share of residents over 65, typical sellers here include heirs, owners moving into assisted living and people who would rather not replace an aging roof or air handler.

Compare net proceeds, not headline numbers. A listing can bring more but adds showings, post-inspection repair requests and a longer wait. A cash buyer may pay less and still close sooner. Ask each one for the closing date, who pays title and recording costs, and whether the offer survives their own inspection. Get each answer in writing before you sign.

Inherited or vacant house

Start by confirming who has authority to sign. A house passing through an estate may need court papers before anyone can convey it, and the Indian River County clerk can tell you what has been filed. Keep utilities on and the yard tidy in the meantime.

Next, ask the building department about permits, call the tax collector for any balance, and gather keys and association papers. With those in hand, you can compare a listing against a cash offer using real numbers.

From offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a file and searches the Indian River County records for mortgages, liens and judgments. Anything found is paid from your proceeds, so ask for payoff letters early. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which is where most conventional delays come from.

  1. Sign the contract and settle who pays title, stamp tax and recording.
  2. Close out or disclose any open permits.
  3. Sign the deed with the title agent or closing attorney.
  4. The clerk records the deed, and stamp tax is collected at that moment.
  5. The buyer files for their own homestead the following year.

If the house is vacant, hand over all keys and any gate or garage openers at closing, and cancel or transfer utilities that day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Records a buyer's agent will want

Put together a short packet: the recorded deed, a recent tax bill, your permit list, and any association or utility account details. Add dated photos of past repairs and invoices for the roof, air conditioning and water heater.

  • Deed and any legal description or survey you have.
  • Permit numbers with final inspection dates.
  • Property tax bill and exemption status.
  • Repair invoices and warranty papers.

With this packet, you can answer a serious offer in a day, and cash buyers tend to return a price faster when the file is organized.

Does Sebastian have its own building department?

Ways to sell a Temple Terrace house

Sellers here mostly choose among a regular listing, an investor's cash bid and a private deal with someone they know. Let two things decide: how fast the money has to arrive, and how much repair the house is asking for.

The city sits just outside Tampa in Hillsborough County, near the University of South Florida and the Hillsborough River. Little undeveloped land is left, so a house with clean title and a sensible price tends to get noticed fast.

  • Listing: reaches the most buyers, but prep, open houses and loan approval stretch the timeline.
  • Cash bid: you choose the closing date and accept a lower figure than a polished listing might bring.
  • Inherited or rented house: the deed history or the lease terms control how quickly anything can happen.

Pull together your deed, a mortgage payoff letter and the newest tax bill before requesting bids. Each buyer then works from identical paperwork.

Temple Terrace housing at a glance

The city has 27,075 residents. Owners live in just 50.4 percent of the housing units, which leaves renters as nearly half of households. Homes lived in by their owners have a median value of $334,800, while median gross rent is $1,594.

Roughly 80 percent of residents stayed put over the past year, a sign that many houses have been held a long time and carry equity. A buyer at the city's income level often needs a mortgage, so a lender's appraisal can shape a retail sale. A cash investor cares more about condition and rent potential.

If your house was a guest rental

A rental history can change how a Temple Terrace house sells, because the city runs its own program for guest stays. The rules cover a home let for stays under 30 days, more than 3 times a year.

Those homes need a Certificate of Use renewed annually and a fire department safety inspection every two years. Each also needs a local contact on call around the clock. Breaking the rules can lead to the Municipal Code Enforcement Board and a civil citation. The city's short-term rental program page has the full text.

  • Headcount limit: two per bedroom, plus two.
  • Parking: guest cars go on approved off-street spots only.
  • Quiet hours: 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday to Thursday, 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
  • Listings must display the limits, a state license number or Exempt, and the Certificate of Use number.

Before accepting an offer, pull the certificate, the latest inspection result and any citations. An investor who plans to keep hosting guests will ask for that file. The city's complaint line is 813-501-6769, so call it if you are unsure whether a citation is still open.

Showing off the neighborhood

Temple Terrace has real selling points, and buyers recognize them. Riverfront parks look out on the Hillsborough River, and the city has a public library, a recreation center and a historic golf and country club. Residents are minutes from USF, Florida College, the Museum of Science and Industry and Busch Gardens.

Nearby public schools include Lewis Elementary, Riverhills Elementary, Temple Terrace Elementary, Greco Middle and King High School in Tampa. Confirm school assignment with the district before you promise a particular school to anyone.

Take a walk around your street first. Jot down how far the closest park, bus stop and school are, then add those facts to the listing text. If your house is near the river or a trail, say so. Buyers who commute or study nearby look for exactly that.

Closing charges for a Temple Terrace seller

Two charges stand out at a Temple Terrace closing: the state's documentary stamp tax on the deed and the clerk's recording fees. The tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars of sale price everywhere but Miami-Dade, and anyone who signs the deed can be held liable for it, whatever your contract says.

The Hillsborough clerk takes the tax at the moment the deed is recorded. Recording fees come from section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each page after, plus a few small extras. A draft settlement statement from your title agent, requested before you agree on a price, keeps the final numbers from catching you off guard.

  • Deed tax, due at recording.
  • Per-page clerk fees.
  • Your share of the year's property tax.

What happens to your property tax status

The county assesses your house as of each January 1 and mails notices in November. Pay early and the discount starts at 4 percent. On closing day the settlement statement divides that year's bill between seller and buyer.

Homestead protection ends once the house sells. The buyer's value is reset on the next January 1, and their bill may bear little resemblance to yours. Point buyers to the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser for their own estimate rather than copying your number.

Foreclosure or an inherited house

Each situation has its own deadline. After a foreclosure judgment, the court holds a sale 20 to 35 days later and the high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit. If you want a say in who buys, you have to sell privately before that.

For a house left by someone who has died, Florida allows a shortened estate process when the non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or the death was more than two years back. The Department of Revenue treats a deed from a personal representative under a probated will as not taxable.

Unpaid taxes lead to a tax certificate sale, and a tax deed application can follow two years later. None of this is easy to undo, so call a Florida attorney or title agent early. A title agent can also tell you what must be paid off from your proceeds.

How a cash sale compares on timing

Without a lender in the deal, nobody orders an appraisal or underwriting review, the two steps that slow most financed closings. A clean title can mean a closing within three weeks or so. The usual order:

  1. You share the deed, payoff figure and any rental paperwork, such as the Certificate of Use.
  2. The buyer walks the house and sends an offer, often within days.
  3. A title agent hunts for liens and drafts the settlement statement.
  4. You sign the deed. The clerk records it and collects the tax.

A listing may bring a higher price, though cleaning, photos and a buyer's mortgage approval all take time. Weigh that gap against what each extra month of mortgage, taxes, insurance and upkeep costs you, and against the risk that a buyer's loan falls through late.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Temple Terrace house close in under a month?

Often, if the buyer pays cash and nothing clouds the title. Two or three weeks is a fair expectation. A buyer with a mortgage waits on an appraisal and underwriting, so plan on longer.

Who owes the deed tax on a Temple Terrace sale?

Florida holds everyone who signs the deed responsible, even if the contract points at one side. The rate is seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, paid through the clerk when the deed is recorded.

I rented my house on Airbnb. What do I hand a buyer?

Give the buyer your Certificate of Use, the fire inspection record and any city citations. Someone who wants to keep hosting needs that registration in good standing.

Does my homestead break when I list the house?

No, it stays until closing because it rests on the house being your permanent residence. Afterward you may carry part of your capped savings to a new Florida home, provided you claim portability within three years.

Which office records the deed?

The Hillsborough County clerk of the circuit court. That office takes the tax and the per-page fees at the moment of recording.

Retirees moving from other states, investors who renovate and resell, and second-home buyers all appear. Some want a turnkey house near the water, while others prefer a house they can update themselves.

Building permits and open work

The City of Groveland Building Division handles residential and commercial permits and checks plans against the Florida Building Code. If you had a roof, windows, an addition or a shed done, ask the division whether each job has a closed permit before a buyer's inspector asks the same thing.

The same office registers building contractors, issues Certificates of Occupancy for new homes and holds the permit and inspection files. Its office is at 6825 SR 50, second floor. Call 352-429-2141, option 2, or write to permitting@groveland-fl.gov. The counter is open Monday to Thursday from 8 to 5, and Friday from 8 to 3 with remote service until 5. Inspections are scheduled through the city's eTrakit portal, and fire inspections go through the Fire Inspector at 352-467-0493.

  • Request the permit record for your parcel early.
  • Ask how to close any permit that never got a final inspection.
  • Gather contractor invoices that show permit numbers.

When do Lake County property taxes come due?

The Lake County Tax Collector starts collecting each November 1 for the January to December tax year. The bill goes to the owner's address on the tax roll. If a mortgage company pays through escrow, an escrow code prints on the notice, and the owner still gets a copy.

Taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and 3% statutory interest is added at that point. A mailed check counts as paid on its postmark date. Homestead and other exemptions

Lake County's homestead exemption lowers assessed value by up to $51,411. Owners who lived in the home on January 1 file by March 1. Approval letters are not mailed, and once approved it carries forward every year until the house is used differently.

  • Widow or widower: $5,000 off assessed value, ended by remarriage.
  • Disability: $5,000 with a physician statement on Form DR-416 or a Social Security letter.
  • Limited income senior: up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older, with a household income cap of $38,686. Lake County and Minneola authorize the full amount, and Clermont, Lady Lake, Mount Dora and Tavares authorize up to $25,000. Ask the appraiser what applies to a Groveland parcel.
  • Military and deployed service members: separate exemptions, each with a March 1 deadline.

When the house sells, the Save Our Homes cap starts over, and the next owner is first assessed at just value. Renting out the house or moving away ends a homestead.

Military and first responder benefits

Honorably discharged service members rated 10 percent or more can take a $5,000 reduction, proven by a VA letter. A homestead can be fully exempt for a person rated totally and permanently disabled, and for some surviving spouses. A buyer in that group who closes early in the year may also qualify for a pro-rated first-year refund, which the tax collector starts after the following bill is paid.

Two more full exemptions cover the unremarried spouse of a first responder killed on duty and a first responder permanently disabled on duty. Each needs paperwork, so call 352-253-2150 if someone in your deal might qualify.

  • Trust ownership: the applicant needs equitable title or a beneficial interest, and the appraiser can ask for the trust agreement.
  • Contract for deed: eligible only if the contract is recorded with the Clerk of the Court and a copy reaches the appraiser. An ordinary purchase contract does not count.
  • A move within Lake County: homestead does not transfer by itself, so the new address needs a new application.

Selling with taxes owed

A delinquent house is a separate problem. If an investor buys a certificate on an unpaid year, that investor may apply for a deed two years later. Pay off any old year first: the tax collector can quote the balance and your closing agent can send it from the sale proceeds.

From offer to closing day

Start with the paperwork you control. Pull the permit record, print the property record card, and get the current tax figure from the Lake County Tax Collector. Then collect written terms from each buyer and compare the net amount, not the headline price.

After the contract is signed, the closing agent orders title work and requests a payoff letter for each loan, then drafts the deed. The county clerk records it and takes the stamp tax. Any property tax still open for the year is divided between you and the buyer at the table. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, which removes one common reason for a delay, but title work and recording still take time. Get the timeline in writing before committing to a day.
